title: Staging->production security-hardening backlog (2026-06-30 audit)
description:
Plain English: a multi-agent security audit of the Phase-1 staging cluster (the hetzner-k3s config + the staging overlay, PR #417) against the project's own posture (ADR-IC-006/IC-016/PC-005/PC-004) plus CIS Kubernetes hardening found 25 gaps, deduped to ~17 root issues. Most are correctly DEFERRED to a production tier — the staging box is an isolated Hetzner project with synthetic data only, so a break-in can't reach production or real customer data. This epic tracks the gaps in two buckets so nothing is "fine for staging by vibes":

1. staging-go-live (label) — data-independent footguns / cloud cost-abuse risks worth fixing BEFORE the box is publicly exposed. 6 children.
2. production-gated (label) — genuine production requirements correctly deferred for an isolated synthetic-data demo box (HA/DR, network segmentation, secrets-at-rest, audit logging). 3 themed children, each enumerating its sub-gaps with file refs.

Source: the staging-prod-hardening-audit workflow, 2026-06-30. The single highest-impact gap is the publicly-reachable Kubernetes API (6443 open to 0.0.0.0/0); it is classified acceptable-for-staging because auth is a strong mTLS client cert, but it is the deviation that most matters for production.
acceptance_criteria: All staging-go-live children closed before the staging box is publicly exposed; all production-gated children resolved as part of the production cutover.

title: Lifecycle driver: InstallmentRule must present the SCA service-principal scope once /installment is gated (6cpq.14 follow-up)
description:
Plain English: once the loan installment endpoint is gated behind step-up SCA (bd 6cpq.14, PR #405), the automated lifecycle driver must present its scoped service-principal credential when it POSTs an installment — otherwise the engine 422s the driver and the loan schedule silently stalls. Today the InstallmentRule (PR #404) presents ServicePrincipalScope: null (correct while the route is ungated). This wires it to present the lifecycle money-mover scope, mirroring how MaturityRule already presents the deposit scope.

Found by central adr-conformance + contract-review on PR #404. The MaturityRule presents a LOCAL literal DepositMoneyMoverScope = "lifecycle:deposit-money-mover" (named locally, not referencing the engine constant, to keep the driver core dependency-free). InstallmentRule should present the SAME lifecycle scope literal (the engine's single LifecycleMoneyMoverScope authorises maturity+interest+installment via AuthorisedOperations after 6cpq.14). 

MERGE ORDER: this is safe in either order IF done as a local literal — present "lifecycle:deposit-money-mover" on a route that is ungated (harmless, ignored) or gated (authorised). Recommended: merge 6cpq.14 (#405) first, then set InstallmentRule.ServicePrincipalScope and merge #404 — OR update #404 before merging it. Do NOT leave #404 merged with the gate live and InstallmentRule still null.

## Acceptance Criteria
- InstallmentRule presents the lifecycle money-mover service-principal scope (the same one MaturityRule uses) so the driver's gated /installment POST is authorised.
- A driver-path test proves the scoped principal is accepted on the gated /installment route (no 422 for the legitimate driver).
close_reason: Closed

title: Engine: gate the loan money-mover endpoints behind step-up SCA (ADR-IC-010 §P8 / MCP_SCA_GATE_CANNOT_BYPASS)
description:
Plain English: the deposit money-movers (maturity, interest) refuse to settle without fresh strong-authentication — the engine 422s them behind an SCA gate. The loan money-movers (installment, early-repayment, write-off) have NO such gate, even though the new pay_installment MCP tool (bd 6cpq.2, PR #400) and its docs claim one. So an LLM agent — or any caller — can collect an irreversible loan installment with no step-up. This wires the loan endpoints behind the same gate, making the documented contract true and keeping the Live MCP_SCA_GATE_CANNOT_BYPASS commitment honest.

Found by central adr-conformance + contract-reviewer on PR #400 (bd 6cpq.2): a genuine ADR-IC-010 §P8 contradiction — NOT an ADR amend/supersede (the ADR is correct; the code must conform). Today: DepositsEndpoints.Map wires app.MapGroup("/v1/deposits/{id:guid}").AddEndpointFilter<ScaPreconditionFilter>() (maturity+interest only); LoansEndpoints.Map maps /installment etc. directly on app with no group/filter; ScaPreconditionFilter/ScaPrecondition/ScaServicePrincipal are internal to Babelstone.Families.TermDeposit.Application; ScaServicePrincipal.AuthorisedOperations = {maturity, interest}. Integration proof: LoansApiIntegrationTests.cs:150-152 — a no-SCA installment POST returns 200.

Scope: promote ScaPreconditionFilter + ScaPrecondition + ScaServicePrincipal to a shared home both families reference (single gate mechanism, not a duplicated loan copy), wire the irreversible loan money-movers (at minimum /installment; consider /early-repayment, /write-off — but NOT a customer-only surface, mirroring how deposits gate maturity+interest but NOT /terminate) behind the filter inside LoansEndpoints.Map, and extend AuthorisedOperations to include 'installment' so the ADR-PC-036 lifecycle driver (bd 6cpq.9) and the agent path are both authorised scoped-not-blanket. Add a loan integration test: a no-SCA installment POST is 422 SCA_REQUIRED before any side effect; a fresh-attested-SCA POST settles. Unblocks PR #400 to merge with its SCA contract true.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The loan irreversible money-mover route(s) are behind the (promoted, shared) ScaPreconditionFilter; a no-SCA POST /v1/loans/{id}/installment returns 422 SCA_REQUIRED before any side effect (engine integration test proves it; the current 200-OK test is updated).
- ScaServicePrincipal.AuthorisedOperations includes 'installment' (scoped, not blanket — terminate/customer surfaces stay human-SCA-only), so the ADR-PC-036 driver and MCP agent are authorised.
- The gate mechanism is shared (one ScaPreconditionFilter), not a duplicated loan implementation; the deposit gate still passes its existing tests.
- adr-conformance + contract-reviewer PASS on the diff; MCP_SCA_GATE_CANNOT_BYPASS stays Live and now genuinely covers the loan money-movers (catalogue row update DESCRIBED for the orchestrator to apply centrally if needed).
- PR #400 (pay_installment) can merge with its §P8 docstrings/reference true.
close_reason: Closed

title: Code-comment four-rule review across engine projects
description:
Bring every engine C# project up to the code-comment guideline by running the same four-rule pass we did on the kernel.

In plain English: our comments are a heavy, deliberate "why + traceability" layer, and a new guideline (docs/product-management/implementation_guidelines/code-comments.md) defines what keeps them trustworthy. title: Staging — Container images: add multi-arch arm64 builds (account-independent FIRST step)
description:
Plain English: our CI builds Docker images only for Intel/AMD (amd64) chips, but the Hetzner box is an ARM machine. An amd64 image will not even start on ARM (exec format error). So before anything can be deployed there, the images must be built for BOTH architectures. This needs no Hetzner account and is fully checkable on the laptop.

Work: add docker/setup-qemu-action + platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64 (and provenance: true for a manifest list) to .github/workflows/image-build.yml for engine, orchestrator, notification, mcp-server (and pack-validate). They keep landing at ghcr.io/jhosm/babelstone-<svc>, cosign-signed by digest.

Verify locally (memory-light, transient): mise exec -- docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 per Dockerfile. engine/Dockerfile already switches on TARGETARCH; mcp-server (Python) and the .NET chiseled runtime bases need their arm64 build confirmed. acl is a stub (excluded) -> decide build-vs-stub on zla1.5.

Why first: hard prerequisite for zla1.5 (app services) and zla1.6 (Backstage image) -- every deploy step is inert if no image runs on the ARM node. Touches no account, no DNS, no cluster.
close_reason: Closed

title: Disbursement atomicity: eager settle-before-append can orphan an outbound debit if the append fails
description: Plain English: opening a loan pays cash OUT before it durably records the loan, with no shared transaction, so a crash between the two can leave money gone with no loan on file. DisburseAsync settles (SettlementDirection.Debit, Principal) at step 4 then AppendAsync(expectedVersion -1) at step 5; the CommandId idempotency key guards only the append, and SettlementInstruction carries no CommandId, so a retry can double-settle. Because the stream does not yet exist (expectedVersion -1), a failed append leaves an orphaned outbound debit with no record. The settlement adapter is a stub today, so this is latent until a real ACL lands. Consolidates abstraction-fit T1 + saga append-after-settle (HIGH). Evidence: PersonalLoanConstitutionService.cs DisburseAsync steps 4-5; TermDepositConstitutionService de-settled constitution.
acceptance_criteria:
- DisburseAsync de-settled: decide + append LoanDisbursed carrying an Originated Movement; NO eager settlement.SettleAsync on the append path.
- Disbursement direction re-derived against the named account (a Credit to the borrower's account, or a Debit to the funding account — consistent with account_ref); the prior Debit-on-borrower wrinkle is corrected.
- The disbursement cash leg is effected by the substrate settlement saga (depends on t7o3.15).
- MOVEMENT_APPEND_FIRST holds for disbursement; settle-succeeds/append-fails and double-settle-prevented tests pass (MOVEMENT_CASH_LEG_IDEMPOTENT).
- The prior interim-eager / thread-CommandId-into-SettlementInstruction option is withdrawn — eager settle is illegal under ADR-PC-032.
notes: RE-SCOPED 2026-06-23 per ADR-PC-032 (the Movement primitive) + feature-design-money-movement-settlement.md. The fix is no longer 'thread CommandId into SettlementInstruction or document a residual' — it is: implement disbursement as the first Originated Movement (append-first) effected by the substrate settlement saga, closing the orphan window by construction and inheriting the ACL double-debit guard the eager call bypassed. The P1-closing first slice (design §9 step 2). Now depends on the platform t7o3.15.
close_reason: Merged earlier in PR #334 (Movement origin/direction CE headers + de-settle disbursement); closing in post-merge cleanup.

title: ADR-PC-030: babelstone product scope & boundary
description:
Plain English: decide and record, once, what babelstone is for and where its responsibility stops — which banking products it will model and which concerns it deliberately leaves to other systems. This stops scope drift and gives every future family ADR a fixed boundary to honour.

Records the scope/posture decision reached with the maintainer: babelstone is a reference product/accrual kernel. It owns product math + account lifecycle + regulatory-pack config; it delegates payment rails, card schemes, origination/underwriting (solvency/CRC/KYC/affordability), and collections enforcement to external/ACL systems. Family roadmap spans the product topology: term deposit (liability, built), crédito pessoal (closed-end asset), credit-card account/revolving slice (open-end revolving asset; scheme/auth/clearing/dispute stay out of boundary). Origination is upstream — the engine receives an already-approved, already-priced instruction (ties to ADR-PC-024). Supported by promoted market research under product_concepts/research/{credit-cards,credito-pessoal}.

Shape: Tool-selection (ADR-PC-000 §D3 residual posture category; F1/F2 degenerate, decision rides on S1–S4).
notes: REVISED pre-acceptance to posture B — a core product & account ledger (was posture A, a narrow accrual kernel). Engine now owns transactional balance accounts (conta à ordem an instance) + the funds-and-rules core of authorization (saldo disponível, pack rules incl. descoberto, the cativo/hold) as a real-time dependency; still stops at the wire (no rails/scheme/SCA/fraud). 4th roadmap shape = conta à ordem (ADR-PC-016 v4 destination). Real-time commitment fixed; sync-vs-async technique deferred. adr-conformance re-run: PASS, no PC-016 amendment owed. PR #271, branch docs/product-scope-adr-and-research. Open until maintainer accepts/merges.

title: Plugin hooks never load: hooks.json missing the top-level 'hooks' wrapper
description: Plain English: the babelstone-engine plugin's §P1 hooks have been silently inert because hooks.json puts the event map (SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop) at the top level, but the Claude Code plugin schema requires it nested under a top-level 'hooks' key (confirmed against every other installed plugin's hooks.json, which all have keys ['description','hooks']). /doctor reports: 'Hook load failed: expected record at path hooks, received undefined'. Effect: the local immutability PreToolUse warning, PII/analyser/spec-coverage surfacing, PlantUML re-render, session-push reminder, and bd-prime-on-SessionStart never ran (CI hard-gates are unaffected). Fix: wrap the event map under a 'hooks' key (+ a 'description' for parity). One-file change to plugins/babelstone-engine/hooks/hooks.json.

title: Cap integration-test container startup concurrency to kill Testcontainers flakiness
description: Surfaced 2026-06-16/17. The integration lane is FLAKY: each of ~24 integration test classes spins its OWN Redpanda+Postgres container in InitializeAsync, and xUnit runs classes as parallel collections — so ~24 containers race for Docker resources/ports at startup. Failures land in InitializeAsync (Testcontainers spin-up), a DIFFERENT subset each run, ALL passing in isolation. (The merged renewal PRs passed CI's dedicated runner, so it bites mainly locally — but flaky tests are unacceptable.) FIX (maintainer choice): a GLOBAL container-startup SEMAPHORE — keep per-class containers + parallelism but cap how many containers START concurrently (acquire before StartAsync, release once ready), so the Docker daemon isn't thundering-herded. Static SemaphoreSlim in Babelstone.TestFixtures, concurrency configurable via env var with a conservative default; route ALL integration container startups (Redpanda + Postgres; the shared fixtures + the per-class ones) through it. VALIDATE by running the full integration lane several times → zero flakes. Then PR C (mtto.4) rebases onto this and its RenewalSagaIntegrationTests inherit the gate.

title: Persist role + funding-account on DepositConstituted; constitute-renewal resolves renewal facts engine-side
description: PR C.0 (precursor to PR C, bd mtto.4) — chosen by the maintainer over orchestrator-side defaults. The auto-started renewal saga has no per-deposit source for the new deposit's product/role/funding; the closing deposit persists product_code but NOT role/funding. Fix: (1) CONTRACT — add role + funding_account (BOTH structural opaque references, not PII per ADR-PC-004; funding_account is 'a reference, not an IBAN') to DepositConstituted (.avsc BACKWARD nullable + EventCatalog + Events.cs + DecideConstitution stamps them from the command) and fold them into DepositPosition; the renewal-produced DepositConstituted ALSO carries them (chain preservation across renewal generations). (2) ENGINE — ConstituteRenewalAsync resolves product_code (already on the position) + role + funding_account from the CLOSING deposit it already loads, instead of the command; the renewal rate re-resolution (SAME_TERM_CURRENT_RATE) sources (product_code, role) from the closing deposit. Drop ProductId/Role/FundingAccount from ConstituteRenewalCommand + the constitute-renewal endpoint body (minimal). Honors #200/ADR-IC-003 A7 (orchestrator holds no product knowledge; engine resolves). Then PR C (mtto.4) re-lands with a minimal saga command + no RenewalCommandDefaults. Financial math preserved (deciders unchanged; only the product/role/funding SOURCE moves command->closing-deposit).

title: RenewalProcess saga module + substrate event-auto-start machinery + host wiring
description: PR C (final) of the renewal-saga build (bd mtto). Three layers: (1) GENERIC substrate auto-start machinery — SagaInboxEvent gains ExtensionHeaders; SagaConsumeLoop extracts non-standard ce_* headers; SagaAdvanceHandler, on UnknownSaga, checks the registered modules' AutoStartRule (EventAutoStarted + StartEventType match + HeaderPredicate on CE headers) and auto-creates+advances the saga in one tx (family-agnostic — reads only the module's declared rule + headers; the two ORCHESTRATOR_* fitness gates stay green). (2) RenewalProcess family module in Babelstone.Families.TermDeposit.Orchestration — the state machine (RENEWAL_STARTED--DepositMatured-->RENEWAL_CONSTITUTING[ConstituteRenewal]--NewDepositConstituted-->RENEWAL_LINKING[LinkRenewal]--RenewalLinkConfirmed-->RENEWAL_COMPLETED + escalation/HIR/OperatorResolved edges, HIR non-terminal BY TABLE so no IsTerminal override), RenewalResultEvents.Bridge (ConstituteRenewal/LinkRenewal Applied->success Refused->failed, synthesised from HTTP 2xx — NewDepositConstituted is NOT read off the bus, dissolving the ce_subject mismatch), RenewalCommandRouter (->the two PR-B endpoints, Idempotency-Key=saga_outbox row id), a deterministic newDepositId=Derived(process_id) for crash-safety, RenewalSagaModule:ISagaModule (EventAutoStarted, AutoStartRule=DepositMatured + ce_autorenewalpolicy!=NONE, own consumer group babelstone-orchestrator-renewal). (3) Host wiring — Program.cs registers the renewal module + a SECOND consume loop/consumer group + threads modules into SagaAdvanceHandler for auto-start. title: Deployed Kong 500s every edge request: Lua sandbox blocks cjson.safe/resty.http (KONG_UNTRUSTED_LUA_SANDBOX_REQUIRES unset)
description:
In plain English: the Kong edge config (infra/kong/kong.yml) enforces the whole edge policy chain — PSD2 SCA, X-Client-Id attestation, SoR routing — in pre-function Lua that calls require('cjson.safe') and require('resty.http'). kong:3.9.1 defaults to untrusted_lua=sandbox with an EMPTY untrusted_lua_sandbox_requires allowlist, so those require()s are BLOCKED and EVERY constitute / SoR / SCA request returns HTTP 500 ('require ... not allowed within sandbox'). The deployed Kong service (infra/compose.yaml + infra/k8s/base/kong.yaml) sets NO untrusted_lua env (confirmed via grep), so the edge is broken at runtime even though kong-config-check (static parse) passes — the static gate loads no Lua module, so it never sees this.

Fix: set KONG_UNTRUSTED_LUA_SANDBOX_REQUIRES=cjson.safe,resty.http on the deployed Kong service in both infra/compose.yaml and infra/k8s/base/kong.yaml (keep the sandbox ON for security; allowlist ONLY the two modules the kong.yml pre-functions need). Surfaced by the bd babelstone-abig / babelstone-1z0r runtime contract harness (test/edge-runtime-contracts), which sets exactly this env to run green against the real kong.yml byte-for-byte — that harness is the regression guard once the env is added. Governing: ADR-IC-006 (the edge gateway must actually enforce the policy chain at runtime), ADR-PC-018 §5 (SoR fail-closed resolution depends on resty.http loading).
close_reason: Closed

title: CI gate: block a forward .avsc evolution until replay-side writer-schema resolution is wired ON
description:
Residual risk after babelstone-ohdk: the per-event pin is THREADED but resolution is OFF by default (no resolver wired — see the enablement follow-up). So if someone evolves a family .avsc FORWARD (additive/reorder) while the replay serializer still has a null resolver, a projection rebuild silently decodes old bytes writer==reader against the new reader schema -> mis-decode/divergence (the §7.2 slow-drift this whole line of work prevents).

In plain English: until the resolver is actually switched on, evolving a schema is still dangerous on replay. This bead adds a CI gate that FAILS if a forward .avsc change lands while the replay path can't resolve writer schemas — i.e. forbid the dangerous edit until the protection is live. Lift the restriction once the enablement bead is done.

The ReplayPinPerEventTests guard proves the pin is THREADED; it does NOT prove resolution is ENABLED — this gate covers that gap. Discovered from babelstone-ohdk.
close_reason: Obsoleted by ADR-PC-028: a JSON store has no .avsc-evolution replay hazard. Bus schema evolution is governed by SR compatibility (ADR-IC-002) + the bus resolver (PR #123).

title: OpenBaoTransitClient: validate subjectId before path interpolation (path-injection)
description:
HIGH security finding (automated security review of PR #34). engine/src/Babelstone.Pii/OpenBaoTransitClient.cs interpolates subjectId into the OpenBao transit request path unvalidated:

  KeyName(subjectId) => $"pii-{subjectId}"
  used in v1/{mount}/encrypt|decrypt/{KeyName}, v1/{mount}/keys/{KeyName}[/config]

A subjectId containing '/', '..', or URL-special chars could inject a path segment or escape the key namespace (path traversal / URL injection / SSRF-shaped). 'Internal-only' is not a valid dismissal — internal services are common targets, and subjectId may originate from upstream data.

Transit key names are limited to [a-zA-Z0-9_-] anyway (the code comments this charset but does not enforce it). Fix: validate subjectId against [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ in KeyName and throw ArgumentException on violation (reject, do not silently mangle), so every call path (encrypt/decrypt/destroy/ensure-key/key-exists) is guarded at the single chokepoint. Add a Docker-free unit test asserting malicious ids ('../../sys/health', slashes, spaces, query chars, empty) are rejected.

Relates to ADR-PC-004 (PII crypto seam). Shipped in A.5 (archie-qzlb).
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #35 (da3d5a3). subjectId validated at the KeyName chokepoint; path-injection closed.

title: Make project subagents spawnable — plugin-namespace the §P3 review agents
description:
DEFECT: the five ADR-PC-020 §P3 review agents in .claude/agents/ (adr-conformance, financial-math-reviewer, contract-reviewer, replay-determinism-auditor, doc-consistency) cannot be invoked by name via the Task/Agent tool — subagent_type:adr-conformance errors 'agent type not found'.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed vs Claude Code docs): project .claude/agents/*.md register only for AUTOMATIC DELEGATION / @-mention; the Task tool's spawnable registry exposes only built-in, plugin-namespaced, and CLI-passed agents. So these agents have no explicit-spawn handle. Today they must be run as plain general-purpose with the rubric inlined — losing the curated tool-scoping and inviting drift.

IMPACT — why P1: the v1 engine build has started (B.1/archie-s8gn landed) and .claude/agents/README.md mandates running adr-conformance before every engine/contract commit. The §P3 review layer is unusable in its intended form exactly when it is needed.

FIX: package the agents behind a minimal babelstone-engine plugin manifest so they register as babelstone-engine:<name> (the documented spawnable path). Acceptance: each of the five is spawnable by its namespaced subagent_type. This pulls the AGENTS portion forward from archie-bhq.8 (full hooks+skills+agents bundle, P3, 'prove loose first'); bhq.8 remains for the complete versioned plugin.

WORKAROUND until fixed: invoke via natural language / @agent-<name> for auto-delegation, or run general-purpose pointed at the agent's rubric file.

Anchors: ADR-PC-020 §P3/§P4; .claude/agents/README.md ('Once stable they fold into the babelstone-engine plugin (archie-bhq.8)').
notes: VERIFIED (2026-05-26, fresh session): all five §P3 agents now appear in the spawnable-agent registry under their namespaced subagent_type — babelstone-engine:{adr-conformance, contract-reviewer, doc-consistency, financial-math-reviewer, replay-determinism-auditor}. title: ADR-PC-011: Synthetic v4-scale load-test harness
description:
The test itself is fully specified in feature-design-two-modes-asymmetry §8 (workload pattern, p50/p95/p99 thresholds, sustained 250 TPS for 24h, burst 1000 TPS for 15min, replay budgets, determinism with seeded RNG and injected clock, every-RC cadence). This ADR picks the tooling.

Candidates: k6, Gatling, Locust, JMeter, in-house Go/Rust harness.

Decision criteria:
- Drives engine through production APIs, not internal entry points (per §8).
- Standard observability integration (OpenTelemetry per ADR-IC-007).
- Determinism support (seeded RNG, injected clock — §8 hard requirement).
- Test-infrastructure ownership by the engine team on production-shaped hardware.

v1 acceptance gate: this test must run green at v1 RC, not as a v4 deliverable.

Source: Q-AK in 04-open-questions.md; full spec in feature-design-two-modes-asymmetry §8.
close_reason: ADR-PC-011 filed: in-house .NET load-test harness on the production boundary (Redpanda + Kong), measuring §8.3 async latency from OpenTelemetry; k6/Gatling/Locust/JMeter rejected. Indexed in adrs/README.md; Q-AK tooling residual marked resolved in 04-open-questions.md.

title: ADR-PC-010: Engine implementation language and process model
description:
The integration-concept ADRs pick infrastructure (broker, registry, gateway) but deliberately do not pick a language for the engine itself. The engine has its own constraints that may force the choice in a different direction from any individual integration component.

Candidates: C# (on .NET), Elixir, Go, Rust, TypeScript on Node. JVM languages (Java, Kotlin, Scala) are explicitly out of scope; C# is in scope because the CLR is a separate runtime family.

Decision criteria:
- LLM-codability (engine-specific). The engine will be authored primarily by an LLM, so the language must offer (a) deep representation in current training corpora, (b) a strong compile-time or type guardrail that catches plausible LLM mistakes before runtime, (c) convention-heavy idioms over expressive metaprogramming the model has to reason about, and (d) lint/format/test tooling tight enough to serve as an outer iteration loop. Languages with known LLM friction — Rust's borrow checker, Elixir's thinner corpus — must be evaluated against this drag.
- Event-store client maturity for the choice landing in ADR-PC-001.
- Typed-schema tooling fit for the choice landing in ADR-PC-006 (CUE, Pkl, etc. have varying language bindings).
- Numerical correctness for EUR retail banking math (decimal arithmetic — feature-design-event-store-projections handler discipline; financial_concepts cash-flow primitive). C# is the only candidate that ships a native 128-bit decimal as a built-in type (`System.Decimal`); the others rely on libraries (Go's shopspring/decimal, Rust's rust_decimal, TS's big.js / decimal.js, Elixir's Decimal). For the non-C# candidates, library ergonomics and protection against accidental float coercion are what differentiate them.
- Operability by a 1–2 person team (ADR-IC-000 S1) and ecosystem coherence with the ADR-IC-* stack (S2).
- Single-codebase commitment (00-product-vision §5).
- Portuguese-market context. EUR-only math (folds into numerical correctness above); a thin local talent pool for human hand-off / incident response — the LLM-coding assumption reduces but does not eliminate the cost of picking an exotic language relative to the Lisbon developer ecosystem.

Process model: single deployable vs modular monolith vs micro-modules. The brief commits to 'one codebase, one set of images' (00-product-vision §5); the within-process module boundaries remain open.

Source: implicit gap — the brief commits to a build but does not pick a language.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-010 (C# .NET 9 + hand-rolled event-sourcing core). Re-decided 2026-05-23: dropped Marten + Wolverine as runtime dependencies (libraries that manage their own tables) in favour of a hand-rolled thin module on PostgreSQL implementing the ADR-PC-001 P1-P5 contract, the ADR-IC-004 outbox, and the ADR-IC-003 in-house orchestrator directly. No IC-003 amendment needed (reverted). Marten/Wolverine kept as working reference implementations. Collateral: ADR-PC-001 amendment (library deferral filled with hand-rolled module). See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-010-dotnet-hand-rolled-engine.md.

title: ADR-PC-009: Per-instance pack and schema version pinning
description:
Two stability invariants run in parallel per 01-product-architecture §5: every constituted instance pins to the pack version AND the family-schema version active at constitution, and carries both for its entire life.

Decide:
1. Storage shape of the pinning fact (columns on the instance projection? Envelope fields on every event? Separate registry?).
2. Replay-time lookup: how a handler running at time T0 resolves the pack vN.M and schema vN.M active for instance I.
3. PackVersionMigrated and SchemaVersionMigrated event semantics — payload, when emitted, how downstream projections react (per 02-v1-scope-term-deposits §2.4.2).
4. Q-N: breaking-change opt-in mechanics — explicit POST /v1/pack-adoptions, no silent upgrades.
5. Pack-effective-date placeholder for §8 (per-primitive pin-or-float policy, v2-relevant).

Coordinates with ADR-PC-007 (pack manifest) and ADR-PC-006 (schema language).

Source: 01-product-architecture §5, feature-design-configuration-surface §3.5-§3.6, feature-design-configuration-authoring §6.
close_reason: ADR-PC-009 drafted (Status: Proposed): pack/schema versions pinned on the event envelope (per-event, not per-instance) and resolved via pack_versions/schema_versions registries; projection-only and separate-registry candidates rejected on replay-correctness (cannot represent the migration boundary, circular/dual-write); PackVersionMigrated/SchemaVersionMigrated operator-initiated one-per-instance; Q-N opt-in via POST /v1/pack-adoptions (adoption != migration); pack-effective-date a reserved v1 no-op. Committed under product_concepts/adrs/ and indexed in README.

title: ADR-PC-008: Rate-sheet storage and deploy API
description:
Rate sheets are a separate artefact family from product configs, with daily-weekly cadence vs days-weeks (per 01-product-architecture §3 table). Collapsing the three artefact families onto one approval path collapses the cheapest change onto the most expensive approval.

Decide:
1. Storage shape (table-per-rate-sheet, time-series store, KV with version stamping).
2. Deploy API (POST /v1/rate-sheets style with idempotency keys, separate from product-config deploy path).
3. Version resolution at constitution (rate_sheet_version_id on DepositConstituted per 02-v1-scope-term-deposits §2.4.1; how the engine resolves 'the rate sheet effective on this date for this product variant').
4. Approval / sign-off workflow integration (treasury / ALM ownership per 01-product-architecture §3 table).
5. Q-J typo-rollback mechanics (forward-only fix plus out-of-band compensation — confirm structural support).

Source: feature-design-configuration-surface §2.2, 01-product-architecture §3.
close_reason: ADR-PC-008 drafted (Status: Proposed): rate sheets stored as versioned immutable rows in the existing PostgreSQL, JSONB body, indexed (product_family, effective_from) point-in-time resolution in the constitution transaction; separate treasury-gated POST /v1/rate-sheets endpoint idempotent on rate_sheet_version_id; Q-J typo-rollback is forward-only fix + decidable out-of-band compensation. Committed under product_concepts/adrs/ and indexed in README.

title: ADR-PC-007: Pack manifest format and distribution
description:
The pack is declarative data, not executable code, and is version-pinned per instance (per 00-product-vision §3 and 01-product-architecture §5).

Decide:
1. Manifest representation (YAML / JSON / CUE / protobuf descriptors).
2. Versioned registry shape — where packs live, how versions are addressed, how breaking changes are flagged.
3. Deploy mechanism (POST /v1/pack-versions style API per feature-design-configuration-surface §3.4, OCI registry, git-tagged release artefacts).
4. Signing / integrity (regulatory provenance: who signed the canonical PT pack, how the engine verifies it at deploy time).
5. Pack overlay reservation for v5+ multi-pack composition (Q-P), no-op at v1.

Coordinates with ADR-PC-006 (schema language) and ADR-PC-009 (pinning storage).

Source: feature-design-configuration-surface §3.4, 01-product-architecture §5.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-007 (signed YAML in OCI artefact, CUE-validated). Re-decided 2026-05-23 following the ADR-PC-006 CUE change: pack format stays auditor-readable YAML data; schemas/ files are now .cue validated by cue vet; OCI distribution + cosign signing unchanged. Full CUE-native pack rejected (canonical regulatory artefact stays plain YAML). See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-007-signed-yaml-oci-pack.md.

title: ADR-PC-006: Family-schema language and validator runtime
description:
Pick the schema language for typed family schemas with variants, evolving under coarse-start fine-drift (the resolved configuration model — Open Question 4 in 04-open-questions.md, full treatment in feature-design-configuration-authoring §9). The schema is the boundary; no DSL escape hatch.

Candidates: JSON Schema, CUE, Pkl, Avro-as-config, hand-rolled typed DSL.

Decision criteria:
- Supports union types, optional fields, range-bounded scalars, pack-bound primitives (per the §9 four-outcome operational procedure: variant reshape / schema fine-drift / primitive release / roadmap-layer decline).
- Validator runtime supports the 6-depth validator surface from feature-design-configuration-surface §3.6.
- Schema-evolution semantics for fine-drift split-merge (interacts with Q-V; the chosen language must support the split-merge tooling story even if Q-V remains open).
- IDE / authoring ergonomics (relevant to Q-T raw-YAML vs form-UI question, but not gated by it).
- Falsifiability preservation: a variant that 'needs' engine code reveals a schema gap or a primitive gap, never a language bypass (per feature-design-configuration-authoring §7.1).

Coordinates with ADR-PC-007 (pack manifest): pack primitives are typed inside family schemas; schema language and pack format should compose cleanly.

Source: 04-open-questions.md §4 (resolved); feature-design-configuration-authoring §6, §9; feature-design-configuration-surface §3.6.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-006 (CUE + purpose-built Go validator). Re-decided 2026-05-23: dropped the prior JSON Schema + NJsonSchema pick in favour of CUE for native cross-field expressiveness at depths 3-4; validator is a single static Go binary embedding cuelang.org/go, invoked out-of-process; JSON Schema retained as named fallback. See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-006-cue-schema-language.md.

title: ADR-PC-005: DR / RTO / RPO posture for the event store
description:
Production-blocking for v1 cutover. The event store is the engine's source of truth; an event-store-volume loss is unrecoverable from projections alone.

Decide:
1. Backup cadence (continuous WAL shipping, hourly snapshots, daily snapshots).
2. Off-site replication topology (warm standby, cold standby, multi-region).
3. RTO / RPO targets (named numbers, not vague 'fast' / 'small').
4. Cold-replay budget under a *recovery* scenario — distinct from the Q-Z benchmark which measures normal-operations cold replay.

Coordinates with ADR-PC-001 (event store tech — different stores have different replication primitives) and ADR-PC-003 (snapshot infrastructure — snapshots accelerate recovery).

Source: Q-AT in 04-open-questions.md.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-005 (DR/RTO/RPO). WAL streaming + synchronous off-site warm standby + PITR; RPO≈0 for committed events, named RTO/RPO numbers (POC defaults pending bank sign-off); projections/snapshots recovered by rebuild; OpenBao key-store DR coordinated; multi-region deferred. Corrected source citation to Q-AY (issue said Q-AT). Production-blocking. See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-005-dr-rto-rpo.md.

title: ADR-PC-004: PII encryption envelope and key management (crypto-shredding)
description:
Implement §7 of 04-open-questions.md's position: PII fields encrypted per data subject under a per-subject key; erasure = key destruction; cipher-text remains in the event log, plaintext unrecoverable.

Decide:
1. KMS / key-store choice (HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, GCP KMS, pgcrypto, custom HSM-backed). Must be self-hostable per ADR-IC-000 F1.
2. Per-event PII field annotation contract (which fields are encrypted, how marked in the envelope or schema).
3. Key rotation policy and the post-erasure projection behaviour (PII fields return null; structural fields remain in the clear).
4. Audit-trail semantics after erasure ('an event occurred at this transaction_time; payload PII is unrecoverable due to subject erasure').

Gated by DPO confirmation that crypto-shredding satisfies the operating bank's interpretation of Article 17 under PT GDPR transposition (Lei 58/2019). If vetoed, fallback is PII off-store; tombstoning is rejected.

Coordinates with ADR-PC-002 (bitemporal projection): the §6.1 candidate paths must each accept the field-level encryption envelope.

Source: §7 in 04-open-questions.md; feature-design-event-store-projections §6.2.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-004 (crypto-shredding with OpenBao). Key store = OpenBao (MPL-2.0 Vault fork; Vault itself BSL fails F1) per deciders' direction — the deliberate exception to the hand-rolled-core posture since key custody is security-critical. Per-subject transit keys; erasure = key destruction; per-event PII annotation contract; crypto-shred-vs-backup-horizon tension flagged jointly with PC-005. Status Proposed pending DPO. See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-004-pii-crypto-shredding.md.

title: ADR-PC-003: Snapshot mechanism for the event store
description:
Decide snapshot storage shape, generation cadence, replay-from-snapshot semantics, and snapshot validation (rebuild-from-log periodic comparison).

Non-negotiable from feature-design-two-modes-asymmetry §6: snapshot infrastructure must be exercised in v1, not retrofitted for v4. Snapshots accelerate rebuild; they do not replace the log (per 01-product-architecture §2).

Coordinates with ADR-PC-001 (event store technology): snapshot storage may be inside the chosen event-store, in PostgreSQL, or in a separate blob store.

Acceptance: snapshot read/write API, validation cadence, retention policy, and operational runbook stub.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-003 (same-database PostgreSQL snapshots table). Eventually-consistent writes, hash-and-verify, advisory-until-6-months, monthly discard-and-rebuild; recomputable, never replaces the log; read/write API hides storage so object-store offload is a non-breaking v4 option. See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-003-postgresql-snapshots.md.

title: ADR-PC-002: Bitemporal projection implementation
description:
Pick the implementation mechanism for bitemporal projections (every row carries valid_time and transaction_time, four time-dimensional capabilities supported).

Candidates: PostgreSQL temporal extensions, XTDB / Datomic-style, application-level bitemporality on plain Postgres.

Spike specification — 5-day timebox per path, four-deliverable scope (deposit-position projection end-to-end, per-subject PII encryption envelope, cold-replay performance run, operational profile doc), six scoring criteria in priority order — laid out in feature-design-event-store-projections §6.3.

Gated by Q-Y outcome (DPO/compliance confirmation that PT regulators expect bitemporality): if bitemporal is required, full scoring proceeds; if unitemporal is sufficient, criteria 1 and 6 fall away and the choice collapses to operational fit; if bitemporal is forbidden, projection schemas simplify materially.

Coordinates with ADR-PC-001 (event store technology): cold-replay scoring crosses the event-store / projection boundary; spikes share fixtures.

Source: Q-X in 04-open-questions.md.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-002 (application-level bitemporality on plain PostgreSQL). Mechanism (Q-X) chosen ahead of the §6.3 spike because ADR-PC-010's hand-rolled-PG decision forecloses XTDB/new-datastore paths and the field-level PII envelope (PC-004) needs field-granular columns; PG temporal extensions add an extension/version coupling without solving field-level erasure. Status Proposed pending Q-Y. See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-002-application-level-bitemporality.md.

title: ADR-PC-001: Event store technology
description:
Pick the engine's source-of-truth store. Candidates: Kurrent / EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL-based event-store-on-tables, Redpanda-as-event-store.

Constraints:
- Outbox co-location with ADR-IC-004 (event-store append and outbox-write commit in one local transaction).
- Forward-only schema discipline, snapshot mechanism, partition_key on every envelope (per feature-design-two-modes-asymmetry §6).
- Replay budgets: cold replay 5s for with-a-plan, 30s for irregular (per feature-design-event-store-projections §8.2).
- Must support the synthetic v4-scale load test (Q-AK) at v1 acceptance.

Coordinates with ADR-PC-002 (bitemporal projection impl): share cold-replay fixtures so the spikes run in lockstep (per feature-design-event-store-projections §6.3).

Source: Q-AC in 04-open-questions.md.
close_reason: ADR-PC-001 committed: PostgreSQL-based event store, co-located with the ADR-IC-004 outbox so event-append and outbox-write commit atomically. Kurrent and Redpanda-as-event-store rejected on outbox co-location, bitemporal-query, field-level PII crypto, and snapshot-transactionality grounds. README index updated. 01-product-architecture §2, feature-design-event-store-projections §10.4, and Q-AC cross-referenced.

title: ADR-PC-000: ADR-PC namespace conventions and contract-shape framework
description:
Establish the ADR-PC namespace as a peer to ADR-IC. Decide:

1. Reuse of ADR-IC-000 evaluation framework (hard filters F1/F2, soft criteria S1-S4) for ADR-PC tool-selection ADRs (ADR-PC-001 through ADR-PC-011).
2. A complementary 'contract-shape' pattern for signal-contract ADRs (ADR-PC-012 through ADR-PC-018) where F1 (cost) and F2 (regulatory fit) don't apply because the deliverable is an event-payload contract rather than a tool pick. Structure: Decision / Consequences / Residual risks core without the evaluation table.
3. Numbering policy: ADR-PC-NNN is independent of ADR-IC-NNN; both namespaces still require disk + bd dual-check before picking a number (per bd memory adr-numbering-check-disk-and-bd).
4. File naming and cross-linking conventions matching CLAUDE.md.

Acceptance: ADR-PC-000 committed; product_concepts/adrs/README.md created with index entry; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md updated to name the second namespace.
close_reason: ADR-PC-000 committed under docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/. README index created. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md updated to name the ADR-PC namespace and the contract-shape template.

title: Create v1 product engine ADRs (ADR-PC series)
description:
Translate the brief and design notes under docs/product-management/product_concepts/ into a series of namespaced ADRs (ADR-PC-NNN) that decide the load-bearing technical commitments needed to start v1 implementation.

Sister namespace: ADR-IC-NNN under docs/product-management/integration_concepts/adrs/ already decides infrastructure (broker, registry, gateway, ACL, observability, etc.) per ADR-IC-000's evaluation framework. The ADR-PC series is a peer set focused on the product engine's own concern surface: source of truth and state, configuration surface, engine runtime, boundary signal contracts, and coexistence with the legacy core.

Scope of the epic:
- Establish ADR-PC namespace conventions (numbering, location, evaluation framework reuse vs amendment for signal-contract ADRs).
- Decide and document the foundational ADRs that block v1 engine code being written.
- Decide and document the configuration-surface ADRs that block product authoring.
- Decide and document the boundary-signal contract ADRs that block integration with out-of-scope systems (GL, AML/KYC, notifications, IFRS 9).
- Decide and document the coexistence ADRs that block strangler-fig adoption for v1.

Out of scope (deferred): pack-effective-date semantics policy, numerical IRR solver for TAEG, bulk-command authorisation model, moratorium catalogue, tax-engine pluggability, customer-master cutover. These are v2+ peers, tracked in 04-open-questions.md.

Acceptance: every child issue closed with its ADR file committed under docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/, cross-linked from the relevant numbered brief or design note, and indexed in a product_concepts/adrs/README.md.
close_reason: ADR-PC series complete: all 22 children closed (ADR-PC-000..018, 019, 020, and the PC-000 Verifiable-commitments amendment). Implementation Open Actions tracked in new epic archie-bhq.

title: Re-argue ADR-002 AWS Glue rejection on F2 grounds, not cross-ADR consistency
description: ADR-002 line 77 rejects AWS Glue Schema Registry partly on the basis that 'Cloud dependency is inconsistent with ADR-001's self-hosted posture'. That is not an F2 criterion — F2 is GDPR/DORA/PSD2 fit. The actual F2 grounds are present in the same cell: data residency requires explicit EU region configuration (GDPR), and DORA resilience testing is not under operator control on a SaaS. Lead with those concrete regulatory grounds; drop the cross-ADR consistency clause. The current framing risks circular reasoning — Glue fails because other ADRs picked self-hosted, not because the regulatory filter actually fails it.
close_reason: Rewrote AWS Glue F2 row in ADR-002 to ground the Fail verdict in actual F2 criteria (GDPR data-residency control surface, DORA operator-control over resilience testing). title: ADR-000: Common evaluation criteria for all tool selections
description:
Define the shared evaluation template that every ADR (001–010) will apply. Produces a reusable criteria rubric and a short prose section that each ADR includes by reference.

## Why this exists

Each ADR will evaluate different tools against different functional requirements, but a set of cross-cutting criteria applies to all of them. Defining these once avoids drift between ADRs and forces each decision to be honest about the same hard constraints.

## Budget constraint

**Budget is effectively 0€.** This is a first-class filter, not a soft preference. It means:
- Managed cloud services (Confluent Cloud, Datadog, Temporal Cloud, AWS MSK, etc.) are disqualified unless they have a genuinely usable free tier with no credit-card-required production cliff.
- Self-hosted open-source is the default mode.
- Tools with open-core models are acceptable only if the features required by the architecture sit in the free/community tier — the ADR must explicitly verify this.
- Licensing traps (BSL, SSPLv1, ELv2, Commons Clause) must be flagged even if currently free, because they constrain future use.

## Criteria to define

1. **Cost / licensing** — total cost of self-hosting (infra, ops time) vs free tier limits; licence type and change risk.
2. **Regulatory fit** — GDPR (data residency, right to erasure), DORA (resilience testing, RTO/RPO documentation), PSD2 (audit trail, SCA). Hard pass/fail before functional comparison.
3. **Operational complexity at small scale** — how much ops burden does this add to a small team? Preference for tools that degrade gracefully when not actively tuned.
4. **Ecosystem coherence** — does it compose with the rest of the chosen stack without bespoke glue? Native OpenTelemetry, standard connectors, etc.
5. **Exit cost** — how painful is migration away in 3–5 years? Does the tool own a data format or protocol that creates lock-in?
6. **Community and longevity** — is this tool likely to still be maintained in 10 years? Red flags: single-vendor control with recent licence change, stagnant commits, small contributor base.
7. **Functional fit** — tool-specific criteria defined per ADR.

## Deliverable

A markdown section titled '## Common Evaluation Criteria' usable as a template block in each ADR, plus a summary rubric table (criteria × weight) that each ADR fills in for its candidates.
acceptance_criteria: Template section written and agreed. Each ADR-001–010 issue updated to reference this template.

title: Thread LifecycleCommandKey through PayInterestCommand — prerequisite for any deposit coupon lifecycle rule
description:
In plain English: paying a deposit coupon twice by accident is currently prevented only by a legality gate and a concurrency check — a sequential retry after a success quietly pays the NEXT coupon. Before the lifecycle driver ever gets a coupon rule (which retries by design), the interest command must carry the same server-derived idempotency key maturity already has.

Thread a CommandId through PayInterestCommand and TermDepositConstitutionService.PayInterestAsync, deriving LifecycleCommandKey.Derive(deposit_id, "pay_interest", CouponsPaid+1) in DepositsEndpoints.PayInterestAsync (mirror MatureAsync: derive + command-log pre-check + DuplicateCommandException catch). ADR-PC-036 already scopes deposit coupons as the future fourth rule, so this is the ADR-conformant hardening. Surfaced by central adr-conformance + contract-reviewer on PR #443 (the spec over-claimed this guarantee; PR #443 corrected the spec to maturity-only and documents the residual — this issue closes the residual). HARD ORDERING: must land before any coupon rule joins the lifecycle driver dispatch.

title: Rebuild the term_deposit.withholding_ledger projection after PR #441 deploys (ordered, alarm-windowed)
description:
In plain English: PR #441 taught the withholding ledger to date legacy tax flows, but the fix only takes effect once the ledger projection is rebuilt from the event store — and until that rebuild runs, the daily reconciliation checks will (correctly) complain.

Run, in order: (1) deploy the PR #441 fold; (2) spot-check a sample of real pre-field WithholdingApplied streams (event order + Tax+Net vs the neighbouring InterestAccrued gross) to confirm the legacy emitter's adjacency premise; (3) run ProjectionDrainer.RebuildAsync for kind term_deposit.withholding_ledger with the relay quiescent for the kind (ADR-PC-002 supersede-all + checkpoint reset + cold re-fold — audit-preserving, not a truncate); (4) re-enable/trust reconciliation. Expected alarms inside the deploy->rebuild window only: §7.1 daily checksum mismatch on every legacy belief row of the kind (explicit PendingAccrual:null member), event-count reconciliation false-alarms (the fold now consumes InterestAccrued), one FullRebuildDrill divergence. Any of these after step 3 completes is real. Exit criterion: statement scheduling passes with zero pre-field InvalidOperationExceptions from WithholdingStatementRule, or each residual un-dated flow is triaged (no paired accrual — needs investigation, per the guard message). Deadline-bound: must complete before the first annual statement window (parent context: babelstone-60n8.13 / PR #441).

title: Settlement substrate: per-occurrence settlement instances for recurring schedules (one-terminal-saga-per-ce_subject gap)
description:
In plain English: the settlement machinery tracks one saga per account/instrument, and once that saga completes it never restarts — so for products that move money repeatedly (monthly installments), the second and later movements have no settlement process of their own to succeed, fail, or park in.

SagaStateStore.TryStartAsync is ON CONFLICT (process_id) DO NOTHING with process_id = ce_subject = aggregate id; SagaAdvanceHandler no-ops events at a terminal saga; SETTLEMENT_COMPLETED is terminal. So after a loan's first Originated leg completes, installment N's leg can neither start nor park under the probed key — exactly the recurring surface LCD-2 gates. Decide + build per-occurrence settlement instances (e.g. derived subjects per occurrence, per ADR-PC-032 §A9/A10's derived-subject scheme, which today covers redelivery/fan-out only) or an explicit re-arm semantics. Needs recording against ADR-PC-032/ADR-IC-018 (open-questions entry rides with PR #442). Also the root cause of the duplicate observation surfaced by the lane: later cash legs may never be driven. Surfaced by central adr-conformance on PR #442.
close_reason: Merged: 3o6m/9z9w via PR #447, qpiw.3 via PR #445, 60n8.* and 2t16.14 via PR #446

title: Personal-loan orchestration module: feed loan Movement-bearing events to the settlement saga (LCD-2 write side)
description:
In plain English: the new settlement-health gate holds a loan's next installment while the previous one's cash is stuck — but today no loan cash leg can ever get stuck, because the personal-loan family ships no orchestration module, so its Movement-bearing events never reach the settlement saga at all. The gate is armed but its trigger is unreachable.

Build the personal-loan Orchestration module (mirroring term-deposit's) so the family's FamilyIntegrationTopics join the settlement saga's consume set (orchestrator Program.cs discovery) and loan Originated Movements are driven through SettlementProcess. Until this lands, commitment-catalogue LCD-2 is scoped Live-for-the-read-side only (see PR #442). Surfaced by central adr-conformance on PR #442. Refs: ADR-PC-036 §Decision 4, ADR-IC-018, ADR-PC-032.
close_reason: Merged: 3o6m/9z9w via PR #447, qpiw.3 via PR #445, 60n8.* and 2t16.14 via PR #446

title: Backfill WithheldOn for pre-field WithholdingApplied events before the first annual statement window
description:
In plain English: old withholding events written before the date field existed now make the statement job fail loudly (on purpose, PR #427) instead of silently under-reporting — but those deposits still can't get a statement until someone writes the missing dates back. That backfill must land before the first yearly statement run or legacy depositors' statements are stuck.

Author the backfill/attribution for pre-field WithholdingApplied events (per-tax-year attribution from the flow's own occurrence data), with replay-determinism + financial-math review. The fail-loud guard (bd babelstone-60n8.9, PR #427) is the detector; this is the cure. The §P3 financial-math review's explicit caveat: confirm this precedes the first annual scheduling window.
close_reason: Merged in PR #441 (feat/withholding-backfill)

title: Guard the SSH allow-list against REPLACE_ME / 0.0.0.0/0 (provisioning preflight)
description:
Plain English: the cloud-firewall rule that decides which IP may SSH into the node ships as the literal text REPLACE_ME/32. The danger is what a hurried operator does when create fails on that invalid value: the quickest "make it work" fix is to type 0.0.0.0/0, which opens the login port to the entire internet on the one machine that holds etcd, the cluster-admin credential, and the cloud token. The risk is independent of the data being synthetic.

Fix: make the SSH source fail-closed and explicit — source it from a required environment variable / CI secret (like HCLOUD_TOKEN already is) so an unset value aborts the provision, and add a pre-create check that rejects REPLACE_ME and any 0.0.0.0/0 (or non-/32) value on the SSH list. Prefer key-only SSH via a bastion / the Hetzner private network rather than a public SSH port at all.

Severity: medium. Refs: infra/hetzner-k3s/cluster.yaml:36 (cluster.yaml is operator-run, not CI-applied, so nothing validates the value today). ADR-IC-006 (minimise public surface); CIS host-hardening.
acceptance_criteria: A pre-create check refuses provisioning if networking.allowed_networks.ssh is unset, still REPLACE_ME, or 0.0.0.0/0; the SSH CIDR is sourced from a required env var/secret so an unset value aborts rather than inviting a 0.0.0.0/0 paste.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make the off-box backup real + alert on backup failure/staleness
description:
Plain English: the one copy of the data that survives losing the whole machine is a nightly database dump pushed to off-site object storage. But its credentials and bucket are still literal REPLACE_ME placeholders, and nothing anywhere raises an alarm if the job fails — you would discover the off-box backup never existed only at the moment you needed to restore. A backup you cannot see failing is a backup you do not have; this footgun applies regardless of data sensitivity.

Fix: provision the real Hetzner Object Storage credentials as an uncommitted / OpenBao-backed secret, add a backup-health signal (alert on Job/CronJob failure AND on freshness: last successful object older than ~26h), and have the job assert an object was actually written before exiting 0.

Severity: high. Refs: infra/k8s/overlays/staging/backup-cronjobs.yaml:110-114 (REPLACE_ME S3 creds), infra/grafana/prometheus/alert-rules.yaml (no Job-failure rule), staging-ops.md §1 step 5 / §3. ADR-PC-005 §P2 (off-site backups, restore not assumed).
acceptance_criteria: Real Hetzner Object Storage creds provisioned as an uncommitted secret; alerts fire on backup Job/CronJob failure AND on backup-freshness (last object older than ~26h); the backup job asserts an object was written before exiting 0.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: PR #440 delivered the authoring half (fail-closed backup job + BackupJobFailed/BackupFreshnessStale alert rules; kubeconform-clean). Remaining is the maintainer half: provision real Hetzner Object Storage credentials as an uncommitted/OpenBao-backed secret (+ optionally Pushgateway/kube-state-metrics so both alert legs go live). Returning the issue to open for that half; see also the new object-lock follow-up issue.

title: Stop rendering committed dev-placeholder Secrets into the staging deploy
description:
Plain English: the staging deploy bundle still contains example secrets with values anyone can read in the repo — the database password is literally 'babelstone', the OpenBao master token is 'root', and the Logto token-signing key is a committed placeholder. The runbook tells the operator to replace these by hand, but every redeploy re-applies the bundle and silently overwrites whatever real secrets the operator set, putting the known placeholder values back.

Fix: remove base/secrets.example.yaml from the applied set in real overlays (a kustomize component/patch that drops it) or source all secrets from an external store (OpenBao / sealed-secrets / SOPS) so the deploy never carries credential bodies; make the deploy fail closed if a placeholder (e.g. token 'root', the dev OIDC key) is detected at apply time so a forgotten swap can't reach the public IAM.

Severity: high. Refs: infra/k8s/base/kustomization.yaml:41, base/secrets.example.yaml:16-24, overlays/staging/logto-jobs.yaml:100-104, cd.yml:199-210 (re-applies the full render). ADR-PC-004 §A1 (never inline literal credentials). Note: the OIDC value is a non-PEM placeholder, so this bricks/forces a broken public IAM rather than directly minting forgeable tokens.
acceptance_criteria: kustomize build overlays/staging emits no placeholder credential bodies (POSTGRES_PASSWORD=babelstone, OPENBAO_DEV_TOKEN=root, dev OIDC key); the apply fails closed if a placeholder value is detected; real secrets are not clobbered on redeploy.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add a Pod Security Admission baseline + hardened securityContexts
description:
Plain English: Kubernetes can refuse to run containers that ask for dangerous powers (running as root, turning off the syscall filter, grabbing host capabilities). That guard is off here, so any app container can run privileged — exactly what turns an ordinary app bug into a full break-out onto the host, the break-out that on a single node hands over every secret. Turning the guard on costs nothing data-wise.

Fix: label the app namespace pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline (then restricted) and add a default-hardened securityContext to every workload (runAsNonRoot, allowPrivilegeEscalation:false, drop ALL capabilities, seccompProfile RuntimeDefault, readOnlyRootFilesystem where feasible), granting back only the specific capability a workload needs (e.g. OpenBao IPC_LOCK). Note: a blanket enforce=baseline would reject OpenBao's IPC_LOCK, so it needs a per-workload exemption, not a one-line flip.

Severity: high. Refs: infra/k8s/base/namespace.yaml (no PSA label), infra/k8s/base/openbao.yaml:61-63 (only securityContext in the tree; it ADDS a cap). ADR-IC-016 (zero-trust internal posture); CIS PSA section.
acceptance_criteria: babelstone-staging namespace carries pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce (baseline, ideally restricted); every workload sets runAsNonRoot, allowPrivilegeEscalation:false, capabilities.drop:[ALL], seccompProfile:RuntimeDefault, with OpenBao's IPC_LOCK granted back explicitly.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cap the in-cluster Hetzner token blast radius (project spend limit + budget alert)
description:
Plain English: the Hetzner cloud-controller + CSI drivers need a read/write Hetzner API token, which hetzner-k3s stores as a plain secret inside the cluster. A break-in could use it to spin up expensive servers (crypto-mining) or delete the box — a money/account-abuse risk that has nothing to do with the (synthetic) data.

Hetzner tokens are binary read-only-vs-read-write and cannot be scoped to specific resources, so the realistic levers are: keep the dedicated babelstone-staging project isolated (already done), set a hard project spend cap + budget alert so a compromised token cannot run up an unbounded bill, and treat the token as rotate-on-incident. Pair with the Pod Security + NetworkPolicy work so an app escape never reaches the kube-system secret in the first place.

Severity: high. Refs: infra/hetzner-k3s/cluster.yaml:9-15 (token), :73-74 (CSI). No governing ADR (CIS hardening).
acceptance_criteria: A hard spend cap / budget alert is set on the babelstone-staging Hetzner project; the project is confirmed isolated from any prod/billing-sensitive account; token treated as rotate-on-incident.

title: Scope CD to a deploy ServiceAccount, not a cluster-admin kubeconfig
description:
Plain English: the deploy pipeline uses an all-powerful, never-expiring master key (a cluster-admin kubeconfig stored as the KUBECONFIG_B64 GitHub secret). If it leaks it cannot be revoked without rebuilding the cluster's certificate authority, and it can read every secret in the cluster including the in-cluster Hetzner token. That cost/abuse blast radius is independent of whether the data is synthetic, which is why it is worth fixing now.

Cheap now-fix: bind CD to a deploy ServiceAccount with a Role scoped to exactly what the overlay apply needs (not cluster-admin), and hand CD that SA token. Later/production: mint a short-lived token per run via OIDC federation rather than a stored secret.

Severity: high. Refs: infra/hetzner-k3s/cluster.yaml:20, .github/workflows/cd.yml:200-210, infra/runbooks/staging-ops.md §1.1. ADR-IC-016 §3 / ADR-PC-004 §A1 set the bar (they scope the OpenBao boundary to app creds, not CI kubeconfigs, but the least-privilege principle is the same).
acceptance_criteria: CD applies the staging overlay with a namespaced deploy ServiceAccount token (RBAC scoped to what 'kubectl apply -k overlays/staging' needs), not the cluster-admin KUBECONFIG_B64.
close_reason: Closed

title: Generalize host-names-no-family + extract a shared FamilyModuleScanner so discovery is the default
description: Two halves of 'composition by discovery, not hand-wiring'. (1) Generalize the engine host's source-scan that asserts Program.cs names no Babelstone.Families.* type (ENGINE_API_HOST_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC) to EVERY composition root (orchestrator, notification, lifecycle). (2) Extract a generic FamilyModuleScanner<TModule> (shared Babelstone.Cadence lib) from the near-duplicate engine HostModuleLoader + lifecycle LifecycleModuleLoader so every host gets assembly-scan for free and none can skip it. Subsumes bd babelstone-kuw2 (notification adopts assembly-scan) as the notification slice.

title: Default-deny universal family->core fitness gate (unmarked project = must-be-agnostic)
description: Replace the per-estate hardcoded allowlists with ONE repo-wide gate that enumerates EVERY .csproj and asserts the family -> core arrow by default. Classification via a single machine-readable signal: an MSBuild <BabelstoneRole> property defaulting to Core (must be family-agnostic) when ABSENT, so a new project is gated by default. Only the ~4 composition roots declare <BabelstoneRole>CompositionRoot</BabelstoneRole> (the explicit, visible opt-out that MAY reference families); family contributions are recognised by families/** path; test projects (IsTestProject) are skipped. Keep the existing per-estate ADR-sync sibling tests as the decision-linked layer; this is the default-deny BACKSTOP that auto-covers new estates.

title: Cross-cutting ADR: the family-agnostic-core + composition-root-discovery covenant
description: Author ONE cross-cutting ADR that states the covenant currently re-decided per estate (ADR-PC-021 engine, ADR-IC-018 orchestrator, ADR-IC-019 notification, ADR-PC-036 lifecycle): every product core/substrate SHALL be family-agnostic (the family -> core arrow, no reverse edge); every composition root SHALL compose families by discovery and name no concrete family in code; both SHALL be enforced by default-deny fitness functions. Rule-of-three is satisfied (four estates prove the pattern identically). A new estate then INHERITS the covenant + cites this ADR instead of synthesizing it from four precedents. Maintainer accepts.
acceptance_criteria: A single Accepted ADR states the covenant; the four estate ADRs reference it; the catalogue's *_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC rows cite it as a shared governing source.

title: Make the family-agnostic substrate covenant default-deny and self-applying
description: Today the 'family -> core arrow' (a family-agnostic core never references families/**) is enforced by SEPARATE per-estate fitness tests, each HARDCODING the list of core projects it guards (engine spine = 8 projects, orchestrator substrate = 1, notification core = 1, lifecycle core = 1). Nothing checks a NEW core/substrate project automatically — it is protected only if someone remembers to write a new per-estate test or extend a list. That is exactly why the lifecycle driver shipped with the arrow reversed (the core referenced both family assemblies) until PR #404 fixed it. The only convention-driven gate is the engine HOST one, which pattern-scans for Babelstone.Families.* and auto-covers any family with zero edits. Goal of this epic: flip the whole invariant to DEFAULT-DENY and self-applying — a new substrate piece is family-agnostic-by-default and CANNOT silently violate the arrow; opting out (declaring yourself a composition root that may name families) is one explicit, visible declaration. Generalize the same way for 'host names no family' and 'compose by discovery, not hand-wiring'.
close_reason: All 4 children closed — ADR-PC-040 covenant + default-deny gate + shared FamilyModuleScanner (now Babelstone.Composition) landed in PR #437; CODE_DIRS auto-derivation in PR #426

title: Notification host: adopt assembly-scan module discovery (NotificationModuleLoader)
description: The notification host still composes its family contributions from a hand-maintained explicit list of IFamilyNotificationModule instances in Program.cs (ADR-PC-021 'explicit-list-now'), so adding a notification family means editing the host. Adopt assembly-scan discovery — a NotificationModuleLoader that scans the Babelstone.Families.* assemblies for IFamilyNotificationModule (base-directory probe), fails loud on a duplicate FamilyName, returns a stable order — matching the engine's HostModuleLoader and the lifecycle driver's LifecycleModuleLoader (the latter landed in PR #404). ADR-IC-019 records this swap as a host-only change with zero family diff. Its OWN PR (decoupled from the lifecycle change at the maintainer's request).

title: Lifecycle driver: relocate family rules to *.Lifecycle contributions + host assembly-scan discovery
description: Adding a clock-driven lifecycle to a product family should not require editing the driver host. Relocate MaturityRule/InstallmentRule out of the family-agnostic Babelstone.Lifecycle core into per-family Babelstone.Families.{TermDeposit,PersonalLoan}.Lifecycle contributions (each an IFamilyLifecycleModule that binds its own Npgsql read-model store + registers its rule), and have the host discover them by assembly-scan (LifecycleModuleLoader, mirroring the engine's HostModuleLoader). This restores the family->core arrow the driver core had violated (it referenced both family assemblies) and resolves PR #404's placement note, which flagged the relocation for the central adr-conformance review (verdict: PASS, no amendment owed).
acceptance_criteria: Driver core Babelstone.Lifecycle has zero families/** ProjectReference (LIFECYCLE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC fitness test green); host Program.cs names no family; LifecycleModuleLoader discovers term_deposit + personal_loan by assembly-scan with no host edit (Babelstone.Lifecycle.Host.Tests green, incl. fail-loud on duplicate FamilyName); full solution builds clean; the rule tests pass in their new family .Lifecycle.Tests homes.
