title: Kong: add the loan-installment edge channel + service-principal route allowance for the lifecycle driver
description:
Plain English: the engine now gates the loan installment money-mover behind step-up SCA (bd 6cpq.14), but Kong's edge has no loan route — its engine-lifecycle-movers service only exposes the deposit maturity/interest routes. So in a real deployment the driver's POST /v1/loans/{id}/installment never gets the X-SCA-Service-Principal attested at the edge, the engine falls back to human-SCA, and 422s the machine driver. It is fail-closed and safe, but the driver's loan path is incomplete end-to-end until Kong is extended.

Found by central adr-conformance on PR #405 (advisory 1). infra/kong/kong.yml engine-lifecycle-movers exposes only ~/v1/deposits/[^/]+/(maturity|interest)$ (no loans route). The scope TOKEN string is already in lock-step (kong.yml ~915); only the loan installment ROUTE allowance is missing. Extend the Kong route-scoped allowance (and any ADR-IC-021 IAM scope mapping) to cover POST /v1/loans/{id}/installment for the driver principal. Relates ADR-PC-036, ADR-IC-021.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Kong's engine-lifecycle-movers (or equivalent) route allows POST /v1/loans/{id}/installment for the gateway-attested service principal.
- The driver's loan installment path works end-to-end through the edge in a deployment (the attested X-SCA-Service-Principal flows; no spurious 422).
notes: 2026-06-29 SCOPE CORRECTION — PR #405 landed the SINGLE-scope design (commit 64eac37): one ScaServicePrincipal.LifecycleMoneyMoverScope = "lifecycle:deposit-money-mover", with installment added to AuthorisedOperations (NOT the per-family two-scope variant that was briefly on the branch as f169424 and then reverted). So this Kong follow-up does NOT need to register a new 'lifecycle:loan-money-mover' scope. The only work is: add POST /v1/loans/{id}/installment to the engine-lifecycle-movers Kong service's route allowance so the EXISTING 'lifecycle:deposit-money-mover' service-principal scope is attested on the loan route. The kong.yml:914 'lock-step with ScaServicePrincipal.LifecycleMoneyMoverScope' comment is ACCURATE under single-scope (that constant exists), so no comment fix needed. Companion: bd 6cpq.15 sets InstallmentRule.ServicePrincipalScope to the same "lifecycle:deposit-money-mover" literal.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lift the async projection relay registration to a family-neutral home
description:
In plain English: today the background worker that fills every family's read models and projections is started inside the term-deposit module. That means any other family (e.g. personal_loan) only gets its projections drained because term-deposit happens to be co-hosted — host personal_loan alone and its read model would never fill. This lifts that worker's registration to the family-neutral composition root so no single family owns shared spine infrastructure.

Move the ProjectionRegistry + ProjectionDrainer + ProjectionRelayOptions + ProjectionRelayService registration out of TermDepositHostModule into a family-neutral home (an AddProjectionRuntime() hosting extension in Babelstone.Engine.Hosting, called once from Program.cs, the ADR-PC-021 §D4 composition root). To keep the neutral registry complete, term-deposit's read-model runner must also flow through the IProjectionModule seam (a new DepositReadModelModule mirroring personal_loan's InstallmentCalendarReadModelModule) rather than being appended directly to a registry term-deposit composes. After this, every family contributes only IProjectionModule(s); the host owns the single relay.
acceptance_criteria: 1. TermDepositHostModule no longer registers ProjectionRegistry/ProjectionDrainer/ProjectionRelayOptions/ProjectionRelayService. 2. The relay is registered once in a family-neutral home (Program.cs via an Engine.Hosting extension). 3. term-deposit's read-model runner is contributed via an IProjectionModule (DepositReadModelModule), not .Append. 4. Hosting either family alone yields a working relay that drains its projections/read model. 5. All affected engine + family test projects pass; EngineFamilyAgnosticTests stays green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: monitoring, health, and alerting for the always-on money-mover host
description:
In plain English: the lifecycle-driver host moves money on a schedule, and its worst failures are silent by construction — a settlement that parks for human intervention quietly stalls a loan's whole schedule (the settlement-health gate holds the next occurrence), with no arrears state anywhere to make the stall visible. This wires up observability — parity with the notification sibling's OpenTelemetry — plus the alert that turns that silent stall into a page.

Builds on babelstone-6cpq.7 (the host skeleton); the settlement-health gate that produces the stall is babelstone-6cpq.10 (LCD-2). Independent of the ADR sibling (this is mechanical wiring, not a mechanism choice).
acceptance_criteria:
- The host wires OpenTelemetry tracing+logging (parity with the notification sibling host, ADR-IC-007 Layer 1) and exposes a liveness/health signal.
- Metrics cover tick liveness, dispatch lag, and POST success/failure.
- A permanently-parked settlement that holds occurrence N+1 (the settlement-health gate, LCD-2) raises an alert — ADR-PC-036 §Residual-risks "must be alerted, not invisible"; there is no arrears state for the miss to land in.
- An on-call runbook entry exists for the parked-settlement / stalled-schedule condition.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: a durable, crash-surviving dispatch ledger (replace the in-memory HashSet)
description:
In plain English: the host's dispatch ledger today is just an in-memory set (a `HashSet<Guid>` behind a lock), so it forgets everything on restart and is not shared between replicas — after a reboot it re-derives and re-POSTs every still-due occurrence, and the engine then dedupes them. This replaces it with a durable, shared ledger so a restart does not re-POST, and so there is an auditable record of what the driver dispatched and when.

Builds on babelstone-6cpq.7 (the host skeleton); the substrate is fixed by the ADR sibling (which blocks this).
acceptance_criteria:
- LifecycleDispatchLedger is backed by a durable store (Postgres), keyed on the number-pinned dispatch id (`LifecycleCommandKey.Derive(instance_id, command_kind, occurrence)`), and shared across replicas.
- A host restart does NOT re-POST an already-dispatched occurrence.
- The ledger records a dispatched-at audit trail.
- Any schema change is a forward-only migration in the correct series.
- Engine command_dedup remains the authoritative backstop; this ledger stays the front-line optimization, not the safety floor.
notes:
2026-06-30: The durable-ledger substrate this issue builds is now pinned to ADR-PC-038 §Decision 1 (durable Postgres lifecycle_dispatch_ledger keyed on LifecycleCommandKey.Derive(instance_id, command_kind, occurrence), dispatched_at audit). Builds commitment LCD-4 (LIFECYCLE_DISPATCH_LEDGER_DURABLE, Planned).
2026-06-30: Catalogue row renumbered LCD-4 -> LCD-5 when #414 merged (LCD-3/LCD-4 taken by LIFECYCLE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC / LIFECYCLE_DRIVER_SINGLE_FIRING). Stable Test ID LIFECYCLE_DISPATCH_LEDGER_DURABLE is unchanged; this issue builds catalogue row LCD-5.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: single-firing / leader-election so a multi-replica host fires each due occurrence once
description:
In plain English: if we run more than one copy of the lifecycle-driver host for availability, each copy's timer independently finds the same due deposit maturity / loan installment and POSTs the command — N duplicate firings. It is safe today only because the engine's idempotency key collapses the duplicates to one money leg, but it is wasteful and racy. This adds a guard so exactly one replica is the active ticker at a time, with the others as hot standbys ready to take over.

Builds on babelstone-6cpq.7 (the host skeleton); the mechanism is fixed by the ADR sibling (which blocks this).
acceptance_criteria:
- With N≥2 replicas running, a single due occurrence yields exactly one schedule-pass dispatch (one active leader); a standby takes over when the leader is lost.
- Implements the mechanism recorded in the hardening ADR (reuse-or-diverge from the `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` / advisory-lock precedent).
- Engine command_dedup remains the correctness floor — leader-election is an efficiency/cleanliness guard, never the safety mechanism.
- No clock enters the engine (NO_CLOCK_DRIVEN_ENGINE_SIGNAL / BENG004 holds); the guard lives entirely in the sibling host.
notes:
2026-06-30: The single-firing mechanism this issue implements is now pinned to ADR-PC-038 §Decision 2 (per-occurrence atomic claim on lifecycle_dispatch_ledger; the durable claim is the single-firing guard, not an elected leader). Builds commitment LCD-3 (LIFECYCLE_DRIVER_SINGLE_FIRING, Planned).
2026-06-30: Catalogue row renumbered LCD-3 -> LCD-4 when #414 merged (a concurrent ADR-PC-036 row, LIFECYCLE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC, claimed LCD-3). Stable Test ID LIFECYCLE_DRIVER_SINGLE_FIRING is unchanged; this issue builds catalogue row LCD-4.
close_reason: Closed

title: ADR: govern the lifecycle-driver hardening mechanism — leader-election + durable-ledger substrate (new ADR or ADR-PC-036 amendment)
description:
In plain English: before we build leader-election and a durable ledger for the lifecycle-driver host, we need to record which mechanism we picked and why — that is an architectural decision, not mechanical work, so it belongs in an ADR. The repo already coordinates work elsewhere with Postgres `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` / advisory locks (the orchestrator saga dispatcher, the engine outbox relay); the open question is whether to reuse that pattern for the lifecycle host or consciously diverge, and what durable substrate the dispatch ledger should use.

This is the gating decision for the two mechanism build siblings (leader-election, durable ledger) — they cite it.

Relates: ADR-PC-036 §Consequences / §Residual-risks (names this hardening, leaves it "not committed here").
acceptance_criteria:
- An Accepted ADR (or a dated ADR-PC-036 amendment per §D5 immutability) records the leader-election mechanism AND the durable-ledger substrate, evaluated against the existing `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` / advisory-lock precedent (orchestrator saga dispatcher, engine outbox relay).
- Follows the explicit-drift gate (ADR-PC-020 §D3): the decision is recorded before/with the build, not silently.
- The leader-election and durable-ledger build issues cite the recorded decision.
- If a new ADR is authored: created via the new-adr skill with the dual disk+bd number-check, and reference/adr-index regenerated (`make docs-gen`) in the same change.
notes: 2026-06-30: Resolved by ADR-PC-038 (Accepted), authored on PR #414 — single-firing by per-occurrence atomic claim on a durable Postgres lifecycle_dispatch_ledger (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + pg_try_advisory_xact_lock; competing-consumers, no elected leader). This is the ADR number this task produced; closes on #414 merge.
close_reason: Closed

title: Epic — Operationally harden the lifecycle-driver host for production: single-firing/leader-election, durable dispatch ledger, monitoring/on-call (ADR-PC-036 §Consequences follow-up)
description:
In plain English: the lifecycle-driver host — the clockless-engine-honoring skeleton built in babelstone-6cpq.7 — is correct but not yet production-operable. Today it has no coordination across replicas, an in-memory dispatch ledger that does not survive a restart, and no monitoring. So a multi-replica deployment fans every due command into N redundant POSTs (safe only because the engine's command_dedup collapses them to one money leg), a host restart re-derives and re-POSTs every still-due occurrence, and a silently-stalled loan schedule — a parked settlement holding occurrence N+1 — pages nobody.

This epic groups the operational hardening that ADR-PC-036 §Consequences *names* ("a new deployable (single-firing/leader-election, monitoring, on-call)") but deliberately left "not committed here" (§Residual-risks), plus the ADR work needed to *govern* the mechanism choices before they are built.

Deferred — to be scheduled after the driver skeleton (babelstone-6cpq.7) and the family rules (babelstone-6cpq.8 / .9) land. Filed now so the hardening stops being untracked prose in PR #391's "scoped out" list. The correctness floor is unchanged throughout: the engine's command_dedup (ADR-PC-029), reached via the number-pinned server-derived idempotency key, is what keeps the un-hardened host safe today — this epic adds efficiency, durability, and observability, not correctness.

Governs/relates: ADR-PC-036 (lifecycle-command-driver decision); builds on babelstone-6cpq (lifecycle-driver epic) and its host skeleton babelstone-6cpq.7. Distinct from the general metrics/SLI platform work (babelstone-f0ic).

## Success Criteria
- A multi-replica deployment fires each due occurrence exactly once (one active leader/ticker); standby replicas take over on leader loss. The engine command_dedup stays the unchanged correctness floor.
- The dispatch ledger is durable: it survives a host restart and is shared across replicas, so a reboot no longer re-POSTs already-dispatched occurrences.
- The host emits liveness/health plus dispatch-lag and POST-failure signals, AND a permanently-parked settlement that stalls a loan schedule raises an alert (ADR-PC-036 §Residual-risks: "must be alerted, not invisible" — there is no arrears state for the miss to land in).
- The leader-election + durable-ledger mechanism choice is recorded in an Accepted ADR (or a dated ADR-PC-036 amendment), per the explicit-drift gate (ADR-PC-020 §D3 / §D5).
- All child issues closed.
notes:
2026-06-29 (central contract-review on PR #404, lifecycle rules): concrete instance of the durable-ledger gap this epic owns. The engine /installment endpoint always pays next-unpaid off the LIVE fold and ignores the caller occurrence; the in-memory LifecycleDispatchLedger absorbs re-ticks within one warm worker. Residual edge: read-model projection lag + a COLD ledger (driver restart, or a future HA replica) — a stale calendar row still showing occurrence N due could drive a POST the engine resolves to N+1 (paying the next installment EARLY). Maturity is immune (constant occurrence). The durable, crash-surviving, shared dispatch ledger this epic builds closes it. v1 scopes it out (in-memory, single worker).
2026-06-30: The gating mechanism decision in this epic's Success Criteria is now recorded as ADR-PC-038 (Accepted, PR #414). Children 1nkm.2/1nkm.3 build its seeded commitments LCD-3/LCD-4; authoring task 1nkm.1 closes on #414 merge; 1nkm.4 (monitoring) stays independent of the mechanism choice.
close_reason: All 4 children closed — ADR-PC-038 (PR #414) + single-firing durable dispatch ledger + monitoring/alerting (PR #438)

title: Ratchet FinancialMath kernel leg back to ~100% under scoped (test-project) mutation mode
description:
Bring the financial-math kernel's FinancialMath mutation leg back to ~100% in its new test-project (scoped) operating mode.

Plain English: we just changed how the kernel's mutation tests run so they stop crashing the CI runner. The trade-off is that the kernel leg now only runs the kernel's OWN tests, and a handful of edge-case checks in the banded-rate-schedule and amortization math were previously only being verified by tests that live in OTHER projects. The kernel still scores 95.88% (well above its 90% floor), but to keep the kernel fully self-pinned we should add those few checks to the kernel's own test suite.

Background: the Money + FinancialMath mutation legs were switched from Stryker SOLUTION context to TEST-PROJECT context to stop the FinancialMath leg exhausting the GitHub runner ("runner received a shutdown signal"). Scoped, Money = 100%, FinancialMath = 95.88% (floor 90). The ~4% gap is 13 boundary mutants in RateSchedule.cs / Amortization.cs that sibling-family tests (e.g. RateScheduleDeciderTests in TermDeposit.Application) killed in solution mode.

Work:
- Pin the 3 GENUINE survivors — the `factor.Days < 0` zero-day-window guards in SimpleInterestRaw, AccrueStepUpWindowRaw, AccrueAmountTieredRaw — with kernel zero-day-window accrual tests (start == end → 0, no throw), killing the `< 0` → `<= 0` mutants.
- Mark the ~6 EQUIVALENT boundary mutants with inline `// Stryker disable once Equality: <reason>` at each site (RateSchedule.cs L261/L262 max/min ternaries, L263/L330 zero-overlap skips, L360/L365 tranche-clip bounds — each produces the identical bound at the boundary, so no test can kill them).
- Pin the 2 Amortization.cs survivors (block removal + the `commission.Cents >= lostInterestCeiling.Cents` equality).
- Re-run the scoped FinancialMath leg; expect ~99–100%.
acceptance_criteria: Scoped FinancialMath mutation leg returns to >=99%; the 3 zero-day-guard survivors killed by kernel tests; equivalent boundary mutants justified with inline Stryker-disable comments; Amortization survivors pinned.
close_reason: Closed

title: Conform term_deposit and personal_loan to the Account abstraction (degenerate IAccount per ADR-PC-033)
description:
Plain English: ADR-PC-033 says every engine-owned aggregate IS an account. The term deposit and personal loan already fold a single balance, so they are "degenerate" accounts (one balance, no holds). Once the Account seam ships, they must declare it — a reclassification, not a behaviour change.

Per ADR-PC-033 slot 1 ("naming the abstraction reclassifies them, it does not change them") and ADR-PC-037 P2: make the existing families conform to the Account abstraction.
- DepositPosition (term_deposit) and LoanPosition (personal_loan) implement the IAccount seam as degenerate accounts: one accounting balance folded over ADR-PC-032 Movements, no holds, no available/accounting split (they do NOT implement IHoldable).
- No behaviour change — purely declaring the seam so the generic balance projector folds them uniformly.

Depends on the IAccount seam shipping in babelstone-hkwp.3. Sits under the babelstone-hkwp foundation epic (every engine-owned aggregate is an account), not the conta a ordem family epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- DepositPosition and LoanPosition implement IAccount (degenerate, no IHoldable); the generic balance projector folds them.
- Replay-determinism is unchanged (the families behave identically before/after); ACCOUNT_BALANCE_IS_A_FOLD covers the degenerate case.
- No family-typed shape enters the engine (ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC holds).
acceptance_criteria: DepositPosition and LoanPosition implement IAccount (degenerate, no IHoldable) and the generic balance projector folds them; replay-determinism unchanged; ACCOUNT_BALANCE_IS_A_FOLD covers the degenerate case; no family-typed shape enters the engine (ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC).

title: Wire current_account into the host (IFamilyHostModule + endpoints + ProjectReference + pack pin) + contracts (avro/cue)
description:
Plain English: make the conta a ordem family actually run in the engine host (its HTTP endpoints, its discovery wiring, its pinned pack) and publish its contracts (Avro event schemas + the CUE family schema).

Per ADR-PC-037 P1 / P5:
- Wire the family into the running host: IFamilyHostModule + endpoints (the authorize command surface + the account read/lifecycle endpoints) + the host ProjectReference (the assembly-scan anchor) + the pack pin.
- Author contracts: contracts/avro/accounts/current_account/*.avsc for any bus-promoted events (and any bus-promoted hold events — contract-reviewer lane) and contracts/cue/families/current-account.cue (including the descoberto/limit constructs from the descoberto pack-rule issue).

Depends on the family scaffold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The host discovers and serves the family via assembly scan (endpoints live), no surgical edit to generic compose code.
- contracts/cue/families/current-account.cue validates (pack-validate); contracts/avro/accounts/current_account Avro round-trips and the AsyncAPI EventCatalog is updated.
- contract-reviewer PASS on the new schemas/events.
acceptance_criteria: the host discovers and serves the family via assembly scan (endpoints live); cue/families/current-account.cue validates and avro/accounts/current_account round-trips with the AsyncAPI catalogue updated; contract-reviewer PASS.

title: Settlement/posting-feed contract-shape ADR — what crosses the ACL per cleared movement (shape, ordering, idempotency)
description:
Plain English: a current account is fed a stream of already-cleared money movements (salary in, bills out, captured card legs) that arrive from outside the engine across the ACL. This issue specifies the contract for that feed — what each posting looks like, in what order, how duplicates are handled, and who detects gaps.

Author the settlement/posting-feed contract-shape ADR-PC. ADR-PC-030 P3 named it ("the settlement/posting feed ... a future contract-shape ADR"); ADR-PC-037 D3 defers the everyday credit/debit posting feed's wire contract to it. The feed delivers already-cleared movements as ADR-PC-032 Movements (Observed). Fill the six contract slots: payload shape, semantics, ordering and delivery, idempotency/dedup, error model, ownership/versioning — plus gap-detection ownership on a feed the engine does not control.

MOVED here from babelstone-d0ob (credit_card): the conta a ordem is built first (ADR-PC-030 amended 2026-06-28) and needs this feed first; the credit_card family reuses the same posting-feed contract. The contract-reviewer is the review lane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A contract-shape ADR-PC is filed with all six slots for the posting/settlement feed (Observed Movements across the ACL).
- Ordering, at-least-once + dedup/idempotency, and gap-detection ownership are specified.
- Both the conta a ordem family and the future credit_card family can consume the same contract; contract-reviewer PASS.
acceptance_criteria: a contract-shape ADR-PC is filed with all six slots for the Observed-Movement posting/settlement feed; ordering, at-least-once + dedup, and gap-detection ownership specified; both conta a ordem and credit_card can consume it; contract-reviewer PASS.

title: descoberto autorizado as a pack rule — ADR-PC-006/007 CUE grammar expansion + descoberto accrual
description:
Plain English: an authorized overdraft (descoberto autorizado) lets a current account go below zero up to an agreed limit. This issue makes that limit a pack rule the authorization decider reads — so the same pack that prices the product also says how far a debit can go — and adds the interest math for a used overdraft.

Per ADR-PC-037 D5 and ADR-PC-030 P3 ("overdraft and limits are pack rules"):
- Model the arranged overdraft as a declarative pack limit evaluated at authorization stage 4, extending the available-balance identity by + authorized_overdraft_limit. A debit within the arranged limit is authorized; a debit beyond it (ultrapassagem / descoberto nao autorizado) is refused (declined: OVERDRAFT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED).
- Expand the ADR-PC-006 / ADR-PC-007 CUE pack grammar with the limit/overdraft constructs (and transaction/velocity limit constructs). This is the named pack-grammar follow-up ADR-PC-033 deferred. The grammar must stay declarative.
- Add the descoberto interest/fee accrual math against a negative balance (the FinancialMath one-boundary Money discipline), modelled like the loan's accrual.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The CUE pack grammar carries an authorized_overdraft_limit construct and transaction/velocity-limit constructs; pack-validate accepts valid packs and rejects malformed ones.
- The authorize decider reads the pack limit at stage 4; within-limit debits authorize, ultrapassagem is refused with OVERDRAFT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
- descoberto interest/fee accrual is implemented and unit-tested to the cent; the fold stays pure (math runs command-side).
acceptance_criteria: the CUE pack grammar carries authorized_overdraft_limit + velocity/transaction-limit constructs (pack-validate passes); the decider reads them at stage 4, within-limit authorizes and ultrapassagem is refused (OVERDRAFT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED); descoberto accrual is tested to the cent with the math command-side.

title: current_account hold-reconciliation policy — partial/late/over-capture, reversal, projection-derived expiry horizon
description:
Plain English: holds do not always resolve cleanly — a capture can be smaller than the hold, arrive after the hold already expired, be larger than expected, or be reversed. This issue defines exactly how the conta a ordem family handles each of those, and how a hold times out.

Implement the family-owned hold-reconciliation policy that ADR-PC-033 deferred to this family, all WITHIN ADR-PC-033's three transitions (policy, not new transitions) — ADR-PC-037 D4:
- Partial capture: a HoldCaptured for less than the held amount releases the remainder (the captured Movement moves the accounting balance; the residual leaves the active set).
- Late capture vs expiry: a capture arriving after the matching HoldExpired is a re-presentment — record it as an Observed posting Movement against the accounting balance, do NOT resurrect the expired hold, and raise a reconciliation signal.
- Over-capture: a HoldCaptured for more than the held amount posts the Movement and raises a reconciliation signal.
- Reversal: an authorization voided before capture is a HoldExpired-style release with no posting (no money moved).
- Expiry horizon: a product/pack time-to-live value; HoldExpired is appended off a projection over the active-hold set against a value-date horizon (ADR-PC-023), NEVER a clock-manufactured engine event.

Depends on the family scaffold and the babelstone-hkwp.3 Account engine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Partial / late / over-capture and reversal are handled exactly per ADR-PC-037 D4, with reconciliation signals for anomalies.
- Hold expiry is projection-derived (value-date horizon), not clock-driven; the fold stays pure.
- The hold lifecycle is replay-deterministic; the HOLD_LIFECYCLE_PURE first-instance test lands.
acceptance_criteria: partial/late/over-capture and reversal handled per ADR-PC-037 D4 with reconciliation signals; hold expiry is projection-derived (value-date horizon) not clock-driven; the hold lifecycle is replay-deterministic and HOLD_LIFECYCLE_PURE lands.

title: current_account authorize command + decider (synchronous, ADR-PC-029/034) + declined taxonomy + AUTHORIZATION_SYNC_IDEMPOTENT test
description:
Plain English: build the part that answers, in real time, "can this debit go through?" — the authorize command. It reads the available balance and the overdraft/limit rules and either earmarks the funds (a hold) and says authorized, or says declined with a reason.

Implement the authorize-style command per ADR-PC-037 D6 and ADR-PC-034 (synchronous technique):
- Request: account_ref (opaque, no PII), amount (Money, integer cents), value_date, command id / Idempotency-Key.
- Response: authorized (with the hold_id of the appended HoldPlaced) OR declined with a reason taxonomy: INSUFFICIENT_AVAILABLE_BALANCE, OVERDRAFT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, LIMIT_EXCEEDED (velocity/transaction), ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE (dormant/closed/blocked).
- Decide = a pure read-state-and-append: fold available balance, apply pack rules (limits, descoberto), append HoldPlaced (authorized) or append nothing and return declined. No clock, no external call.
- Synchronous on the ADR-PC-029 command surface (a heavier load profile, not a new ingress). Idempotent: a replayed command id returns the original verdict (same hold_id) with no second HoldPlaced. De-settled: the authorize append never moves money; capture arrives later as HoldCaptured.
- Write the AUTHORIZATION_SYNC_IDEMPOTENT integration test (ADR-PC-034 seeded the catalogue row; this family lands it).

Depends on the family scaffold and the babelstone-hkwp.3 Account engine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- authorize answers synchronously on the ADR-PC-029 surface; a declined is terminal and gated.
- A replayed authorize command id returns the original verdict and the same hold_id, with no second HoldPlaced.
- The declined reason taxonomy is implemented and covered by tests.
- The AUTHORIZATION_SYNC_IDEMPOTENT test passes (Testcontainers) and its catalogue row flips Planned -> Live.
acceptance_criteria: authorize answers synchronously on the ADR-PC-029 surface, declined is gated; a replayed command id returns the original verdict and same hold_id with no second HoldPlaced; the declined reason taxonomy is tested; AUTHORIZATION_SYNC_IDEMPOTENT passes and its catalogue row flips to Live.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Orchestrator note from the PR #444 §P3 review (adr-conformance finding 6): ADR-PC-030 §P3 / ADR-PC-033 slot 5 say the decision path appends HoldPlaced OR A REFUSAL FACT. PR #444 ships the pure decider returning Declined data; the refusal-fact APPEND is deferred to this family command shell. When building the current_account authorize command, the shell must actually record the refusal fact — otherwise the deferral becomes silent drift.

title: current_account family scaffold — events, pure folds, lifecycle table, projections, IFamilyModule (AccountPosition : IAccount, IHoldable)
description:
Plain English: build the skeleton of the conta a ordem family — its events, the pure fold handlers, the lifecycle table, the projections, and the module that binds it into the engine. This is the first family whose account is a real transactional account (two balances + holds), not a degenerate one.

Author the current_account family the ADR-PC-021 / ADR-PC-031 way (ADR-PC-037 D1/D2/D3, P1/P2/P3):
- Event records: AccountOpened, AccountOpeningFailed, AccountMarkedDormant, AccountReactivated, AccountClosed (family-owned). Holds are NOT family events — they are the engine cross-cutting operations.HoldPlaced / HoldCaptured / HoldExpired, instantiated here.
- Pure fold handlers (no clock, no I/O, no randomness).
- LifecycleTransitions legality table: Pending -> Active -> (Failed | Closed); Dormant <-> Active; Erased. Dormant is a non-terminal reversible state.
- AccountPosition declares the ADR-PC-033 IAccount + IHoldable seam: folds the accounting balance over ADR-PC-032 Movements AND the active-hold set, so the generic projector derives available = accounting - sum(active holds) [+ authorized overdraft]. First non-degenerate account.
- Projections + IFamilyModule binding. No PII; GDPR erasure via the shared IErasable seam (operations.PersonalDataErasureRequested).

Depends on the IAccount/IHoldable seam shipping in babelstone-hkwp.3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Family projects exist under families/current-account/src (folds project + Application project) on the ADR-PC-021 shape.
- AccountPosition implements IAccount and IHoldable; folds are pure (DETERMINISM_GATE holds).
- Replay/fold tests cover the lifecycle and the balance/hold folds and pass.
- The host discovers the family via assembly scan with no per-family hand-edit; zero generic-engine diff (ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC holds).
acceptance_criteria: Family projects exist under families/current-account/src on the ADR-PC-021 shape; AccountPosition implements IAccount and IHoldable; folds pure (DETERMINISM_GATE); replay/fold tests pass; host discovers it with no per-family hand-edit; zero generic-engine diff (ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC).

title: EPIC — current_account (conta à ordem) transactional-account family build (ADR-PC-037)
description:
Plain English: build the conta a ordem (current / demand account) family — the 4th product shape and the hub the other products settle against. Per ADR-PC-030 (amended 2026-06-28) it is now built BEFORE credit_card. It is the FIRST non-degenerate instance of the ADR-PC-033 Account abstraction: the first family to actually carry the accounting/available-balance split and a hold ledger.

This epic implements ADR-PC-037 (Accepted 2026-06-28). The heavy machinery is already decided and (being) built: the Account abstraction + hold lifecycle (ADR-PC-033), the Movement read side (ADR-PC-032), and the synchronous real-time authorization technique (ADR-PC-034) — grouped under the babelstone-hkwp "Shape-3 foundations" epic. This epic is the FAMILY build ON TOP of that foundation; it is deliberately SEPARATE from babelstone-hkwp (which is the engine foundation only and says so).

Holds are the engine cross-cutting operations.HoldPlaced / HoldCaptured / HoldExpired events (family-agnostic, no PII) — NOT family-owned events. The old bd framing (MontanteCativado / CativoCapturado / CativoExpirado) is superseded by ADR-PC-033 and is only instantiated here, not re-decided.

Scope (ADR-PC-037): the family scaffold (AccountPosition : IAccount, IHoldable), the synchronous authorize-command + declined taxonomy, the hold-reconciliation policy, descoberto autorizado as a pack rule, the settlement/posting-feed contract, and host wiring + contracts. Depends on the babelstone-hkwp foundation.

## Success Criteria

- The current_account family is authored on the ADR-PC-021 spine and wired into the running host with no per-family hand-edit; zero generic-engine diff (ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC).
- AccountPosition declares the ADR-PC-033 IAccount + IHoldable seam; available balance = accounting balance - sum(active holds) [+ authorized overdraft] is a rebuildable fold (ACCOUNT_BALANCE_IS_A_FOLD).
- The authorize command answers synchronously and idempotently (AUTHORIZATION_SYNC_IDEMPOTENT) on the ADR-PC-029 surface; declined verdicts are gated.
- The hold-reconciliation policy (partial / late / over-capture, reversal, projection-derived expiry) is implemented and replay-deterministic (HOLD_LIFECYCLE_PURE).
- descoberto autorizado is a pack rule (CUE grammar expansion); ultrapassagem is refused.
- Contracts (avro/accounts/current_account, cue/families/current-account) land; all child issues closed.

title: movement-ledger projector host-drive wiring (the read side of the IMovementBearing seam)
description:
Plain English: PR #379 (bd hkwp.1) landed the IMovementBearing seam, the account-keyed movement-ledger projector, its store, and the migration — and registered them in DI — but no host loop yet FEEDS decoded appended/replayed events to MovementLedgerProjector.ApplyAsync, so the movement_ledger table is created and read-wired but never populated at runtime (covered by unit tests via the in-memory store). ADR-PC-032 §A1 explicitly scopes the live projection drive to this follow-up.

Scope: wire the host-drive that feeds decoded events to MovementLedgerProjector.ApplyAsync. It is cross-family and account_ref-keyed (one account receives movements from many streams), so it is NOT the per-family/per-stream ProjectionDrainer — register it as a spine singleton driven at the composition root. Confirm at-least-once re-apply stays a no-op (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and the rebuild path (TRUNCATE+refold) is deterministic.
acceptance_criteria: MovementLedgerProjector.ApplyAsync has a production caller in the engine host; movement_ledger is populated at runtime from appended/replayed IMovementBearing events; an integration test proves an account's ledger + signed-sum balance after real appends; rebuild is byte-identical.
close_reason: Merged in PR #444 (feat/account-hold-spine)

title: Feed read_model.installment_calendar — producer + Layer-2 driver presents the occurrence number
description:
Plain English: PR #380 (bd 6cpq.5) created the personal_loan read_model.installment_calendar table and applies it on startup, but nothing yet WRITES rows into it — the forward calendar belief currently lives only in the generic bitemporal projections table (a point lookup), so the range-scan surface the lifecycle driver needs is empty. This wires the producer and ties off a related precision point on the idempotency key.

Scope:
1. Add an IInstallmentCalendarReadModelStore + InstallmentCalendarReadModelRow + a ReadModelRunner<LoanPosition,…> mapping the folded installment_calendar projection into read_model.installment_calendar (Upsert with the ADR-IC-005 §P2 last_sequence guard), registered via ReadModelInfra in PersonalLoanHostModule — mirroring term-deposit's read_model.deposits feed. Surfaces the next-unpaid occurrence per Active loan for the 'installments due in [from,to)' range scan.
2. When the Layer-2 lifecycle-command driver (6cpq.7) is built, it MUST read this calendar and present the occurrence number to LifecycleCommandKey so the number-pinned key is pinned to the caller-asserted stable installment number (ADR-PC-036 §Decision 3), completing the 'a re-dated retry of occurrence N reuses the same key' guarantee that the Layer-1 endpoint only realises for concurrent/forward firings (live-fold derivation) — see the LCD-1 catalogue scope note.
acceptance_criteria: read_model.installment_calendar is populated by a ReadModelRunner for Active loans (next-unpaid occurrence per loan), with the last_sequence idempotency guard; the range scan 'loans with an installment due in [from,to)' returns rows. The Layer-2 driver presents the calendar occurrence number to the number-pinned key.
close_reason: Closed

title: event-store migration ConfigMap missing 0018_bulk_operations.sql — infra CI drift
description: Plain English: the engine event-store migration 0018_bulk_operations.sql was added to the source tree (by the closed qpiw.2) but never added to the k8s migration ConfigMap list in infra/k8s/apps/kustomization.yaml. The CI 'Assert the event-store migration ConfigMap lists every Sql file' check (bd babelstone-zla1.5.1) therefore fails on EVERY infra-touching PR — a pre-existing main drift, not caused by any one PR. Fix: add the missing 0018 entry so the list matches the on-disk Sql/ dir.
acceptance_criteria: infra/k8s/apps/kustomization.yaml lists 0018_bulk_operations.sql; the event-store-migration-ConfigMap drift assertion in the CI infra job passes again on infra-touching PRs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Update parallel-backlog-orchestrator skill with 2026-06-28 lifecycle-driver run learnings
description:
Plain English: a large parallel-lane backlog run on 2026-06-28 (the lifecycle-command-driver epic, babelstone-6cpq) surfaced places where the parallel-backlog-orchestrator skill instructs the wrong thing or omits a discipline we needed. Fix the skill doc so the next run avoids those traps.

Changes to plugins/babelstone-engine/skills/parallel-backlog-orchestrator/SKILL.md:
1. Footprint diff: two-dot (origin/main..<branch>) -> three-dot (origin/main...<branch>). Two-dot inflates a branch that is BEHIND main (this run: comment branches falsely appeared to touch the ADR ledger; three-dot gave the true authored set).
2. Ultracode/Workflow path: lane agents do NOT run babelstone-engine:adr-conformance (they cannot spawn subagents); the orchestrator runs it centrally post-run. The Step-4 brief currently tells lanes to run it.
3. Verify your OWN asserted collisions, not just asserted blockers: an inferred collision (from a title/ADR) is a claim -> pull the real file-level footprint before excluding an issue.
4. Pack file-colliding ready issues into ONE sequential lane this run (combined PR, multiple Closes lines); reserve 'defer to next run' for unmerged-PR dependencies only.
5. Distinguish ledger types: wholesale-regenerated adr-index = single writer; row-addressable commitment-catalogue = disjoint-row writers OK (each lane owns its own verified non-adjacent row).
6. Add an agent_dispatchable filter to Step 1 (drop human/account-bound tasks; note account-independent artifact authoring stays dispatchable even when the live apply is account-gated).
7. Document the reserved-set incremental-planning pass (adding lanes to an already-committed plan: check new candidates against the union of committed-lane footprints).
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md carries all 7 fixes; the two near-bugs (#1 two-dot->three-dot footprint, #2 lanes do not run adr-conformance in the Workflow path) are corrected; PR opened naming this issue under '## bd issues closed on merge'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: share the dispatch mapping with SimulationRuntime so the forecast is a fitness function
description:
In plain English: the simulation already forecasts these lifecycle milestones; if production and the simulation share the same milestone-to-real-command mapping, the simulation becomes a cheap drift guard that proves the forecast is exactly what production fires.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 7 (candidate D's one harvested idea). Factor the LifecycleMilestone-to-command dispatch mapping so both engine/src/Babelstone.Engine/SimulationRuntime.cs and the A4a/A4b production rules consume it, and add a fitness test asserting the two agree.
acceptance_criteria: - SimulationRuntime and the production driver share one dispatch mapping; a fitness function fails if a forecast milestone and the production command for the same occurrence diverge.
close_reason: Merged in PR #442 (feat/lifecycle-settlement-gate)

title: Lifecycle driver: settlement-health gate so catch-up never outruns parked settlement (LCD-2)
description:
In plain English: the engine advances a loan's paid-count on the installment event, not on settled cash -- so after an outage a catch-up could fire installment N+1 while N's cash is still stuck in human intervention, advancing the schedule past money actually collected. This gate holds N+1 until N's de-settled cash leg is healthy.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 4. A settlement-health predicate the recurring path consults before firing N+1 -- it refuses while occurrence N's Originated Movement (ADR-PC-032) is parked in HUMAN_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED (the SettlementProcess state, babelstone-t7o3.15). Realises LIFECYCLE_DRIVER_SETTLEMENT_HEALTH_GATE (LCD-2, catalogue row 106). Residual: a permanently parked settlement silently stalls the schedule and must be alerted -- flag as an ops follow-up.
acceptance_criteria:
- The driver holds occurrence N+1 while N's cash leg is parked in HUMAN_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED, and resumes once N settles (the LCD-2 integration test).
- An automated catch-up after an outage never advances the paid-count past collected cash; LIFECYCLE_DRIVER_SETTLEMENT_HEALTH_GATE flips Planned to Live.
close_reason: Merged in PR #442 (feat/lifecycle-settlement-gate)

title: Lifecycle driver: personal-loan InstallmentRule over the installment_calendar (recurring)
description:
In plain English: the recurring family rule -- read the loan installment calendar and fire PayInstallment for the next-unpaid occurrence per Active loan. Because PayInstallment is legal repeatedly from Active, safety rests entirely on the E1 number-pinned key.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 2, 3 and 5. An InstallmentRule behind the ADR-IC-019 family-to-core arrow (P2) reading the A1 installment_calendar, POSTing /v1/loans/{id}/installment with the E1 server-derived stable-installment-number key.
acceptance_criteria:
- For an Active loan with occurrence N next-due, the driver fires PayInstallment once; a re-tick/backfill of N reuses the E1 key and appends no second leg.
- The rule advances to N+1 only once N is recorded paid (next-unpaid surfaced by A1's fold).
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: term-deposit MaturityRule over the maturity_calendar (one-shot)
description:
In plain English: the first family rule -- read the deposit maturity calendar as-of today and fire Mature once per deposit that has reached maturity. Maturity is the degenerate single-occurrence case, so it needs no catch-up gate.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 2 and 6. A MaturityRule behind the ADR-IC-019 family-to-core arrow (P2) reading the existing MaturityCalendar.cs, POSTing Mature with the E3 CommandId; fires on/after the maturity date only and INHERITS the already-built renewal opt-out / saga-start gates (babelstone-mtto.3) -- no renewal-suppression logic here. Distinct from babelstone-60n8.2's MaturityReminderRule (same calendar, but that emits a notification, not a command).
acceptance_criteria:
- A deposit at/after its maturity date is matured exactly once by the driver; a driver-outage backfill re-derives the still-due occurrence and stamps its own valid_time (correct business date).
- The rule never fires Mature before the maturity date (the one ordering invariant it owns); an opted-out deposit starts no renewal (inherited gate, not re-encoded).
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: a new sibling driver host (Cadence worker + LifecycleSchedulePass + dispatch ledger + command-POST sink)
description:
In plain English: this is the new always-on service that owns the clock, ticks on a cadence, and turns this-occurrence-is-due into an HTTP POST to the engine. It deliberately lives in its OWN host -- not inside the read-only notification context, not inside the engine (a timer there trips BENG004).

ADR-PC-036 Decision 2. A new sibling host running the Babelstone.Cadence worker with a LifecycleSchedulePass, a dispatch ledger, and a command-POST sink that fires through the E1 contract under the E4 SCA principal; single-firing/leader-election + monitoring are operating concerns it owns. Mirrors the notification host pattern (babelstone-60n8.1) but is a SEPARATE deployable.
acceptance_criteria:
- The host runs the Cadence worker, derives a composite dispatch id per occurrence, and the dispatch ledger makes a re-tick of an already-dispatched occurrence a no-op.
- The host is a separate deployable (not in Babelstone.Notification, not in the engine assembly); a smoke test POSTs a command end-to-end through the sink.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: extract the notification poll-loop machinery into a shared Babelstone.Cadence library
description:
In plain English: the notification subsystem already owns a tested, clock-owning poll loop (a background worker, a per-tick pass, composite-id derivation, a dedupe ledger). Rather than rebuild it, pull that machinery into a shared library so the new driver host becomes a second consumer.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 2. EXTRACT (not re-implement) from notification/src/Babelstone.Notification/ -- NotificationWorker, NotificationSchedulePass, NotificationDedupeLedger, composite-id (built by babelstone-60n8.2, PR #329) -- into a new Babelstone.Cadence assembly that Babelstone.Notification then consumes unchanged (ADR-IC-019 mechanism reuse). Frame as a refactor of 60n8.2's output.
acceptance_criteria:
- Babelstone.Cadence exposes the clock-owning worker + per-tick SchedulePass abstraction + dedupe ledger; Babelstone.Notification is refactored onto it with its existing tests green.
- No behavioural change to the notification estate (NotificationSchedulePassTests still pass); NOTIFICATION_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC still holds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: a forward installment_calendar projection for personal loans
description:
In plain English: loans only have a backward-looking what's-been-paid projection; there is no forward view of which installment is next due, so the driver has nothing to poll. This adds a forward installment_calendar that surfaces the next-unpaid occurrence per Active loan.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 5. A new pure projection folded deterministically from LoanDisbursed (StartDate, FirstInstallmentDate = StartDate + 1mo, TermMonths, InstallmentAmount) AND LoanInstallmentPaid (so a paid occurrence drops off and the next surfaces -- folding from LoanDisbursed alone re-fires forever). New artifact under families/personal-loan/src/Babelstone.Families.PersonalLoan/ + PersonalLoanProjectionModule registration + a forward-only family read-model migration; NO clock in the fold (ADR-PC-002 / ADR-PC-010 P5 purity; the projection IS the temporal signal, ADR-PC-023). Sits beside the existing descriptive AmortizationScheduleProjection (babelstone-g6ar).
acceptance_criteria:
- For an Active loan with installment N paid, the projection surfaces occurrence N+1 as next-due; a fold/replay test proves determinism with no clock read.
- A fully-paid or closed loan surfaces no further due occurrence; the read-model migration is forward-only and lands in the family ledger.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: a scoped non-interactive SCA service principal for the money-mover routes
description:
In plain English: the money-mover routes run a step-up SCA filter that expects a gateway-attested X-SCA-Acr from a human session -- a machine driver has no such session, so it needs its own narrowly-scoped, audited identity rather than a blanket exemption.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 1 / Consequences (a scoped, audited principal, never a blanket exemption). Provision a non-interactive service principal scoped to exactly the /maturity + /installment money-mover routes, consistent with the settlement-leg step-up gate already built in babelstone-t7o3.19 (ADR-IC-006 P2 attest-not-deny). Independent security surface -- can run parallel to E1-E3.
acceptance_criteria:
- A scoped, audited service principal authorises the money-mover routes for the driver; its scope is limited to maturity + installment, not a global SCA bypass.
- A request on a non-money-mover route under that principal is refused; principal use is audit-logged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: thread a CommandId through MatureDepositCommand so maturity dedupes uniformly
description:
In plain English: maturity carries no mandatory idempotency key today -- it leans on the legality gate (a second Mature from a non-Active state simply rejects). For the driver to dedupe maturity the same way it dedupes everything else, maturity needs a real command id.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 1. Thread a CommandId (the E1 one-shot occurrence key, command_kind = mature) through MatureDepositCommand / the /v1/deposits/{id}/maturity path so driven maturity dedupes at command_dedup (ADR-PC-029 slot 4) rather than relying on the lifecycle legality gate alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two Mature firings for the same deposit occurrence dedupe at command_dedup to a single append, independent of the legality gate.
- MatureDepositCommand carries the server-derived CommandId; the maturity endpoint / MCP mature_deposit no longer depends on the legality backstop for at-least-once safety.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: add a pay_installment MCP tool (the loan family has none today)
description:
In plain English: the MCP surface is deposit-only -- an agent or operator can mature a deposit via MCP but has no tool to pay a loan installment. This adds the loan family's first MCP tool so the manual/agent path drives an installment through the same canonical contract.

ADR-IC-010. Add a pay_installment tool in mcp-server/src/babelstone_mcp/server.py alongside mature_deposit, POSTing /v1/loans/{id}/installment and reusing E1's server-derived key (the tool supplies no key of its own). Inherits the MCP step-up-SCA money-mover gate (babelstone-ziu3.5).
acceptance_criteria:
- A pay_installment MCP tool exists and pays installment N via the engine command surface, deduped by the E1 server-derived key.
- A repeat call for the same occurrence appends no second money leg.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lifecycle driver: server-derived per-occurrence idempotency key, superseding the loan endpoint's caller-supplied key (LCD-1)
description:
In plain English: today the loan installment endpoint trusts the caller to supply the Idempotency-Key, so a human and the future automated driver paying installment N could present different keys and double-collect. This pins one canonical key derived server-side so every caller converges on the same key for the same occurrence.

ADR-PC-036 Decision 1 and 3. Add a shared key-derivation helper computing key = hash(instance_id, command_kind, stable_occurrence_key) -- for a recurring installment the occurrence key is the STABLE INSTALLMENT NUMBER, never the due-date -- and route PayInstallmentAsync (families/personal-loan/.../LoansEndpoints.cs) through it instead of the caller-supplied [FromHeader] Idempotency-Key. Rides the ENGINE_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENT (row 19) command_dedup authority (ADR-PC-029 slot 4). Realises LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_NUMBER_PINNED_IDEMPOTENT (LCD-1, catalogue row 105). CONFORMANCE: this inverts the caller-supplied-key provenance shipped by ADR-PC-029 / babelstone-t7o3.6 / 9w0g / ziu3.1 -- if the endpoint key provenance changes, file an ADR-PC-029 amendment in the SAME change (ADR-PC-020 D3 explicit-drift gate).
acceptance_criteria:
- Two firings of installment N with different due-dates dedupe to ONE Originated money leg (LCD-1 integration test against real Postgres command_dedup).
- The installment key is computed server-side from the stable installment number; a caller-supplied Idempotency-Key is not trusted as the dedupe key.
- If endpoint key provenance changes from caller-supplied to server-derived, an ADR-PC-029 amendment lands in the same change (explicit-drift gate).
- LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_NUMBER_PINNED_IDEMPOTENT flips Planned to Live in the commitment catalogue.
close_reason: Closed

title: Epic — Lifecycle-command driver: a downstream clock-owning actor that POSTs the engine's due maturity/installment commands (ADR-PC-036)
description:
In plain English: nothing automated today issues a deposit's maturity or a loan's monthly installment command on its due date — an operator or the Claude agent has to press the button. This epic builds that missing actor in two layers: Layer 1 (E) hardens the existing manual command path so firing twice is provably safe, then Layer 2 (A) stands up a downstream poll-loop driver that finds due work in a forward calendar projection and POSTs the engine's existing ADR-PC-029 command endpoint with a server-derived, number-pinned idempotency key.

Governed by ADR-PC-036 (chosen candidate A on the E foundation; the write-side twin of ADR-PC-023's clockless-engine stance. The engine stays clockless (BENG004 / NO_CLOCK_DRIVEN_ENGINE_SIGNAL); the driver reaches the engine only through the ADR-PC-029 command surface. New cross-family estate — deliberately NOT in the read-only notification context (babelstone-60n8), the saga substrate (babelstone-t7o3; ADR-PC-036 rejected the saga-timer candidate C), or the loan-tensions review epic (babelstone-5r9n).

## Success Criteria

- A deposit maturity AND a loan installment both fire automatically on their due date through the driver, end-to-end, with no operator action.
- LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_NUMBER_PINNED_IDEMPOTENT (LCD-1) and LIFECYCLE_DRIVER_SETTLEMENT_HEALTH_GATE (LCD-2) are Live in the commitment catalogue.
- The driver runs in its own sibling host (not in Babelstone.Notification, not in the engine assembly); the engine stays clockless (NO_CLOCK_DRIVEN_ENGINE_SIGNAL holds).
- All child issues closed.
EOF
)

title: Staging zla1.10.5 — IAM security verification: RFC 8707 replay-reject, refresh-family revoke, SCA step-up (ADR-IC-021 C1-C4/C7)
description: Plain English: prove the security-critical behaviours actually work before anyone relies on them. Contract/integration tests for ADR-IC-021 commitments: (C1) a token minted for the MCP-server resource is REJECTED at any other resource — RFC 8707 aud-binding enforced end-to-end (the abig / babelstone-5ot0 gateway-contract pattern); (C3) refresh-token reuse-detection revokes the WHOLE token family — empirically verify since Logto does not document it (the gating residual risk before relying on it for theft response); (C4) acr/auth_time present + SCA step-up enforced as a precondition for irreversible ops; (C7) ops-console step-up. Plus: assert the MCP SDK always sends 'resource' (default-resource fallback never weakens aud), and load-test the manual upgrade Job. Seed the Test IDs into commitment-catalogue.md as each gate flips Planned/Gap to Live. ADR-IC-021 rollout step 5.

title: Staging zla1.10.4 — Boundary 9: register MCP server as a Logto API resource (RFC 8707) + scopes; curated agent registration
description: Plain English: make the AI-agent channel issue audience-bound tokens that cannot be replayed elsewhere, and onboard the handful of agents we trust. Register the MCP server as a Logto API resource whose identifier IS the canonical MCP-server URI (trailing slash per the MCP-Auth SDK); define deposits:read / deposits:write / transfers:write as its scopes (narrow, per-tool — commitment C5). Confirm the agent SDK ALWAYS sends the 'resource' parameter so Logto binds aud and the default-resource fallback never silently un-binds it (the footgun verification flagged). Hand-register the curated cohort (Claude, ChatGPT, self-hosted) in the Logto Console — DCR is NOT available (the accepted, tracked gap C6). This child is the explicit open-Boundary-9 PRODUCTION GATE: ship DCR (RFC 7591) or a RFC 7591->Logto-Management-API shim before open agent onboarding. Builds on zla1.5.3 (mcp-server Deployment + mTLS). ADR-IC-021 rollout step 4.
close_reason: Closed

title: Staging zla1.10.3 — Boundary 1: register owned channels as Logto apps; PKCE + SCA; repoint Kong at Logto
description: Plain English: make the user-facing apps log in through Logto. Register the Mission Control UI (app.babelstone.dev, zla1.5.5) and the web/mobile clients as Logto applications; enforce authorization-code + PKCE (S256), no tokens in query strings. Configure WebAuthn/TOTP MFA for PSD2 SCA at login and emit acr + auth_time on the tokens. Repoint Kong OIDC/JWT validation (currently a placeholder) at Logto /.well-known/openid-configuration + JWKS — no edge-contract change (ADR-IC-006 honoured/unchanged). Realises commitments C2 (PKCE) + C4 (acr/auth_time). ADR-IC-021 rollout step 3.
close_reason: Closed

title: Staging zla1.10.2 — Logto Deployment: container + Postgres + OpenBao signing keys + upgrade Job + key-rotation
description: Plain English: run the token issuer. Deploy Logto (single container) as a k3s Deployment in overlays/staging, reusing the existing Postgres (DB_URL to a new database; run 'logto db init'), with a public Ingress on an auth subdomain via Traefik + cert-manager TLS. Store SECRET_VAULT_KEK + the OIDC signing keys in OpenBao (the engine secret boundary, ADR-PC-004 / the babelstone-4c81.1 deck-sync pattern) — never on the bus, never committed. Node 22.14+ runtime; ARM64 image (per zla1.8). Wire the manual 'db alteration deploy' upgrade step as a one-shot k3s Job (the recurring chore the verification flagged); schedule annual OIDC signing-key rotation ('rotate oidc.privateKeys', grace-period on) as a cron Job. ADR-IC-021 rollout step 2.
close_reason: Closed

title: Staging zla1.10.1 — Boundary 6: operator SSO + step-up MFA + RBAC via Logto (ops console + Grafana OIDC)
description: Plain English: give operators single sign-on with a second factor, and make Grafana use the same login — all through Logto, with no separate gate. Register the operations console and Grafana as Logto OIDC clients; enforce SSO + step-up MFA (TOTP/WebAuthn) for operator access (doc 10 Boundary 6: strong auth + step-up + RBAC). Map Logto roles to Grafana's NOC/compliance/developer org roles via Grafana's native auth.generic_oauth (ADR-IC-007 §P6 — the Boundary-7 RBAC surface). Realises commitment C7 (ops-console step-up + role-scoped Grafana access). Depends on zla1.10.2 (Logto must exist first). NOTE: Authelia is NOT used (ADR-IC-021 — a second IdP would duplicate Logto's user store); if a future non-OIDC surface ever needs a perimeter gate, a stateless oauth2-proxy->Logto is the reserved option, not part of this task.
close_reason: Closed

title: Staging — IAM: deploy Logto (the single OAuth 2.1/OIDC AS for Boundaries 1/6/9) — ADR-IC-021
description:
Plain English: stand up the identity layer for the public staging box — the one thing that logs users in and issues the OAuth tokens the rest of the stack already expects. Deploy Logto (the SINGLE OAuth 2.1/OIDC Authorization Server) onto the single-node k3s, wired to the existing Postgres and OpenBao, gated by Traefik + cert-manager TLS, serving every human-and-agent boundary: owned channels (1), operators/ops-console/Grafana SSO (6), and MCP agents (9). Deployment of ADR-IC-021 (bd babelstone-54rf); does NOT reopen the closed J.1 MCP rebuild (babelstone-e50n).

Logto-only: a SINGLE IdP covers all three boundaries (one user store, one MFA config). Authelia is NOT used — it is itself a second IdP and would duplicate Logto's user store with no benefit, since every protected surface (Grafana, Backstage, the Kong-fronted API) speaks OIDC natively. A stateless oauth2-proxy->Logto is reserved ONLY if a future non-OIDC surface ever needs forward-auth.

Decision recap (ADR-IC-021): Logto chosen for native RFC 8707 aud-binding (the un-fakeable anti-replay MUST); DCR deferred (curated hand-registration) and tracked as the open-Boundary-9 production gate.

Structure: phase-level umbrella mirroring zla1.5. Sub-children: Logto deployment, Boundary-1 wiring, Boundary-6 (operator + Grafana SSO via Logto), Boundary-9 (MCP) wiring, and security verification (commitments C1-C7).

Approach (per the zla1 epic notes): EXTEND via overlays/staging, never fork base; reuse Postgres + OpenBao; ARM64 images. GOVERNANCE: the Logto public ingress (auth.babelstone.dev) extends the public surface — an ADR-PC-020 §D3 drift event governed by ADR-IC-021; run babelstone-engine:adr-conformance on the manifest change.

title: ADR-IC-021: IAM — OAuth 2.1/OIDC Authorization Server selection (Logto)
description: Plain English: picks the software that logs users in and issues OAuth tokens for the public staging environment — the missing token issuer Kong only validates (ADR-IC-006) and the MCP server consumes (ADR-IC-010). Chosen: Logto as the SINGLE OAuth 2.1/OIDC Authorization Server for every human-and-agent boundary — owned channels (1), operators/ops-console/Grafana SSO (6), and MCP agents (9). Recorded in ADR-IC-021 (Accepted). Decisive finding: no self-hosted OSS IdP clears both MCP Boundary-9 must-haves, so RFC 8707 resource-bound aud (the un-fakeable anti-replay MUST) outranks DCR (recommended/MAY, deferrable at curated staging). Logto is the only survivor with native, adversarially-verified RFC 8707 + project-DNA fit (non-JVM, reuses Postgres, self-host/EU); the DCR gap is accepted-and-tracked. ONE IdP, not two: Authelia evaluated and NOT adopted (it is itself a second IdP with its own user store, redundant beside Logto, since every protected surface speaks OIDC natively); a stateless oauth2-proxy->Logto is reserved only if a non-OIDC surface ever needs forward-auth. Rejected: Keycloak (RFC 8707 experimental-flag + JVM), Zitadel/Ory/Authentik (no native RFC 8707), Auth0/Cognito (F1), WorkOS/Clerk (F2 US residency), Zitadel Cloud (managed). Implementation: zla1.10.
close_reason: Closed

title: Config-provenance strip — Postgres pin read + OCI /registry proxy + engine product_config_version DTO
description:
Plain English: Show the real signed / pinned regulatory-pack identity for an instance instead of fake digests.

What the UI needs: real pack name@version, schema subject, rate-sheet id, cosign ✓ / CUE ✓ chips, oci · <digest>, and pinned-@-constitution product_config_version.
Exists, mostly SQL-readable: events.pack_version is a top-level non-PII column on every event (head pin = latest by sequence); public.pack_versions resolves (pack_version, oci_ref, image_digest, signature_digest); OCI registry exposes Distribution v2 at :5001 (manifests, referrers for cosign).
Gap: serve.py has no DB driver / no registry arm. The ONE piece NOT SQL-readable: product_config_version (sha256 content-hash) lives inside the Avro events.payload BYTEA on DepositConstituted — folded onto the position but not a SQL column.
Wiring: mostly B + one small A. B-direct-Postgres for the pin (head-pin read + pack_versions join). B-proxy /registry/* -> :5001 for a "present + signature-referrer-exists" badge (surface signature_digest as the fact; full cosign verify stays a CI/deploy attestation; "CUE-validated" derives from signature presence per ADR-PC-006 §P3). Strategy A: extend GET /v1/deposits/{id} to project the already-folded product_config_version (small engine change + additive-default-aware projection).
Effort: M (B parts) + M (engine DTO); the /registry/* proxy itself is S. Depends on the psycopg prerequisite (for the pin read).
Risk: pre-fk7m.9 / pre-v794 deposits carry empty-default product_config_version and can't be back-filled (show "—"); the engine DTO change passes adr-conformance.
acceptance_criteria: Strip shows the real pinned pack_version + oci digest + signature_digest from the estate; product_config_version is read from the engine for deposits that carry it ('—' otherwise); no PII; registry proxy read-only.
close_reason: Closed

title: Logs lens — Loki /loki proxy + build the net-new lens UI (BFF PII allowlist)
description:
Plain English: Build a real, trace-correlated Logs lens that queries Grafana Loki, filtered by the trace id the UI already captures. (The lens UI itself is net-new.)

What the UI needs: reverse-chron structured logs (ts/level/logger/msg/field chips) correlated by trace_id, no PII.
Exists: logs emitted through the SAME OTel provider as traces, so trace_id/span_id are stamped (Tempo<->Loki correlation intact); the UI already captures X-Trace-Id per write.
Gap: no /loki/* proxy; Loki :3100 not exposed (P-PORTS prereq); the Logs lens UI does not exist yet.
Wiring: B-proxy /loki/* -> LOKI_URL querying query_range filtered by the captured trace id; build the lens UI; KEEP a BFF-side structural-field allowlist — do NOT rely solely on the emit-time PII guard (the collector has no redaction yet — Epic K).
Effort: L (net-new UI). Depends on P-PORTS.
Risk: defense-in-depth on PII — belt-and-suspenders allowlist on the BFF, not just the emitter.
acceptance_criteria: Logs lens queries real Loki logs filtered by the active trace id; a BFF-side structural allowlist is in place independent of the emit-time guard; DEMO mode renders offline.
close_reason: Merged in PR #428 — /loki proxy arm with BFF PII allowlist + live Logs lens UI

title: Metrics lens — Prometheus /prom proxy + verify/instrument the 5 SLIs
description:
Plain English: Drive the five SLI cards from real Prometheus metrics instead of hardcoded numbers — but FIRST confirm each metric is actually emitted, because 2-3 of them may not be.

What the UI needs: live value + sparkline for commands_total, command_dedup_hits_total, events_appended_total, outbox_publish_lag_ms, inbox_handled_total.
Exists: some are genuinely emitted (outbox_publish_lag_seconds gauge, inbox_handled_total) via OTLP->LGTM; alert-rules.yaml is the authoritative SLI list.
Gap (twofold): (1) Prometheus :9090 not host-exposed (the P-PORTS prereq); (2) BLOCKING VERIFICATION — commands_total, events_appended_total, command_dedup_hits_total are NOT in the emitted-instrument list and may need NEW engine instrumentation.
Wiring: B-proxy /prom/* -> PROM_URL (mirror /tempo/*). UI: range-query fetches, build sparklines from the series, convert seconds->ms, histogram p50 via histogram_quantile over *_bucket.
Effort: L (raised from M — the unverified instruments may add engine instrumentation work). Depends on P-PORTS.
Risk: PII stripped at emit by the metric View allowlist — safe. Saga-health SLIs (saga_state, saga_compensation_total, pg_replication_lag) are NOT emitted yet — out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 5 cards maps to a verified emitted instrument (or a new instrument is added); cards show live Prometheus values + sparklines in LIVE mode; DEMO mode unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Outbox·Inbox lens — direct Postgres tails + verbatim publish-lag SQL
description:
Plain English: Show the real transactional-outbox drain and consumer-inbox dedup state instead of a setTimeout simulation.

Exists, all real & PII-free: engine public.outbox, public.inbox, public.command_dedup; the publish-lag SQL is reusable VERBATIM from OutboxLagObserver.cs (oldest PENDING age). Orchestrator adds saga_outbox + its own inbox.
Gap: no endpoint exposes these internal drain/dedup tables (by design); serve.py has no DB connection.
Wiring: Strategy B-direct-Postgres. Routes: /bff/outbox/summary (counts by status + verbatim lag SQL + recent published_at-created_at latency), /bff/inbox/tail, /bff/command-dedup/tail, optional /bff/saga-outbox/{process_id}.
Effort: M. Depends on the psycopg prerequisite.
Note: dedup is a SILENT PK collision — there is NO "a redelivery was deduped" event. The lens must show resulting ledger STATE (one row per logical command/event); an actual replay hit is only visible via dispatcher OTel counters (saga.dispatch.delivered/refused) through Prometheus.
Risk: structural columns only; the cross-DB read crosses the engine boundary — adr-conformance check.
acceptance_criteria: Outbox table shows real rows with real publish-lag from the verbatim SQL; inbox/dedup tail shows real handled rows; no PII; routes read-only + local-only.
close_reason: Closed

title: Topic·Avro lens — read real Redpanda topics + Schema Registry proxy
description:
Plain English: Show the REAL messages on the Redpanda topics in the Topic·Avro lens — read from the broker itself, plus the Schema Registry for the schema/catalog badge. (Per the 2026-06-27 decision: read the actual topics, NOT the outbox table.)

What the UI needs: per-topic reverse-chron records with partition/offset, a "catalog ✓ · Avro · schema #sid" badge, and CloudEvents headers (ce_type/ce_id/ce_subject/ce_time/ce_source) + optional amount-class.
Exists: Schema Registry is a real Confluent API at :18081 (GET /subjects, /subjects/{s}/versions/latest, /schemas/ids/{id}); subject = {Avro-fullname}-value.
Gap: Redpanda exposes ONLY the Kafka listener (:19092) + Admin (:9644) + SR (:18081) — there is NO HTTP/REST (pandaproxy) listener today, and serve.py is stdlib-only (no Kafka client).
Wiring: Strategy B, two arms.
  (1) Enable Redpanda's pandaproxy (REST proxy) listener + publish its port, then add a B-proxy /pandaproxy/* arm so serve.py reads topic records over HTTP with no Kafka client (keeps serve.py stdlib-only) — OR add a Kafka consumer dependency to serve.py if pandaproxy is undesirable.
  (2) Add a B-proxy /sr/* arm to the Schema Registry for the schema-id / catalog badge.
Map ce_* from the record headers; decode only STRUCTURAL payload fields against the on-disk .avsc; keep PII-bearing fields opaque.
Effort: L (enabling+wiring the broker read is the bulk; /sr/* proxy is S). Does NOT depend on the psycopg prerequisite (this is a broker read, not a DB read).
Risk: no-PII — surface only structural / amount-class payload fields; CE headers come from the record, never invented.
acceptance_criteria: Lens shows real records consumed from the live Redpanda term_deposit topic (partition/offset/headers from the broker); the schema badge resolves a real Schema Registry subject/id; serve.py reaches the broker via pandaproxy REST (preferred) or a Kafka client; DEMO mode unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: Topology lens — light the real saga legs + event chain (not canned)
description:
Plain English: Make the "follow the event" topology animation trace the REAL path an event/saga took instead of a canned sequence.

What the UI needs: real leg/event routing to light the actual path + an estate-derived node/edge manifest.
Exists: saga_transition (from/to state, event_type, ordered) is the ideal leg source; public.events carries causation/correlation chains; orchestrator SSE GET /api/v1/processes/{id}/stream is already proxied for live current-state.
Gap: SSE emits only current state (no legs/history); no HTTP route exposes saga_transition or raw events.
Wiring: hybrid — Strategy A (existing SSE) for live state + Strategy B-direct-Postgres for leg/event history (GET /bff/processes/{id}/transitions, GET /bff/streams/{id}/events, structural columns only). Derive the nodes/edges manifest from the estate (C4 model and/or Redpanda admin topics+consumer-groups) rather than re-hardcoding it. UI: replace canned FLOWS with fetched legs; fall back to canned in DEMO.
Effort: M (data) + M (UI). Depends on the psycopg prerequisite.
Risk: never decode events.payload (PII). Crossing the ENGINE bounded context for the events read needs an adr-conformance check — the ADR-IC-003 §S2 permission the analysis leaned on is orchestrator-scoped, not engine-scoped.
acceptance_criteria: Topology lights the real saga legs for a live process (from saga_transition) and the real event chain; the node/edge manifest is sourced from the estate, not hardcoded; DEMO mode still animates offline.
close_reason: Closed

title: Staging zla1.5.6 — agent-host (DEFERRED: real-Claude, billable key, replicas:0)

title: Staging zla1.5.3 — mcp-server Deployment + mutual-TLS cert seam (behind Kong)
description:
Plain English: Put the MCP server (the secured tool edge that AI agents use) on the cluster behind Kong, with the mutual-TLS certificate chain it requires so only Kong can reach it.

Builds on zla1.5.1/.2. Delivers:
- The mcp-server Deployment + Service (port 8080, HTTPS; image already multi-arch). Stateless; inbound ONLY from Kong over mutual TLS. Env: BABELSTONE_ENGINE_URL=http://engine:8080, BABELSTONE_ORCHESTRATOR_URL=http://orchestrator:8080, DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT (fail-fast), OTLP http://otel-collector:4318, and the MCP_TLS_* set pointing at a mounted /certs Secret.
- The mTLS cert seam: a TLS Secret (mcp-server.crt with CN/SAN=mcp-server + key + ca.crt) issued by a cert-manager INTERNAL-CA Issuer (reusing the cert-manager installed for zla1.3). The SAME CA must sign this server cert, be what Kong verifies, and sign Kong's client cert — Kong's POC client cert + CA are swapped for the real internal-CA material via scripts/deck-sync.sh (no committed literals). Honours ADR-IC-006 §P5 / ADR-IC-010 §P5 (bd babelstone-29ic).
acceptance_criteria: kustomize+kubeconform pass; rendered staging output has the mcp-server Deployment + Service (8080) mounting /certs read-only with MCP_TLS_CERT_REQS=2 and MCP_TLS_CERTFILE/KEYFILE/CA_CERTS set; a cert-manager internal-CA Issuer + Certificate provisions the mcp-server TLS Secret (CRDs kept out of the kustomize build per the strict-kubeconform constraint); the shared-CA contract and the Kong client-cert swap via deck-sync are documented.
