title: L2/A — typed inline structural value substitution on DepositCorrected (prospective)
description:
Plain English: make a correction actually change the deposit's principal/rate/maturity that a consumer reads — going forward. Carry the corrected structural value on the event (not an opaque ref), have the pure fold apply it, and let the existing accrual→withholding→payout price future flows on the corrected value.

Mechanism A (typed inline value), ambition L2 (prospective). Chosen 2026-06-26.

Scope:
- Replace the opaque `PreviousValueRef`/`CorrectedValueRef` with a **typed corrected value carried inline** on `DepositCorrected` — structural fields only (principal as Money cents, rate as bps, dates). These are not PII, so ADR-PC-004 §P2 does not bind them; follow the `DepositPartiallyWithdrawn`/`RemainingPrincipal` typed-field precedent.
- The **pure fold** substitutes the corrected value into `DepositPosition` (and still bumps `CorrectionCount`). Model a data-entry correction as "this is what the value always was" (rewrite from the original value-date), NOT a step-change at `effective_from` (that is what a partial withdrawal is).
- Re-trigger the per-event Avro/AsyncAPI catalogue gates + the BACKWARD registry compatibility check (the `new-event` discipline) for the changed payload.
- Make the §6.4 €10k→€100k scenario pass.

Out of scope (→ the L3 placeholder epic): retroactive recompute of already-crystallized flows — paid PERIODIC coupons, ADVANCE up-front interest, a completed maturity. NOTE: for an AT_MATURITY deposit corrected before maturity, the eventual payout is already fully correct under L2, because nothing financial has crystallized yet (the F.3 gate only allows Correct from Active). L3 matters only for PERIODIC/ADVANCE (and any correction reaching a closed deposit).

Reconciliation: when this lands, ADR-PC-002 §P2 is satisfied in full for structural corrections — supersede / close out the S1 deferral.
acceptance_criteria:
- DepositCorrected carries a typed corrected structural value; the pure fold substitutes it; CorrectionCount still increments.
- Cold replay reproduces byte-identical current-belief rows (ADR-PC-010 §P5 / determinism gate).
- The D.5 ForcedCorrectionRoundTripTests asserts the corrected VALUE (not just CorrectionCount) on CurrentBelief and the original on AsOf(then).
- The §6.4 €10k→€100k scenario passes end-to-end.
- ADR-PC-002 §P2 satisfied in full for structural corrections; the S1 deferral is closed/superseded.
notes: Scope add 2026-06-26: also delivers the typed CorrectedField validation (reject unknown/non-correctable field → 422; a test covers it), moved here from babelstone-j7mm.1 because the correctable-field allow-list is intrinsic to the mechanism-A typed-value design.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make the correction-value drift explicit (ADR-PC-002 §P2 amendment + 04 Q-BG deferral + 01 §2 caveat)
description:
Plain English: before Epic F closes, make honest the fact that a "correction" today changes a counter, not the value a consumer reads — so the gap is tracked, not silently shipped — and close the cheap hole where `CorrectedField` is an unvalidated free string.

This is the "now, honest" step (no value-substitution build yet). It exists to keep the explicit-drift gate (ADR-PC-020 §D3) honest before k6r8.11 closes Epic F with no open issue carrying the gap forward.

Scope:
- Append a dated **ADR-PC-002 §P2 amendment** (via the `amend-adr` flow — do NOT edit the Decision in place, ADR-PC-000 §D5) recording that the read model presently reflects supersession + a `CorrectionCount` tally, NOT the "corrected values" §P2's text promises; value substitution is tracked in the parent epic.
- Add a dated **04-open-questions deferral** entry for the value-substitution / retroactive-recompute decision, pointing at the parent epic (and the L3 placeholder epic).
- **Validate `CorrectedField`** against a typed `DepositPosition` field set in `DecideCorrection`; reject an unknown/non-correctable field with a `DomainRejectedException` (→ 422) instead of silently tallying.

Sequencing note: the `CorrectedField` validation depends on PR #339's decider code (`DecideCorrection` does not exist on `main` yet), so land it on #339's branch or stacked on it; the ADR amendment + 04 deferral are doc-only and can branch off `main` immediately.
acceptance_criteria:
- ADR-PC-002 carries a dated §P2 amendment acknowledging the counter-only read-model state (Decision not edited in place; ADR-PC-000 §D5).
- 04-open-questions has a dated entry deferring the value-substitution mechanism, pointing at this epic and the L3 placeholder.
- DecideCorrection rejects an unknown/non-correctable CorrectedField (→ 422); a test covers it.
- The explicit-drift gate (ADR-PC-020 §D3) is satisfied for the correction thread before Epic F closes.
notes: Scope narrowed 2026-06-26: this issue delivers the governance/honesty artefacts only — ADR-PC-002 §P2 amendment + 04 Q-BG deferral + 01 §2 caveat (branch docs/correction-drift-explicit). The typed CorrectedField validation moves to babelstone-j7mm.2 (L2): the correctable-field set is intrinsic to the mechanism-A typed-value design, and validating a free string before any value is substituted would be a throwaway guard (today every field name is equally inert — only the counter moves).
close_reason: Closed

title: Correction read-model value semantics — make the corrected value queryable (beyond the store-only counter)
description:
Plain English: today an operator can *record* that a correction happened (PR #339 / k6r8.11), and the bitemporal machinery preserves both the old and the new belief without ever overwriting history — but the actual corrected value never reaches the read model. After correcting a principal from €10,000 to €100,000, the engine's bitemporal query still returns €10,000 with a "CorrectionCount = 1" flag. This epic closes that gap: make the corrected value the one a consumer/auditor actually reads.

Context. Epic F (babelstone-k6r8) closes with the *store-only* correction front door (k6r8.11 / PR #339): the fold (`DepositCorrectedHandler`) only ticks `CorrectionCount`; the opaque `PreviousValueRef`/`CorrectedValueRef` resolve to nothing anywhere in the repo; `CorrectedField` is an unvalidated free string. Surfaced as a "necessary but not sufficient" gap on 2026-06-26: the supersession substrate + the operator door are built, the *act of correcting a value* is not.

This contradicts the governing doc's own words — ADR-PC-002 §P2 ("a `DepositCorrected` … inserts new rows **with the corrected values**") and the §6.4 Q-Y worked example (€10k→€100k must be queryable as "what we now know") — and Q-Y is RESOLVED ("bitemporality is required for v1").

Chosen mechanism: **typed inline structural value (option A)**, following the `DepositPartiallyWithdrawn`/`RemainingPrincipal` precedent. Ambition for this epic is **L2 (prospective)**; retroactive recompute is the separate placeholder epic. PII-valued corrections (name/NIF) stay reference+envelope and are out of scope — the fields in play (principal/rate/maturity) are structural, not PII (ADR-PC-004 §P2 does not bind them).

## Success Criteria

- The §6.4 €10k→€100k worked scenario is an executable gate: `CurrentBelief` returns the corrected principal while `AsOf(then)` returns the original.
- `DepositCorrected` carries a typed corrected structural value; the pure fold substitutes it; cold replay is byte-identical (ADR-PC-010 §P5).
- `CorrectedField` is validated against a typed `DepositPosition` field set (unknown field → 422).
- The drift between ADR-PC-002 §P2 and the as-built fold is reconciled (amended now, satisfied-in-full when L2 lands).
- All child issues closed.
close_reason: Closing — all five Success Criteria verified met against main (commit bf24e93). DepositCorrected now carries a typed inline structural value, the pure fold substitutes it, and the §6.4 €10k→€100k bitemporal round-trip / unknown-field→422 / ADR-PC-002 §P2 reconciliation are all test-backed (ran green). Both children (j7mm.1, j7mm.2) closed. The L3 retroactive-recompute work stays tracked separately in placeholder epic np7p (a depends-on edge, not a child — does not gate this epic). Minor non-blocking residual: CorrectedField is a string-constant allow-list rather than reflected from DepositPosition — functionally equivalent, no action.

title: Epic — Always-on staging/demo environment on Hetzner k3s
description:
Plain English: Stand up one always-on server in an EU datacenter, install lightweight-but-real Kubernetes (k3s) on it, and run the whole babelstone stack plus Backstage behind a public HTTPS address so people can try it and we can demo it. It mirrors the production shape (same services, same event flows) but as single copies with no failover -- right-sized for a demo box, not CI.

Locked spec: Hetzner Cloud (EU), 1x CAX41 (16 vCPU / 32GB ARM, ~EUR30/mo), single-node k3s, Hetzner CSI block volumes for stateful data, Traefik + cert-manager/Lets Encrypt TLS, ARM64 images to ghcr.io via GitHub Actions, Helm/kustomize deploys. Region: Helsinki (FI). Full rationale + rejected options in bd memory key staging-env-decision.

Delivered as 7 sequential phases (child issues): 0 Prerequisites, 1 Provision, 2 Platform baseline, 3 Port infra to k8s, 4 Deploy babelstone, 5 Deploy Backstage, 6 Ops baseline.
notes: RE-SCOPE 2026-06-26 (after estate gap-analysis): the repo is FAR more built-out than the 7-phase greenfield plan assumed. A full kustomize estate already exists: infra/k8s/base/ (12 backing-infra resources) + overlays/dev (replicas=1, the non-HA shape a CAX41 wants) + overlays/ha (the divergence pattern to copy), PLUS a working env-gated CD lane (.github/workflows/cd.yml) that cosign-verifies images, gates migrations, renders+kubeconforms an overlay, applies it, and deck-syncs Kong. So Phase 3 (port infra) is largely DONE. The genuinely-new repo work concentrates in three areas the estate deliberately scoped OUT: (1) NO public exposure exists (zero Ingress/cert-manager/ClusterIssuer; README line 39: ingress beyond Kong out of scope) -- the #1 gap; (2) NO app/engine k8s manifests (engine/orchestrator/acl/notification/mcp-server/Mission Control are compose-only); (3) images are amd64-ONLY (no arm64 in image-build.yml) so nothing runs on the ARM CAX41, and the Backstage image is a literal :placeholder. KEY INSIGHT: nearly all of this is ACCOUNT-INDEPENDENT and statically validatable (kustomize build | kubeconform) on a 16GB laptop -- only the actual provision + apply + cert issuance need the Hetzner account/DNS. Approach everywhere: EXTEND via a new overlays/staging sibling, never fork base. GOVERNANCE: adding public ingress changes the documented out-of-scope posture -> an ADR-PC-020 §D3 explicit-drift event (amend README/ADR in the same change; run babelstone-engine:adr-conformance).

title: Substrate: per-Movement settlement for multi-direction events (renewal debit + credit)
description:
Plain English: a single event can carry more than one money movement in opposite directions — a deposit renewal rolls the principal over (a debit) AND pays interest (a credit) on the same event. The settlement platform wired up by babelstone-t7o3.20 carries ONE movementdirection header per event and the settlement saga substitutes one direction per instance, so a two-direction event cannot be settled correctly yet. t7o3.20 deliberately deferred this (its "AC#4 second half") and made the engine-spine MovementHeaders helper FAIL LOUD on a debit+credit event rather than silently mis-settle.

Technical: decide and build the multi-Movement model — either (a) one event per Movement, or (b) per-Movement header carriage with one SettlementProcess instance started per Originated Movement, each gated by its own movementdirection. Anchors: ADR-PC-032 (Movement primitive, slot 2); babelstone-t7o3.20 (single-direction producer + the MovementHeaders fail-loud guard + the new header-predicate auto-start dispatch); ADR-IC-018 §P5/§D5 (header-keyed, family-agnostic auto-start). Surfaced while completing t7o3.20.
acceptance_criteria:
- A multi-direction Movement-bearing event (renewal rollover-debit + interest-credit) settles each Movement on its own correct direction branch, with no silent loss.
- The t7o3.20 MovementHeaders fail-loud guard on a debit+credit event is replaced by the chosen model (one-event-per-Movement OR one settlement instance per Movement).
- The (a)-vs-(b) decision is recorded; family-agnostic substrate and no-PII-on-headers are preserved; ENGINE/ORCH family-agnostic fitness functions stay green.
close_reason: Merged in PR #341 (settlement substrate: multi-direction Movement fan-out, settlement-leg step-up-SCA gate, constitution shared-leg cleanup).

title: OpenAPI spec<->code drift contract tests (Option A drift guard)
description:
Hand-written specs can lie about the code, so this is the test that catches it — it asserts each published OpenAPI shape matches the C# DTO it documents and the fields the Kong edge actually validates. This is the Option-A drift guard (we chose hand-authored specs). It is NOT Pact: Pact checks consumer<->provider compatibility (both sides running, against a broker); this checks spec<->code honesty (a single provider, doc vs code). Complementary axes — keep both.

A .NET test project in the hermetic `contracts` CI job (sibling to Babelstone.OutboxPublisher.Tests), three layers:
- Layer 1 — spec<->DTO structural equality: read the committed spec (Microsoft.OpenApi), reflect the DTO (e.g. ConstituteRequest, the deposit read-model DTO) honouring [JsonPropertyName]/required/nullability via System.Text.Json semantics, assert property-name sets, required sets, and primitive types match. (Round-trip-of-example is an acceptable lower-maintenance variant.)
- Layer 2 — spec<->edge: assert the documented required set is consistent with the fields Kong's pre-function validates (from kong.yml or a shared validated-fields manifest), for the public write path.
- Layer 3 — spec superset-of pact (only where a pact already exists, e.g. POST /v1/deposits): assert the spec describes at least what the orchestrator->engine pact exercises.
SSE endpoints (x-sse-stream: true) are exempt from body assertions.
acceptance_criteria:
- A .NET test project runs in the `contracts` CI job (hermetic; no running server/broker) with one Layer-1 case per documented surface.
- Mutating a DTO (add/rename/require a field) without updating its spec turns the suite RED and points at the mismatch.
- Layer 2 asserts the constitute spec's required set against the Kong-validated fields; Layer 3 cross-checks any surface that already has a pact.
- x-sse-stream endpoints are skipped for body assertions.
close_reason: Merged in PR #443 (feat/openapi-tier2-completion)

title: Author OpenAPI specs — public edge + engine reads + process status (tier 1)
description:
Write and catalogue the OpenAPI specs for the load-bearing public REST APIs, so they show up in Backstage. These are the client-facing surfaces engineers and integrators most need to discover.

Author contracts/openapi/specs/*.openapi.yaml (OpenAPI 3.1, with the governance x-* fields) for:
- POST /api/v1/deposits/constitute (orchestrator edge front door; ConstituteRequest — product_code, amount cents, opaque account refs, NO PII).
- GET /v1/deposits/{id} and GET /v1/deposits/maturities (engine CQRS reads; likely one API entry — ADR-IC-005 / ADR-PC-027).
- GET /api/v1/processes/{id}/status (orchestrator saga-status snapshot; shipped in babelstone-vjoi / PR #251; currently an mcp->orchestrator read, NOT yet a public Kong route — document the routing nuance).

Then add the kind: Location + one kind: API / spec.type: openapi entity per spec into contracts/catalog/catalog-info.yaml ($text pointer ONLY — never inline the schema; no-drift). The SSE stream GET /api/v1/processes/{id}/stream is documented with an x-sse-stream: true marker, NOT a normal OpenAPI operation.
acceptance_criteria:
- OpenAPI 3.1 specs exist for constitute, deposit read + maturities, and process-status, each carrying the governance x-* fields and passing scripts/openapi-catalog-validate.sh.
- catalog-info.yaml gains the matching kind: API / spec.type: openapi entities via $text (no schema inlined).
- The contract tests cover these surfaces green.
- The SSE stream is documented with x-sse-stream: true (exempt from body validation), not forced into an OpenAPI body.
close_reason: Closed

title: OpenAPI catalogue governance gate — Spectral + oasdiff + Kong-route reconciliation
description:
A CI gate that keeps the hand-written OpenAPI specs well-formed, free of breaking changes, and in lockstep with the real public route surface — the REST mirror of the existing AsyncAPI catalogue gate.

Build scripts/openapi-catalog-validate.sh (hermetic PR lane, folded into the existing path-scoped `contracts` CI job, ADR-PC-019), doing per contracts/openapi/specs/*.openapi.yaml:
- Spectral lint: the oas ruleset + a FROZEN project .spectral.yaml carrying governance-field rules (require info.x-owner, x-owner-contact, x-status [active|deprecated|sunset enum], x-gdpr-legal-basis, x-authorized-consumers — the mirror of the AsyncAPI §P1 field set).
- oasdiff breaking-change diff vs origin/main; fail unless info.x-breaking-change-approved: true (mirror of §P4).
- Kong-route <-> spec reconciliation (the no-drift anchor): FORWARD — every public Kong route (kong.yml orchestrator-edge / engine-query, normalising regex paths like ~/v1/deposits/[^/]+$ -> /v1/deposits/{id}) has a matching spec path+method; REVERSE — every spec path is an exposed public Kong route; NEGATIVE INVARIANT — the internal command surface (POST /v1/deposits) and mTLS-only/admin endpoints must NEVER appear as public specs (agrees with kong-config-check.sh's POST /v1/deposits absence assertion). EXCLUDE the mcp-server routes (ADR-IC-010).
- SSE exemption: an x-sse-stream: true marker waives response-body checks (mirror of the x-compacted special-case).

Add Make targets openapi-catalog-validate (+ optional live openapi-catalog-reconcile) beside the asyncapi ones, composed into preflight. Extend the dorny/paths-filter `contracts` trigger to contracts/openapi/**, the new scripts, and infra/kong/kong.yml. PIN @stoplight/spectral-cli and the oasdiff version (no @latest drift — the AsyncAPI gate's pinning discipline).
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/openapi-catalog-validate.sh runs hermetically (Node/jq + pinned Spectral + pinned oasdiff; no live server/registry), wired into the `contracts` CI job + a make target composed into preflight.
- A seeded good spec passes; each of these FAILS the gate: a spec missing a governance x-* field; a breaking change without x-breaking-change-approved; a public Kong route with no spec; a spec path that is not a public Kong route; any spec describing POST /v1/deposits.
- The mcp-server routes and the x-sse-stream endpoint are correctly excluded/exempt.
- Spectral + oasdiff versions are pinned.
close_reason: Merged in PR #431 — OpenAPI catalogue gate: Spectral + oasdiff + Kong reconcile, self-test fixtures, CI wiring

title: ADR: adopt OpenAPI as a second catalogue spec format + select REST governance tooling (new ADR-IC) and amend ADR-IC-015
description:
Before we add REST APIs to the catalogue we record the decision in the ADR estate, so the change is not silent drift. Two artefacts in ONE change: a NEW ADR-IC that (a) adopts OpenAPI 3.1 as a second canonical specification format alongside AsyncAPI/Avro and (b) selects the REST governance tooling; AND an AMENDMENT to ADR-IC-015 noting its catalogued surface now also includes OpenAPI API entities.

Why both (explicit-drift gate, ADR-PC-020 §D3): adding REST WIDENS but does not contradict ADR-IC-015 — its event-governance Decision still holds in full, so amend, not supersede. But OpenAPI adoption + the REST validation tool are genuinely new decision content beyond a one-paragraph clarification, so a new ADR-IC is the right home (mirroring how IC-015 bundles format + portal-mapping + gate).

Tooling to select via the ADR-IC-000 F1/F2 + S1-S4 framework: Spectral (@stoplight/spectral-cli, Apache-2.0) for lint/governance-field enforcement and oasdiff (Apache-2.0) for breaking-change diff — both hermetic and free, re-running the F1 license-posture hard filter that drove the EventCatalog->Backstage supersession; Redocly CLI (MIT) documented as considered-but-rejected. Use the new-adr + amend-adr skills.

Implicated/honoured: ADR-IC-006 (Kong owns the producing REST surface), ADR-IC-002 (already names OpenAPI as the future sync-format upgrade path), ADR-IC-008 (retired; license-drift precedent), ADR-IC-017 (the event-promotion biconditional must NOT entangle the REST catalogue), ADR-IC-000 (framework), ADR-PC-020 (drift gate compelling the IC-015 amendment same-change).
acceptance_criteria:
- A new ADR-IC (next free number after the disk+bd dual-check; disk ceiling currently ADR-IC-019, so likely 020) is Accepted: adopts OpenAPI 3.1 as a second canonical spec format AND selects Spectral + oasdiff via the IC-000 framework, with the F1 license rationale and the Redocly-rejected note.
- ADR-IC-015 carries a dated, additive amendment widening its catalogued surface to spec.type: openapi entities, cross-referencing the new ADR (Decision NOT edited in place — §D5 immutability).
- The namespace README index + generated reference/adr-index are regenerated (mise exec -- make docs-gen) in the same change.
- adr-conformance subagent PASS.
close_reason: Merged in PR #338 (ADR-IC-020 OpenAPI second catalogue format + ADR-IC-017 downstream-producer amendment).

title: Epic — REST/OpenAPI APIs in the Backstage catalogue
description:
Right now Backstage only knows about the async event catalogue; the synchronous REST APIs (the deposit edge, the read APIs, the internal command surface, the operator surfaces) are invisible in the portal. This epic makes those REST APIs discoverable as first-class catalogue entries, governed by a CI gate that mirrors the existing AsyncAPI one and recorded properly in the ADR estate, then rendered by the live portal the existing deploy issues stand up.

Approach (decided 2026-06-26 with the maintainer):
- HAND-AUTHOR OpenAPI 3.1 specs now (matching how the AsyncAPI catalogue is authored), with "generate the specs from .NET code" tracked as a later follow-up.
- Catalogue ALL REST-shaped surfaces, TIERED by priority: public edge + reads first; internal command + operator surfaces second.
- REFERENCE the existing portal-deploy issues (babelstone-s4ol.1, babelstone-1taq) rather than duplicating them. The verified Backstage @backstage/plugin-api-docs already renders spec.type: openapi alongside asyncapi (one plugin, not two), so NO new deploy work is required beyond a one-line clarification on babelstone-1taq.

Scope EXCLUDES (not cleanly REST/OpenAPI-shaped): the SSE saga-progress stream (documented via an x-sse-stream marker, not an OpenAPI body), the MCP protocol surface /mcp + /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (ADR-IC-010), the SoR gateway routing key (ADR-PC-018), and the demo agent host.

ADRs touched/honoured: ADR-IC-015 (amended — catalogued surface widened to OpenAPI), a NEW ADR-IC (adopts OpenAPI as a 2nd canonical spec format + selects the REST tooling), ADR-IC-006 (Kong owns the producing surface), ADR-IC-002, ADR-IC-017, ADR-IC-000, ADR-PC-020 (explicit-drift gate), ADR-PC-019 (path-scoped CI).

## Success criteria
- The catalogue-worthy REST surfaces are discoverable in Backstage as kind: API / spec.type: openapi entities, $text-referencing governed contracts/openapi/specs/*.openapi.yaml files (no schema restated in catalog-info.yaml — the ADR-IC-015 no-drift invariant holds).
- A hermetic CI gate (Spectral lint + oasdiff breaking-diff + Kong-route<->spec reconciliation) plus an Option-A spec<->code drift contract-test harness keep the specs honest.
- The governance is recorded: a new ADR-IC adopts OpenAPI + selects tooling, and ADR-IC-015 is amended in the same change.
- The live portal (via babelstone-1taq / s4ol.1) renders the OpenAPI REST entities.

title: Engine populate hop: promote Movement origin/direction (+SCA claims) to CloudEvents headers so the settlement saga auto-starts
description:
Plain English: PR #326 (bd babelstone-t7o3.15) built the settlement saga so it is *auto-started* by a money-moving event and picks its debit/credit branch from the movement's direction — but it reads BOTH facts from CloudEvents **headers** (`ce_movementorigin`, `ce_movementdirection`), and nothing on the engine side puts them there yet. The Movement value object (bd babelstone-t7o3.14) carries the Movement only inside the event's opaque Avro **payload**; the outbox relay never looks inside the payload. So in production the settlement saga's auto-start predicate can never fire: the producer of the headers it consumes does not exist. This issue builds that one missing wire — the "populate hop" — so a family's Movement-bearing event lifts the movement's `origin` / `direction` out of the payload into the event's CloudEvents extension headers, which the relay already promotes.

This is the single connective wire that turns the settlement platform from dormant to live, and it is a shared prerequisite for BOTH family-migration issues (deposits bd babelstone-t7o3.13, loans bd babelstone-t7o3.16) — which is why it is filed as its own unit rather than buried inside one of them. Surfaced while reviewing PR #326 (bd babelstone-t7o3.15): the saga consumes `ce_movementorigin` / `ce_movementdirection` (`SettlementSagaModule` AutoStartRule + `SettlementProcess` IEventSubstitutor) but no event declares them, and neither t7o3.13 nor t7o3.16 names the promotion in its acceptance criteria — it is only implied by "emit Originated Movements ... effected via the substrate settlement saga."

## Technical

- **The existing promotion seam.** A `DomainEvent` declares CloudEvents extension attributes by overriding `DomainEvent.IntegrationHeaders` (`engine/src/Babelstone.Engine/Handlers.cs:20`); these persist to the `integration_headers` JSONB column (`engine/src/Babelstone.EventStore/PostgresEventStore.cs`) and the outbox relay promotes each `(key,value)` to a `ce_<key>` header (`engine/src/Babelstone.OutboxPublisher/OutboxDrainer.cs:192-196`). The live precedent is `autorenewalpolicy → ce_autorenewalpolicy` (`families/term-deposit/src/Babelstone.Families.TermDeposit/Events.cs:134-140`).
- **The gap.** `movementorigin` / `movementdirection` appear ONLY in `Movement.cs` (the enum/record) and `AvroEventSerializer.cs` (payload) — no event's `IntegrationHeaders` override declares them, so the relay never emits `ce_movementorigin` / `ce_movementdirection`, and the settlement saga's `AutoStartRule` (`movementorigin == Originated`) + direction substitutor are unreachable at runtime. PR #326's integration tests start the saga by seeding state directly, which is why the suite is green despite the missing wire.
- **Scope.** When a decider records an Originated Movement on an event, that event — or a generic engine-spine helper over the `IReadOnlyList<Movement>` carrier — must declare `movementorigin` and `movementdirection` in `IntegrationHeaders`. Header values are the closed-enum strings only, never PII, never amount (the opaque-payload boundary, ADR-PC-004 §P2 / ADR-PC-032 slot 1). `Observed` movements have no cash leg (slot 2) and need not auto-start a saga.
- **SCA co-carriage.** The same hop is where the gateway-attested `acr` / `auth_time` reach an event-auto-started cash leg on the event's CloudEvents headers (ADR-PC-032 §A7/§A8; ADR-IC-010 §A11–A12). bd babelstone-t7o3.19 *gates* on those claims but assumes they arrive; this hop is the populate point those amendments name. (The ADR prose says "header carriage lands with t7o3.15" — but t7o3.15 is the *consumer*; the *producer* is this issue.)
- **Open design point (resolve here or split).** The **multi-Movement-per-event** case. The header model is one `ce_movementdirection` per event, but a renewal event carries a debit (rollover) + a credit (interest) Movement. The saga effects each Movement gated by its own direction, yet a single event carries one direction header — so either (a) one event per Movement, or (b) the auto-start / substitution model extends to per-Movement header carriage. This is exactly the "AC #4 second half" PR #326 deferred ("the engine relay to emit a multi-Movement event with promoted headers").

Anchors: ADR-PC-032 slot 1/2 + §A7/§A8; ADR-IC-018 §P5 (family-declared CE extension attributes); ADR-IC-015 (CloudEvents binary-mode Kafka headers). Sibling prerequisite of bd babelstone-t7o3.13 / babelstone-t7o3.16; pairs with the consumer bd babelstone-t7o3.15 and the SCA gate bd babelstone-t7o3.19.
acceptance_criteria:
- A family Originated Movement-bearing event declares movementorigin (Originated|Observed) and movementdirection (Debit|Credit) as CloudEvents extension attributes (via DomainEvent.IntegrationHeaders or a generic Movement-carrier helper); the outbox relay promotes them to ce_movementorigin / ce_movementdirection.
- Header values are the closed-enum strings only — no PII, no amount, no account number (opaque-payload boundary holds; ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC stays green; any generic helper names no family).
- An end-to-end test proves a Movement-bearing event auto-starts the SettlementProcess saga (AutoStartRule fires on ce_movementorigin == Originated) and the correct debit/credit branch is selected from ce_movementdirection — closing PR #326 deferred AC #4 second half for the single-Movement case.
- The multi-Movement-per-event header model (renewal debit + credit) is either resolved here (per-Movement carriage) or explicitly split into a follow-up with the decision recorded.
- The SCA acr/auth_time co-carriage point is identified and consistent with bd babelstone-t7o3.19 (no double-populate, no PII on headers).
close_reason: Merged earlier in PR #334 (Movement origin/direction CE headers + de-settle disbursement); closing in post-merge cleanup.

title: boundary-7 telemetry — correct OBS-3 honesty + re-scope the BENG005 no-PII analyser (don't flip Live on it; fix docstring/PR body; wire it as a tripwire)
description:
Plain English: PR #314 (babelstone-njt2.8) marks the no-PII commitment OBS-3 as "Live" as if mechanical enforcement now exists, but the analyser it adds catches nothing on babelstone's real telemetry — every real key is an admitted `babelstone.*` const and every real value is a runtime expression the analyser cannot read, so it fires on none of the 24 real `Activity.SetTag` sites. It also ships a code comment falsely claiming it scans `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`, and its PR body says it does not edit the commitment catalogue while the diff does (+19/-11). A green "Live" gate that enforces nothing on a GDPR/Article-17-load-bearing commitment is worse than an honest "Planned". This corrects the commitment to tell the truth and re-scopes the analyser as a secondary build-time tripwire, not the gate.

Required changes (before #314 merges, or as a fast-follow):
1. Do NOT flip OBS-3 to Live on the analyser alone. Either leave OBS-3 Planned until the runtime guard lands, or — once it lands — scope the gate column as `unit / analyser / runtime`, documenting the analyser as a tripwire and the runtime processor as the load-bearing leg. The analyser alone may never flip OBS-3 to Live.
2. Delete the `NoPiiTelemetryAttributeAnalyzer.cs` class-docstring claim that the `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` structured-state path "is covered by its message-template scanning below" — there is no logging branch in `IsAttributeSetter` and no message-template scanning anywhere in the file.
3. Fix the PR-body contradiction: it states the PR "does not edit the catalogue (applied centrally)" while the diff edits `commitment-catalogue.md`. Disclose the catalogue change honestly and respect the central-catalogue-write discipline.
4. Apply the proven 4-line csproj wiring — attach `Babelstone.Engine.Analyzers` via `OutputItemType="Analyzer" ReferenceOutputAssembly="false"` to `Babelstone.Families.TermDeposit.Application`, `…TermDeposit.Orchestration`, `Babelstone.Orchestrator`, and `Babelstone.Orchestrator.Substrate` (analyzer ProjectReferences are non-transitive, so the analyser currently runs on none of these). Document it as future-proofing a literal-leak shape, explicitly vacuous on today's sites. Empirically verified: builds clean on existing code, and a positive-control inline-literal PII tag fails the build with error BENG005.
5. Keep the analyser fail-closed at build time; do NOT expand its denylist/regex to chase coverage it structurally cannot reach (runtime values, logs, metrics, wrapper/extension helpers, the dynamic `AggregateRuntime.cs:262` SetTag) — that is the runtime guard's job (sibling issues).

Governed by ADR-IC-007 §P4, commitment OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS (OBS-3), and ADR-PC-020 §D3 (catalogue honesty / explicit-drift). Relates to babelstone-njt2.8 / PR #314.
acceptance_criteria:
- OBS-3 is NOT marked Live on the analyser alone; the commitment-catalogue status honestly reflects that mechanical enforcement of the real (runtime) vectors is still pending the runtime guard.
- The false logging-coverage claim is removed from the analyser docstring (or message-template scanning is actually implemented).
- The #314 PR body no longer contradicts the diff about catalogue edits; the central-catalogue-write discipline is honoured.
- The analyser is attached via the 4-line csproj wiring to the four impure-shell projects (TermDeposit.Application, TermDeposit.Orchestration, Orchestrator, Orchestrator.Substrate) and documented as a secondary build-time tripwire, with a positive-control test/PR note showing it fires on an inline-literal PII attribute there.
- The analyser's denylist/regex surface is NOT expanded to chase coverage it cannot structurally reach.
close_reason: Closed

title: boundary-7 telemetry — extend the runtime no-PII guard to metric tag dimensions (MetricsView)
description:
Plain English: metric tag dimensions (the labels on `Counter.Add` / `Histogram.Record`) are a third telemetry surface the no-PII rule covers, and neither the build-time analyser nor a span/log processor can see them — a `BaseProcessor<Activity>` and a `BaseProcessor<LogRecord>` simply do not touch metrics. A PII value used as a metric dimension would reach the metrics backend unguarded. This adds the metrics-side enforcement.

Scope:
- Add a `WithMetrics(... .AddView(...))` MetricsView that keeps only allowlisted tag keys (the `babelstone.*` + semantic-convention dimensions) on Babelstone meter instruments, so a non-admitted dimension is dropped at emit (an OTel `View` with an explicit `TagKeys` allowlist is the only emit-time metric filter — a processor cannot do this).
- Wire a MeterProvider where metrics are emitted but none is configured today: the saga inbox/dispatch counters in `orchestrator/src/Babelstone.Orchestrator.Substrate` (`SagaConsumeLoop.cs`, `SagaCommandDispatchDrainer.cs` — `Meter.CreateCounter` / `Counter.Add`), and confirm the engine MeterProvider applies the view.

Governed by ADR-IC-007 §P4 (as amended) and commitment OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS (OBS-3). Completes OBS-3 coverage across traces + logs + metrics; depends on the trace-processor issue for the shared allowlist definition.
acceptance_criteria:
- A MetricsView (WithMetrics .AddView with an explicit TagKeys allowlist) drops metric tag dimensions whose key is outside the babelstone.* + semantic-convention allowlist; proven by a test on a Babelstone meter instrument.
- Hosts that emit metrics configure a MeterProvider with the view, including the orchestrator saga inbox/dispatch counters (Babelstone.Orchestrator.Substrate).
- A test confirms a PII-shaped tag dimension is dropped at emit.
- The OBS-3 scope note is updated to record metrics as covered, so OBS-3 Live covers traces + logs + metrics with no remaining uncovered telemetry surface.
close_reason: Closed

title: boundary-7 telemetry — extend the runtime no-PII guard to structured logs (LoggerProvider + BaseProcessor<LogRecord>)
description:
Plain English: babelstone's no-PII rule covers logs as well as spans (commitment OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS / ADR-IC-007 §P4 says "span/log attributes"), but the runtime guard for traces does not see log records — and no host even configures an OpenTelemetry LoggerProvider today, so a structured-log field carrying personal data goes straight through. A concrete leak already exists: `engine/src/Babelstone.Engine.Api/HostServices.cs:34` logs a `{Account}` field — a funding account number, exactly the `account` PII fragment the rule forbids. This wires log telemetry and extends the same allowlist enforcement to it.

Scope:
- Wire an OTel LoggerProvider on each host (`WithLogging(logging => logging.AddProcessor(...))` / `AddOpenTelemetry().WithLogging(...)`), net-new — orchestrator and notification configure no LoggerProvider today.
- Add a `BaseProcessor<LogRecord>` enforcing the same `babelstone.*` + semantic-convention allowlist over `LogRecord.Attributes` and the structured state, sharing the allowlist with the trace processor (the `AddBabelstonePiiGuard` seam).
- Close the `HostServices.cs:34` `{Account}` leak specifically: carry a reference/pseudonym (or drop the field), never the raw account number.

Governed by ADR-IC-007 §P4 (as amended by the trace-processor issue) and commitment OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS (OBS-3). Extends OBS-3 from traces-only toward full coverage; depends on the trace-processor issue for the shared allowlist + AddBabelstonePiiGuard registration seam.
acceptance_criteria:
- A LoggerProvider is configured on each host (engine, orchestrator, notification) and a BaseProcessor<LogRecord> enforces the babelstone.* + semantic-convention allowlist over log attributes and structured state.
- The HostServices.cs:34 {Account} structured-log field no longer emits a raw account number (proven by a test) — it carries a reference/pseudonym or is dropped.
- A test confirms a PII-bearing structured-log field (e.g. a NIF/IBAN/email value) is stripped or redacted at emit before export.
- The strip emits the same corrective signal as the trace guard (a counter/log on each dropped field).
- The OBS-3 scope note is updated to record logs as covered.
close_reason: Closed

title: boundary-7 telemetry — runtime emit-time no-PII guard for spans (BabelstoneAttributeTierProcessor); the load-bearing OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS control
description:
Plain English: the build-time analyser from babelstone-njt2.8 (PR #314) only catches PII written as a hard-coded literal at a call site — but every real span attribute in babelstone carries a value computed at runtime (an id's `.ToString()`, a money-cents `long`, an interpolated string), so the analyser inspects none of them. The control that actually keeps personal data out of the regulated trace store is a runtime filter that inspects each attribute as the span ends and strips anything outside the admitted `babelstone.*` tier. This builds that filter for traces — and it, not the analyser, is what legitimately flips OBS-3 to Live.

Scope: a `BabelstoneAttributeTierProcessor : BaseProcessor<Activity>` in `Babelstone.Telemetry.Hosting` (the SDK-aware leaf; `Babelstone.Telemetry` itself stays SDK-free, only `System.Diagnostics`). Its `OnEnd` walks `activity.TagObjects` and drops/redacts any tag whose key is outside an allocation-free ordinal-prefix allowlist. The allowlist MUST admit the `babelstone.*` key contract (`engine/src/Babelstone.Telemetry/BabelstoneAttributes.cs`) PLUS the OTel/Npgsql/AspNetCore semantic-convention prefixes the auto-instrumentation legitimately emits (`db.*`, `http.*`, `url.*`, `server.*`, `network.*`, `service.*`) — a `babelstone.*`-only allowlist would strip the auto-instrumentation tags and blind Tempo/Grafana for the very debugging ADR-IC-007 exists to serve.

Registration: a shared `AddBabelstonePiiGuard(this TracerProviderBuilder)` extension in `Babelstone.Telemetry.Hosting` (mirroring the existing `AddNpgsqlQueryTelemetry`), called once per host inside each `WithTracing(...)` lambda just before `.AddOtlpExporter()` at the three composition roots:
- `engine/src/Babelstone.Engine.Api/Program.cs`
- `orchestrator/src/Babelstone.Orchestrator/Program.cs`
- `notification/src/Babelstone.Notification/Program.cs`

Governance (load-bearing): this is a NEW runtime-enforcement control category that ADR-IC-007 §P4 does not currently contemplate — §P4 names a cultural/design-time control (tier classification + a justifying call-site comment + code review) plus read-side Grafana RBAC, and the only runtime transform the ADR estate names is the OTel Collector (§P1). Per the explicit-drift gate (ADR-PC-020 §D3) this MUST land WITH an ADR-IC-007 §P4 amendment and the OBS-3 gate-column change in the SAME change. The `babelstone-engine:adr-conformance` subagent should be run on the diff.

Why this and not the analyser flips OBS-3: the BENG005 analyser is vacuous on all 24 real `Activity.SetTag` sites (every key is an admitted `babelstone.*` const; every value is a non-constant runtime expression it cannot fold). It can never fire on the actual estate, so it cannot honestly earn Live. This runtime guard is the first control that inspects what is actually emitted.

Scope note for OBS-3 Live: a span processor sees traces only. OBS-3's Live row must carry an explicit traces-only scope note naming logs and metrics as still-uncovered until the sibling issues land.
acceptance_criteria:
- A BaseProcessor<Activity> enforces the babelstone.* + semantic-convention allowlist at OnEnd: a span tag whose key is outside the allowlist is dropped/redacted before export, proven by a test.
- The allowlist walk is allocation-free on the hot path (no LINQ/ToArray per span; foreach + ordinal StartsWith), since OnEnd runs on every Npgsql/AspNetCore span.
- The guard is registered once per host via a shared AddBabelstonePiiGuard() extension in Babelstone.Telemetry.Hosting, called at all three composition roots (engine, orchestrator, notification).
- Legitimate auto-instrumentation tags survive: a regression test confirms Npgsql (db.*) and AspNetCore (http.*) spans keep their semantic-convention attributes.
- A corrective signal (a counter and/or structured log) is emitted on each stripped tag, so the strip is not silently fail-open and bad call-site patterns still surface.
- ADR-IC-007 §P4 is amended (in the same change) to admit the runtime emit-time enforcement category, and the OBS-3 gate column is extended (unit / analyser / runtime), per the explicit-drift gate (ADR-PC-020 §D3).
- OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS (OBS-3) flips to Live on the strength of this runtime control, carrying an explicit traces-only scope note that names logs and metrics as still-uncovered.
close_reason: Closed

title: Wire the four cross-cutting events as bulk-runner adapters; fold in #324 + schema write-path (fk7m.13)
description:
In plain English: make each real operation run on the generic runner. Each operation supplies a per-instance event factory + an optional precondition + optional per-item params:

- PackVersionMigrated and SchemaVersionMigrated: narrow by from-version (only re-pin instances currently on from_version).
- FundsHeld: carries per-item held_amount_cents (Money, integer cents — never a float, ADR-PC-010 §P1/§P2).
- AccountFrozen: carries a machine freeze-reason code (never PII, ADR-PC-004 §P2).

This realizes the schema-migration operator write-path (bd babelstone-fk7m.13) via the generic runner instead of a bespoke path, and supersedes #324's bespoke pack path: re-point pack migration at the runner, salvage #324's matched_count + LIMIT read + reusable tests, and retire the synchronous over-cap 422 in favour of job registration.

Depends on the events from bd babelstone-5w90 / PR #316 (the four store-only cross-cutting event records must exist first). Adjacent but out of scope: the operation-CONSTRAINING semantics of holds/freezes (honoring a hold once applied) live in bd babelstone-32hf — this issue only APPLIES the events in bulk.
acceptance_criteria: All four operations execute through the generic runner; pack + schema honor from-version narrowing; FundsHeld preserves integer-cents Money per item; AccountFrozen carries a machine reason code (no PII); the synchronous over-cap 422 is removed; #324 reusable tests retained; replay-determinism tests per adapter.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Orchestrator note from the PR #445 §P3 review (replay-determinism finding 3): when the four adapters land here, ALSO (a) extend the determinism gate or adr-conformance watchlist to IBulkOperationStrategy implementations (CreateEvent/EvaluatePrecondition purity is load-bearing for content determinism but currently contract-only), and (b) add a per-adapter fixture test pinning CreateEvent's output bytes for a fixed row. Optional ops nicety from the same review: a job-level circuit-breaker on N identical per-item failures (a whole-job defect currently surfaces as N FAILED rows).

title: Bulk-ops command/query surface: register, GET progress, retry-failed, cancel
description:
In plain English: the operator-facing endpoints. POST registers a bulk operation over an explicit frozen id set (sourced from one-off queries) with a set_digest + total_count and returns the job id; GET /v1/bulk-operations/{id} returns live {total, applied, skipped, failed, pending} + status from a read model over the job; a retry endpoint re-drives only FAILED targets; a cancel endpoint stops a running job (BulkOperationCancelled).

- Preview returns counts + a sample + the set_digest — never the full id echo (the 500k-id payload problem #324 surfaced).
- Milestones default store-only (ADR-IC-017 §P1); progress is exposed by query, not published to the bus unless a named consumer exists.
- Family-agnostic surface that dispatches by operation/family, the same shape as the single /v1/pack-migrations route (ADR-PC-021 §P2).
acceptance_criteria: Register, progress, retry-failed, and cancel are implemented and tested; progress counts are accurate against a drained job; preview returns counts + sample + digest (no full-set echo); milestones store-only; family-agnostic dispatch surface.

title: Generic BulkOperationService + BulkOperationDrainer (BackgroundService, SKIP-LOCKED, idempotent, failure-isolated)
description:
In plain English: the engine that actually does the work, generic over the operation. Registering a job freezes the universe into the targets table; a BackgroundService drains it in batches the same way OutboxDrainer does (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, transactional status flips), and for each instance runs an optional precondition then appends the operation's store-only event using the deterministic (action_id, instance_id) command id — so re-drive is idempotent and a restart resumes from Pending. A failing instance is marked FAILED with a reason and the run continues; one bad item never aborts the rest.

Salvage from PR #324 (not merged): matched_count becomes the job total_count; the LIMIT-bounded read primitive; the reusable service tests.

The service + drainer are family-agnostic (ADR-PC-021 §P2) and parameterized by an operation strategy (a per-instance event factory + an optional precondition); the actual event factories are supplied by the per-operation adapters (sibling child).
acceptance_criteria: A frozen target set drains to completion; idempotent re-drive appends nothing new; a mid-run host restart resumes from Pending with no double-apply; a single failing item is isolated (FAILED + reason) and the batch continues; batch size is configurable; unit + Testcontainers coverage; replay-determinism honored.
close_reason: Merged: 3o6m/9z9w via PR #447, qpiw.3 via PR #445, 60n8.* and 2t16.14 via PR #446

title: Bulk-ops store migration: bulk_operation_jobs + bulk_operation_targets tables + state machines
description:
In plain English: add the database tables the runner walks. A forward-only migration adding a jobs table (one row per registered bulk operation) and a targets work-table (one row per instance in the frozen universe, carrying status + optional per-item params), both family-agnostic / spine-owned (no family-named columns).

- Job lifecycle: Registered → Draining → Completed | Failed | Cancelled.
- Target lifecycle: Pending → Applied | Skipped | Failed (with a reason).
- Index the targets table for a FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED batch claim, mirroring the outbox drainer.
- The targets row supports optional per-item params (e.g. held_amount_cents for FundsHeld) and an optional per-item precondition input (e.g. from_version for pack/schema migration).

Use the new-store-migration skill; pick the correct Postgres series and keep the append-only / role-grant invariants for the chosen series.
acceptance_criteria: Forward-only migration applies cleanly; jobs + targets tables are family-agnostic (no family-named columns); status enums + a SKIP-LOCKED claim index present; targets row supports optional per-item params and precondition input; series role-grant invariants honored.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bulk-ops governance: new ADR-PC for the pattern + ADR-PC-009 §A3 (cap → batch size)
description:
In plain English: write the architectural decision down before building it. Author a new ADR-PC for the generic bulk-operations execution pattern (it spans four cross-cutting event types, broader than ADR-PC-009's per-instance version-pinning scope), and append an additive §A3 to ADR-PC-009 recording that the cap becomes the runner's batch size and a migration becomes a registered job over a frozen matched-set — so the single-auditable-matched-set principle of §A2 / §P3 is preserved, not weakened (one job owns the whole frozen set; batching is an internal execution detail of one audited plan, not separate migrations).

The new ADR should capture: register → drain → complete lifecycle; work-table-not-topic substrate (with the rationale: event-store bottleneck, mutable per-item status, audit-by-query, transactional registration, reuse of the outbox pattern); store-only milestones by default (ADR-IC-017 §P1); idempotency reuse via the deterministic (action_id, instance_id) command id; per-item failure isolation; family-agnostic spine placement (ADR-PC-021 §P2).

Use the new-adr and amend-adr authoring skills; run the disk + bd dual number-check before picking the ADR-PC number.
acceptance_criteria: New ADR-PC authored via new-adr (Accepted; disk+bd dual number-check passed) covering register-drain-complete, work-table-not-topic, store-only milestones, idempotency reuse. ADR-PC-009 §A3 appended (immutability gate clean, Decision prose unchanged). commitment-catalogue row added and make docs-gen regenerated adr-index committed.

title: Epic — Bulk cross-cutting operations runner (async, resumable, observable)
description:
In plain English: some operator actions must be applied across a large population of product instances at once — a regulator forcing a pack change, the engine evolving its own schemas, a court freezing funds on every account tied to an order, a compliance team freezing a set of accounts. Today the only path is a single synchronous HTTP request capped at N instances (PR #324), which cannot realistically execute or resume a run over a low-millions population. This epic builds a generic, family-agnostic bulk-operations runner that freezes the target universe into a work-table, drains it in bounded batches with a background service (the same shape as the OutboxDrainer: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, transactional status flips), appends the correct store-only cross-cutting event per instance (idempotent on the deterministic (action_id, instance_id) command id already in the engine), isolates per-item failures, and exposes progress / selective retry / cancel.

It is generic over the operation, so the four cross-cutting events from bd babelstone-5w90 / PR #316 — PackVersionMigrated, SchemaVersionMigrated, FundsHeld, AccountFrozen — all ride it as thin adapters (a per-instance event factory + an optional precondition + optional per-item params). The pack-migration cap (PR #324, bd babelstone-fk7m.12) is superseded: the cap becomes the runner's batch size, and the single-auditable-matched-set principle of ADR-PC-009 §A2/§P3 is preserved because one job owns the whole frozen set.

## Decisions carried in (2026-06-24 design session)

- Do NOT merge PR #324; salvage its matched_count + LIMIT-bounded read + reusable tests into the runner.
- Build the runner GENERIC from the start (not pack-specific): #316 proves the class (pack/schema/hold/freeze share the operations.* shape, an (action_id, instance_id) idempotency key, a store-only no-op fold, and a bulk-over-a-universe need).
- Scale target: low millions, single-or-few drainers. Use a Postgres SKIP-LOCKED work-table, NOT a Redpanda work-topic — the execution bottleneck is the event store (head read + append per instance), not the work feed; a log is bad at the mutable per-item status / selective retry / audit-by-query this job needs; the engine already chose table-drained-by-relay for the outbox (ADR-IC-004).
- Job milestones stay store-only (ADR-IC-017 §P1) with progress exposed by query; publish to the bus only when a named consumer exists.

## Success Criteria

- A generic bulk-operations runner exists: register a frozen universe, drain in bounded batches via a BackgroundService, idempotent per-instance append, per-item failure isolation, progress query, selective retry, cancel.
- All four cross-cutting operations (PackVersionMigrated, SchemaVersionMigrated, FundsHeld, AccountFrozen) execute through the runner as adapters.
- A low-millions population runs to completion, survives a host restart mid-run (resumes from Pending), and reports accurate {total, applied, skipped, failed, pending} counts.
- The synchronous pack-migration cap path (#324) is superseded (cap becomes batch size) and the decision is recorded (new ADR-PC + ADR-PC-009 §A3).
- All child issues closed.

title: Clarify the notification subsystem architecture (underspecified, conflicting purposes) — resolves #317 §D1
description:
In plain English: the notification subsystem looks like it is trying to be several different things at once, and the lines between them were never drawn cleanly. A conformance review of the maturity-scheduler PR (#317) caught term-deposit-specific logic (the 14-day opt-out window, the `pt.notice.maturity` template ref, the "deposit entering its window → reminder due" decision) living inside the supposedly family-agnostic notification core. That is a symptom, not the disease: the core / family-rule / emit-contract / delivery responsibilities are smeared together, and the mechanical gate can't see it. Before we fix #317 one way or the other, we should specify what the notification subsystem actually IS — its bounded purposes — and let #317's fate (and 60n8.3, oyts, a7d4.2, ta8d) fall out of that.

Surfaced 2026-06-24 by the Round-1 adr-conformance pass (workflow run on PR #317 / bd babelstone-60n8.2).

## The conflicting purposes (currently smeared)

1. **Generic notification core** — an agnostic poll loop, cadence/retry/backoff, the dedupe ledger, composite-key idempotency, the storage-opaque read-contract client. Governed by ADR-IC-019 §D2/§P2 (NOTIF-1) + ADR-PC-023 (clock/scheduler ownership) + ADR-PC-027 (read contract).
2. **Family-owned scheduling rules + templates** — e.g. term-deposit's 14-day auto-renewal opt-out window → `pt.notice.maturity`. ADR-IC-019 §D1 says these belong in a per-family `Babelstone.Families.<X>.Notification` contribution, composed at the host edge (§D4), NOT in the core. Pack templates live in the regulatory pack (bd oyts / `pt.notice.maturity`).
3. **Emit contract / signal** — `NotificationDue` (SCHEDULED trigger_kind), ADR-PC-025. It is DOWNSTREAM-produced (by the scheduler, not the engine), and has no sanctioned schema home under the catalogued-⇔-relay-capable-engine-event rule (ADR-IC-017 §P3). That gap is bd babelstone-ta8d.
4. **Delivery adapters** — GL/notification post-flag emission ports (DEF-2), which ADR-PC-012/ADR-PC-025 place OUTSIDE the engine, counterparty-owned. That is bd babelstone-a7d4.2.

## The tension to resolve

- PR #317 (bd 60n8.2) collapsed layers 1+2 into the core (`notification/src/Babelstone.Notification/MaturityScheduler.cs`), violating ADR-IC-019 §D1. The NOTIF-1 fitness function (`NotificationFamilyAgnosticTests`) only inspects `.csproj` `ProjectReference`s, so it missed family knowledge embedded as string/int LITERALS — green gate, real violation. The personal-loan family already exists on disk (ADR-PC-031, Accepted), so the second-family open/closed pressure §D1 protects against is not hypothetical.
- Layer 3's signal has nowhere to live (ta8d), and layer 4 is explicitly out-of-engine — so "what does the notification service own?" is genuinely ambiguous.

## Decide (the session's job)
- The crisp separation-of-concerns across the four layers, and the family-contribution discovery model (mirror `IFamilyHostModule` / `ISagaModule` per ADR-IC-019 §D4).
- Where the family scheduling rule + template selection live, and how the pack parameter `AutoRenewalOptoutWindowDays` is sourced family-side rather than hard-coded in the core.
- How `NotificationDue` (downstream-producer) is catalogued — resolve jointly with ta8d.
- Whether NOTIF-1 should be hardened to catch embedded family literals, not just project references.
- **As a consequence**, #317's resolution: fix-the-code (relocate into `Babelstone.Families.TermDeposit.Notification`) vs amend ADR-IC-019 §D1 (a deliberate, time-bounded v1 in-core deviation, recorded). Either way it must not merge silently against an Accepted §D1.

## Artifacts
- ADRs: ADR-IC-019 (notification family-ownership), ADR-PC-023 (scheduler/clock), ADR-PC-025 (NotificationDue emit contract), ADR-PC-027 (read contract), ADR-IC-017 §P3 (catalogued⇔relay-capable engine event), ADR-PC-012 (GL post-flag).
- Code: `notification/src/Babelstone.Notification/{MaturityScheduler.cs,NotificationWorker.cs,DepositReadClient.cs}`; `engine/tests/.../NotificationFamilyAgnosticTests.cs` (NOTIF-1); families/personal-loan/** (the existing 2nd family).
- bd: 60n8.2 (#317, the §D1 violation), 60n8.3 (emit contract, blocked by ta8d), oyts (#322, pack template), a7d4.2 (delivery ports), ta8d (downstream-producer schema home), epic 60n8.
- The conformance finding lives in the Round-1 conformance workflow result (PR #317).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: jhosm
comments.text:
DECISION (2026-06-24, notification-architecture session): adopted the four-layer bounded-purpose model.

Plain English: the notification service is split into four bounded purposes — (1) a generic family-agnostic CORE that owns the poll loop, cadence/retry/backoff, the dedupe ledger, the composite notification_id, the storage-opaque read client and the outbox; (2) family-owned SCHEDULING RULES + template selection that plug into the core through a named interface; (3) the NotificationDue EMIT CONTRACT; (4) out-of-engine DELIVERY adapters. The architecture was already decided by ADR-IC-019 §D1/§D4; this session names the one piece §P1 left open and decides PR #317's fate as a consequence.

Resolutions:
- Define IFamilyNotificationModule (the notification-side mirror of IFamilyHostModule/ISagaModule). The core owns the loop; the family module owns only "is this row due?" + "which template_ref + data?". Compose via an explicit host list now, assembly-scan later (§P4/§A3). Recorded as an ADDITIVE ADR-IC-019 §D4 amendment (amend, not supersede — §P1 deferred the shape, so naming it clears no drift). Drafted on branch feat/notification-family-contribution (worktree), awaiting review before commit.
- AutoRenewalOptoutWindowDays (the 14-day window) and pt.notice.maturity are PACK data (ADR-PC-007), version-pinned per instance, sourced family-side via NotificationModuleContext — never hard-coded in the core (§D1).
- NOTIF-1 hardening (catch family knowledge embedded as LITERALS, not just ProjectReferences — the root cause of the green-gate/real-violation gap, G1) lands as a TEST + commitment-catalogue change, referenced from the ADR by the one-way pointer rule, NOT restated in the ADR body (ADR-PC-020 §P5–§P7).
- PR #317 (bd 60n8.2): RELOCATE the term-deposit literals out of the core into Babelstone.Families.TermDeposit.Notification — the "fix the code to conform" branch of ADR-PC-020 §D3. Must NOT merge as-is; the relocation + the §D4 amendment ride in the SAME change. "Merge-as-is + a time-bounded §D1 amendment" was rejected: re-proposing ADR-IC-019's explicitly-Rejected candidate C is a violation to fix, not a divergence an amendment can bless.
- ta8d (separable): NotificationDue is engine-OWNED (ADR-PC-025 slot 1/6), not homeless; only the SCHEDULED variant is downstream-produced. Lean = amend ADR-IC-017 §P3 to segment the reverse-orphan gate by an x-producer marker + narrow NO_UNCATALOGUED_EVENT_ON_BUS; resolve intra-vs-cross-context first. ta8d's call.

Adversarial ADR-conformance verdict: sound-with-caveats; honorsExplicitDriftGate = true; PR #317 correctly classified as the §D3 "fix the code" branch. Full memo in the session transcript.

Supersedes #317. Closes 9u70 + 60n8.2 on merge.

title: ADR: home + cataloguing for downstream-producer (non-engine-emitted) event schemas
description:
In plain English: our event catalogue currently assumes every catalogued event is emitted by the engine and is relay-capable. But some events are produced downstream — by another service, not the engine — and we have nowhere sanctioned to put their schemas. The first concrete case is the maturity-notice signal: the notification scheduler raises it, the engine never does. We need to decide where such downstream-produced event schemas live and how they're catalogued, before that contract can be authored.

Surfaced by the Round-1 lane for bd babelstone-60n8.3 (2026-06-24), which correctly refused to author `contracts/avro/operations/NotificationDue.avsc` + an EventCatalog entry because doing so would contradict Accepted ADRs:

- ADR-IC-017 §P3 — catalogued ⇔ relay-capable ENGINE event (enforced by `scripts/asyncapi-catalog-validate.sh` §P3 reverse-orphan + the .NET `CatalogGatedRelayReverseOrphanTests`).
- ADR-PC-023 / ADR-PC-025 — the engine emits no SCHEDULED signal and has no scheduler; `NotificationDue(SCHEDULED)` is DOWNSTREAM-produced by the notification scheduler service (bd babelstone-60n8.2). So there is no `NotificationDue:DomainEvent` engine record, and `contracts/avro/` has no sanctioned slot for a non-engine-emitted schema.

Per ADR-PC-020 §D3 the lane did not silently break the gate; it flagged the contradiction for an ADR-level decision.

## Decide
- Where downstream-producer (non-engine-emitted) event schemas live (a separate catalogue namespace/section? a distinct `contracts/` subtree?).
- Their Schema-Registry subject + BACKWARD-compat rules.
- How the reverse-orphan gate (`asyncapi-catalog-validate.sh` §P3 + `CatalogGatedRelayReverseOrphanTests`) is segmented or relaxed so a downstream-producer schema is catalogued without being mistaken for an un-relayed engine event.

This is the precondition for bd babelstone-60n8.3 (NotificationDue emit contract) and for any future non-engine producer. Likely an ADR-IC (shared integration estate) or an amendment to ADR-IC-017.
close_reason: Merged in PR #338 (ADR-IC-020 OpenAPI second catalogue format + ADR-IC-017 downstream-producer amendment).

comments.author: jhosm
comments.text:
Framing from babelstone-9u70 (notification-architecture session, 2026-06-24).

CORRECTION to the framing: NotificationDue is engine-OWNED, not homeless. ADR-PC-025 slot 1 makes it "a new engine-cross-cutting event" and slot 6 says "the engine owns the NotificationDue schema and the trigger_kind taxonomy." The engine emits it for EVENT_DRIVEN + PRE_CONTRACTUAL; the enum merely RETAINS SCHEDULED for a downstream producer. So the precise gap is narrower and is a build-sequencing artifact: a SECOND, non-engine producer (the maturity scheduler, SCHEDULED) needs to catalogue an engine-owned schema while the engine's own EVENT_DRIVEN emission is DEF-2-deferred (no DomainEvent/.avsc on disk today — NotificationDue currently appears only in EmitContractFitnessTests). IC-017 §P3's reverse-orphan gate (asyncapi-catalog-validate.sh + CatalogGatedRelayReverseOrphanTests) therefore rejects the catalogue entry as having no relay-capable engine event behind it.

Option space (lean = B):
- A) New ADR-IC downstream-producer class: separate contracts/avro/notification/ subtree + catalogue segment + producer-segmented reverse-orphan gate keyed on a required x-producer marker. Principled end-state; over-built for one v1 event. Still amends IC-017 §P3.
- B) In-place ADR-IC-017 §P3 amendment (LEAN): an x-producer marker in the existing catalogue; §P3 reverse-orphan scoped to x-producer=engine; non-engine entries keep full shape/PII/BACKWARD-compat governance, exempt only from the relay-capable leg; + a fitness assertion that x-producer resolves to a registered non-engine service (guards active mis-marking); + narrow NO_UNCATALOGUED_EVENT_ON_BUS (catalogue row 22) to engine-produced. Lands on IC-017's pre-armed "producer topology flagged for explicit sign-off" hook.
- B') Pull the engine's EVENT_DRIVEN emission forward so NotificationDue is a normal catalogued engine event (operations/ namespace, alongside PersonalDataErasureRequested) and the scheduler is a 2nd producer — cleanest governance, but premature (no EVENT_DRIVEN driver yet).
- C) Pact-only, no catalogue — abandons no-PII/compat/discoverability governance; valid ONLY if NotificationDue is confirmed intra-context.

Decisive prerequisite: intra- vs cross-context. ADR-IC-019 gives the notification estate its own service + outbox → reads cross-context → A/B, not C. operations/ namespace already exists as the engine-cross-cutting catalogue slot. Validated against commitment-catalogue row 22.

title: Optimize parallel-backlog-orchestrator skill: detect non-bd in-flight work, verify asserted blockers, filter epics
description:
In plain English: running the `parallel-backlog-orchestrator` skill on the real backlog surfaced several gaps that led to wrong planning moves before they were caught by hand. The skill plans collision-free lanes against bd state, but the real collisions and blockers this session came from places bd doesn't see — uncommitted worktrees, pushed-but-unmerged branches, stale "BLOCKED" prose in titles, and epics mixed into `bd ready`. This issue captures concrete, prioritized fixes to the skill doc (`plugins/babelstone-engine/skills/parallel-backlog-orchestrator/SKILL.md`) so the next run plans correctly without manual correction.

Scope: documentation/process changes to the skill file only. No engine/contract code. Discovered while dry-running the skill against the ready backlog on 2026-06-24.

## Tier 1 — gaps that produced real planning errors

1. **In-flight detection must go beyond bd status.** Step 1 only drops issues "already claimed/in-progress." The dominant no-go regions this session were invisible to bd: a worktree with UNCOMMITTED edits (no claim, no PR) and a branch PUSHED with no open PR (no claim). Step 1 must additionally enumerate `git worktree list` + local/remote branches, compute each branch's `git diff --name-only origin/main..<branch>` AND each worktree's uncommitted changes, and treat those file sets as no-go regions regardless of PR or bd state. Collision-freedom is defined against the whole repo's working state, not bd.

2. **Treat "BLOCKED"/"precondition" as claims to verify, not facts.** A blocker asserted in a title or a prose "hard precondition" in a description is unverified until checked against current repo + bd state. This session both modes appeared: `hkwp.1`'s prose precondition was already satisfied (`hkwp.2` closed = stale), while `njt2.3`'s "BLOCKED on acl/ source" was real (`acl/` holds only a Dockerfile). Step 2 should require verifying each asserted blocker (`ls` the dir, `bd show` the dependency) before honouring or dismissing it.

3. **Filter epics out of the candidate pool.** `bd ready` returns epics (containers) mixed with leaf issues — 17 of 53 rows this run. The skill should state plainly: dispatch leaf issues (`task`/`feature`), never epics.

## Tier 2 — mechanics

4. **Footprint from `git diff`, not `git log`.** `git log origin/main..<branch>` over-counts (commits already merged via other paths make a branch look huge). Name `git diff --name-only origin/main..<branch>` as the footprint command.

5. **In ultracode, Workflow the planning phase too.** The skill prescribes a dynamic Workflow for the lane lifecycle (Steps 4-6) but Step 2 still has footprint prediction done solo. For a large backlog, add an Understand-phase Workflow (one read-only investigator per candidate -> footprint + verified-blocker map) before carving lanes.

6. **Resolve the default-path contradiction.** Step 4's default path tells the orchestrator to both `git worktree add` manually (so self-heal can use `git -C <abs-path>`) AND launch the Agent with `isolation: "worktree"` (its own uncontrolled tree). Pick one; if manual, point the Agent at that path rather than self-isolate, so the self-heal `git -C <abs-path>` forms are valid.

## Tier 3 — minor

7. Handle stale `started_at`/assignee with `status: open` (ambiguous availability; `njt2.8` had this).
8. Mode-detection robustness: if the ultracode signal is absent from context at planning time, confirm the mode rather than assume the default path (this session the skill ran defaulting to non-ultracode because the signal arrived later).
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md updated so: (1) Step 1 enumerates git worktrees + branches and treats their diffs/uncommitted changes as no-go regions independent of bd status; (2) Step 2 requires verifying each title/prose-asserted blocker against repo+bd state before honouring or dismissing it; (3) epics are explicitly excluded from the dispatchable pool; (4) footprint uses 'git diff --name-only origin/main..<branch>' not git log; (5) ultracode path adds an Understand-phase footprint/blocker Workflow before lane-carving; (6) the default-path worktree contradiction (manual git worktree add vs Agent isolation:'worktree') is resolved to one consistent mechanism. Plain-English lead retained per CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Merged via PR #313.

title: Anglicize descriptive Portuguese in term-deposit code comments and runtime messages
description: Code files should read in English. The term-deposit family (and a few shared spots) carried Portuguese in doc-comments, runtime thrown-exception messages, AND one contract field. This PR anglicizes all three: (1) comments/messages (crescente→step-up, escalonada→amount-tiered, carência→lock-up, resgate→partial-withdrawal/early-redemption, juros→interest, antecipada→advance); (2) the carência thrown message + its pinning test; (3) the contract field carencia_days → lockup_period_days across Avro (DepositConstituted), CUE (term-deposit), C# (LockupPeriodDays on event/position/decider/config-store), Go pack-validate (struct tag + the carencia_exceeds_term→lockup_exceeds_term diagnostic), YAML configs, and tests. babelstone is not in production, so the field rename is a clean rename (no Avro alias; field keeps int/default 0; not in the signed corpus). title: Enforce step-up-SCA freshness on the SettlementProcess cash leg (relocate the saga-path gate from the engine to settlement)
description:
Plain English: when an AI agent — or any saga-driven flow — matures a deposit or pays a coupon, the bank must confirm the customer recently passed strong authentication (SCA) right before the money actually moves. Today that check lives on the engine's `/maturity` and `/interest` endpoints. But once money movement becomes append-first and the real cash leg moves to the orchestrator's settlement saga (ADR-PC-032 / bd t7o3.13 / bd t7o3.15), the engine's check no longer sits in front of the cash — it gates a record, and by the saga's own ordering the cash has already moved. This issue moves the freshness check to where the cash actually moves: the SettlementProcess cash leg.

Technical: build the step-up-SCA freshness gate on the SettlementProcess **Originated** cash leg (ConfirmDebit / ConfirmCredit at the Core ACL, ADR-PC-016 slot 5). Consume the `X-SCA-Acr` / `X-SCA-Auth-Time` rail that PR #309 (bd babelstone-ls44) already ships on `saga_outbox` + the dispatcher. The substrate **attests** (re-emits the gateway-attested claims on the cash-leg delivery); the **receiver denies** fail-closed on absent/stale SCA *before* the irreversible debit/credit — never the substrate (attest-not-deny, ADR-IC-006 §P2; family-agnostic substrate, ADR-PC-019 §P2 / ADR-IC-018 §D2). Re-check freshness at the **settlement-dispatch instant** against `SCA_MAX_AGE` (300 s), NOT inherited from saga entry (the saga duration ceiling ~1800 s is 6× the window, so a proof fresh at saga start can be stale at the cash leg). For event-auto-started standalone legs (ADR-PC-032 §4.2 — maturity/coupon) the attested `acr`/`auth_time` must reach the leg on the Movement-bearing event's CloudEvents headers (the populate hop). Enabled by ADR-IC-010 §A11–A12 + ADR-PC-032 §A7 (the amendments that relocate the gate).

This closes the gap surfaced when ls44/PR #309 (Accepted assumption: "the engine stays the single freshness authority") met ADR-PC-032 (Accepted same day, silent on SCA, moves every cash leg off the engine).
acceptance_criteria:
- The SettlementProcess Originated cash leg refuses to dispatch ConfirmDebit/ConfirmCredit when the gateway-attested SCA proof is absent or stale at the dispatch instant — returning the fail-closed SCA_REQUIRED verdict and parking/compensating per the leg's policy — BEFORE any irreversible cash movement.
- Freshness is re-checked at the settlement-dispatch instant against SCA_MAX_AGE (300 s), independent of saga entry: a proof fresh at saga start but stale when the cash leg fires is refused.
- The gate consumes the X-SCA-Acr / X-SCA-Auth-Time claims carried on saga_outbox (bd babelstone-ls44 / PR #309); the substrate ATTESTS (re-emits the headers on the cash-leg delivery), the RECEIVER DENIES — no substrate-side deny (ADR-IC-006 §P2 attest-not-deny; ADR-PC-019 §P2 / ADR-IC-018 §D2 family-agnostic substrate).
- For an event-auto-started standalone leg (maturity / coupon, ADR-PC-032 §4.2) the attested acr/auth_time reach the leg on the Movement-bearing event's CloudEvents headers.
- A commitment-catalogue Test ID registers the saga-path no-client-side-bypass invariant (the MCP_SCA_GATE_CANNOT_BYPASS analogue for the settlement leg), flipped Live when this lands.
- Integration test (WireMock Core): a saga-driven maturity money-mover with no/stale SCA is refused at the settlement leg before cash moves; with fresh SCA it settles.
close_reason: Merged in PR #341 (settlement substrate: multi-direction Movement fan-out, settlement-leg step-up-SCA gate, constitution shared-leg cleanup).

title: boundary-7 telemetry — no-PII span/log build-time analyser gate (OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS)
description:
Plain English: today the rule that telemetry spans and logs must never carry personal data (NIF, IBAN, account number, name, email) is checked only by a runtime test an author can forget to extend, and we pseudonymize the client id — but nothing fails the build the moment someone adds a PII-bearing span attribute. This writes the dedicated compile-time analyser that turns that rule into a mechanical gate, so a PII attribute on telemetry breaks the build instead of leaking into a regulated observability store.

Scope: the dedicated build-time ANALYSER leg of commitment `OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS` (commitment-catalogue row OBS-3, status `Planned`; reserved gate column `unit / analyser`), governed by ADR-IC-007 §P4 and tied to ADR-IC-016 plane (iii). The structural assertion already rides inside `TelemetrySpanTests` (with the bus-surface companion in `EmitContractFitnessTests.No_event_schema_field_carries_pii`), and span pseudonymization landed via `babelstone-njt2.2` (`ClientPseudonym.Of`, HMAC-SHA-256) — but neither flips the row. The `Live` bar is the dedicated analyser, which is not yet written and has no open tracker.

Startable now — no blocker (unlike the two integration-leg siblings, this needs no CI infrastructure).

Surfaced by PR #306 (doc-10 Realisation note, Boundary 7).
acceptance_criteria:
- A build-time Roslyn analyser fails the build when a span or log attribute key/value carries NIF, IBAN, account number, customer name, or email (only the structural babelstone.* operational tier is admitted; money rides as integer cents).
- The analyser ships with positive and negative tests (a PII-bearing attribute fails; a structural-only attribute passes) and is wired into the build as a Roslyn analyser alongside the existing engine analysers (the handler-purity/determinism gate pattern).
- OBS_NO_PII_ATTRS (OBS-3) flips Planned->Live in the commitment-catalogue, resolving to its reserved 'unit / analyser' gate.

title: boundary-7 observability RBAC — end-to-end enforcement test (OBS_PLANE_RBAC integration; BLOCKED on live Grafana in CI)
description:
Plain English: we already provision Grafana's roles as code so NOC, compliance, developer, and admin each get the right scope, and the trace datasource is locked to engineers/admins — but no test yet proves a live Grafana actually turns away an under-privileged user and records who read a financially-attributed trace. This stands up a Grafana instance in CI and asserts that a NOC token is genuinely refused a Tempo trace query and that the trace read lands in the access log, making the role split enforced rather than only configured.

Scope: the end-to-end ENFORCEMENT integration leg of commitment `OBS_PLANE_RBAC` (commitment-catalogue row SEC-2, status `Planned`), governed by ADR-IC-016 §7 (plane iii) and ADR-IC-007 §P6. The config leg is `Live` and CLOSED via `babelstone-njt2.4` (declarative `infra/grafana/rbac/` — the four ADR-IC-007 §P6 roles, the Tempo datasource locked to engineer+admin, dataproxy access logging). The remaining refusal/audit assertion has no open tracker.

Out of scope: folder-granular RBAC and a tamper-evident audit log are the Enterprise / upstream-gateway hardening the ADR explicitly names, not part of this `Live` bar.

Named prerequisite recorded per ADR-PC-020 §D3. (Distinct from the now-closed K.2 / `babelstone-o60b`, which stood up the dev-stack Grafana, not a CI instance.)
