title: boundary-3/4 Kafka SASL — broker-side topic-ACL enforcement leg (KAFKA_SASL_TOPIC_ACL integration; BLOCKED on authenticated cluster in CI)
description:
Plain English: we already make every Kafka client log in with its own SASL/SCRAM identity, and we ship a declarative list of which service may use which topic — but nothing yet proves the broker actually turns away a service that tries to write or read a topic it has no business touching. This adds an end-to-end test against an authenticated Redpanda/Kafka cluster confirming a cross-context produce and a cross-context consume are really rejected, turning the paper policy into an enforced one across both the producer (Boundary 3) and the consumer fan-out (Boundary 4) halves.

Scope: the broker-enforced INTEGRATION leg of commitment `KAFKA_SASL_TOPIC_ACL` (commitment-catalogue row SEC-1, status `Planned`), governed by ADR-IC-016 §4–§6 (plane ii). The unit leg is `Live` and CLOSED via `babelstone-njt2.1` (`KafkaSaslOptionsTests` credential applier) + `babelstone-njt2.5` (host-side credential energize via `ISecretProvider`); only the broker-side enforcement assertion over the declarative `infra/redpanda/topic-acls.yaml` + `apply-acls.sh` remains, and it has no open tracker. Merges Boundary 3 (producer) and Boundary 4 (consumer fan-out) — one authenticated CI cluster serves both halves of the same SEC-1 commitment.

Surfaced by PR #306 (doc-10 Realisation notes, Boundaries 3 and 4).

BLOCKED on: an authenticated SASL/SCRAM Redpanda/Kafka cluster running in CI (e.g. a Testcontainers integration lane). No authenticated cluster is in scope today; the broker-side topic-ACL enforcement leg stays integration-`Planned` until one exists. Named prerequisite recorded per ADR-PC-020 §D3.
acceptance_criteria:
- An authenticated SASL/SCRAM Redpanda/Kafka cluster runs in CI (e.g. Testcontainers) with infra/redpanda/topic-acls.yaml applied via apply-acls.sh before the assertions run.
- A producer presenting a non-deposit SCRAM identity is REJECTED when it attempts to write a deposit topic (Boundary 3 cross-context produce denied).
- A consumer presenting an identity not authorized for a topic is REJECTED when it attempts to subscribe/read that topic; each consumer reads only the topics it subscribes to (Boundary 4 cross-context consume denied).
- The authorized producer and consumer paths still succeed (no false-positive lockout).
- KAFKA_SASL_TOPIC_ACL flips Planned->Live in commitment-catalogue row SEC-1, and the SEC-1 note recording the broker-ACL integration leg as a residual is updated.

title: Account abstraction + available-balance split + hold lifecycle (ADR-PC + engine impl)
description: Plain English: ADR-PC-030 deferred the full Account model to shape 3-4. This task decides and builds it: every engine-owned aggregate is an account; the accounting-balance vs available-balance split; and the hold lifecycle (HoldPlaced -> HoldCaptured -> HoldExpired). Needs a contract-shape ADR-PC plus engine support. The shape-4 balance is the fold of Movements over an account (ADR-PC-030 §95), so this builds on the Movement read model (sibling). Governed by ADR-PC-030 (shapes 3-4 deferral).
close_reason: Merged in PR #444 (feat/account-hold-spine)

comments.author: jhosm
comments.text:
Plain English: the ADR decision for this issue is delivered — what remains is the engine build, which can't start until the movement read model (hkwp.1) exists.

ADR delivered in PR #307 (branch docs/movement-shape3-adrs): ADR-PC-033 (Account abstraction — every engine-owned aggregate is an account; accounting vs available balance as rebuildable folds, never stored; hold lifecycle HoldPlaced->HoldCaptured|HoldExpired as operations.Hold* cross-cutting events keyed by hold_id; expiry projection-derived), plus the ADR-PC-032 append-only amendments for the family-declared IMovementBearing seam (hkwp.2) and the operations.MovementObserved feed (hkwp.4). PR #307 deliberately does NOT close hkwp.3.

Remaining (engine implementation): the family-declared IAccount/IHoldable seam; the spine-owned generic accounting/available-balance + active-hold fold projector; operations.HoldPlaced/HoldCaptured/HoldExpired event records + governed Avro; the funds-and-rules authorization decider (ADR-PC-030 stages 3-5); the read-model migration — landing the Planned commitments ACCOUNT_BALANCE_IS_A_FOLD / HOLD_LIFECYCLE_PURE as live CI gates. Depends on hkwp.1 (the movement read model), which unblocks once #307 merges. Status set back to open; the ADR session that claimed it is complete.

title: Movement generic-discoverability seam — known payload slot or family-declared seam
description: Plain English: for a single, engine-owned projection to fold movements off events from ANY family, the spine must be able to find the Movement(s) on an arbitrary carrying event without knowing that family's payload schema. Today ADR-PC-032 slot 1 leaves Movement placement to each family's own payload. This task defines the generic seam — either a well-known payload slot every money-moving event uses, or a family-declared seam the spine calls (the IErasable-style pattern, ADR-PC-021/ADR-PC-004). This is the PRECONDITION for the account movement ledger (sibling). Decide as part of the shape-3 grounding ADR work. Governed by ADR-PC-032 residual-risk §2.
close_reason: Closed

title: Account movement ledger — one spine-owned, account-keyed Movement read model
description:
Plain English: ADR-PC-032 introduced the Movement write-side atom (recorded append-first on money-moving events) but deliberately said nothing about how movements are read back. This is the read side: a single, engine-owned projection that lists every Movement keyed by the account it moved against — the substrate a balance ("a balance is a fold over postings", ADR-PC-030 §95), an account statement, and reconciliation all read from.

Decision to record (as a contract-shape ADR-PC when taken):
- ONE spine-owned, account_ref-keyed projection — NOT per-family. Rationale: the Movement is family-agnostic (ADR-PC-032 slot 1/6); Observed movements have no owning family; reconciliation (ADR-PC-016 flow 1) and the shape-4 balance fold are account-centric, not family-centric.
- Stays family-agnostic (folds only the opaque Movement, never a family-typed shape) so ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC (ADR-PC-021 §P2) holds.

Hard precondition: a generic projector can fold movements off arbitrary family events only if the Movement is GENERICALLY DISCOVERABLE — via a known payload slot or a family-declared seam (IErasable-style, ADR-PC-021/ADR-PC-004). That seam is its own sibling under this epic and blocks this task.

Governed by ADR-PC-032 residual-risk §2. Decide when shape-3 (conta à ordem) lands and a live consumer exists (v1 has no Observed producer).
close_reason: Closed

title: Shape-3 foundations — the Account abstraction & Movement read/Observed completion
description:
Plain English: two Accepted ADRs deliberately deferred a bounded set of foundational pieces to shape 3 (the conta à ordem transactional account). ADR-PC-030 deferred the full Account model — every engine-owned aggregate as an account, the accounting/available-balance split, and the hold lifecycle. ADR-PC-032 deferred the *read side* of the Movement primitive — an account-keyed movement ledger, the Observed capture/settlement feed, and the balance-as-fold (PC-030 §95). This epic groups exactly those deferred pieces so the shape-3 grounding is planned as one coherent foundation instead of scattered, and so the conta à ordem family can later be authored on top of a built foundation.

This epic is deliberately BOUNDED and CLOSEABLE: its scope is *only* the items the two ADRs named as deferred — nothing open-ended. It closes when that foundation is decided (the contract-shape ADRs) and built, such that the conta à ordem family can be authored on it. Authoring the conta à ordem family itself is a SEPARATE (future) family epic, NOT part of this one.

## Success Criteria

- The Account abstraction is decided (a contract-shape ADR-PC) and the engine support is built: every engine-owned aggregate is an account; the accounting/available-balance split and the hold lifecycle (HoldPlaced → HoldCaptured → HoldExpired) exist.
- The Movement read side is decided (a contract-shape ADR-PC) and built: ONE spine-owned, account_ref-keyed Movement projection that folds the balance per ADR-PC-030 §95 — not a per-family copy.
- The Movement generic-discoverability seam (a known payload slot or a family-declared seam, IErasable-style) the read model depends on is defined — the ADR-PC-032 precondition.
- The Observed capture/settlement feed contract is specified (schema + dedup + gap-detection ownership); a live producer arrives with shape 3 (dormant in v1).
- All child issues are closed.

## Known child workstreams (the finite set)

1. The Movement generic-discoverability seam (precondition for everything below).
2. The account-movement ledger projection — the spine-owned read model (governed by ADR-PC-032 residual-risk §2).
3. The Account abstraction + available-balance split + hold lifecycle (ADR-PC + engine impl).
4. The Observed capture/settlement feed contract.

Governed by ADR-PC-030 (shapes 3-4 deferral) and ADR-PC-032 (Movement read-side deferral).

title: Add parallel-backlog-orchestrator plugin skill (fan ready bd work into collision-free lanes, self-heal, ship)
description:
Plain English: a model-invocable skill that takes the ready bd backlog, splits it into the maximum number of groups that cannot touch the same files, and runs each group as its own background agent in its own git worktree — every group ending in a pushed branch and an open PR. It supervises the batch: re-launching crashed agents, nudging GitHub's stale mergeability cache with an empty commit, and rebasing on real conflicts, until no ready work is left. It codifies the user's most-used 'parallel lanes' workflow and is the orchestration companion to post-merge-cleanup.

Technical: new skill at plugins/babelstone-engine/skills/parallel-backlog/ (ADR-PC-020 §P2 skills layer). Hard invariants: ONE central Dolt writer — the orchestrator owns every bd write (claim/close/dolt push); lane agents are read-only on bd (-C primary) and never push to main or self-merge. Lanes branch off origin/main in isolated worktrees (mise trust --yes; git -C + absolute paths to avoid the cwd-leak failure mode); collision-free lane design (disjoint file footprints) is enforced; PR bodies carry the In-plain-English lead + CI-required ADRs-touched section; adr-conformance runs before PR on engine/contract/docs-adr diffs. Issues stay claimed while their PR is open — closing is post-merge-cleanup's job (no double-ownership of the lifecycle).
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md exists at plugins/babelstone-engine/skills/parallel-backlog-orchestrator/ with frontmatter name+description; README skills index has a row for it; the four load-bearing invariants (one central Dolt writer / collision-free lanes / never-to-main+no-self-merge / closing-is-post-merge-cleanup's-job) are each stated as guardrails; passes doc-consistency review.
close_reason: Closed

title: Re-apply main-protect ruleset so pr-body-bd-issues actually blocks merges
description:
Plain English: PR #288 adds the `pr-body-bd-issues` CI check and registers it as a required status check in the version-controlled ruleset source (.github/rulesets/main-protect.json). But GitHub branch rulesets are remote state, not config read from the repo — so the check currently RUNS on PRs but does not yet BLOCK a merge. A maintainer must re-apply the live ruleset for it to become blocking.

Follow-up to babelstone-2t16.25 (do after PR #288 merges). Maintainer action:

  gh api repos/jhosm/babelstone/rulesets --jq '.[] | {id, name}'   # find main-protect id
  gh api -X PUT repos/jhosm/babelstone/rulesets/<ID> --input .github/rulesets/main-protect.json

Acceptance Criteria:
- The live main-protect ruleset lists pr-body-bd-issues among its required status checks (verify via `gh api repos/jhosm/babelstone/rulesets/<ID>`).
- A test PR with no bd-issues section is blocked from merging (not merely red).
- In-flight PRs opened before the job existed are re-pushed so the now-required check reports.
close_reason: Live main-protect ruleset (id 16900658) re-applied at user request; pr-body-bd-issues is now a required status check (verified via gh api). #288 stays mergeable (check green). NOTE: job reaches main only when #288 merges, so a new PR off main is blocked until then.

title: Add post-merge-cleanup plugin skill (retire merged lanes, preserve open ones)
description:
Plain English: a model-invocable skill that tidies the repo after PRs land — it sweeps every local branch and git worktree, retires the ones whose PR has merged (delete branch local+remote, remove worktree, close the linked bd issue), and crucially preserves any lane whose PR is still open. It is the executable half of the new ## Cleanup / Post-Merge convention in CLAUDE.md.

Technical: new skill at plugins/babelstone-engine/skills/post-merge-cleanup/ (ADR-PC-020 §P2 skills layer). Authority for the merged/open decision is GitHub PR state via gh, not git branch --merged (squash merges defeat the latter). Guards: never force-remove a dirty worktree (skip the whole lane, branch + bd included); never delete primary/current/main; flag no-PR / closed-unmerged branches rather than deleting. Verified 3/3 against a disposable fixture (squash-merge trap, dirty-worktree block, no-PR preserve, selective bd-close); trigger-description optimization confirmed the original description (precision 100%, recall inherently low for inline-doable tasks).

title: Add a CI-enforced "bd issues closed on merge" PR-body section
description:
Plain English: PRs have no explicit record of which bd issues a merge should close. A bd issue is not a GitHub issue, so nothing closes it automatically and the merger has to infer it. This adds a required `## bd issues closed on merge` PR-body section (listing the bd IDs, or stating "None"), enforced exactly like the existing "ADRs touched/honoured" gate, so the Cleanup/Post-Merge step knows precisely which `bd close` to run.

Scope:
- Document the section in CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md (Branching & PR Policy, Communication Style, Cleanup/Post-Merge).
- Add a `pr-body-bd-issues` job to .github/workflows/adr-governance.yml mirroring the security-hardened `pr-body-adrs` gate (PR body passed via env, double-quoted; dependabot-exempt).
- Register `pr-body-bd-issues` as a required status check in .github/rulesets/main-protect.json + its README (maintainer re-applies the live ruleset via `gh api -X PUT`).

Acceptance Criteria:
- A PR whose body lacks a recognizable `## bd issues closed on merge` section fails the `pr-body-bd-issues` check.
- A PR whose body carries the section (listing IDs or stating None) passes.
- Dependabot-authored PRs are exempt.
- CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md describe the section identically.
- main-protect.json lists `pr-body-bd-issues` among required_status_checks.

title: Early-termination: add the missing HTTP entry point + relocate its payout onto the gated settlement leg
description:
Plain English: a customer breaking a deposit early is fully worked out in the engine — the penalty/settlement math, the lifecycle rule, and the tests all exist — but there is NO way to actually trigger it (no HTTP endpoint), and when it runs internally it pays out to a log-only stub instead of the real settlement path. So early termination is the least-wired of the lifecycle operations: decided and tested, but neither reachable nor settled.

Two concrete gaps:

1. No entry point. DepositsEndpoints.cs exposes constitute / maturity / interest / partial-withdrawal / erase / constitute-renewal / renewal-link — but NO terminate route. TermDepositConstitutionService.TerminateEarlyAsync (with TerminateEarlyCommand + TermDepositDecider.DecideEarlyTermination + EarlyTerminationPolicy, all tested by EarlyTerminationDeciderTests / EarlyTerminationHappyPathTests / RateReductionPenaltyTests) is unreachable from the family HTTP surface.

2. Eager settle. TerminateEarlyAsync calls settlement.SettleAsync(Credit, NetSettlementAmount, ..., "early_termination") eagerly against LoggingSettlementPort — not the confirmation-gated path ADR-PC-016 slot 5 requires (a credit is never funds-gated but must have a confirmed legacy-journal counterpart for reconciliation flow 1).

Scope: add POST /v1/deposits/{id}/terminate (or /early-termination) wired to TerminateEarlyAsync with the same idempotency contract as the other money-movers; and relocate the early-termination payout ((principal - penalty) + net accrued interest, floored) onto the parent issue's confirmation-gated settlement leg. Append DepositTerminatedEarly first, then drive the gated ACL credit. WireMock ACL at v1.

Anchors: ADR-PC-016 sections 74/127/128, ADR-PC-029 section 60; parent = the lifecycle-credit settlement relocation. Flagged "real-gap P2" by the 2026-06-21 term-deposit feature-completeness audit (the one lifecycle op that is neither reachable nor settled).
acceptance_criteria:
- A POST early-termination endpoint exists on the term_deposit family surface, wired to TerminateEarlyAsync, with the money-mover idempotency contract (id-keyed; rejects double-terminate).
- The early-termination payout settles via the confirmation-gated saga leg (parent issue), not the eager LoggingSettlementPort call.
- DepositTerminatedEarly is appended before the gated credit; the engine fact is not treated as final until the ACL credit is confirmed.
- Endpoint + settlement are covered by integration tests (including the GatedSettlementWireMock path).
close_reason: Merged to origin/main in PR #353 (rebase-merged: 7afae3f t7o3.16 / 3ca8912 t7o3.13 / a481167 t7o3.13.1). Loan installment+early-repay and term_deposit lifecycle credits relocated onto the ADR-PC-032 Movement + gated substrate settlement saga; POST /v1/deposits/{id}/terminate added. CI all-green; central adr-conformance review PASS (no ADR contradiction).

title: Relocate remaining lifecycle-credit settlements onto confirmation-gated saga legs (maturity / coupon / early-termination / renewal)
description:
Plain English: when a deposit is opened we already moved the money leg (debiting the customer's account) out of the engine and onto a proper saga that waits for the bank's core to confirm before the deposit is treated as final (babelstone-t7o3.4). Every OTHER money movement — paying out at maturity, paying a coupon, paying out an early break, and the renewal rollover — still moves money the old eager way, by calling a log-only stub directly inside the engine. The architecture docs already admit this is temporary ("eager until their own sagas land"), but the follow-up issue that finishes the job was never filed. This is that issue.

Today TermDepositConstitutionService.MatureAsync / PayInterestAsync / TerminateEarlyAsync / ConstituteRenewalAsync each call settlement.SettleAsync(...) eagerly against the wired LoggingSettlementPort dev stub (engine/src/Babelstone.Engine.Api/HostServices.cs), which never confirms. Per ADR-PC-016 slot 5 (sections 74/127/128) every lifecycle credit (interest, maturity, early-termination, partial-withdrawal) is NOT gated on funds — the legacy core always accepts a credit — but IS gated on CONFIRMATION, because reconciliation flow 1 requires every credit to have a confirmed legacy-journal counterpart. ADR-PC-029 section 60 and the ADR-PC-016 section 128 note both record the remaining eager-settle as an acknowledged, dated drift whose closure is "their own future issues" — which did not exist until now.

Scope: relocate each remaining lifecycle money leg off the eager in-engine SettleAsync onto a confirmation-gated saga step delivered through the dispatcher to the (WireMock at v1) Core ACL, exactly as babelstone-t7o3.4 did for the constitution debit. Keep ADR-IC-003 section P6 in force: the renewal/maturity sagas must NOT add compensation — the payout already moved, a failure parks in HUMAN_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED. The money-OUT vs money-IN settlement shape should converge with the asset-side decision in babelstone-5r9n.2 so deposits and loans share ONE parameterised confirmation-gated settlement concept, not per-operation forks. Real ACL is DEF-1 (babelstone-ub9s); WireMock-gated legs can land now.

Early-termination is delivered by a child issue (it also needs a missing HTTP entry point). Maturity (incl. the policy=NONE path that starts no saga today), coupon, and the renewal rollover/credits are covered by the acceptance criteria here.

Anchors: ADR-PC-016 sections 74/127/128, ADR-PC-029 section 60, ADR-IC-003 sections P5/P6; sibling of babelstone-t7o3.4; related to the settlement-shape decision babelstone-5r9n.2.

Source: surfaced by the 2026-06-21 term-deposit feature-completeness audit (the "missing sagas" review).
acceptance_criteria:
- Maturity (incl. the policy=NONE path that starts no saga today), coupon (PayInterest), early-termination, and the renewal rollover/credits emit Originated Movements; the eager settlement.SettleAsync calls are removed.
- Cash legs effected via the substrate settlement saga (t7o3.15); renewal as a multi-Movement event (rollover Debit + interest Credit) in per-account FIFO order.
- Credits are confirmation-gated (not funds-gated) with the indeterminate-clearance path covered (ADR-PC-016 slot 5); no silent drop.
- Append-first finality: the engine fact is final on append; the credit is a downstream gated consequence that parks in HUMAN_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED on failure, NO compensation (ADR-IC-003 §P6). The remaining-eager-settle drift notes in ADR-PC-016 §128 / ADR-PC-029 §60 are updated to point at this issue.
- WireMock-stubbed Core ACL at v1 (real ACL DEF-1, babelstone-ub9s); GatedSettlement integration tests cover each relocated leg.
- Early-termination's leg (endpoint + settlement) delivered by its child issue.
notes: RE-SCOPED 2026-06-23 per ADR-PC-032 (the Movement primitive) + feature-design-money-movement-settlement.md §6/§9. The 4 deposit legs migrate onto the SAME substrate settlement saga as the loan legs — this IS the 'one parameterised confirmation-gated settlement concept' this issue asked to converge on (decided by ADR-PC-032, formerly tracked as 5r9n.2). FINALITY re-worded: 'fact not final until confirmed' → the fact is final append-first and the cash leg is a gated consequence that parks on failure (design §6). Now depends on the platform t7o3.15.
close_reason: Merged to origin/main in PR #353 (rebase-merged: 7afae3f t7o3.16 / 3ca8912 t7o3.13 / a481167 t7o3.13.1). Loan installment+early-repay and term_deposit lifecycle credits relocated onto the ADR-PC-032 Movement + gated substrate settlement saga; POST /v1/deposits/{id}/terminate added. CI all-green; central adr-conformance review PASS (no ADR contradiction).

title: Resolve the FinancialMath cohesion policy: RateSchedule.cs is deposit-shaped in a family-agnostic kernel
description: Plain English: the shared math library is meant to name no product, but it already contains a large term-deposit-shaped rate resolver, while the new loan math is the well-behaved tenant. Decide the policy: accept shared financial primitives with product vocabulary allowed in doc-comments and say so, OR hold the kernel to literal family-agnosticism and relocate deposit rate-resolution into the term-deposit family. The mechanical ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC gate checks project references only and is blind to in-file product vocabulary. Evidence: RateSchedule.cs 7-54 deposit vocabulary; Amortization.cs generic; EngineFamilyAgnosticTests.
acceptance_criteria:
- A recorded decision (kernel README note or ADR) states whether product vocabulary is permitted in FinancialMath, with the rule the next family author follows.
- If literal agnosticism is chosen, deposit rate-resolution is relocated or a tracked plan exists.
- The decision notes why the mechanical gate cannot enforce this.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide and record the asset-side settlement end-state: disbursement engine-eager vs saga-gated
description: Plain English: the deposit was deliberately moved so a saga moves the money after the engine records the decision; the loan instead fires the cash-out inline at disbursement, with no until-its-saga-lands framing the deposit eager steps carry. Decide and record whether asset disbursement is permanently engine-eager or should become saga-gated like deposit constitution (ADR-PC-029), and capture the asset-direction (money OUT) cash-flow shape as a first-class saga concept so a third family has a canonical target rather than discovering a fork. Consolidates saga eager-contradicts-de-settled + divergent-saga-wiring/fork-risk. Evidence: CreditoPessoalConstitutionService DisburseAsync step 4; ADR-PC-031:157; ADR-PC-029 slot 2.
acceptance_criteria:
- ADR-PC-031 (or ADR-PC-029) records an explicit decision: disbursement is deliberately engine-eager OR to be saga-gated, with the failure-mode rationale.
- If saga-gated, the money-OUT cash-flow shape is modelled so deposit and loan share one parameterised constitution-settlement concept, not two forks.
- DisburseAsync is annotated to match the decision.
notes: RESOLVED-BY ADR-PC-032 (the Movement money-movement primitive, Proposed 2026-06-23) + feature-design-money-movement-settlement.md. The decision: disbursement (and every cash leg) is an append-first Originated Movement effected by ONE substrate settlement saga — neither permanently engine-eager nor a per-operation saga fork, but one parameterised concept. CLOSE this issue when the ADR-PC-032 PR merges AND the ADR is Accepted (the ADR is currently Proposed).
close_reason: Closed

title: [EPIC] personal_loan second-family architecture tensions — PR #283 review deep-dive
description:
Plain English: PR #283 added the engine's second product family (personal_loan, a closed-end personal loan). A multi-agent review of that PR surfaced a set of architectural tensions that a second, asset-shaped family raised against a spine previously shaped by a single liability (term_deposit). This epic tracks a deep dive on each confirmed tension so none is left as a silent omission — each is resolved as a code/contract change, an explicit recorded decision, or a deliberate accept-as-is with written rationale.

Provenance: the findings come from the PR-#283 review (5 concern-maps + 17 adversarially-verified tensions + 4 refuted non-tensions). The host-integration gap the review also found is tracked separately as babelstone-9g77 (delivery, not a tension).

## Success Criteria

- Every confirmed tension from the PR-#283 review is resolved as a code/contract change, an explicit recorded decision (ADR amendment/note), or a deliberate accept-as-is with written rationale.
- The HIGH-severity disbursement-atomicity finding (C1) is closed with either a fix or a documented residual-risk plus an orphaned-debit recovery procedure in ADR-PC-031.
- No finding is left a silent omission.
- All child issues are closed.

## Refuted non-tensions (recorded for completeness; no work)

- Collection-bearing amortization_schedule projection default equality — verified clean (projection replay-safety is source_sequence idempotency, not state equality).
- Namespace / subject / internal-vs-published split scaling — verified clean (the loans/ namespace makes cross-family collisions structurally impossible).
- TAN/m proportional-rate conversion re-implemented in the decider — refuted (no reusable Rates primitive existed; the int truncation is contract-driven for replay).
- FinancialMath has no named owner — refuted (CODEOWNERS resolves /engine/ by prefix, same owner as /families/).

## Baseline that holds (keep doing this)

Repo/solution structure scales cleanly to N families: adding the family was purely additive (two project files + two solution entries, zero spine edits), the one-way family->engine arrow held, and the per-family triangle (pure-fold + .Application + tests) is the template to preserve.
close_reason: All 16 children closed — personal_loan second-family architecture tensions from the PR #283 deep-dive fully worked off

title: Wire credito_pessoal into the running engine host (IFamilyHostModule + endpoints + host ProjectReference + pack pin)
description:
Plain English: PR #283 delivered the credito_pessoal domain core (pure folds, decider, amortization math, contracts, ADR-PC-031, tests) but did NOT wire the family into the running engine host. Today a loan cannot be disbursed / paid / repaid end-to-end — the family is reachable only from its own test projects, not from the running Engine.Api. This issue adds the host-side integration so credito_pessoal is operable in the running engine, mirroring the term_deposit host wiring.

Verified gap (origin/feat/credito-pessoal-family): `engine/src/Babelstone.Engine.Api/Babelstone.Engine.Api.csproj` ProjectReferences only term-deposit; credito_pessoal ships NO `IFamilyHostModule`, NO HTTP endpoints, and is NOT pinned in any pack family-manifest. `HostModuleLoader.FamilyHostAssemblies` discovers families by probing `Babelstone.Families.*.dll` in the host OUTPUT directory, and that DLL lands there only via a host `ProjectReference` — so the running host will not discover the family. term_deposit ships `TermDepositHostModule.cs` + `DepositsEndpoints.cs` + the `Engine.Api` ProjectReference; credito_pessoal ships none of these. ADR-PC-031 §P5 names "the host `ProjectReference` (the scan anchor)" as part of authoring a family; this completes that step.

Scope: the operability/wiring layer only. The disbursement-settlement end-state (eager-in-engine vs saga-gated) is a separate architectural decision tracked in the PR-#283 review epic and is explicitly NOT resolved here.

ADRs touched/honoured: honours ADR-PC-031 §P5, ADR-PC-021 §A3/§A13–A19 (assembly-scan host composition), ADR-PC-009 §P1 (pack family-manifest pin / fail-closed cross-check), ADR-PC-016 (settlement port). No ADR amended.
acceptance_criteria:
- An IFamilyHostModule for credito_pessoal constructs its AggregateRuntime<LoanPosition> and registers DI, mirroring TermDepositHostModule; discovered by HostModuleLoader with no per-family hand-edit beyond the ProjectReference.
- Babelstone.Engine.Api.csproj gains a ProjectReference to both Babelstone.Families.CreditoPessoal and .Application (the assembly-scan load anchor), so the family DLLs land in the host output dir.
- HTTP endpoints for disburse / pay-installment / repay-early / write-off / erase, mirroring DepositsEndpoints.
- credito_pessoal@2026.1 is declared in the pinned pack family-manifest (families.yaml) so HostModuleLoader.CrossCheckAgainstPackManifest passes fail-closed.
- A family-owned read-model + migration set is added if the loan needs a Postgres read model (mirroring read_model.deposits), OR it is explicitly recorded that the bitemporal projections suffice.
- End-to-end proof: an integration test (or demo slice) boots the host and disburses -> pays -> settles a loan; ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC and ENGINE_API_HOST_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC stay green.
notes: UPDATED 2026-06-23 per ADR-PC-032: the disbursement-settlement end-state (formerly 'a separate decision, NOT resolved here') is now decided — disbursement is an Originated Movement. Wire the loan Movement-shaped: the disburse endpoint uses the de-settled DisburseAsync from 5r9n.1. Now depends on the platform t7o3.15 and the disbursement impl 5r9n.1, so the loan never lands eager.
close_reason: Closed

title: acl/Dockerfile: name the explicit .csproj + join the image-build.yml matrix when acl source lands
description:
Plain English: the acl service still has a placeholder Dockerfile that says 'build the .NET project here' without naming which project, and acl/ has no source code yet. The moment acl source lands and acl joins the image build/scan workflow, the build will fail (a bare dotnet restore/publish with no project arg is ambiguous — no root .sln/.slnx, ~35 .csproj repo-wide). Fix the Dockerfile in the SAME change that adds acl source.

Detail: the acl HALF of the now-closed bd babelstone-dq8q. The notification half shipped in PR #281 (notification/Dockerfile names its .csproj + joined the image-build.yml matrix). acl/Dockerfile still runs 'dotnet restore' then 'dotnet publish -c Release -o /app --no-restore' with NO project argument, and image-build.yml (ADR-IC-013) intentionally excludes acl ('stub with no source… joins the matrix when its .NET source lands'). Copy the engine/orchestrator/notification pattern: name the explicit .csproj on BOTH restore and publish, set the repo-root build context, and add the matrix entry + ENTRYPOINT in the same change. Triggered by acl source landing under this DEF-1 epic. Refs: ADR-IC-011, ADR-IC-012, ADR-IC-013, .github/workflows/image-build.yml; origin bd babelstone-dq8q (closed).

Acceptance criteria:
- acl/Dockerfile names the explicit .csproj on BOTH dotnet restore and dotnet publish, with the engine/orchestrator/notification build-context pattern and an ENTRYPOINT set.
- The image-build.yml matrix (ADR-IC-013) gains the acl entry in the same change.
- The acl image-build leg succeeds.

title: Relocate notification read off the engine kernel onto the ADR-PC-027 read contract + add NOTIFICATION_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC gate
description:
Plain English: the notification worker skeleton (bd babelstone-60n8.1 / PR #281) reads term-deposit projections by compile-referencing the engine kernel (Babelstone.Engine + Babelstone.EventStore) and the term-deposit family, hand-deserializing the family's internal projection state types. ADR-IC-019 (Accepted) makes the notification service a family-agnostic core that must NOT do that. This task makes the code conform and gates it.

Scope:
- Replace TermDepositProjectionReader's IProjectionStorage/BitemporalProjectionQuery/JsonStateSerializer binding with a client over the storage-opaque ADR-PC-027 read surface (GET /v1/deposits/...); extend that resource additively (ADR-PC-027 slot 6) if the scheduler needs per-entry maturity/accrual/withholding detail the flat DepositResponse does not expose today.
- Drop the Babelstone.Engine, Babelstone.EventStore, and Babelstone.Families.TermDeposit ProjectReferences from the notification core (move any genuinely family-specific content/scheduling into a family-owned contribution composed at the host edge, if needed).
- Add the NOTIFICATION_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC fitness test (parses the notification core .csproj like EngineFamilyAgnosticTests / OrchestratorFamilyAgnosticTests), flip catalogue row NOTIF-1 from Planned to Live.

Acceptance criteria:
- The notification core carries no ProjectReference to any families/** project nor to an engine-spine project; host composition root is the standing ADR-PC-021 §A2 exemption.
- NOTIFICATION_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC runs in CI and is green; NOTIF-1 catalogue status = Live.
- Behavior-preserving: the service reads the same maturity/accrual/withholding facts, now over the read contract.

Governing: ADR-IC-019 §D2/§D3/§P2/§P3. Blocks/relates: PR #281 (babelstone-60n8.1) should land conforming to this, or be reworked by it.
close_reason: Delivered by PR #281 (merged): read relocated off the engine kernel + term-deposit family onto the storage-opaque ADR-PC-027 HTTP contract (DepositReadClient → GET /v1/deposits/{id}); NOTIFICATION_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC gate live (catalogue NOTIF-1), conforming to ADR-IC-019.

title: Author credito_pessoal family (closed-end amortizing loan)
description:
Plain English: build the personal-loan product family — the 'next' family on the ADR-PC-030 roadmap and the lowest-risk one, because it mirrors the term deposit (closed-end, deterministic schedule). It proves the family abstraction generalises from a liability to an asset before the heavier revolving/transactional shapes land.

Scope (ADR-PC-030 §Open Action 2): a family ADR (ADR-PC-021 shape) + the family build — event records, pure fold handlers, lifecycle legality table, projections, IFamilyModule wiring. Origination stays upstream (ADR-PC-024). Supported by research/credito-pessoal/. Follows scope decision babelstone-nyan (ADR-PC-030).

title: L.3g — Testcontainers integration coverage for the load-harness runner host
description:
Plain English: the load-harness runner's live-stack code (the in-process engine rig that drives a real PostgreSQL event store, and the drive/measure loop that orchestrates it) has no automated test today — it's verified by hand against a live stack and re-run by 'make load-test'. Because the Docker-free unit lane structurally can't reach it, those members are marked [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] (with justifications) so they don't drag the engine branch-coverage floor. This issue tracks replacing that exclusion with real Testcontainers integration coverage.

Add a [Category("Integration")] test suite for Babelstone.LoadHarness.Runner (EngineProjectionRig + LoadRunner) using the same Testcontainers machinery as Babelstone.LoadHarness.Tests (PostgreSQL; Redpanda + Schema Registry for the bus path), then remove the [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] attributes added in PR #261 (the EngineProjectionRig class and the LoadRunner live members) so those branches are measured rather than excluded.
acceptance_criteria: A Category=Integration test drives EngineProjectionRig.AppendWithSpanAsync / DrainAsync / TimeColdReplayAsync / RunNoDivergenceDrillAsync and LoadRunner.RunAsync against a Testcontainers PostgreSQL (and Redpanda+SR for the bus path); the [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] attributes on EngineProjectionRig and LoadRunner's live members are removed; the engine coverage floor (line ≥85%, branch ≥75%) still passes with those branches now measured.
close_reason: Implemented by PR #267 (open, awaiting maintainer merge): Testcontainers [Category(Integration)] suite for Babelstone.LoadHarness.Runner (EngineProjectionRig + LoadRunner) driving AppendWithSpanAsync/DrainAsync/TimeColdReplayAsync/RunNoDivergenceDrillAsync + LoadRunner.RunAsync against real Docker Postgres (+Redpanda/SR for the bus path); [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] removed from EngineProjectionRig + LoadRunner live members; engine coverage floor still passes (line ≥85% / branch ≥75%). CI FULLY GREEN after a fix: the initial cut had LoadRunner integration tests falling back to a hardcoded 127.0.0.1:5432 (passed locally only via an ambient Postgres, failed in CI 'connection refused') — fixed by threading the fixture's Testcontainers-mapped connection string into LoadRunner (commit a386a26d). Branch rebased onto merged main so the PR diff shows only the integration-test additions. engine job 7m6s pass.

title: C.7 follow-up — implement PackVersionMigrated operator migration write-path (ADR-PC-009 §P3)
description:
A live deposit is locked to the regulatory pack it was opened under, and the only sanctioned way to move it to a newer pack is an explicit, audited operator migration. The DESIGN for that migration — the `PackVersionMigrated` event plus the operator command that emits it — is fully specified and Accepted, but none of it is BUILT: a repo-wide search finds zero implementation (no C# event record, no Avro `.avsc`, no EventCatalog entry, no API endpoint). This issue tracks building that write path so the "pinned for life, except by explicit migration" guarantee is executable, not just documented.

Context: C.7 (babelstone-c8d8) named the "PackVersionMigrated / SchemaVersionMigrated path" in its scope but closed (PR #200) having delivered only pin-at-constitution + per-event pins on replay. The READ/resolve half (every event carries `pack_version`; `pack_versions` registry resolves version→OCI digest) exists; the WRITE half (re-pin) does not.

Designed shape (ADR-PC-009 §P3, 02 §2.4.2, feature-design-configuration-surface §3.6):
  PackVersionMigrated { instance_id, from_pack_version, to_pack_version, migration_id, operator_actor }
operator-initiated, one event per affected instance, pin changes from that sequence forward.

Sibling: `SchemaVersionMigrated` is the identical-shape engine-evolution analogue, also unbuilt; the five shared operational events (PackVersionMigrated, SchemaVersionMigrated, LegacyInstanceObserved, FundsHeld, AccountFrozen) in feature-design-event-store-projections.md are all currently undefined in code. SchemaVersionMigrated is out of scope here but should follow the same pattern.
acceptance_criteria:
- `PackVersionMigrated` event record exists in the shared/engine operational-event catalogue with payload { instance_id, from_pack_version, to_pack_version, migration_id, operator_actor } (ADR-PC-009 §P3; 02 §2.4.2).
- Governed Avro `.avsc` authored and registered in the EventCatalog/AsyncAPI; the BACKWARD schema-registry compatibility check passes (ADR-IC-002).
- Operator command + `POST /v1/pack-migrations` endpoint (ADR-PC-009 §3.6 / surface §3.6): accepts an instance filter, the matched set is previewable before emission, emits exactly one `PackVersionMigrated` per matched instance, records operator_actor + migration_id.
- Replay resolves the pin from the migration sequence forward (events < M old pack, ≥ M new); a fixture proves the pre/post-migration boundary replays to identical state.
- Adoption (`POST /v1/pack-adoptions`, §P4) stays distinct from migration — no silent upgrades.
- docs/product-docs explanation page callout (PR #254) updated to drop the "not yet built" note once this lands.
notes: Filed from investigation of PR #254 (docs/pack-lifecycle-diataxis): the explanation page presents PackVersionMigrated in present tense as the working escape hatch, but it is unimplemented. A scoped "planned, not yet built in v1" callout is being added to that page citing this issue.
close_reason: Merged to main (post-merge cleanup of PRs #258–#277)

title: Plugin hooks loaded twice: drop the redundant manifest.hooks reference in plugin.json
description: Plain English: after bd-93yq made hooks.json schema-valid, Claude Code auto-loads it from the standard hooks/hooks.json location — but plugin.json ALSO references it via 'hooks': './hooks/hooks.json', so it loads twice and /doctor reports 'Duplicate hooks file detected'. Every other installed plugin omits the hooks field and relies on auto-load. Fix: remove the 'hooks' line from plugins/babelstone-engine/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (manifest.hooks should only reference ADDITIONAL hook files, not the standard one). The §P1 hooks already load via auto-load (17 hooks confirmed); this only clears the duplicate error. Follow-up to bd babelstone-93yq.
notes: Fixed in PR #259 (fix/plugin-hooks-dedup): removed the redundant manifest.hooks reference. Close on merge.
close_reason: Merged to main (post-merge cleanup of PRs #258–#277)

title: Add product-owner capability catalogue: catalogue/ quadrant + term-deposit menu
description:
Plain English: A product owner who defines term-deposit offerings has no single readable page telling them what the family can provide in business terms — the answer is scattered across the generated CUE schema, §2 of the v1-scope doc, and the financial-math reference, none of which is written for them. This adds a new 'catalogue' quadrant under docs/product-docs/ with a readable, decision-by-decision menu of what a term deposit can be (current reality only).

Scope:
- New docs/product-docs/catalogue/README.md establishing the catalogue as a distinct information type alongside the four Diataxis quadrants (audience: the config-author/product-owner persona named in product-docs/README.md).
- New docs/product-docs/catalogue/term-deposit.md: one section per business decision — interest timing, rate shape, auto-renewal, early-exit penalty, partial withdrawals, eligibility gates, amount/timing limits — plus a 'fixed givens' box (28% withholding, Act/360, EUR, integer cents).
- Organised by decision, not schema field; follows the corpus 'link-don't-restate' rule, citing the generated family-schema (reference/family-schemas/term-deposit.md), 02-v1-scope §2, financial_concepts §5, and ADR-PC-024 for the precise truth. A small amount of drift is accepted in exchange for readability (deliberate, per product-owner request).
- Link the new quadrant from product-docs/README.md.

Out of scope: v2+ roadmap items (moratoria etc.); engine/event/ACL mechanics; any edit to the generated reference.

ADRs honoured: ADR-PC-022 (product documentation architecture / link-don't-restate); ADR-PC-024 (preconditions) and ADR-PC-006/007/008 cited as sources, not modified.
notes: Drafted on branch docs/term-deposit-catalogue; PR #258 open (https://github.com/jhosm/babelstone/pull/258). doc-consistency review PASS. Awaiting maintainer merge.
close_reason: Merged to main (post-merge cleanup of PRs #258–#277)

title: Hand-authored ADR index drifts from ADR-PC-029's Accepted status
description:
In plain English: the hand-maintained ADR index table summarises ADR-PC-029 as "Proposed" with its commitments "Planned", but the ADR is actually Accepted and one of its two commitments is already Live. The summary copy simply fell out of sync — ADR-PC-029's own Status field and the generated adr-index both say Accepted. This is cosmetic-but-misleading drift in convenience copy that no CI gate watches.

Technical scope — docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/README.md, the ADR-PC-029 row only:
- Status prefix `**Proposed.**` → `**Accepted.**` (matches ADR-PC-029 `| Status | Accepted |` and docs/product-docs/reference/adr-index/README.md, which already render Accepted).
- Commitment annotation `ENGINE_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENT + ENGINE_COMMAND_PACT Planned.` should split per commitment-catalogue.md: row 19 ENGINE_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENT is **Live**; row 20 ENGINE_COMMAND_PACT stays **Planned** by design (the Pact-style CDC ships, only the formal PactNet broker round-trip is deferred).
- No generated-file or docs-verify impact; the hand-authored README is convenience copy outside the generated reference/ gate.

Discovered while accepting ADR-PC-026/027/028 (branch docs/accept-adr-pc-026-027-028); deliberately kept out of that PR to keep it scoped to the three ADRs it accepts.
acceptance_criteria: README.md ADR-PC-029 row reads '**Accepted.**'; commitment annotation reflects IDEMPOTENT=Live, PACT=Planned; no other rows touched; git grep confirms no remaining 'Proposed' summary for an Accepted ADR.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #253 (commit 72f7e6a): hand-authored ADR index row corrected to Accepted; IDEMPOTENT=Live/PACT=Planned.

title: Link the demo pages from the DocFX navbar + fix the home page's broken corpus links
description:
In plain English: the DocFX docs site now links to the two demo pages (deck + principles) from its navbar, and the home page (the product-docs README) no longer shows broken links. The README's relative links used to 404 on the site because the corpus they point to isn't published there; we now render docfx/index.md from the README with those links rewritten to absolute main GitHub URLs.

Technical: (1) docfx/toc.yml gains two absolute-URL navbar entries to the /demo/ pages (staged post-build, so relative hrefs can't be used). (2) scripts/docs-gen/generate.py (the ADR-PC-022 generator) now also emits docfx/index.md from docs/product-docs/README.md, absolutising corpus-relative links to .../blob|tree/main/...; the file is byte-drift-gated by make docs-verify + the pre-commit hook, same as reference/. ADR-PC-026 (Proposed) §P3 got a dated Revised 2026-06-20 line. Follow-up to babelstone-q096.

title: F.12 depth-5 sealed-corpus leg: withdraw → then mature (lock the re-base at simulation level)
description:
Plain English: the engine fix (bd babelstone-emtr) that re-bases interest/maturity on the principal actually held after a partial withdrawal is locked by decider-level + fold-level + API integration tests. The sealed depth-5 corpus, however, drives the partial-withdrawal variant only as far as the withdrawal (it is state-preserving and stops Active). This adds the simulation-level regression: a constitute → partial-withdraw → mature lifecycle that asserts the matured payout returns the REDUCED principal plus the piecewise interest.

Needs: a new SimulatedLifecycle (e.g. PartialWithdrawalThenMature) + VariantShape mapping + a canonical-instances.yaml instance + the expected-event-sequence + terminal assertions in PackSimulationDepth5Tests. Keep the existing state-preserving PartialWithdrawal leg as-is (it proves F.3 state-preservation). Budget must stay under PACK_SIM_DEPTH5_BUDGET (30s).

Deferred from babelstone-emtr because the corpus-lifecycle plumbing is disproportionate to the already-comprehensive decider/fold/API coverage; behaviour is not at risk, this is defense-in-depth at the sealed-corpus layer.
notes: Work complete; implemented in PR #260 (open, awaiting maintainer merge) — Tier-1 parallel build 2026-06-20.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #260 (2026-06-20): depth-5 withdraw→mature re-base simulation regression (reduced principal + piecewise net, <30s budget).

title: L.6 — Discard-rebuild drill on populated snapshots + §P6 operations
description:
Plain English: with snapshots now written in the running engine, the monthly rebuild drill (bd j67l) becomes the real correctness exercise ADR-PC-003 §8.3/§P4 intends — discard all snapshots, rebuild cold, and prove byte-identity. Today the drill runs with snapshots off, so it only proves cold-fold. This wires the drill against populated snapshots and adds the operational surface §P6 requires.

Honours ADR-PC-003 §P4 (hash-verify, advisory-until-six-months trusted promotion) and §P6 (runbook). Adds: snapshot-lag metric + alarm, hash-mismatch recovery path, and the advisory→trusted promotion mechanism/runbook. Cross-links bd j67l (the existing monthly drill automation) and bd 2e6q.4.
acceptance_criteria: Monthly drill discards populated snapshots, rebuilds cold, and asserts byte-identity; snapshot-lag alarm and hash-mismatch recovery documented in infra/runbooks; trusted-flag promotion path exists and is exercised.
close_reason: Merged to main (post-merge cleanup of PRs #258–#277)

title: L.5 — Snapshot-accelerated replay budget in the load harness
description:
Plain English: once snapshots are generated for real, prove they actually help and never lie. After a load run, measure cold replay vs snapshot-accelerated replay over the same populated event store, and confirm the snapshot-accelerated state is byte-identical to the cold-fold state (no divergence).

Extends the existing cold-replay/rebuild budget gate (bd 2e6q.4) with a snapshot-accelerated measurement. Folds a snapshot-vs-cold parity verdict + the speedup into RunArtefact. Honours ADR-PC-003 §P3 (snapshots accelerate, never gate correctness) and the §8.2 30s v4 budget.
acceptance_criteria: Run --measure replay after a load run reports BOTH cold and snapshot-accelerated rebuild times AND asserts identical state; snapshot-accelerated path is within the 5s/30s budgets and demonstrably faster than cold on a deep stream.
close_reason: Merged to main (post-merge cleanup of PRs #258–#277)

title: F.12: re-base interest/maturity on remaining principal + forbid partial withdrawal on ADVANCE
description:
Plain English: today a partial withdrawal only reduces the 'remaining principal' field, but interest accrual and the maturity payout still use the ORIGINAL principal — so after a withdrawal the engine over-pays future interest and, at maturity, returns the full original principal (double-paying the withdrawn part). This fixes that by accruing/maturing on the principal actually held over time (exact, piecewise across each withdrawal), and forbids partial withdrawal on ADVANCE (juros antecipados) products where interest is pre-paid up front and cannot be re-based.

Scope (lands on PR #243, feat/f12-partial-withdrawal-wiring):
- FinancialMath: PrincipalSegment + AccrueGrossWindowOverPrincipal (un-rounded sum across principal-time-segments, round once; single-segment == today byte-for-byte).
- DepositPosition: folded PrincipalTimeline (DepositConstituted seeds, DepositPartiallyWithdrawn appends) — no event/Avro change.
- TermDepositDecider: coupon + maturity accrual over the timeline; maturity returns RemainingPrincipal; PartialWithdrawalDecider rejects InterestVariant==ADVANCE.
- pack-validate depth-4: reject partial_withdrawal + interest_variant: ADVANCE.
- Tests: FinancialMath piecewise; ADVANCE-reject; depth-5 corpus withdraw->mature regression (the path that currently hides the over-return).
- product-configs: PERIODIC + partial variant (orthogonality); docs note in 02 §2.4.1.

Discovered while adding an orthogonality variant for #243; the depth-5 sim stops at the withdrawal so the over-return was latent/untested.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #243 (merged 2026-06-20) — F.12 partial-withdrawal wiring chain (schema→config→variant→command path→sealed corpus + interest re-base).

title: A.13 — As-of replay honors snapshots
description:
Plain English: point-in-time (as-of) reads currently rebuild from event zero every time, ignoring snapshots. Make as-of replay start from the newest snapshot that is not in the future of the as-of point, then fold only the tail up to that point.

Honours ADR-PC-003 §P3 + ADR-PC-002 (bitemporal). LoadAsOfSequenceAsync (engine/src/Babelstone.Engine/AggregateRuntime.cs:142) must pick the snapshot with AtSequence <= asOfSequence and fold the tail to asOfSequence — closes the TODO comment at lines 145-149.
acceptance_criteria: LoadAsOfSequenceAsync uses a snapshot when one exists at or below the as-of sequence and matches cold-fold-to-as-of byte-for-byte; property test covers split points including asOf < earliest snapshot (cold path).
close_reason: Implemented by PR #268 (open, awaiting maintainer merge): as-of replay honors snapshots (ADR-PC-003 §P3 + ADR-PC-002). LoadAsOfSequenceAsync seeds from TryGetAtOrBeforeAsync (newest hash-verified snapshot ≤ asOfSequence) and folds only the tail, with a cold-fold fallback below the earliest snapshot; byte-for-byte match vs cold fold. Covered by AsOfSnapshotReplayTests incl. the asOf < earliest-snapshot cold path. CI all-green; recovered from a 529-killed implementation agent — work was committed from the worktree + rebased, no code fixes needed.

title: A.12 — Configure the composing snapshot policy (per-N / lifecycle / calendar)
description:
Plain English: decide WHEN a snapshot gets taken. ADR-PC-003 §P2 composes three triggers — every N events, at lifecycle boundaries, and at calendar boundaries — taking a snapshot if any fires. CountBasedSnapshotPolicy exists; this wires the boundary triggers and the per-family configuration so the policy is actually driven in the running engine.

Honours ADR-PC-003 §P2. Feed SnapshotContext (EventsSinceSnapshot, IsLifecycleBoundary, IsCalendarBoundary) from the runtime; configure thresholds per family/host. Pairs with A.11 (which calls the policy).
acceptance_criteria: All three triggers fire in the running engine and are covered by a test each; per-family threshold config is honoured; snapshot writes are eventually-consistent (a failed write does not fail the append).
close_reason: Implemented by PR #268 (open, awaiting maintainer merge): composing snapshot policy (ADR-PC-003 §P2) — count + lifecycle + calendar triggers fire if ANY matches, per-family thresholds, SnapshotContext fed from the runtime. Calendar boundary derived from the event-stamped transaction_time (NOT a fresh clock read — handler/fold purity preserved); snapshot write is post-commit + fail-soft (TrySnapshotAsync swallows to onSnapshotError, a failed write never fails the append). Covered by SnapshotPolicyCompositionTests. CI all-green (engine test job: 76 engine + 104 EventStore tests, 86 integration vs Docker Postgres).

title: A.11 — Wire snapshot generation into the live runtime/host
description:
Plain English: the snapshot machinery is built and unit-tested, but the running engine never turns it on — AggregateRuntime is constructed with snapshots = null, so no snapshot is ever written and every rehydrate is a cold fold from event zero. This flips snapshots ON for v1: inject the policy + store into the live runtime and write a snapshot after a successful append when the policy says so.

Honours ADR-PC-003 (Accepted), which calls v1 snapshots non-negotiable and requires v1 to build AND continuously exercise them — so this resolves the current 'snapshots off' posture toward the ADR. Inject ISnapshotPolicy + SnapshotStore<TState> into AggregateRuntime/the family host (today the ctor param defaults to null at engine/src/Babelstone.Engine/AggregateRuntime.cs); in the post-commit path evaluate the policy and call SnapshotStore.PutAsync. LoadAsync already does snapshot-then-tail — this is the missing write side.
acceptance_criteria: Running engine writes snapshots per the configured policy after append; LoadAsync rehydrates snapshot-then-tail (not cold) when a snapshot exists; existing SnapshotEquivalenceProperties still passes (snapshot-then-tail ≡ cold fold).
notes: Work complete; implemented in PR #256 (open, awaiting maintainer merge) — Tier-1 parallel build 2026-06-20.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #256 (2026-06-20): snapshot generation wired into AggregateRuntime + term-deposit host (per-N policy, fail-soft write, snapshot-equivalence test). Unblocks e6fr.12/.13/.14 + 0uau.1/.2.

title: Add a YAML-native rate-sheet deploy tool + wire the demo to deploy from the committed source
description:
Plain English: a rate sheet's source of truth is now a committed YAML file under /rate-sheets/ (the treasury-owned config-as-code artefact, sibling of product-configs/). But the deploy endpoint POST /v1/rate-sheets only accepts JSON, and nothing yet reads the YAML and deploys it — the demo scripts still deploy an equivalent inline JSON heredoc. So today the YAML→deploy bridge is a manual 'yq -o=json | curl' step. This issue closes that loop.

Scope:
- A small deploy tool (or make target) that reads a /rate-sheets/<family>/<version>.yaml source and POSTs it to /v1/rate-sheets (serialise YAML→JSON, attach X-Deploy-Actor), so authoring is pure-YAML end to end.
- Wire scripts/demo-mcp.sh and scripts/demo-saga.sh to deploy FROM rate-sheets/term_deposit/pt-deposits-2026.1.yaml instead of an inline JSON heredoc, so the committed YAML is the single source and cannot drift from what the demo deploys.
- Optional: path-scoped CI to validate rate-sheet YAML shape on PRs touching /rate-sheets/ (the README already promises 'rate-sheet schema validation').

Context: surfaced while reframing docs/product-docs/how-to/author-and-deploy-a-rate-sheet.md to the YAML-source model (PR #240) and seeding the first committed rate-sheet YAML. ADR-PC-008 §P1/§P2 (the stored JSONB body is '1:1 with the deployed YAML').
close_reason: Implemented by PR #264 (open, awaiting maintainer merge): YAML-native rate-sheet deploy. scripts/deploy-rate-sheet.sh + 'make deploy-rate-sheet SHEET=…' reads rate-sheets/<family>/<version>.yaml, serialises YAML→JSON 1:1 via pinned js-yaml (npx, the repo's pinned-Node path — not unpinned yq), POSTs to /v1/rate-sheets with X-Deploy-Actor, reports the ADR-PC-008 §P2 status contract. demo-mcp.sh, demo-saga.sh AND demo-all.sh now deploy from rate-sheets/term_deposit/pt-deposits-2026.1.yaml (single source, no heredoc drift); demo-mcp's 409 probe stays divergent on purpose. BONUS (optional item delivered): scripts/rate-sheet-check.sh + rate-sheet-check.mjs replace the no-op 'rate-sheets' CI job (whose glob couldn't even reach the 2-level-deep file) with a real shape gate re-expressing RateSheetValidator — the README's long-promised rate-sheet schema validation. CI green incl. the new rate-sheets gate. ADR-PC-008 §P1/§P2 honoured (CI mirrors the pack-resolved 2000bps ceiling, not §P1's illustrative ≤5000). Verified statically (shellcheck/node --check/6 malformed-sheet rejections); live 201/200/409 needs the Docker stack (unchanged deploy body, byte-equivalent to prior heredoc).

title: Deepen principles.html into a teaching deck (educational ramp + opt-in deep-dives)
description:
Make the design-principles companion deck (docs/demo/principles.html) teach, not just prove. Today each of the five principles is a single slide that demonstrates a payoff to a viewer who already owns the concept. Many of its actual viewers don't have solid architectural concepts, so the payoff lands on empty ground.

Rework it into a 'spine + optional depth' deck. Each principle becomes a three-beat ramp on the main (left-right) track — (1) the naive way, shown failing; (2) the idea that fixes it, jargon expanded with a plain analogy; (3) the existing payoff animation — plus one opt-in deep-dive slide reachable by pressing the down-arrow, carrying the real signatures/ADR refs/tests for the technically curious.

Scope:
- 7 slides -> ~17 linear + 5 optional deep-dives. Title + closing kept.
- Animate all five new 'naive way' beat-1 slides (the strongest new-diagram opportunities: a calc giving two answers, an UPDATE erasing history, PII fanning across topics, etc.).
- Plain non-banking analogies allowed (recipe/chef, locked box, running total).
- Keep it a single self-contained principles.html (the deck's 'never breaks offline' design).
- Refactor the index-hardcoded animation triggers (if i===1 / i===2) to a data-anim attribute, since inserting slides shifts every index.
- Add a vertical nav axis: arrows walk the main track (skipping deep-dives), down enters a deep-dive, up/Esc returns; progress bar + counter track the main line only.
- Deep-dive content must be verified against the repo (real decide() signature, the family composition line + ADR-PC-021 §D4 + EngineFamilyAgnosticTests, ADR-PC-020 §D3/§P9 + the three enforcement layers, OpenBao/crypto-shredding envelope) — source wins, no paraphrase-from-memory.

ADRs honoured: PC-020 (explicit-drift), PC-021 (family-agnostic spine). No ADR changes expected (docs/demo asset, not engine/contract code).
notes: Built and verified; PR #245 open against main (branch docs/principles-teaching-deck). Deck reworked into spine + opt-in deep-dives, 17 main slides + 5 deep dives, all five 'naive way' beats animated, deep-dive facts verified against repo. Awaiting maintainer review/merge — leave open until merged.
close_reason: Closed

title: M.6 — Validate OpenBao transit at v4-scale key cardinality (millions of per-subject keys) or pick a sharding/datakey mitigation
description:
Plain English: crypto-shredding (ADR-PC-004) gives every customer their own OpenBao transit key (pii-<subjectId>) so 'erase me' = destroy that one key. A retail bank has millions of customers, so this is MILLIONS of named keys living in OpenBao — and nobody has validated OpenBao can carry that many. OpenBao's own transit docs neither bless nor bound one-key-per-end-user at high cardinality, and with Integrated Storage (Raft) the whole keyspace is memory-resident, so RAM footprint, snapshot size, unseal time, and replication/join time all scale with key count. We need to either load-test it at v4 scale or choose a mitigation before this is a production gate.

The crux (why we can't just use fewer keys): the standard high-cardinality answer is envelope encryption — a few KEKs + a per-record data key (DEK). That scales, but it BREAKS per-subject crypto-shredding, because destroying a shared KEK shreds everyone. Per-subject erasure needs the per-subject DEK to be the destroyable unit, which lands back at a destroyable per-subject key. So key count cannot be collapsed without redesigning how erasure targets one person.

Scope / options to evaluate:
1. Measure: stand up OpenBao with N=v4-scale subjects' worth of transit keys (millions), record steady-state memory, Raft snapshot size, unseal/join time, encrypt/decrypt/destroy p99, and replication lag. Derive an HA/DR sizing budget per key-count (feeds ADR-PC-005).
2. Mitigations if (1) is untenable: shard the transit keyspace across multiple mounts/clusters keyed by subject hash; OR per-subject DEKs stored as EDEK where the DEK is individually destroyable (a destroyable per-subject key store) — note the ADR-PC-004 §P2 datakey-envelope optimisation is framed as a LATENCY mitigation and still keeps a per-subject NAMED key as the shred root, so it does NOT reduce key count; OR accept per-subject named keys with a sized, load-tested HA/DR budget.
3. Decision + a residual-risk note appended to ADR-PC-004 (cardinality is currently unaddressed — the ADR covers per-read latency and the DR backup-retention horizon only) and, if a mitigation changes the key model, an amend/supersede per ADR-PC-020 §D3.

Context / why this is open: ADR-PC-004 is SILENT on key cardinality / OpenBao scale even though the running example is a banking system. The existing v1 acceptance gate (the Q-AK synthetic v4-scale load test) targets the PostgreSQL event-store topology, NOT the OpenBao keyspace. Relates to babelstone-84ww (L.2 — v4-scale workload) — the OpenBao key-cardinality test naturally rides alongside it — and to ADR-PC-005 (DR/RTO/RPO, the backup-retention horizon that already bounds 'true' erasure).

Acceptance: either a measured key-count budget + passing load test at v4 cardinality, OR a chosen-and-documented mitigation, with a residual-risk note (and any decision change) folded into ADR-PC-004 / ADR-PC-005.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #242 (test/load-harness-parity-cardinality). M.6 OpenBao transit key-cardinality: KeyCardinalityProbe seeding per-subject keys through IPiiKeyStore/OpenBaoTransitClient with a Testcontainers integration leg (400 keys, flat-latency + crypto-shred isolation). title: boundary-3 follow-up: energize SASL/SCRAM — resolve credentials from ISecretProvider into KafkaSaslOptions at the host
description:
Plain English: PR #229 (bd njt2.1) added all the SASL/SCRAM *plumbing* — the KafkaSaslOptions.ApplyTo() helper, the Sasl property on the relay/consumer options, the broker-side topic ACLs + apply-acls.sh — but it does NOT yet fetch the actual username/password and put them on those options. Program.cs still constructs OutboxRelayOptions (and the inbox options) with no Sasl, so KafkaSaslOptions.IsConfigured is false and SASL is OFF for every client. This issue connects the secret seam to the option so a deployment actually authenticates to Redpanda. njt2.1's scope NAMES the ISecretProvider resolution but its 'close on merge' comment would close it on a PR that defers exactly this — so without this issue the host-side wiring is untracked.

Scope / technical:
- In engine/src/Babelstone.Engine.Api/Program.cs, populate OutboxRelayOptions.Sasl (relay producer) and the InboxConsumerOptions equivalent (InboxPump consumer) by resolving the per-service SCRAM username + password through ISecretProvider at the composition root — OpenBaoKvSecretProvider when OpenBao:Enabled=true, ConfigurationSecretProvider otherwise — mirroring the ConnectionStrings:Engine pattern (ADR-PC-004 Amendment A1). Today the relay options are built with no Sasl (Program.cs ~L227), with the code comment 'When SASL credentials land later, THOSE will resolve through ISecretProvider.'
- Distinct username per client to match the grant matrix in infra/redpanda/topic-acls.yaml: svc-outbox-publisher (relay producer), svc-engine-deposits (Deposits API / inbox consumer). A compromised client must only reach its own topics.
- Preserve the OFF-when-unconfigured local-dev posture: no secret -> Username empty -> ApplyTo is a no-op -> plaintext loopback Redpanda unchanged (make up). SASL_SSL is the deployment default; SCRAM-SHA-256 baseline; PLAIN never offered.
- Honour ISecretProvider.RefreshAsync for credential rotation if the seam exposes it.
- Verify end-to-end against the broker ACLs (apply-acls.sh on an authenticated cluster): each identity reaches only its granted topics; an Integration-tier test is the natural home (PR #229 catalogued the broker-ACL leg as Planned).

ADRs: ADR-IC-016 plane ii §4-§6 (service identity + topic ACLs); ADR-PC-004 §A1/Amendment A1 (secret boundary — credential resolved at the composition root, never logged/spanned/on the bus). Catalogue Test ID KAFKA_SASL_TOPIC_ACL (seeded by njt2.1) is satisfied only once this lands.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #244 (feat/engine-host-sasl-and-hosting-relocation). boundary-3 SASL/SCRAM energized: HostSasl resolves the svc-outbox-publisher SCRAM password via ISecretProvider into OutboxRelayOptions.Sasl at the composition root (OFF-when-unconfigured preserved). KAFKA_SASL_TOPIC_ACL unit leg live; the broker-ACL leg legitimately stays catalogue-Planned (no authenticated CI cluster in scope).

title: Make product-docs the docs front door: DocFX home = product-docs/README.md, move generated reference/ under product-docs/
description:
**Plain English:** Today the published DocFX site lands on a thin "API reference only" page, and the generated lookup reference lives under `docs/product-management/reference/` (the engine-team design corpus). This change makes the **config-author product docs** the front door: the DocFX home page becomes `docs/product-docs/README.md`, the top-nav "Docs on GitHub" link points at `docs/product-docs/`, and the generated `reference/` quadrant moves to `docs/product-docs/reference/` so the product-docs tree is the one coherent docs root a reader lands in.

## Scope / what changes

1. **Move** `docs/product-management/reference/` → `docs/product-docs/reference/` (the tree is generated — the move is done by repointing the generator, then `make docs-gen`, not by hand-editing pages).
2. **Generator** (`scripts/docs-gen/generate.py`): change the `REF` output path **and** every relative-link prefix it emits — the new location is a sibling of `product-management/` under `docs/`, so links from a generated page to a concept doc / ADR gain a `../../../product-management/` (or `../../product-management/` for the shallower `reference/README.md` + `glossary.md`) hop.
3. **DocFX**: home page = `docs/product-docs/README.md`; `docfx/toc.yml` "Docs on GitHub" → `.../tree/main/docs/product-docs/`.
4. **Plumbing**: `docs-verify` banner step + `find` path (ci.yml), the `docs_gen` path filter (ci.yml), the `docs-site.yml` trigger inputs, and the `git add` path + comments in `.githooks/pre-commit`.
5. **Inbound links**: top `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and the `docs/product-docs/**` pages (tutorials/how-to/explanation) that link into `../../product-management/reference/...` now link `../reference/...`; rewrite the README's "Where is the reference quadrant?" section (it currently argues the reference is NOT here).
6. **ADR governance (explicit-drift gate)**: ADR-PC-022 is **Accepted** and §P1 pins `reference/` under `docs/product-management/reference/` — append a dated amendment acknowledging the move (do not edit the Decision in place, §D5). ADR-PC-026 (Proposed) §P3 says the corpus is not stitched and the navbar is API-only — revise it for the new home page + nav link.

## Acceptance criteria

- `make docs-verify` passes with the tree under `docs/product-docs/reference/` and nothing left under `docs/product-management/reference/`.
- `make docs-site` builds; the DocFX home page renders the product-docs README; the "Docs on GitHub" nav points at `docs/product-docs/`.
- No dangling relative links repo-wide (generated pages → concept docs/ADRs, and inbound links → the new reference home).
- ADR-PC-022 + ADR-PC-026 carry the drift acknowledgement; PR body lists ADRs touched/honoured.
notes: Implementation complete and pushed as PR #235 (branch docs/product-docs-front-door). Mechanically verified: make docs-verify green, make docs-site 0 errors (home renders the product-docs README, navbar repointed), 389 relative links resolve, adversarial multi-agent review found no blockers. Awaiting maintainer merge. Follow-up sfnt.27 filed for the pre-existing docs_gen CI-filter gap.

title: L.3f — Composite RC gate + CI cadence wiring
description:

title: L.3e — Synchronous-replication append-latency (ADR-PC-005 §P1)
description:
Plain English: measure how much the RPO-near-zero safety guarantee (a warm standby that must confirm every write) costs in extra write latency — the ADR-PC-005 §P1 claim that today has NO test behind it. title: L.3d — Cold-replay/rebuild budget (5s/30s) + no-rebuild-divergence invariant
description:

Adds a replay-budget measurement: trigger a projection cold-rebuild over the populated event store, time it, and diff rebuilt-vs-live projection state. Folds a replay verdict + a no-divergence verdict into RunArtefact. Cross-links bd j67l (L.4).

title: Wave 3 — Pack lifecycle to production: versioning, signing/publishing, sealed corpus
description:
Takes the config author from "validated locally" to "released, signed, and pinned for life" — the full pack lifecycle for the worked example. The counterintuitive crux here is pinning: rate sheets change live, but a pack is immutable for any instance constituted under it. This wave makes that legible and documents the publication path.

## Pages

1. **(explanation) Pack effective-date semantics and per-instance pinning** — why packs are immutable per instance, why `pack_effective_from` is metadata-only in v1.
   - Links: `explanation/why-packs-and-rate-sheets-are-separate.md`, `reference/pack-format`.
2. **(how-to) Version and release a pack** — `based_on`, `delta_summary`, `breaking_changes`; immutable-once-published.
   - Links: `pack-author` skill, ADR-PC-007.
3. **(how-to) Sign and publish a pack with cosign and ORAS** — validate → sign → `oras push` by digest → verify.
   - **PROVISIONAL — surface partly unbuilt.** cosign/oras publish and the OCI production registry are PENDING per the config-author surface map. Write this provisional with a built-vs-pending callout, OR sequence it to land after that code does.
4. **(how-to) Write sealed test-corpus instances for regression evidence** — `canonical-instances` are hand-authored INPUTS; `expected-events.yaml` is generated, never authored.
   - **Honest deferral:** flag ADR-PC-006 A1/A2 — depth-5 gates the event SEQUENCE, not the full payload, until C.3 lands.

## Acceptance criteria
- Pages land; README updated.
- The cosign/ORAS page carries a clear provisional / built-vs-pending banner.
- The A1/A2 depth-5 deferral is stated honestly on the sealed-corpus page.
- No restating of `pack-format` fields; relative links resolve.

Surface maturity: **mixed** — versioning/pinning/sealed-corpus are built; cosign/oras publish is pending.

title: Unify the Mission Control demo launchers behind a shared lib + a one-command 'make demo'
description: Plain English: the three demo bring-up scripts (demo-mcp, demo-saga, demo-agent) duplicate a lot of bash and are each organised around what they PROVE, not around the Mission Control UI the operator actually drives. This makes 'run everything and flip modes in the browser' impossible and forces the operator to juggle scripts (and hit a misleading port-8080 clash). Extract the shared steps into a sourced scripts/demo-lib.sh, rewrite the three scripts as thin entrypoints over it, and add scripts/demo-all.sh + 'make demo' that stands up the SUPERSET backend (Postgres+Redpanda+ACL stub + a Redpanda-wired engine + orchestrator + MCP + agent host + serve.py) so the browser can flip DEMO/LIVE-engine/LIVE-saga + YOU/CLAUDE + Telemetry against one bring-up. The Redpanda-wired engine is a strict superset of the Postgres-only one, so a single engine on :8080 serves every mode. De-dup also unifies the migration guard on the robust 'command_dedup' sentinel and makes the partial-volume case fail loud. Cannot be smoke-tested from the agent sandbox (no Docker reachable) — needs a live 'make demo' run to confirm.

title: Mission Control LIVE·saga: fail-closed checklist mislabels 'Constituted' + Telemetry tab stays empty
description:
In plain English: when you constitute a deposit in LIVE·saga mode and force the insufficient-funds refusal, the right-hand panel's progress checklist still lists 'Constituted' with a neutral bullet (reads as if the deposit was constituted, when it was fail-closed), and the Telemetry tab shows nothing at all. Two rendering gaps in the demo's saga path.

Bug 1 — checklist marks: renderSagaProcess() forces every step's mark to the muted '·' on failure (both 'done' and 'here' are gated on !failure), so the failure point isn't shown and 'Constituted' looks like a bullet-list item. Fix: track the furthest milestone the saga actually reached, mark passed steps ✓, mark the step it died on ✗ (red), leave unreached steps muted — so 'Constituted' is unambiguously not-reached.

Bug 2 — empty Telemetry: the saga branch of doConstitute()/onSagaState() never calls pushSpan(), unlike the demo/live branches, so state.spans stays empty and the Telemetry waterfall shows 'Run an operation…'. The trace-foot copy was already written for an illustrative saga trace. Fix: emit illustrative saga spans (constitution_requested, reserve_balance, validate_limits, confirm_debit, activate_deposit, deposit.constituted | constitution_failed) as the saga crosses each phase.

Scope: docs/demo/mission-control/index.html only (demo UI; no engine/contract impact).

Both rendering gaps resolved + verified end-to-end against a running demo-saga stack: fail-closed checklist now shows ✓ Requested · ✗ Validating · · Approved · · Constituted, and the Telemetry tab renders the saga's illustrative span waterfall (ending in a red constitution_failed span). title: Renewal: pre-maturity opt-out-window enforcement + F.3 Renew-from-Matured modelling (post-decomposition follow-up)
description:
Surfaced by the PR B (mtto.2) review of the RenewAsync decomposition. Three linked residuals the decomposition exposed, all to address before the auto-firing maturity scheduler (DEF-2) lands:
(1) OPT-OUT WINDOW: the monolith's pre-maturity opt-out-window guard (renewalDate < maturityDate; the 14-day auto_renewal_optout_window_days, ADR-PC-023 §P / 02 §2.4.4) was removed from the engine renewal path. The opt-out-VIA-termination path is still safe (a terminated deposit isn't Matured, so ConstituteRenewalAsync's Matured precondition rejects it), but the WINDOW-TIMING protection (don't fire renewal before the opt-out right closes) now has NO engine code owner + NO fitness test — it is delegated to whoever triggers maturity/the saga. Enforce it (in the maturity scheduler or as a saga-start gate) + add a fitness test before the auto-firing scheduler lands.
(2) F.3 MODELLING: post-decomposition the engine gates Renew via a direct Lifecycle==Matured literal (ConstituteRenewalAsync/LinkRenewalAsync), bypassing the F.3 LifecycleTransitions table (which still models Renew as Active-only). The modelling decision — add a Renew-from-Matured row, or model renewal as a single Active->Renewed transition — is open but was deferred to bd 29v8, which is CLOSED. This issue is the live tracker; update the TermDepositConstitutionService LinkRenewalAsync comment to cite it.
(3) DEAD PARAM: AutoRenewalOptoutWindowDays (VerifiedPack.cs / PackParameters) now has zero engine consumers pending (1). Either wire it into the window enforcement or mark it reserved.
Not a blocker for PR B/C (manually-triggered maturity); precedes the auto-firing scheduler.
