title: MCP step-up-SCA enforcement: wire SCA-trigger detection (Q1) + post-SCA token re-entry (Q2), flip ELICITATION_URL_MODE_ENABLED
description:
Today the MCP agent channel can *prompt* a human to do a strong-customer-authentication (SCA) re-challenge before an irreversible money-mover (mature_deposit / pay_interest), but it cannot *enforce* it. PR #202 (bd babelstone-ar1y) shipped the URL-mode elicitation transport behind ELICITATION_URL_MODE_ENABLED (default OFF) precisely because turning it on does NOT make a security gate: settlement would proceed on the agent-reported "human consented to navigate", which is the exact signal ADR-IC-010 §P8 forbids relying on. Real enforcement needs the bank's own out-of-band "SCA passed" signal wired in — that work is this issue.

This is the durable bd home for the fork recorded as **Q-BE** in docs/product-management/product_concepts/04-open-questions.md (ADR-PC-020 §D3/§P9). It stays effectively blocked until a maintainer decides Q1 and Q2 with the saga-orchestrator and edge owners.

## Two decision points (do NOT resolve speculatively)

**Q1 — SCA-trigger detection** (how a money-mover knows fresh SCA is needed):
- (a) engine returns a structured `SCA_REQUIRED`; the tool catches it, fires the step-up, then retries. **Recommended** — cleanest signal, bounded engine-side addition.
- (b) a Kong `pre-function` SCA gate on the `/mcp` route mirroring the constitute REST route (ADR-IC-006 §P2). Structurally incompatible: it 403s before this server is reached, killing the call before elicitation can start. `/mcp` has no such gate today.
- (c) proactive prompt on every money-mover (the current stub shape) — over-prompts users who already hold fresh SCA.

**Q2 — post-SCA token re-entry** (how the fresh proof flows back into the call):
- (a) agent re-call with a refreshed Bearer (PKCE/refresh).
- (b) out-of-band engine nonce tied to the `elicitation_id`, accepted within a TTL.
- (c) `session.send_elicit_complete(elicitation_id)` from the bank's SCA callback + agent retry.

## Definition of done
- Maintainer decision on Q1 + Q2 recorded.
- Bank's out-of-band SCA-completion signal wired (the §P8 saga-transition invariant: the irreversible action transitions on the bank's signal, not the agent's report) — realised in the saga-orchestrator lane.
- `ELICITATION_URL_MODE_ENABLED` default flipped to ON.
- Q-BE resolution folded back into Document 11 / ADR-IC-010 §P8; Q-BE removed from 04-open-questions.md.
- Money-mover docstrings + generated reference/mcp-tools/* updated to drop the "consent-prompt demo, not a gate" warning.

## Pointers
- Transport + maintainer flag: `mcp-server/src/babelstone_mcp/server.py` (`_maybe_stepup_sca`), `mcp-server/src/babelstone_mcp/elicitation.py`.
- Governs: ADR-IC-010 §P8, Document 11 §Human-in-the-Loop, ADR-IC-006 §P2 (SCA precedent).
- Interacts with the `/mcp` route plugin-shape question and the constitute-route SCA precedent.

title: SBOM workflow flakes: publishing the whole solution to one shared --output dir races (GenerateMvcTestManifestTask + ref-copy IOException)
description: In plain English: the SBOM workflow's 'Restore + publish the solution' step runs 'dotnet publish engine/Babelstone.slnx --output $RUNNER_TEMP/publish', which publishes EVERY project (including all test projects) into ONE shared output dir under parallel MSBuild. title: Close the engine->saga event path end-to-end (relay routing + ActivateDeposit->ConstituteDepositRequest/DepositId correlation) — runtime completion of 3klm + prerequisite for mtto
description:
In plain English: bd babelstone-3klm (PR #196) fixed the saga so it ADVANCES to COMPLETED when it hears the engine's DepositConstituted event (ADR-PC-029 slot-2), proven by an integration test that produces the event on the committed topic. But two pre-existing engine<->saga gaps mean the event does NOT actually reach the saga at true runtime, so the happy path still won't complete on its own — and these SAME two gaps block the renewal saga (mtto, event-driven on DepositMatured + new-stream constitution). Close BOTH here.

GAP A (relay routing) — VERIFIED: engine OutboxDrainer.cs publishes every fact to a topic named after aggregate_type (term_deposit), but the saga's SagaConsumeLoop subscribes to deposits.process.events (the ADR-IC-003 §S2 / Document 05 / Document 10 committed domain topic). No router bridges them. FORK (maintainer): (a) add an engine outbox router that re-publishes DepositConstituted (and DepositMatured for mtto) to deposits.process.events when ce_subject carries a process_id — honours the ADR, keeps the engine family-agnostic via config; (b) subscribe the saga to term_deposit and accept the NoTransition noise — deviates from the ADR, needs an amendment.

GAP B (command body + DepositId pin) — agent-reported (code-read): the saga's ActivateDepositCommand body {ProcessId, CausationMessageId, CorrelationId, DepositRef, CoreTxnRef} is structurally incompatible with the engine's ConstituteDepositRequest {PrincipalCents, ProductId, Role, TermDays, StartDate, InterestVariant, AutoRenewalPolicy, FundingAccount, PaymentPeriodMonths}, AND DepositId is not pinned to process_id (so ce_subject->process_id correlation won't fire at runtime). FORK (maintainer): can the engine constitute with only deposit_id + a minimal saga-owned field set, or must ALL business facts flow from the saga (TermDays/StartDate/InterestVariant/AutoRenewalPolicy/PaymentPeriodMonths) — the latter needs EdgeBusinessFacts + SagaBusinessReference(+Store) + a saga_business_references migration + a Pact-contract change?

Both are flagged in PR #196's diff (SagaConsumeTopics.cs doc comment) per ADR-PC-020 §D3, deferred not silently decided. Closing this is what makes the INTENDED 'SSE reaches a terminal state on the happy path' TRUE end-to-end, and unblocks bd babelstone-mtto. Governing: ADR-PC-029 slot-2, ADR-IC-003 §S2, Document 05/10, ADR-PC-008 (in-tx rate-resolve+constitute).
close_reason: Merged via PR #200 — engine->saga path closed end-to-end (orchestrator reads term_deposit family topic; engine resolves product_code in-tx; deposit_id=process_id correlation; happy path reaches COMPLETED).

title: MCP well-known route not publicly reachable on Kong CE — route-level jwt enabled:false doesn't suppress the global jwt (ADR-IC-010 §P2 / Q-BD)
description:
In plain English: the public OAuth discovery document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource must be reachable WITHOUT a token so an agent can find the authorization server before it has one (ADR-IC-010 §P2, RFC 9728). On kong:3.9.1 it actually 401s — the mcp-well-known route sets the jwt plugin to enabled:false, but Kong CE falls back to the GLOBAL jwt plugin instance, so the route stays token-gated. Discovered by the bd babelstone-5ot0 runtime harness (a minimal 2-route repro confirms it) and recorded as Q-BD in docs/product-management/product_concepts/04-open-questions.md. The defect predates the mTLS lane (committed in e50n / 3cfaf01); the 5ot0 mcp-contract-test currently prints the well-known half as a non-blocking KNOWN-FAIL.

Fix (CE-correct, NO anonymous consumer): de-globalize the jwt plugin — attach it explicitly to each authenticated route (deposits-constitute, processes-stream/sse, engine-query, engine-sor-ops, mcp-streamable-http) and leave it OFF mcp-well-known — WITHOUT adding an anonymous: consumer (which would break the pre-function ordering-safety property the no-anonymous global jwt provides; kong-config-check asserts none exists). Re-verify the pre-jwt-read ordering-safety per route after de-globalizing. Carry an ADR-IC-010 §P2 amendment (the enforcement MECHANISM changes), update scripts/kong-config-check.sh (the well-known jwt-disable assertions ~lines 311-315 + the global-jwt assumption), and flip the 5ot0 harness A5 well-known half from KNOWN-FAIL to a hard assertion. Governing: ADR-IC-010 §P2, ADR-IC-006 §P2/§P7.
close_reason: Merged via PR #199 — de-globalized the Kong jwt plugin so the RFC 9728 well-known route is publicly reachable on CE; adversarial mutation-probe proved per-route jwt coverage is non-vacuous; Q-BD resolved + ADR-IC-010 §P2 amended.

title: MCP gateway runtime contract test (the abig-pattern for /mcp): live token through Kong into the aud pre-function + app re-check
description: In plain English: babelstone-e50n validates the MCP edge statically (deck validate + kong config parse + kong-config-check assertions) and at the Python app layer (pytest 24/24), but NOT end-to-end through a running Kong. Mirror the bd babelstone-abig/1z0r runtime harness for the /mcp route: against live kong:3.9.1 + the secured MCP server, assert (a) a token with aud != MCP server URI -> 401 AUDIENCE_MISMATCH from Kong, no upstream; (b) a valid-aud token missing sub -> 403, no upstream; (c) a valid token (aud+sub+acr) -> the MCP initialize handshake succeeds through Kong; (d) a valid token + a client-supplied X-Client-Id: spoofed -> the upstream sees X-Client-Id = the token sub (overwrite); (e) GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource reachable unauthenticated, POST /mcp NOT. This is the runtime lock on the CE plugin-ordering safety property for the agent channel. Flagged as a deliberate follow-up by the e50n blueprint. Governing: ADR-IC-010 §P2/§P3, ADR-IC-006 §P2.

title: Enforce upstream mTLS at the MCP uvicorn before production (app header-trust currently rests on Kong-sole-ingress)
description: In plain English: the secured MCP server (babelstone-e50n) trusts the gateway-attested X-Client-Id / X-OAuth-Scope headers Kong stamps from the validated JWT sub. The app re-checks aud authoritatively but does NOT itself enforce that the request came through Kong — so the anti-spoofing defense rests on Kong being the sole ingress (no host port) plus upstream mTLS, and the uvicorn upstream currently runs plain HTTP (no ssl_cert_reqs) while the Kong mcp-server service has tls_verify:false. This is PARITY with the sanctioned orchestrator EdgeAuth trust model (only Kong-fronted mTLS traffic reaches the upstream), not a new regression — but before production: wire uvicorn ssl_cert_reqs=CERT_REQUIRED (or an equivalent mTLS terminator) and Kong client_certificate + tls_verify so a Kong-bypassing actor on the upstream network cannot present a forged token + spoofed X-Client-Id to a money-moving tool. Optionally also have the app middleware DERIVE X-Client-Id/scope from the (Kong-verified) token sub/scope and overwrite inbound headers as defense-in-depth. Surfaced by the e50n adversarial-security review (should-fix). Governing: ADR-IC-006 §P5 (mTLS), ADR-IC-010 §P3, Document 10/11 trust model.
close_reason: Merged via PR #194 — uvicorn upstream mTLS (CERT_REQUIRED) + mcp-server-scoped Kong tls_verify; fail-closed proven both ways; dev-stack healthcheck+gate verified end-to-end.

title: Saga-side reissue budget for indeterminate-clearance RETRY_PERMITTED (defense-in-depth)
description: In plain English: PR #183 (t7o3.10) made the saga REISSUE ConfirmDebit when a Core clearance finds the debit not-executed (ADR-IC-012 RETRY_PERMITTED). This conforms today — the authoritative bound on retries is the ACL's clearance job + the ADR-IC-012 §244 INDETERMINATE-backlog alert, not a saga busy-retry — but the saga itself has no cap: a Core that repeatedly answers not-executed would reissue indefinitely. Add a saga-side reissue BUDGET as defense-in-depth: reissue up to N (e.g. 3), then escalate to HUMAN_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED via the existing (AwaitCoreClearance -> HumanInterventionRequired) edge. Cleanest form without a new migration: a small decider mirroring SelfEmitApprovalForkAsync that counts prior AwaitCoreClearance entries from the saga transition log. Governing: ADR-IC-003 §P4 (waiting state, not busy retry) / §P6 (escalate, never strand), ADR-IC-012 §P5/§244. Flagged by adr-conformance + replay-determinism + financial-math reviewers.

title: Edge: runtime contract test for the SoR resolver (split-brain guard, ADR-PC-018 §5)
description:
In plain English: PR #182 (r3rt) added a Kong pre-function that resolves instance_id -> sor by calling the engine read surface (GET /v1/deposits/{id} over resty.http) and proxies to the engine ONLY on sor=='engine', failing closed 503 SOR_UNRESOLVED otherwise. The static gate (kong config parse + grep assertions) validates the config + Lua SYNTAX but does NOT execute the resolver, so the split-brain guard is unproven end-to-end. Mirrors the abig gap for SCA.

Add a request-level contract test against a live kong:3.9.1 + a stub engine read surface: (a) an instance whose read returns sor=='engine' -> the op proxies to the engine; (b) sor=='legacy' -> 503 SOR_UNRESOLVED, no proxy; (c) read 404 (unknown instance / projection lag) -> 503; (d) read transport error / non-200 / non-table body -> 503 (fail closed on every error path); (e) confirm require('resty.http') resolves at RUNTIME in the CE image (the static parse does not prove the module loads). This is the genuine split-brain lock (ADR-PC-018 §5 'never guess a backend'); ADR-PC-018 §Verifiable-commitments notes the fail-closed guard has no catalogue row today. Relates to babelstone-abig (the SCA/identity runtime test — could share one live-Kong harness).

title: Edge: Kong must inject X-Client-Id from the JWT sub (I.1/I.3 binding gap)
description:
In plain English: the orchestrator binds per-process ownership to a gateway-attested X-Client-Id header (EdgeAuth.ClientIdHeader), trusting Kong to set it from the authenticated caller. But infra/kong/kong.yml does NOT actually inject X-Client-Id — the jwt plugin validates the token and knows the sub/consumer, yet no request-transformer or pre-function copies the JWT sub into X-Client-Id. So a request through Kong passes jwt + SCA but reaches the orchestrator WITHOUT the attested client id, and the ownership binding has nothing to key on. Surfaced 2026-06-14 while writing the local edge-token helper (scripts/mint-edge-token.sh): the through-Kong path can't complete end-to-end today; only the direct-to-orchestrator dev bypass (supplying X-Client-Id manually) works.

Wire Kong to set X-Client-Id from the validated JWT sub on the edge routes (cleanest: the constitute route's existing pre-function already decodes the token for SCA — it can kong.service.request.set_header('X-Client-Id', claims.sub) from the validated payload; or a request-transformer mapping from the Kong consumer's custom_id). Add a kong-config-check assertion so it can't be silently dropped. Governing: ADR-IC-006 §P4 (gateway validates token, app enforces ownership), Document 05 §Step 0; relates to babelstone-pxj9 (I.1 edge binding) and babelstone-a079 (I.3 Kong config).
close_reason: Merged in PR #179 (commit 59e1bdf): gateway-attested X-Client-Id from the validated JWT sub on both orchestrator routes; security-reviewed (IDOR-safe, plugin-ordering hardened).

title: v1 happy-path completion: advance the saga on the engine DepositConstituted event (ADR-PC-029 slot-2)
description:
In plain English: with the t7o3.8 result-event bridge merged, the constitution saga auto-compensates correctly (settlement debited but activation fails -> money reversed), but the HAPPY path does not yet reach Completed on its own. The bridge deliberately does NOT advance the saga on the engine's ActivateDeposit HTTP 2xx — ADR-PC-029 slot-2 says the 2xx is not the advance signal; the saga must advance on the engine's resulting DepositConstituted event. At v1 nothing produces that advance, so a successful constitution parks the saga at APPROVED.

Wire the missing advance: the engine's DepositConstituted must drive the saga (Approved --ProcessConstituted--> Completed). Two shapes to choose from: (a) the engine emits a ProcessConstituted domain signal to deposits.process.events echoing the saga process_id carried on the ActivateDeposit command payload (ce_subject = process_id), consumed by the already-wired SagaConsumeLoop; or (b) the orchestrator consumes DepositConstituted from the term_deposit integration topic and correlates AggregateId -> process_id via the saga's pinned business reference (the deposit_ref). (a) is cleaner (no reverse lookup); both honour slot-2 (advance on the event, not the 2xx). This is the remaining half of t7o3.8 parts (b) engine DepositConstituted -> ProcessConstituted and (c) ce_subject -> process_id correlation, deferred to DEF-1 per maintainer decision 2026-06-14. Relates to babelstone-ub9s (DEF-1 real Core ACL) and babelstone-t7o3.2 (consume-loop ce_subject gap). Governing: ADR-PC-029 slot-2, ADR-IC-003 §S2 (+ the 2026-06-14 amendment recording the v1 in-process synthesis of the ACL legs), Document 05 step 4b/6.

title: Edge SCA: request-level gateway contract test (ADR-IC-006 §P2)
description:
In plain English: PR #179 added PSD2 SCA enforcement at the Kong edge — a request with no/weak 'acr' or a stale 'auth_time' is rejected 403 SCA_REQUIRED before the saga starts. The static kong-config-check gate proves the SCA rejection EXISTS in config, but it cannot prove the check keys on the RIGHT claims — a future edit could swap 'acr'/'auth_time' for a wrong claim name and the gate would still pass. ADR-IC-006 §P2 explicitly requires a contract test 'at the gateway level — not the application level'.

Add a request-level test against a running Kong (Document 07 testing strategy): send a signed JWT with no acr / a stale auth_time and assert a real 403 SCA_REQUIRED from the gateway; send one with a fresh acr+auth_time and assert pass-through. This locks the acr/auth_time claim contract end-to-end against the IAM. File/execute when the IAM SCA claim set is pinned. Governing: ADR-IC-006 §P2 (residual risk: 'SCA enforcement drift' / claim-name drift).
notes:
EXPANDED 2026-06-14 (security review of bd bkqo): this request-level gateway test is the end-to-end LOCK on the Kong CE plugin-ordering property, not just the claim names. On CE the SCA + X-Client-Id pre-functions run BEFORE jwt (static priority pre-function 1000000 > jwt 1450; CE has no dynamic 'ordering' — verified rejected by kong config parse), so the safety rests entirely on the GLOBAL jwt plugin 401'ing a forged/tampered token before the upstream proxy. Static gates (kong-config-check: SCA_REQUIRED + exit(403) present, set_header X-Client-Id from claims.sub on >=2 routes, jwt has no anonymous fallback) cannot prove that ordering holds at runtime. The contract test MUST, against a live kong:3.9.1 + a stub upstream that echoes received headers: (a) no/weak acr or stale auth_time => 403 SCA_REQUIRED, no upstream call; (b) a token with a TAMPERED sub (signature broken) => 401 from jwt, no upstream call (proves a pre-jwt payload read cannot leak through); (c) a valid token for 'attacker' + a client-supplied 'X-Client-Id: victim' header => upstream sees X-Client-Id=attacker (proves the overwrite + the attested source); (d) a valid compliant token => 202/passes. ADR-IC-006 §P2 mandates this 'at the gateway level'.
GOVERNANCE (security review of bkqo, 2026-06-14): abig must be a HARD merge-blocker before PRODUCTION hardening, not just filed — it satisfies ADR-IC-006 Residual Risks (a CI contract test MUST assert a request without the SCA claim gets 403 SCA_REQUIRED at the gateway), an obligation that predates the 6imx/bkqo PRs and is still unmet. PR #179 lands on the safe-by-construction argument (global no-anonymous jwt gates the proxy) + the static locks; the estate must not reach production with this runtime test still open.
close_reason: Closed

title: demo-mcp.sh stale: missing Idempotency-Key + naive migration-skip
description:
Plain English: the one-command walking-skeleton script scripts/demo-mcp.sh no longer completes a clean run, for two independent reasons found while smoke-testing the demo UI's LIVE mode (2026-06-14).

1) ADR-PC-029 drift: step 5 ('constitute → read → mature') sends no Idempotency-Key header, so the engine returns 400 ('Idempotency-Key header is required and must be a UUID') and the script aborts (set -euo pipefail). The script predates ADR-PC-029 (commit 2f0bbf7). Fix: have step 5's constitute curl send -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)".

2) Naive migration skip: step 2 skips ALL event-store migrations when public.events exists. On a Postgres volume created before a later migration (e.g. 0015_command_dedup, 0012_inbox), those tables stay absent — and the ADR-PC-029 constitute path then 500s on the missing command_dedup table. Fix options: track applied migrations (a schema_migrations table) and apply only the unapplied ones, or at least re-run all forward-only files. Workaround today: docker compose -f infra/compose.yaml down -v before 'up' so migrations apply fresh.

Repro: with an older pgdata volume, scripts/demo-mcp.sh up → step 5 400; constitute with a UUID key → 500 (relation command_dedup does not exist). Impact: the headline demo command is broken on returning machines; the engine itself is fine.
notes: PARTIAL FIX on branch feat/investor-demo-deck (2026-06-14): step 5's constitute now sends -H 'Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)', so the self-check no longer 400s. REMAINING: the naive migration-skip (skips all migrations when public.events exists) still leaves newer tables absent on a pre-existing volume → constitute 500s; needs a real applied-migrations check or re-running forward-only files.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #237 (fix/demo-migration-ledger). Replaced the naive migration-skip with a real migration-ledger applier in scripts/demo-lib.sh (matching the engine MigrationRunner ledger shape, with legacy-volume backfill); the Idempotency-Key half was already on main. Verified with shellcheck + a 4-scenario dry-run.

title: Wire AwaitCoreClearance entry/exit edges (Scenario C — indeterminate Core debit clearance)
description:
Plain English: the saga has a declared state AwaitCoreClearance for the case where a Core debit returns an INDETERMINATE outcome (we don't yet know if money moved) — Document 05 Scenario C, resolved by a clearance job rather than a busy retry. The state exists in the SagaState enum but is DELIBERATELY NOT wired into the ConstitutionProcess transition table: it has no entry edge (an indeterminate debit outcome should enter it) and no exit edge (the clearance event should leave it). The enum comment attributes these edges to 'H.2's business decision', but H.2 (babelstone-n55u) is CLOSED and no open issue tracks finishing them — an orphaned gap.

Scope:
- Add the entry edge: an INDETERMINATE Core debit outcome out of APPROVED (alongside DebitConfirmed -> ActivateDeposit and ActivationFailed -> CompensatePostDebit) moves the saga to AwaitCoreClearance.
- Add the exit edges: the clearance-job result leaves AwaitCoreClearance — confirmed-debit continues the happy path, reversed/failed routes to the appropriate compensation/terminal state.
- Account for the clearance-job PRODUCER: what emits the indeterminate outcome and the clearance result onto deposits.process.events (relates to the t7o3.8 command-outcome -> result-event bridge; the indeterminate branch is the third Core ACL outcome alongside reserve/confirm/reverse).
- Tests for the indeterminate-debit path end-to-end against the WireMock ACL stub.

Governing: ADR-IC-003 §P5/§P6 (long waits as first-class states, never busy retry; compensation as domain action), Document 05 Scenario C. Real Core ACL is DEF-1 (babelstone-ub9s).
close_reason: Merged in PR #183: AwaitCoreClearance wired for Scenario C indeterminate Core debit; not-executed disposition is RETRY_PERMITTED (reissue ConfirmDebit) per ADR-IC-012 (maintainer chose conformance over the fail-closed divergence). Saga-side reissue budget follow-up: babelstone-rq3e.

title: Make edge-pinned business references mandatory; remove the consume-loop fallback (pre-prod, no backward-compat)
description:
Plain English: PR #175 (t7o3.1) added the approval-fork self-emit and full command payloads, but kept a backward-compat dual path for sagas that were started by the consume loop and never went through the I.1 edge — those have no pinned business references, so the self-emit is skipped (the saga rests in ValidationsComplete) and the command outbox sink falls back to the minimal seam envelope instead of the full body. babelstone is not in production and every real saga starts at the edge, so this fallback is dead weight. Make edge-pinned references MANDATORY and delete the compat path.

Scope:
- SagaCommandOutboxSink: remove the seam-envelope fallback; always assemble + write the full typed CommandPayload from the pinned references. A saga reaching the sink without references is an error, not a fallback.
- SagaAdvanceHandler.SelfEmitApprovalForkAsync: remove the 'reference is null -> return (rest in VALIDATIONS_COMPLETE)' skip; absence of pinned references is a hard failure (the fork cannot be decided), not a silent rest state.
- Ensure the only saga start path is the edge (EdgeSagaStarter pins references); if a consume-loop start path still exists, either route it through the same pinning or remove it.
- Update/remove the tests that exercise the fallback (the 'no pinned references' substrate cases).

Honours the pre-prod no-backward-compat preference (bd memory backward-compat-ask-first). Confined to orchestrator/; bus stays events-only; no engine-kernel ProjectReference.
close_reason: Verified on main: deliverable landed in commit 3d581bd. SagaCommandOutboxSink fails closed when a saga reaches the sink without pinned references (the seam-envelope fallback is gone, lines 44-80) and SagaAdvanceHandler no longer rests reference-less sagas in VALIDATIONS_COMPLETE; the consume-loop start path (AdvanceOutcome.Started/StartAsync) is removed. Honours backward-compat-ask-first (pre-prod, no compat path). Unblocked by closing its umbrella t7o3.1.

Made edge-pinned references mandatory: SagaCommandOutboxSink + SelfEmitApprovalForkAsync now fail-closed (no seam-envelope fallback, no skip); removed the consume-loop start path entirely (StartEventType, StartAsync, AdvanceOutcome.Started) so the edge is the sole saga starter. 8 test files converted to edge-start / reference-pinning; orchestrator suite 109/109. title: Inject real edge mTLS + IAM key material from OpenBao at deck-sync time
description:
Plain English: PR #174 wired Kong's edge mTLS to the internal services and JWT validation, but the certificate/key material it ships is deliberately throwaway POC placeholder PEM committed to infra/kong/kong.yml (CN=babelstone-edge-poc) so the declarative config parses and CI can assert the boundary is wired. Real environments must replace that placeholder material with internal-CA-signed certs and the real IAM signing public key, sourced from the OpenBao secret boundary (M.2, babelstone-puu3) and injected at deck-sync time — never committed. This is the deploy-time half of "how the certs are replaced" that the kong.yml comments describe as intent but nothing yet implements.

Scope (the concrete gap left by PR #174 / babelstone-a079):
- Source the edge gateway client mTLS keypair (the 'certificates' entity referenced by client_certificate on both upstream services) from OpenBao at deck-sync time, replacing the committed POC keypair.
- Source the IAM issuer's real RS256 signing public key (consumers[].jwt_secrets[].rsa_public_key) the same way, replacing the POC placeholder.
- Flip 'tls_verify: false' to true on the orchestrator-edge and engine upstreams once the internal CA bundle is mounted, so Kong verifies the upstream cert (the reverse half of Boundary 2 mTLS, ADR-IC-006 §P5) — not just presents its own.
- Implement the JWT key rotation path as the deliberate 3-step deck sync ADR-IC-006 §P7 describes (add new, retain old until tokens expire, remove old).

This lives inside Q.6's 'declarative Kong deck sync' line but is broken out so the security-relevant step is visible rather than implicit. Honours ADR-IC-006 §P5 (Boundary 2 upstream mTLS) and §P7 (JWT key registration/rotation); consumes the OpenBao boundary (M.2). Relates to the M.3 trust-boundary umbrella (babelstone-njt2).
close_reason: Merged to main (post-merge cleanup of PRs #258–#277)

title: Command-outcome -> result-event bridge: emit saga result events onto deposits.process.events so compensation fires
description:
In plain English: the constitution saga's state machine fully specifies the compensation path (e.g. settlement debited but the deposit activation fails -> ReverseCoreDebit -> CancelledAfterDebit), and the consume loop (#167) is wired to RECEIVE the events that drive it. But nothing yet PRODUCES those result events onto the internal domain topic deposits.process.events, so end-to-end the compensation path does not actually fire today — a real debit-then-activation-failure would strand the saga in APPROVED with the customer's money debited and no auto-reversal.

The missing bridge has three parts:
1. Core ACL responses -> domain events: the ACL (WireMock stub at v1, real ACL is DEF-1/babelstone-ub9s) must emit BalanceReserved / DebitConfirmed / DebitReversed / ReservationReleased onto deposits.process.events when its reserve/confirm/reverse/release calls complete. Today the WireMock stub returns HTTP 200/422 but emits no event. A v1 shim could translate the dispatcher's HTTP delivery outcome (PUBLISHED/FAILED, SagaCommandDispatchDrainer) into the corresponding result event, or the real ACL emits them (DEF-1).
2. Engine event -> saga inbox event: the engine appends DepositConstituted and the catalog-gated relay publishes it, but nothing maps it to the saga's ProcessConstituted inbox event (Approved + ProcessConstituted -> Completed). Likewise an engine ActivateDeposit refusal (4xx, terminal FAILED on the saga_outbox row) must become an ActivationFailed event (Approved + ActivationFailed -> CompensatePostDebit + ReverseCoreDebit).
3. ce_subject / process_id routing: relates to the consume-loop gap already flagged on t7o3.2 — the producer sets ce_subject = deposit AggregateId, not the saga process_id; the bridge must address how a result event is correlated back to its saga instance.

Governing: ADR-IC-003 §P5/§P6 (compensation as a domain action, gated settlement), ADR-PC-016 (gated, InsufficientBalance compensates -> DepositConstitutionFailed), Document 05 Scenarios A/B. Prerequisite for the post-debit compensation to be exercised end-to-end, and for t7o3.1 (fork self-emit) / DEF-1 (real ACL). Surfaced answering 'settlement OK but deposit fails — what is the compensation path?' (transition table ConstitutionProcess.cs:204-208).
close_reason: Merged in PR #180 (89e3836): saga command-outcome -> result-event bridge; compensation auto-reversal end-to-end. Happy-path completion deferred to babelstone-3klm/DEF-1 per maintainer.

description:

title: Engine idempotent command endpoint (de-settled append) — build ADR-PC-029
description:
In plain English: ADR-PC-029 decided HOW saga/edge/MCP commands reach the engine — synchronous idempotent REST — but the decision issue (babelstone-t7o3.5) was type=decision and explicitly did NOT build the code. This is the dedicated impl issue for the endpoint itself: the linchpin that unblocks the dispatcher (t7o3.3) and settlement relocation (t7o3.4).

Builds ADR-PC-029's six contract slots on the engine's POST /v1 command surface:
- Slot 1 (payload): command-id ingress via Idempotency-Key header or command_id field (deterministic UUID = saga_outbox row id).
- Slot 2 (semantics): validate -> pure decider (ADR-PC-021) -> append -> return new head commit_sequence (ADR-IC-005 read-your-writes token). 2xx confirms applied, NOT the saga advance signal. DE-SETTLED: append only, no eager debit.
- Slot 3 (ordering): synchronous req/resp; at-least-once from the dispatcher; expectedVersion optimistic concurrency on (stream_id, sequence_number) preserved.
- Slot 4 (idempotency): RECEIVER dedupes keyed on command-id, scoped per aggregate; replay of an applied command-id returns the ORIGINAL commit_sequence with no second append; composes with expectedVersion.
- Slot 5 (error model): 2xx applied/idempotent-replay; 4xx engine-refuses (illegal transition/validation) -> terminal failure branch; 5xx/timeout transient -> safe to retry. Never gates on downstream GL/notification.
- Slot 6 (ownership/versioning): engine owns the /v1 command contract; Pact CDC pins dispatcher<->engine.

Spec-first (ADR-PC-020 §P10): flip commitment-catalogue rows ENGINE_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENT and ENGINE_COMMAND_PACT from Planned -> Live (failing test first, implement to green). De-settling itself is t7o3.4 (this endpoint must not re-introduce the eager call); coordinate so the de-settled path is the one this endpoint exercises.

Refiled per the t7o3.5 close note ('refile a dedicated impl issue if that work needs its own tracking').
notes: PR #164 opened (feat/engine-command-endpoint), awaiting maintainer merge. Implements ADR-PC-029; ENGINE_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENT flipped to Live. Unblocks t7o3.3 (dispatcher) + t7o3.4 (settlement relocation). Follow-ups: ziu3.1 (MCP key), e6fr.10 (retention sweeper).

title: Engine command-ingress contract: REST (idempotent) — ADR-PC + engine command endpoint
description:
In plain English: how the saga commands actually reach the engine was never decided or written down. This records the decision — synchronous idempotent REST (Option 2) — and builds the engine side of it.

Deliverables: (1) a contract-shape ADR-PC (next free number) recording the REST ingress, cross-linking ADR-IC-003 (saga orchestrator) and ADR-PC-016 (settlement gating), naming the Kafka command-inbox as the reversible scale-up path (see the post-v1 revisit issue); (2) the engine-side idempotent command endpoint(s) the saga calls (deterministic command-id dedup, pairing with the existing expectedVersion concurrency), de-settled per the settlement-relocation issue. Load-bearing commitments migrated to the commitment catalogue as rows 19 ENGINE_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENT and 20 ENGINE_COMMAND_PACT (both Planned). The endpoint build + the two Planned commitments are carried by the dispatcher/settlement work this issue blocks (t7o3.3, t7o3.4); refile a dedicated impl issue if that work needs its own tracking.

title: Relocate settlement onto the saga gated path (WireMock at v1); stop eager in-engine settlement
description:
In plain English: today the engine debits Core itself, eagerly, on the constitution request path before recording the deposit — which contradicts ADR-PC-016 (the constitution saga blocks on settlement confirmation before completing). This moves the money leg to where it belongs: a gated saga step.

Remove the eager ISettlementPort call from TermDepositConstitutionService.ConstituteAsync; the engine command step just appends DepositConstituted (settlement removed from that path). Settlement becomes the saga gated step (ReserveBalance then ConfirmDebit) delivered via the dispatcher to a WireMock ISettlementPort adapter at v1; DEF-1 later swaps WireMock for the real ACL. Record the ADR-PC-016 divergence acknowledgment per the explicit-drift gate (ADR-PC-020 D3).

Constitution path de-settled (engine appends only); settlement is the saga's gated ReserveAccountBalance->ConfirmDebit via the dispatcher to a WireMock-stubbed Core ACL (infra/compose core-acl-stub + k8s + in-process WireMock.Net for tests). title: Saga command dispatcher: drain saga_outbox to idempotent HTTP (REST ingress)
description:
In plain English: the saga writes the commands it decides into saga_outbox, but nothing reads them — so no saga-decided command ever leaves the orchestrator. This builds the dispatcher that drains saga_outbox and delivers each command.

Per the REST ingress decision: the dispatcher drains saga_outbox (transactional-outbox, at-least-once) and delivers engine-bound commands (e.g. ActivateDeposit) by idempotent HTTP POST to the engine command endpoint (deterministic command id / Idempotency-Key). v1 settlement commands (ReserveBalance / ConfirmDebit) go to the WireMock settlement stub; the real ACL is DEF-1. The engine resulting event returns via the orchestrator event-consume loop to advance the saga — the HTTP response only confirms delivery.

Hosted drainer: saga_outbox PENDING -> idempotent HTTP (Idempotency-Key=message_id, traceparent), ADR-PC-029 slot-5 error model, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (active-active safe). Pact-style CDC in code (consumer+provider in CI). 2 reviewers PASS. Row 20 ENGINE_COMMAND_PACT kept Planned (formal PactNet broker round-trip deferred). FIFO-guard follow-up: babelstone-t7o3.7.

title: Host-wire the orchestrator event-consume loop (run InboxConsumerService + SagaAdvanceHandler)
description:
In plain English: the saga state machine is built and tested, but nothing runs it — the orchestrator wires the handler into DI yet starts no consume loop, so a started saga never advances. This stands up the live loop.

AddHostedService(InboxConsumerService) in the orchestrator host; plug SagaAdvanceHandler as the IInboxMessageHandler; add the Confluent/Avro consume surface to the orchestrator (its csproj is Npgsql-only today). The loop consumes EVENTS (engine integration events at v1; ACL events post-v1) and advances the saga via the optimistic-concurrency transition. Mirror of the closed engine relay-hosting issue (G.1 follow-up, s5gd). Under the REST ingress decision, this loop consumes events only — engine-bound COMMANDS are delivered by the dispatcher (the saga command dispatcher issue), not a Kafka command topic.

title: Catalog-gated integration-event relay + promotion criterion (implements ADR-IC-017)
description:
In plain English: today the engine publishes every event it records onto the integration bus, with no rule for which events belong there — so an event becomes "public" by accident of being appended. This makes the outbox relay refuse to publish anything that has not been deliberately promoted to an integration event, and writes the criterion down.

Implements ADR-IC-017 (Proposed).
- P1 catalog-gated relay (fail-closed): the relay publishes a row only if its event_type resolves to a catalogued integration event (AsyncAPI / .avsc per ADR-IC-015 / ADR-IC-002). An uncatalogued event is store-only (still appended, folded, replayable).
- P3 reverse orphan check: extend scripts/asyncapi-catalog-validate.sh so every relay-publishable event_type has a catalog entry — making catalog-entry equivalent to on-the-bus, hermetically.
- P4 ratify the v1 integration-event set per-event against the criterion (reclassify InterestAccrued / WithholdingApplied vs InterestPaid; DepositConstitutionFailed stays internal — its coarse fact rides the saga DepositCancelled).
- Seed commitments INTEGRATION_EVENT_CATALOG_GATED and NO_UNCATALOGUED_EVENT_ON_BUS into the commitment catalogue.
Attach point: the ADR-PC-028 store/bus encode split (bd 36mk).
close_reason: Merged via PR #168 (feat/catalog-gated-relay). Append-side IIntegrationEventCatalog gate + §P3 reverse-orphan check; rows 21/22 Live; ADR-PC-001 §P2 §D5 amendment for the per-event outbox coupling. §P4 reclassification deferred to babelstone-a7d4.4. CI green.

Rows 21/22 flipped Planned->Live. adr-conformance caught + same-PR fixed an ADR-PC-001 §P2 drift (§D5 amendment narrowing per-event outbox coupling to <=1, per ADR-IC-017 §P1). §P4 InterestAccrued/WithholdingApplied-vs-InterestPaid reclassification deferred to a follow-up (no .avsc removed). title: acl + notification Dockerfiles will fail to build when they join the image-build matrix
description:
Plain English: the acl and notification services have placeholder Dockerfiles that say 'build the .NET project here' without naming which project — and they have no source code yet. They're intentionally left out of the image build/scan workflow for now. But the moment their real code lands and they're added to that workflow, the build will fail, because a bare 'dotnet restore'/'dotnet publish' with no project (and no solution file) is ambiguous. This is a heads-up so whoever adds the source fixes the Dockerfile in the same step.

Detail: acl/Dockerfile:9-10 and notification/Dockerfile:9-10 run 'dotnet restore' then 'dotnet publish -c Release -o /app --no-restore' with NO project argument. There is no root .sln/.slnx (only engine/Babelstone.slnx) and ~35 .csproj repo-wide. With the service dir as build context: no project found. With repo-root context (the engine/orchestrator pattern): MSBUILD ambiguity error. Either way the leg breaks. The image-build.yml matrix (ADR-IC-013) intentionally excludes acl/notification today ('stubs with no source… join the matrix when their .NET source lands').

Fix when source lands: name the explicit .csproj on BOTH restore and publish and set the correct build context — copy the engine/orchestrator Dockerfile pattern — and add the matrix entry + ENTRYPOINT at the same time. Pre-existing (PR #145 only touched the FROM line, switching to the chiseled runtime base); flagged by the PR #145 post-merge audit so the acl/notification build tasks (ADR-IC-012 / ADR-IC-011) inherit a buildable Dockerfile. Refs: ADR-IC-011, ADR-IC-012, ADR-IC-013, .github/workflows/image-build.yml.
acceptance_criteria:
- acl/Dockerfile and notification/Dockerfile name the explicit .csproj on BOTH dotnet restore and dotnet publish, with the engine/orchestrator build-context pattern and an ENTRYPOINT set.
- The image-build.yml matrix (ADR-IC-013) gains the acl and notification entries in the same change.
- Both image-build legs succeed.

title: Engine OCI pack mode cannot boot in the chiseled runtime image (oras/cosign absent)
description:
Plain English: when the engine loads regulatory packs from an OCI registry instead of disk, it runs two external command-line tools (oras and cosign) to pull and verify them. The engine's container image is now a 'chiseled' image with no shell and no extra binaries, so those tools aren't present — an engine started in OCI mode would crash at startup. Nothing runs in OCI mode today (dev/CI/prod all default to disk mode, and CI never actually starts the image), so this is a latent gap, not a live outage. But it needs handling before OCI mode is ever switched on.

Detail: HostPackLoading (Engine:PackRegistry=oci, ADR-PC-007 §P3/§P4) builds OrasPackSource + CosignPackVerifier + OciPackStore, which shell out via ProcessRunner (UseShellExecute=false, bare-PATH names 'oras'/'cosign'). The chiseled engine image (engine/Dockerfile, aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra per ADR-PC-010 §A1 amendment 2026-06-11) contains only the published app + the .NET runtime — no oras, no cosign, no shell. Pre-existing: the prior non-chiseled mcr aspnet base didn't bundle them either, so PR #145 did not regress this; but chiseling also removes the docker-exec escape hatch an operator could have used.

Fix when OCI mode is wired: bundle pinned static oras + cosign binaries into the runtime stage (COPY from a tools stage), OR move pull/verify in-process (no shell-out), AND add an OCI-mode 'docker run' smoke test so the image's boot path is exercised in CI (today CI only builds/scans images, never runs them). Surfaced by the PR #145 post-merge audit. Refs: ADR-PC-007, ADR-PC-010, .github/workflows/image-build.yml.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #218 (merged 2026-06-17): fail-fast OCI pack guard when oras/cosign absent + tightened rate-sheets CI cue-vet filter. 4ow6 decided scope = conservative guard; multi-stage-image bundling remains a follow-up.

title: Auto-discover families in contracts/cue/check.sh (drop hard-coded FAMILIES list)
description:
The CUE soundness gate that proves each family's schema accepts its valid fixtures and rejects its invalid ones currently only checks the families named in a hand-maintained list inside the script. Add a second product family and forget to add it to that list, and there is NO error — the new family's fixtures are silently skipped, so a broken schema could merge looking green. The fix makes the gate auto-discover families so a new one is checked the moment its schema file lands.

Technical: contracts/cue/check.sh hard-codes FAMILIES='term-deposit|families/term-deposit.cue|#TermDeposit' and loops over it. The Avro (avro-compat-check.sh) and AsyncAPI (asyncapi-catalog-validate.sh) gates already auto-discover via recursive globs; this CUE gate is the one shared chokepoint that scales O(manual-edit) with family count. Fix: glob families/*.cue, derive the testdata dir from the basename and the #<Family> root definition as the PascalCase form (the ADR-PC-006 / new-family-schema convention); a mis-named definition fails 'cue vet' loudly rather than being skipped. Found during the term_deposit-coupling audit of PR #142; resolved within that same PR (branch feat/authoring-skills-family-event).
close_reason: Resolved in PR #142 (commit 0ad929c): contracts/cue/check.sh now auto-discovers families from families/*.cue (testdata dir = basename; root def = #<Family> PascalCase), dropping the hand-maintained FAMILIES list and the silent-skip risk. Verified: gate still passes all term-deposit accept/reject + pack-manifest fixtures.

title: Adopt JSON event-store payload (ADR-PC-028): split store/bus encode, harden the JSON codec, add the two fitness gates
description:
ADR-PC-028 implementation. Tracks the move to a self-describing JSON event-store payload.

DONE (PR #131):
- EVENT_STORE_PAYLOAD_SELF_DESCRIBING gate is LIVE — structural fitness (the replay/decode spine Babelstone.Engine + Babelstone.EventStore reference no Confluent.SchemaRegistry / Babelstone.Engine.Avro) + behavioural unit (JsonEventSerializer round-trips the store payload from the bytes alone, no registry). Mutation-tested.
- JSON store-codec hardening (partial): determinism (same event -> identical bytes) and PII-ciphertext-as-base64 round-trip are pinned by unit tests; JsonEventSerializer promoted from 'deferred-Avro stand-in' to the tested decided store codec.

REMAINING — blocked on Avro-on-the-bus (Epic E/G); the outbox is JSON today, so there is no Avro encoding to split into or compare against:
- Split the single Encode at the append boundary (AggregateRuntime ~line 146) into store-encode (JSON) + bus-encode (Avro+schema_id on the outbox row, ADR-IC-004 §P3).
- STORE_BUS_ENCODING_EQUIVALENCE gate (the JSON store payload and the Avro outbox payload are semantically equal — no skew). Stays Planned in ADR-PC-028 until then.
- Deeper codec hardening (explicit payload versioning) once the format stabilises.
notes: ADR-IC-017 / bd a7d4.3 dependency: 36mk owns flipping the durable relay from JSON+placeholder schema_id=1 to real Avro + a registered Schema-Registry schema_id (the bus-encode half of the store/bus split). The catalog-gated promotion filter (a7d4.3) attaches at this split point.

title: Wire the writer-schema resolver into the replay/rebuild serializer (turn REPLAY_PIN resolution ON)
description:
babelstone-ohdk landed the PLUMBING: the 5 replay/rebuild sites thread envelope.PayloadSchemaId through IEventSerializer.Decode(payload, type, writerSchemaId), and AvroEventSerializer resolves writer→reader WHEN an ISchemaByIdResolver is wired. But it stays OFF in prod: Program.cs:133 registers JsonEventSerializer (not AvroEventSerializer), and even the Avro codec has a null resolver by default, so replay is still writer==reader.

In plain English: the safety mechanism is installed but not switched on. Flipping it on means (1) registering AvroEventSerializer as the engine IEventSerializer where replay/rebuild runs, and (2) handing it a ConfluentSchemaByIdResolver (the rebuild host needs Schema Registry access). Beware legacy events written with the walking-skeleton constant schema_id=1 (HostServices) that was never registered in the SR — resolving those will fail loud; plan a backfill/registration or a sentinel-id fast-path bypass.

Discovered from babelstone-ohdk. Pairs with the forward-evolution CI gate follow-up.

title: G.x — Lifecycle-event Avro persistence coverage
description:
Close the schema-coverage gap where a term-deposit lifecycle event's decider logic lands ahead of its Avro schema + persistence wiring, so a missing .avsc only fails loud at runtime (AvroSchemaCatalog.ForRecordName throws at append time).

Today only the 4 E.1 AT_MATURITY events have .avsc (DepositConstituted, InterestAccrued, WithholdingApplied, DepositMatured). The 7 F.2 lifecycle events (DepositConstitutionFailed, InterestPaid, DepositRenewed, DepositTerminatedEarly, DepositPartiallyWithdrawn, DepositCorrected, DepositTransferredToHeirs) have records + (some) decider logic but no schema. G.3 delivered only the SR compat gate (added no schemas); F.3 + F.4 are pure-unit only; G.6 is emit-side fitness (PII / post-flag-never / no-clock) and would sail past a missing .avsc.

Scope:
1. A catalog-driven round-trip SWEEP (default CI lane, no container): for every catalogued .avsc, the matching CLR DomainEvent Encode->Decode round-trips losslessly, with distinct non-default field values (drop AND swap detector). Catalog-driven, NOT type-driven — schema-less events are legitimately not-yet-on-the-wire and must not fail the sweep.
2. Add each lifecycle event's .avsc as it is wired to the append/publish path (ADR-IC-002 §P1 path/namespace layout, §P2 null-first unions, forward-only evolution).
3. A decider->append INTEGRATION test per lifecycle event proving the schema exists and survives serialize->replay (the half the catalog sweep cannot cover, since the sweep is driven by the catalog not the wiring).

Note: distinct from the replay-side SR writer-schema-by-id resolution gap (babelstone-0ho1 / babelstone-ohdk) — that is cross-version Decode, this is persist-side schema coverage.

title: Q.y — Wire code-coverage (line/branch) instrumentation + threshold gate into CI
description:
No code-coverage instrumentation exists anywhere in the repo today. Neither ci.yml nor any .csproj references coverlet / Microsoft.CodeCoverage; Go runs `go test` without -coverprofile in CI; pytest has no pytest-cov. This is distinct from j72w/spec-coverage (which asserts every Live Test ID resolves to a running test — a *test-presence* gate, not a line/branch gate).

GOAL: emit per-toolchain coverage in CI, publish a merged report, and (phase 2) gate on a floor.

SCOPE
- .NET: add coverlet.collector (CPM: one PackageVersion in Directory.Packages.props + versionless PackageReference per *.Tests.csproj — 15 projects) and run `dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"`, merge the 15 cobertura via `dotnet-coverage merge`. NOTE: the CLR-profiler route (`dotnet-coverage collect -- dotnet test`) silently produces an EMPTY report on macOS/.NET 10 ("Profiler was not initialized" → 178-byte cobertura with line-rate=1) — use the XPlat VSTest collector, not collect.
- Go: `go test -coverprofile` in the pack-validate job + `go tool cover -func` summary (Go = statement coverage only; no native branch).
- Python: pytest-cov (`--cov --cov-branch`) in the mcp-server job.
- Publish: merged cobertura as a CI artifact (optionally a PR summary / badge). Decide reporter (e.g. ReportGenerator).

PHASE 2 (gate): pick per-toolchain floors and fail-closed, then add to the 'CI gate' aggregator + main-protect.json required checks (same pattern j72w used for spec-coverage / CodeQL gate).

BASELINE measured 2026-06-10 (local, full suite incl. Testcontainers integration tier; 555 .NET + 103 Go + 10 Python tests, all green):
- .NET: 88.9% line (4005/4505), 80.3% branch (1136/1415)
- Go: 81.6% statements
- Python: 84% line / 81% line+branch
WEAK SPOT to inform the floor: Babelstone.Engine.Api 67.8% line / 32.4% branch (HTTP host error/branch paths); InboxConsumer 79%, EventStore.Migrations 79%, Orchestrator 81.5%. Pure cores (EventStore fold, FinancialTypes, Telemetry) at 100%.

ANCHORS: ADR-PC-019 §P1 (always-run required-check pattern), ADR-IC-009 (test tiers), ci.yml, .github/rulesets/main-protect.json.
notes:
PR #162 (lane D, feat/code-coverage-ci) opened — coverlet+Go+pytest phase-1, CI green. Phase-2 floor gate deferred (needs maintainer sign-off). Pending review/merge.
UPDATE 2026-06-13 (supersedes the 'Phase-2 floor gate deferred' line above): Phase 2 floor is now WIRED in PR #162 (commit d355022 on feat/code-coverage-ci), pending review/merge. Floors: .NET >=85% line / 75% branch via .github/scripts/coverage-floor-cobertura.py (reads merged-cobertura dedup'd root counts, fails closed on the empty-trap); Go >=78% statements via awk on 'go tool cover -func'; Python --cov-fail-under=80 (combined line+branch). All three run as steps INSIDE the path-scoped engine/pack-validate/mcp-server jobs, which already feed the always-run 'CI gate' aggregator (ADR-PC-019 §P1) — so a breach blocks the PR with NO new required check in main-protect.json (chosen over the j72w discrete-required-check pattern precisely because a skipped required check would block unrelated PRs). Verified against this branch's real CI artifact (run 27474645928): live full-suite kernel-excluded .NET merged = 94.51% line (2446/2588) / 81.89% branch (529/646) — passes with ~9.5pt/~6.9pt headroom. title: Replay-side SR writer-schema resolution: thread EventEnvelope.PayloadSchemaId through Decode in projection/rebuild paths
description: PR #123 (babelstone-0ho1) added SR writer-schema-by-id resolution to the InboxConsumer BUS-consume path (new 3-arg AvroEventSerializer.Decode(payload, type, writerSchema)). But the event-store REPLAY / projection-rebuild path still calls the single-arg writer==reader Decode and ignores the per-event-pinned EventEnvelope.PayloadSchemaId (EventEnvelope.cs:25). Call sites: AggregateRuntime.cs:184, ProjectionRunner.cs:51, ProjectionReconciler.cs:217 (the §7.2 rebuild-drill fold), SimulationRuntime.cs:40, ReadModelRunner.cs:84. Once a family .avsc evolves forward (the additive/reorder change #123 enables on the bus), a periodic full rebuild (§7.2) decodes OLD writer-schema bytes against the NEW reader schema with no resolution -> mis-decode (throw) or, for a reorder, silently wrong field values -> divergent projection rows (the slow-drift class §7.2 exists to catch). Fix: thread envelope.PayloadSchemaId through the new 3-arg Decode in all replay/rebuild call sites. Relates to REPLAY_PIN_PER_EVENT (adr-conformance lane). Flagged by replay-determinism review of PR #123.

title: Carry catalogue product code onto DepositConstituted + denormalize into D.4 read model (yfr2 follow-up)
description:
Carry the catalogue product code onto DepositConstituted so the D.4 read model can denormalize and expose it — the queryable "which product is this" dimension that rate_sheet_version_id cannot provide.

## Why

The D.4 read model (yfr2) can only denormalize facts the event already carries. Today DepositConstituted carries the *price* identifier (rate_sheet_version_id, e.g. pt-deposits-2026.1) but NOT the *structure* identifier (the catalogue product code, e.g. dpz_pt_12m_juros_venc). The catalogue code arrives as ConstituteDepositCommand.ProductId, is consumed at constitution to resolve the TAN against the rate sheet (ADR-PC-008 §P3), and is then discarded — only the resolved TAN + rate-sheet version survive onto the event.

The first D.4 commit had a `product_id` column populated from the rate-sheet version (a mislabelled column whose name lied about its contents — a client filtering on the catalogue code would match nothing); the domain review dropped it and exposed only rate_sheet_version_id under its true name. This issue restores a HONEST catalogue-code dimension.

## Scope (event-contract change, governed)

- Add an additive, defaulted `product_code` field to DepositConstituted: the Avro .avsc (default "" → BACKWARD/FULL compatible per ADR-IC-002 §P3; mirror the payment_period_months precedent) and the C# event record.
- Stamp it in the decider from the already-available command.ProductId (no new command input).
- Carry it through the fold onto DepositPosition (deterministic, byte-identical rebuild — ADR-PC-010 §P5).
- Denormalize into the D.4 read surface under its honest name: read_model.deposits column, ReadModelRow, DepositReadModelResponse, the family mapper.
- Tests: Avro old→new decode with default, read-model round-trip + column-set guard (product_code present, product_id still absent), decider stamps from command.ProductId. Pass the schema-compat CI gate.

## Important caveat — prospective only

Because the catalogue code is discarded at constitution and rate_sheet_version_id → product is one-to-many (one rate sheet prices many variants), the code CANNOT be recovered from the event log for deposits already constituted. The new field is prospective: historical rows carry the default empty code. The longer this waits, the larger that permanently-uncategorizable backlog grows — an argument for doing it sooner.

## Disposition

Per maintainer request (2026-06-08), being implemented in the SAME PR as D.4 (PR #115, branch feat/d4-read-model-surface) rather than as a separate change. Discovered-from yfr2 (D.4); relates to b4wp (I.2 Query API), which gains a product-filter dimension once this lands.

title: Q.x — Audit CI pipelines for freshness & coverage (fuzz, mutation, DB-level engine↔family independence)
description:
Periodic review of the GitHub Actions pipelines under `.github/workflows/` — are they up to date and do they cover everything they *could*? Three areas the workflows have visibly outgrown:

## 1. Fuzz coverage is pack-validate-only
`fuzz.yml` fuzzes **only** the Go `pack-validate` surfaces (`FuzzLoad` in `internal/pack`, `FuzzRun` in `internal/validate`). Every other untrusted-bytes ingress point is unfuzzed. Candidates that parse external/attacker-influenced input and arguably warrant a fuzz target:
- engine **Avro decode path** (`Babelstone.Engine.Avro` / `OutboxPublisher` inbox decode — the schema-registry writer-schema-by-id path, bd babelstone-0ho1)
- engine **command/query API** JSON envelopes (`Babelstone.Engine.Api`)
- **mcp-server** (Python) request parsing (ADR-IC-010)
- `acl` / `orchestrator` / `notification` boundary parsers
- `contracts` CUE/Avro parsing

Decide which are worth a target vs. explicitly out-of-scope, and record the rationale.

## 2. Mutation scope is 4 of ~10 .NET projects, and .NET-only
`mutation.yml` runs Stryker.NET on **EventStore, Engine, FinancialTypes (Money), FinancialMath** only. Projects that ship tests but have **no** mutation scope:
- `families/term-deposit` handler (the canonical family — arguably the most important to pin)
- `Babelstone.RateSheets`, `Babelstone.Packs`, `Babelstone.Engine.Avro`, `Babelstone.OutboxPublisher`, projection runtime (`Engine.Api`)
- **Go** `pack-validate` (no mutation tooling wired — e.g. gremlins/ooze)
- **Python** `mcp-server` (no mutation tooling — e.g. mutmut/cosmic-ray)

Decide coverage targets + score floors per `engine/docs/mutation-testing.md`, or explicitly defer with rationale.

## 3. DB-level engine↔family independence is NOT guarded
`EngineFamilyAgnosticTests` (ADR-PC-021 §P2) enforces the one-way *family → engine* arrow **at the .csproj reference level only** — it proves no spine project code-references `families/**`. There is **no** guard that the same independence holds **at the database level**:
- no family-specific tables/columns leak into the engine's event-store schema (migrations `0001`–`0011` are all engine-owned today)
- no FK from engine tables into family-owned data (or vice-versa)
- the event store stays family-agnostic (events as opaque payloads keyed by family id, not family-typed columns)
- family state lives only in family-owned projections/stores

Add a schema-level fitness function (or document why the .csproj guard is deemed sufficient).

## 4. General freshness sweep
- action pin currency (`checkout@v6`, `upload-artifact@v7`, `cache@v5`, `mise-action@v4`) — any stale/security-advisory'd?
- per-PR `changes`/paths-filter matrix in `ci.yml` — do newer areas (Engine.Api, projection runtime, rate-sheets, notification) trigger the right jobs?
- scheduled-scan cadence sanity (CodeQL 04:00, SBOM 05:00, mutation Mon 03:00, fuzz Mon 06:00)

## Deliverable
A findings note (gaps + recommendation + which to action vs. defer) and follow-up child issues under Epic Q for anything actioned. No code change required by this issue itself — it is the audit.

title: Q.7c — Gate the grype SBOM scan: flip sbom.yml fail-build + add .grype.yaml CPE suppressions
notes:
Q.7c done on branch ci/q7c-grype-sbom-gate → PR #92 (all checks green; pending maintainer merge).

OUTCOME — the issue's framing (flip grype fail-build) was superseded by investigation into a LAYERED per-ecosystem blocking-SCA model:
- NuGet: NuGetAudit (NU1901-1904) + TreatWarningsAsErrors ALREADY blocks vulnerable NuGet packages in the engine build (engine/Directory.Build.props → CI gate). Proven: seeded System.Text.Encodings.Web 4.5.0 → NU1904 build failure. Now RECORDED in ADR-IC-014 (the Decision named only Dependabot for the NuGet leg).
- Go: ADDED govulncheck (reachability) to the pack-validate CI job. Baseline triaged clean first: go 1.26.3→1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037 crypto/x509, GO-2026-5039 net/textproto) + golang.org/x/net 0.52.0→0.55.0 (GO-2026-5026) — the 3 reachable findings.
- Actions/Python(later)/npm: ADDED GitHub-native dependency-review-action (required check 'dependency-review', runs every PR). Cross-ecosystem catch-all. NOTE it is NuGet-BLIND here (CPM without packages.lock.json → graph versions '>= 0') — confirmed via dependency-graph compare API; NuGetAudit is the NuGet authority, so this is fine. No lockfiles added (would only duplicate NuGetAudit).
- grype SBOM (sbom.yml): stays REPORT-ONLY (CycloneDX/DORA evidence + native-closure defense-in-depth; catches bundled native libs the package graph misses, e.g. zlib). Flipping it = perpetual CPE-FP suppression for no unique signal.
- Dependabot: unchanged, non-blocking companion (graph freshness + update PRs + alerts).

FILES: dependency-review.yml (new), ci.yml (govulncheck step), main-protect.json + rulesets/README.md (dependency-review required check, source of record), sbom.yml (comment), mise.toml (go 1.26.4), pack-validate/go.mod+go.sum (x/net 0.55.0), ADR-IC-014 (dated Amendment 2026-06-06 recording the layer; Decision untouched §D5).

adr-conformance: PASS (twice — initial + after redesign). No supersession; layered language-native gates do not re-propose the rejected Trivy/OSV option (they BLOCK, which Dependabot can't).

⚠️ POST-MERGE: re-apply the live ruleset so 'dependency-review' becomes a required check (gh api PUT repos/jhosm/babelstone/rulesets/<id> --input .github/rulesets/main-protect.json) — only AFTER merge (dependency-review.yml must be on main first, else it blocks all open PRs). Documented in PR #92 body + rulesets/README.md.
close_reason: Merged in PR #92 — layered per-ecosystem blocking SCA: recorded NuGetAudit (NuGet), added govulncheck (Go) + go 1.26.4/x-net 0.55.0 fixes, added dependency-review-action (cross-ecosystem required check, now live in main-protect ruleset); grype SBOM stays report-only. ADR-IC-014 amended.

title: E.3 follow-up — ADR-PC-008 §S2 in-transaction rate-resolve + constitute append
description: ADR-PC-008 §S2 ('same-transaction resolution as decisive force') wants the rate-sheet resolution and the DepositConstituted append committed in ONE local transaction, so a backdated rate-sheet deploy (effective_from <= constituted_at) cannot read-skew between resolve and append. E.3 (babelstone-eyof) ships resolve->stamp->append as TWO transactions: the stamped tan_basis_points + rate_sheet_version_id are correct and frozen on the event, but the resolve+append pair is not race-atomic. This is an acknowledged, explicit divergence (allowed under ADR-PC-020 §D3 because it is recorded here, not silent).
design: Implement the in-transaction path: add tx-aware overloads IRateSheetStore.ResolveAsync(NpgsqlConnection, NpgsqlTransaction, ...) + IEventStore.AppendAsync(NpgsqlConnection, NpgsqlTransaction, ...) (the existing zero-arg-connection AppendAsync that owns its own tx — the ES_ATOMIC_APPEND_OUTBOX guarantee — stays byte-for-byte intact), plus an AggregateRuntime path; OR a generic engine 'transactional constitution' helper that owns the NpgsqlTransaction so the family decider stays Npgsql-free. Touches the carefully-guarded IEventStore contract — run replay-determinism + adr-conformance before PR.

title: Central Package Management (Directory.Packages.props)
description:
Adopt NuGet Central Package Management to declare every dependency version once at the repo root, instead of duplicating Version= attributes across ~20 csproj files.

Symptom today (versions repeated across projects): xunit 2.9.3 (8×), xunit.runner.visualstudio 3.1.5 (8×), Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.6.0 (8×), Npgsql 10.0.3 (4×), FsCheck.Xunit 3.3.3 (4×), Testcontainers 4.12.0 (3×). Bumping any of these is currently an N-file edit; Dependabot PRs touch every consumer.
design:
- Add Directory.Packages.props at the REPO ROOT (not engine/). MSBuild discovers it by walking up the physical directory tree, like Directory.Build.props — a root file reaches both engine/src/** AND families/term-deposit/** (a sibling tree). An engine/-level file would miss families/, repeating the cross-tree problem that families/Directory.Build.props already works around via <Import Project="../engine/..."/>.
- Set <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>; move each version to a <PackageVersion Include=.. Version=.. /> item; strip Version= from every <PackageReference>.
- Preserve analyzer nuances: PrivateAssets="all" stays on the PackageReference; use VersionOverride= where a project genuinely needs a different pin (e.g. Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.3.0).
- Orthogonal to the existing Directory.Build.props (settings) — both compose.
- Verify: dotnet build engine/Babelstone.slnx is green; dotnet list package shows unchanged resolved versions.
acceptance_criteria: Single root Directory.Packages.props is the only place versions are declared; no csproj carries a Version= on a PackageReference (except deliberate VersionOverride); solution builds green; a version bump is a one-line edit. PR body carries the ADRs-touched/honoured section (touches engine/ build wiring) and passes adr-conformance.

title: A.8 — Event-sink seam for side-effect-free SimulationRuntime
description: Introduce an event-sink abstraction (IEventSink: durable EventStoreSink vs in-memory NullSink) so the append+outbox path (A.2) and the handler-dispatch runtime (A.6) are built sink-agnostic from day one. This enables a SimulationRuntime that runs the pure engine core for forward projection (capability #4) and counterfactual replay (#3) WITHOUT side effects — never writes an outbox row, never mints OpenBao PII material (A.5), never persists a snapshot (A.4) or projection (Epic D). Side-effect-freedom must be STRUCTURAL (the wiring isn't there), not a dry_run flag threaded through AppendAsync. → ENGINE_SIM_SINK. Emerged from the simulation-feature design review; forward projection and counterfactual replay are already committed engine capabilities (event-store §2, #3/#4).
design: AppendAsync is the single mutation point (event-store-skeleton.md §3, §4.5: 'the only place in the engine that touches the events and outbox tables') — so the sink seam goes exactly there. The footgun this story exists to prevent: implementing simulation as a dry_run boolean through AppendAsync, where one missed branch publishes a real event onto the durable bus (a correctness AND PII-on-bus compliance incident — see the outbox commit-boundary in event-store §2 and the no-PII-on-bus rule). Make it impossible by absence of wiring, mirroring how the skeleton makes 'no I/O in handlers' true by absence of a ProjectReference (§3.2). On-existing-instance simulations rehydrate read-only via A.3 then apply hypothetical future events into the NullSink. The boundary surface (MCP 'simulate' verb) and bulk dry-run gate (Q-AQ) are downstream consumers, out of scope here. May warrant a one-line amendment to event-store-skeleton.md / ADR-PC-010 pinning the simulation no-side-effect contract (run adr-conformance before that lands).
acceptance_criteria: 1) IEventSink seam exists; AggregateRuntime/AppendAsync writes through it, not directly to events+outbox. 2) A NullSink (in-memory) variant exists; a SimulationRuntime composes dispatch + fold + financial-math over it. 3) A simulation provably cannot: write an outbox row, call OpenBao/create PII envelope material, write a snapshot, or write a projection — enforced structurally (no project reference / no wiring), and covered by a test that asserts zero rows in events/outbox/snapshots after a simulate call. 4) Pack version, rate-sheet, and clock are per-invocation inputs so counterfactual inputs flow in. 5) Forward lifecycle (daily accrual / month-end / maturity) is generated by advancing the injected clock, reusing the ADR-PC-011 clock-advance pattern — not by hand-faking events.

title: I.1 — Command API → dispatcher
description:
The edge's non-blocking front door for constitution: POST a command, get back a 202 with a process_id and an SSE stream URL, then follow the saga's progress live until it reaches a terminal state. This is the EDGE-over-SAGA contract — not an in-host async wrapper over the engine's direct synchronous append.

Re-scoped 2026-06-13 (first attempt, PR #149, closed without merge). PR #149 reproduced the 202 + process_id + SSE *shape* but wrapped a direct, synchronous `TermDepositConstitutionService.ConstituteAsync` append (resolve→decide→settle→append, sub-100ms, no external wait) on a background task, tracked in a new in-memory `ProcessRegistry` — fronting no saga and using no durable process aggregate. Per ADR-IC-006 §Context / Document 05 §Step-0 the 202+SSE is the edge GATEWAY's contract over the cross-context constitution SAGA, and it exists *because the saga is long-running* (workflow-approval steps sit in HUMAN_DECISION_PENDING "for minutes or longer"; Kong read_timeout is 1800s, ADR-IC-006 §P4). A single in-engine append doesn't clear that bar — the direct synchronous `POST /v1/deposits` (already on main) is the correct shape for direct command dispatch. Dropping the async surface is therefore NOT drift against ADR-IC-006: that ADR governs Boundary 1 (the Kong edge over the saga), not the engine host (Boundary 2).

Correct scope for this issue:
- 202 means the SAGA started (deposit DRAFT, ConstitutionProcess STARTED, ConstitutionRequested in the outbox — Document 05 §Step-0), not "deposit constituted".
- process_id = the durable ConstitutionProcess saga aggregate (H.1, done), not an in-memory registry entry that dies with the host.
- SSE streams the H.2 orchestrator's progress to a terminal state (done), including the per-process authorization check (the requester's token client_id must match the process's owning client; the process_id is not a capability token — Doc 05 §Step-0 note / ADR-IC-006 §P4).
- This is the upstream APPLICATION contract (the Deposits API endpoint + its per-process authz, ADR-IC-006 §P4) that the Kong edge proxies into Boundary 1 — NOT gateway config itself. Build order is app-then-gateway: I.1 ships the upstream 202/SSE route and dispatch; I.3 (Kong config) then proxies it with SSE-aware settings (read_timeout 1800s, X-Accel-Buffering: no, proxy_buffering off). Hence I.1 blocks I.3 (correct as graphed) — I.1 does NOT sit behind I.3.
notes: Scope note (2026-06-13): the SSE /api/v1/processes/{id}/stream endpoint bundled here is a substantial new HTTP surface on the headless orchestrator — may be carved into its own child if finer tracking is wanted. End-to-end SSE-to-terminal depends on the saga actually advancing (orchestrator consume loop, bd t7o3.2).

I.1 edge-over-saga front door on the orchestrator: POST /api/v1/deposits/constitute -> 202 + process_id (PROC-…) + SSE GET /api/v1/processes/{id}/stream that STARTS the saga (one tx, nothing on the bus). Per-process authz bound to the gateway-attested X-Client-Id header (security fix). NOTE: SSE advances to terminal only once the result-event bridge (babelstone-t7o3.8) produces the saga result events; Kong fronting is babelstone-a079 (PR #174).

title: ADR-PC-018: Channel routing for state-changing operations during coexistence
description:
During coexistence, a state-changing operation (e.g. open a term deposit, settle interest) lands either on the new engine (term deposits, v1) or on the legacy core (current accounts, v1-v3). Channels need a routing decision per request.

Three credible locations for the routing logic:
(a) In the channel itself (each channel knows the cutover state per product family).
(b) In a unified API gateway (the bank's gateway routes per product type to the right backend).
(c) In a unified read model (the read model exposes one query API; writes get routed via the read model's metadata).

Contract-shape ADR — should align with the operating bank's existing channel architecture, not introduce a new pattern. Pending channel-team review.

Source: Q-AI in 04-open-questions.md; feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence.

title: ADR-PC-017: Legacy batch ingest contract
description:
The daily batch file from legacy DDA drives LegacyInstanceObserved events (per 02-v1-scope-term-deposits §2.4.2 and feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence §5). Contract-shape ADR.

Decide:
1. File schema (fixed-width vs CSV vs Avro vs JSONL; per-record fact_kind taxonomy).
2. Cutoff times and completeness guarantees (when the file is considered final, what 'late records' look like).
3. Idempotency on re-ingest (file replay vs incremental).
4. Schema-drift coordination protocol (what the engine team does when legacy adds / removes / renames a column).
5. Reconciliation invariant (every legacy instance observed should map to a one-side fact in the engine's view; mismatches feed Q-AG alert thresholds).

Depends on what the operating bank's legacy core can produce; unblocked by a legacy-extract audit (peer to ADR-PC-016).

Source: Q-AH in 04-open-questions.md; feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence §5.

title: ADR-PC-016: Legacy current-account adapter implementation
description:
Strangler-fig coexistence ([01 §6], [02 §3]): which legacy systems the engine ships first-class adapters for vs generic ACL-only handling.

The legacy current-account module is the load-bearing first-class candidate (every term-deposit constitution debits a legacy current account; every interest payment and maturity credits it).

Decide:
1. First-class engine adapter vs generic ACL atop the dedicated ACL service from ADR-IC-012.
2. Connection topology (synchronous calls through ACL vs event-driven through ACL outbox).
3. Idempotency and indeterminate-state handling (per integration_concepts §02, ADR-IC-012 D5).
4. Reconciliation contract (engine outbox vs legacy incoming credit journal — per 02-v1-scope-term-deposits §3).

Pending: the legacy-inventory meeting agenda specified in feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence §12 (ten-dimension questionnaire, three-way classification per system, five named decision outputs). This ADR captures the option space now; the decision lands when the meeting outputs are in.

Source: §1 in 04-open-questions.md.

title: ADR-PC-014: Customer-notification emit contract
description:
Pack-shipped disclosure templates (FIN, SECCI, FINE, maturity notices, annual IRS withholding statements) are specified in feature-design-configuration-surface §3.4; the *trigger* and *delivery* contract is not. Contract-shape ADR.

v1 must deliver FIN (Ficha de Informação Normalizada) for depósito a prazo (per 02-v1-scope-term-deposits §2.2).

Candidates:
(a) Engine emits NotificationDue events per template-ref; a separate system renders and delivers; engine carries no notification state.
(b) Engine emits NotificationDue + carries a notification-state projection (sent / acked / bounced).
(c) Pack-side renderer with channel-side delivery.
(d) Channel-side both render and deliver.

Decide trigger event shape, whether engine maintains notification state, delivery acknowledgement contract, and PII handling for templates that interpolate encrypted fields (coordinates with ADR-PC-004).

Source: Q-AV (cross-cutting) in 04-open-questions.md.

title: ADR-PC-013: AML / KYC gate-vs-post-flag contract
description:
AML and KYC are out of scope as products but in scope as integration shapes (per 00-product-vision §4). Contract-shape ADR.

Two credible shapes:
(a) Async post-flag: constitution completes; AML reviews asynchronously; a compensation flow runs if AML rejects.
(b) Sync pre-gate: AML pre-gates constitution as a synchronous check on the constitution saga (per integration_concepts §05).

Decide which shape (or hybrid — pre-gate for high-risk segments, post-flag for low-risk), the compensation semantics if (a) is chosen, and the legacy-seam implications for products on the legacy core during coexistence (per feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence).

title: ADR-PC-012: GL posting signal contract
description:
GL is out of scope as a product but in scope as an integration shape (per 00-product-vision §4). This is a contract-shape ADR, not a tool-selection ADR — uses the structure declared in ADR-PC-000 (Decision / Consequences / Residual risks; no F1/F2 evaluation table).

Decide:
