title: Brief edits: fold design-notes consequences into the numbered series
description:
Three design-notes companions have shipped, each naming explicit changes to the numbered brief in their "Consequences for the Brief" sections. The numbered brief (00–04) has not yet been updated. Until the edits land, the brief and the design notes are inconsistent — new readers form wrong mental models from the brief and only discover the resolution in the design notes (which they may not read).

This issue consolidates all pending brief edits from the three shipped design-notes documents:

- `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` §4.1 (shipped earlier; some edits may already be in)
- `feature-design-configuration-authoring.md` §9.1 (shipped in commits fce1ce0+bcd79b1+060df6b)
- `feature-design-event-store-projections.md` §11.1 (shipped in e564f36)

## Scope by file

### `00-product-vision.md`

- **§2 (The Wedge).** Add a one-line pointer to `feature-design-configuration-authoring.md` for the falsifiable shape of the wedge (zero engine code per variant; ≤ 5 working days PM commit to production). Do not turn the wedge bullets into commercial promises; the target is internal challenge. (from authoring §9.1)
- **§2.4 (in the wider context the pack is sketched).** Replace the pack sketch with the three-layer model from `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` §3.2 and a cross-reference to the manifest in §3.4. (from surface §4.1)
- **§3 (What's In Scope).** The three-deliverable list currently includes "the product subledger." Replace with "the event store + product projections" — the engine's source of truth (event log) and the bitemporal projections built over it. Cross-reference `feature-design-event-store-projections.md` for the full treatment. Drop "subledger" as a primary concept across the brief. (from event-store §11.1)

### `01-product-architecture.md`

- **§1 (The Cash-Flow Primitive).** Clarify that the cash-flow primitive is the mathematical rule that governs event handlers. The handlers update the event log; projections derive state. The §1 framing remains; the connection to the event-sourced model is now explicit. (from event-store §11.1)
- **New section between §1 and §2.** Title: "The Event Store and Projections." Covers event log as truth, deterministic side-effect-free handlers, bitemporal projections derived from the log, snapshots as performance optimisation not architecture, schema-evolution discipline (events forever readable; migrations versioned), replay correctness as a testable property. Short section; points at `feature-design-event-store-projections.md` for the full treatment. (from event-store §11.1)
- **§2 (The Configuration Surface).** Implies a single artefact family; name three (configs, rate sheets, pack) with the cadences and approvers from `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` §1. Add a cross-reference to `feature-design-configuration-authoring.md` for the three-authoring-layer split (primitives / family schemas / variants) and the named workflow. The Q4 depth question (templates vs DSL) is still open; the layering question is resolved in authoring. (from surface §4.1 + authoring §9.1)
- **§4 (The Regulatory Pack).** Commits to "swappable from day one" without saying what a pack is; cross-reference `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` §3.4 (manifest) and §3.5 (pack pinning invariant). Add the schema-pinning parallel from `feature-design-configuration-authoring.md` §6 so both pinning invariants are visible. (from surface §4.1 + authoring §9.1)

### `02-v1-scope-term-deposits.md`

- **§2.3 (Subledger outputs).** Rename to "Projections" or "Product projections." The four items listed (deposit position, accrual schedule, maturity calendar, withholding ledger) are projections, not subledger outputs. Update prose accordingly. The BdP retail-rate-statistics signal is a pack-defined reporting hook (`reporting.bdp_estatisticas_taxas_juro`), not a separate engine module. (from event-store §11.1 + surface §4.1)
- **§2.4 (event contract).** Several edits compound:
  - `DepositConstituted` gains `rate_sheet_version_id` and `pack_version` from surface §4.1.
  - Add `schema_version` to the envelope alongside `pack_version` from authoring §9.1.
  - Add the three new family-specific deposit events (`DepositPartiallyWithdrawn`, `DepositCorrected`, `DepositTransferredToHeirs`) to the event table from event-store §11.1.
  - Add a separate sub-section listing the five cross-cutting generic events (`PackVersionMigrated`, `SchemaVersionMigrated`, `LegacyInstanceObserved`, `FundsHeld`, `AccountFrozen`) declared by the engine from event-store §11.1.
  - Add `NetInterestCredited` event from surface §4.1.

### `03-roadmap.md`

- **Major restructure: ES pack as parallel track starting v2.** Currently the roadmap sequences v5+ (ES) after v4 (current accounts + cards on PT). Read literally, ES pack work lands after the entire PT product family set is complete — too late for the multi-country-within-2-years constraint. The reshape: pack abstraction work for ES overlaps v2 and v3, not v5. v5+ becomes a *deployment* milestone (turn on ES), not a *design* milestone (start building the ES pack now). Surface this as an explicit parallel track in the phase table. (from authoring §8)

### `04-open-questions.md`

- **§3 (Time-Travel / Point-in-Time Correctness).** Close as resolved. The architectural answer is in `feature-design-event-store-projections.md`: event store with bitemporal projections. Annotate the question with a pointer to that document. The remaining open question (bitemporal implementation choice) is captured as Q-X in the same document. (from event-store §11.1)
- **Fold all lettered open questions** from the three design-notes documents into a new section "Lettered questions from design-notes companions":
  - Q-I through Q-Q from `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` (rate sheets + pack)
  - Q-R through Q-W from `feature-design-configuration-authoring.md` (configuration authoring)
  - Q-X through Q-AC from `feature-design-event-store-projections.md` (event store + projections)
  - Note: Q-K is retired per surface §4.3 (the SaaS-tenancy question is out of scope under single-operator framing); letter preserved for cross-reference stability.

### `README.md`

- Refresh the Document Map row for `04-open-questions.md` to mention the lettered question series once they fold in. Small textual change; verify against on-disk state before editing.

## Verification before editing

Per memory `bd-state-can-lag-disk-reality`: before touching any file, read its current on-disk content and check which edits are already applied (some may have landed via an upstream session). The pattern from this session's earlier work: an upstream session shipped the configuration-authoring document and partially refreshed cross-references. Do not assume the pre-shipment state of the brief.

## Why this is one issue, not several

The edits are tightly coupled. Changing `00-product-vision.md §3` to reference "event store + projections" requires the new section in `01-product-architecture.md` to exist. Adding `schema_version` to the `02-v1-scope §2.4` envelope requires `feature-design-configuration-authoring.md` §6 to be cross-referenced. The lettered open questions cross-reference each other (Q-W refers to Q-P; Q-X resolves Q3). Splitting these into per-file issues fragments work that has to land together for the brief to read coherently.

That said, the roadmap restructure (§03-roadmap.md ES pack parallel track) is the largest single change and could plausibly be split out if scope grows. If so, it should be filed as a child issue, not a parallel one — it depends on the v2 and v5 sections being internally consistent first.
design:
This issue is the consolidation point for brief edits accumulating from design-notes companion documents. The pattern in `product_concepts/` is that design-notes are written first (they're where the load-bearing detail lives), and the numbered brief is updated afterward to summarise and cross-reference them. The brief stays short by design; the design notes carry the depth.

The pattern means:
- A new design-notes document creates a new brief-edits backlog.
- The brief-edits backlog is consolidated, not handled per-document, because edits across the brief tend to interact.
- One brief-edits issue accumulates work until a worker picks it up; new design-notes consequences are appended as they ship.

When this issue is closed and a new design-notes document later ships, file a fresh brief-edits issue rather than reopening this one. Reopening accumulates context across long time horizons; fresh issues keep scope readable.

The roadmap restructure (§03 ES pack parallel track) is the highest-effort single edit and the most likely to be split out. If the worker on this issue finds it growing too large, splitting the roadmap restructure as a child issue is encouraged. The remaining edits are smaller and more interlocked.

Three persistent memories apply:
- `product-concepts-single-operator`: no commercial framing in edits.
- `product-concepts-no-calendar-effort`: project-effort framings remain forbidden in edits to the brief; falsifiable workflow + financial claims are in-scope.
- `product-concepts-terminology`: 'the operating bank' / 'the operating organization' in any new prose.

The `bd-state-can-lag-disk-reality` memory is particularly relevant — verify on-disk state before editing.

title: Two-operating-modes asymmetry — design-notes companion (interfaces for v4, implementations for v1)
description:
The brief admits in `01-product-architecture.md §3` that with-a-plan (v1-v3) and irregular (v4) operating modes share the cash-flow equation but differ materially on operational profile. It warns: "the engine architecture has to be built with the irregular profile as the upper-bound design point, even if the irregular mode lands later in the roadmap. Sizing for with-a-plan only and retrofitting irregular is one of the ways 'one engine, two modes' turns into two engines under the same name." The brief states the warning but does not commit to what "size for the irregular profile from day one" concretely means.

## The asymmetry, quantified

| Property | With-a-plan (v1-v3) | Irregular (v4) | Asymmetry |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active instances | ~500k | ~1.5-3M | 3-6x |
| Events per instance per year | ~24 | ~50-200 | 2-8x |
| Annual event volume | ~12M | ~100M-600M | 10-50x |
| Peak rate | ~100k events on month-end | Sustained 100s TPS, bursts to 1000s | 100x+ at peaks |
| Per-event latency budget | Hours (accrual is batch) | Seconds (balance, fraud, overdraft) | 1000x+ |
| Event source | Engine generates internally | External transactions arrive | Opposite direction |
| Lifecycle | Bounded (constitute → mature) | Unbounded (open → close) | Different state machine |
| Failure mode | Missing accrual = recoverable | Missing transaction = customer incident | Different operational stakes |

The runtime IS the same (event handlers, projections per archie-d63). The operational profile is materially different.

## Decisions landed in brainstorm

### 1. v4 is a committed long-term goal

Not aspirational. The engine MUST be ready to absorb the irregular profile when v4 ships. The unification claim from `01-product-architecture §1` depends on this commitment being honoured.

### 2. Approach C: interfaces for v4, implementations for v1

Three credible answers (A: design for irregular from v1; B: refactor before v4; C: interfaces for v4, implementations for v1). C is the architectural commitment. Interfaces are cheap to get right and expensive to retrofit; implementations are the opposite. Reserving the v4 interfaces in v1 keeps the v4 door open without paying for v4-scale infrastructure in v1.

### 3. Six v1 architectural commitments (non-negotiable)

The six commitments that distinguish Approach C from Approach B:

1. **Event store technology with a clear scale path.** Choice deferred (see #4 below), but must support v4 throughput. NOT something that hits a wall at v3.

2. **No batch-only assumptions in core code paths.** Handler interfaces don't know about batch vs real-time. v1 may invoke them in batch; v4 invokes them inline. Same handler signature, different invocation pattern.

3. **`partition_key` on every event envelope.** Typically `instance_id`. v1 ignores it (runs unsharded). v4 uses it for routing across shards. Reserving the field in the envelope schema is free; adding it later is a breaking schema change.

4. **Projection update mechanism designed for sync OR async per projection.** Each projection has a latency budget. v1 may declare all projections async (eventually consistent within batch window); v4 marks some projections sync (current balance, available credit, overdraft check). The mechanism supports both; the choice is per-projection metadata, not engine code.

5. **Snapshot infrastructure built in v1, even if minimally exercised.** Snapshotting is the hardest part of event sourcing; getting it right takes time. Build it in v1 against modest replay needs (lifecycle boundaries, calendar boundaries); v4 turns up the frequency (every N events) without architectural change.

6. **Synthetic v4-scale load test as part of v1 acceptance.** Even though v1 won't see v4-scale traffic in production, run synthetic high-volume tests against the v1 engine (simulated TPS, simulated event volume, simulated burst patterns). Surface bottlenecks while v1 is still malleable; fix them before v4 commitment hardens.

### 4. Event store technology choice deferred to design notes

Three candidates with explicit tradeoffs:

- **Kurrent / EventStoreDB.** Purpose-built event store. Mature event sourcing patterns; native high throughput; new operational dependency for the team. Ecosystem smaller than Postgres.
- **Postgres-based.** Familiar ecosystem; scales to ~1k TPS without sharding; needs careful sharding strategy for v4. Cheaper operationally; more engineering work to scale.
- **Kafka-as-event-store (Redpanda per ADR-001).** Reuse the bank's event backbone as engine's event store. Single technology; high throughput natively; trades SQL query ergonomics for streaming-first semantics. Unusual but increasingly viable (used by some modern fintechs).

Decision deferred pending team experience and operational comfort. Design notes must capture all three with explicit pros/cons for the operating bank's specific context.

## Interactions with other in-flight design notes

- **archie-d63 (event store + projections).** This issue extends archie-d63's recommendations with operational-profile considerations. archie-d63's "battle-tested event store" recommendation refines to "Kurrent, Postgres, or Kafka — chosen for scale path to v4." The two design-notes documents reference each other.
- **archie-g1a (configuration depth).** Family schemas for irregular families (v4) declare different event types and handler patterns than with-a-plan families. The configuration model accommodates both; the design notes for archie-g1a should mention this asymmetry.
- **babelstone-119 (coexistence).** Legacy DDA's batch-file emission pattern is one async ingest source. v4 card transactions are another (real-time) ingest source. The unified read model must absorb both. Design notes should reference this.

## Open sub-questions to surface in this design notes document

- **Event store technology selection criteria.** Beyond throughput: query patterns, replay performance, schema evolution support, operational maturity. The design notes spell out the decision framework.
- **Synthetic load test specification.** What workload patterns simulate v4? What pass/fail criteria do they trigger? Who owns the test infrastructure?
- **Sharding strategy when v4 lands.** Even if v1 runs unsharded, the strategy must be designed (key choice, rebalance approach, cross-shard transactions). 
- **Real-time projection backpressure.** What happens when projection updates can't keep up with event ingestion rate? Acceptable lag bounds; alerting; recovery.
- **Cross-mode reconciliation.** A deposit maturing into a current account (with-a-plan event → irregular event). How is the cross-mode flow modelled?
- **Operational tooling asymmetry.** With-a-plan tools (manual deposit lookup, batch reports) vs irregular tools (real-time dashboards, transaction search, fraud screening). The engine's MCP server / admin APIs must accommodate both styles.

## Why this is load-bearing

The engine's identity as "one engine, two modes" lives or dies on whether the brief's promise ("size for the irregular profile from day one") is honoured concretely. The current brief states the promise; this document operationalises it. Without this document, the promise is aspirational and the failure mode is years of v1-v3 work followed by a v4 effort that finds itself rewriting the engine.

This is also the one place where the architecture has to think about v4 *now*, even though v4 is years away. Every other design decision in v1 can be made for v1's needs alone (configuration depth, coexistence, event store, projections, build-vs-buy). The two-modes asymmetry forces v4 thinking into v1 — which is exactly what the brief warned about.
design:
Fifth design-notes companion in the `product_concepts/` series. The four already queued plus this one form the architectural commitment set surfaced from this brainstorm session.

This document is unusual in that it forces v4 thinking into v1. Every other in-flight design notes document treats v4 as future scope; this one treats v4 as a v1 design constraint. That's the right framing because the architecture can't accommodate v4 retroactively without breaking v1 contracts.

Three persistent memories apply:
- `product-concepts-single-operator`: no commercial framing.
- `product-concepts-no-calendar-effort`: workflow + financial falsifiable claims allowed; project-effort framings forbidden. The synthetic load test pass/fail criteria are workflow falsifiable claims (in-scope).
- `product-concepts-terminology`: 'the operating bank' / 'the operating organization'.

The user's insight that drove this design notes commitment: the brief warned about the asymmetry but did not commit to what "size for irregular from day one" concretely means. Approach C with the six v1 commitments is what it means. Without this concretion, the warning is decorative.

This document is the most expensive-to-defer of the five. The other four shape the brief's coherence; this one shapes v1's deliverable scope. Every v1 design decision after this lands either with or against the Approach C commitments. Decisions made against them are decisions that have to be undone before v4.

title: Event store + bitemporal projections — design-notes companion
description:
A PM-mode brainstorm pass on the subledger reframed the engine's source-of-truth model. The current brief uses "subledger" as a primary concept (`00-product-vision §3`, `02-v1-scope §2.3`) but never defines its shape. This issue commits to the reframing landed in brainstorm: drop "subledger" as a primary concept; replace with "event store + bitemporal projections" with strict separation between generic engine core and family-specific event logic. This is the largest remaining architectural unknown in the brief.

## Decisions landed in brainstorm

### 1. Subledger → event store + bitemporal projections

The engine's source of truth is the **event store**, co-located with the outbox. State is *derived* by deterministic, side-effect-free event handlers. Projections (positions, accrual schedules, maturity calendar, withholding ledger) are bitemporal tables built from the event store. The CQRS read model, the GL system, and the IFRS 9 system are all *consumers* of these projections; none of them is "the subledger."

Vision document drops "subledger" as a primary concept in §3 deliverables. Open Question 3 (Time-Travel) closes — the answer is "event store with bitemporal projections."

### 2. Event taxonomy: family-specific events declared by family schemas, with cross-cutting generic events declared by the engine

The user surfaced the core tension: the engine must be generic (one engine, many families) but events must be semantically rich (audit trails, regulator-readable). Approach B from the brainstorm is the answer:

- **Family schemas declare their event types.** `TermDepositSchema` declares `DepositConstituted`, `DepositMatured`, etc. `PersonalCreditSchema` declares `CreditConstituted`, `InstallmentPaid`, etc.
- **Family schemas declare event handlers.** Pure functions `(state, event) → new_state`. The handler for `DepositConstituted` lives in the deposit family schema, not in the engine.
- **The engine code is generic.** Event-store primitives, outbox emission, handler dispatch, projection runtime, validator runtime, and a small set of cross-cutting generic events.
- **Cross-cutting events ARE generic.** `PackVersionMigrated`, `SchemaVersionMigrated`, `FundsHeld`, `AccountFrozen`, `LegacyInstanceObserved` apply to any instance regardless of family.

This is consistent with the configuration-depth answer in archie-g1a: family schemas contain everything family-specific (variants, event types, handlers, projections); the engine remains generic at every layer.

### 3. v1 event catalogue gaps

The current 8 deposit events in `02-v1-scope §2.4` are happy-path. Under event sourcing they are *insufficient* — operational events that are inevitable in production must be in the catalogue from v1 or audit trails will have gaps. Two additions:

**Cross-cutting events the engine declares (apply to all families):**
- `PackVersionMigrated` — see `feature-design-configuration-surface.md §3.6`
- `SchemaVersionMigrated` — new, per archie-g1a
- `LegacyInstanceObserved` — coexistence per babelstone-119
- `FundsHeld` — court orders, garnishments
- `AccountFrozen` — compliance holds

**Family-specific events the term-deposit schema declares (v1 additions):**
- `DepositPartiallyWithdrawn` — pack-conditional (some PT products allow partial early withdrawal)
- `DepositCorrected` — clerk-data-entry correction; needed for bitemporal correctness
- `DepositTransferredToHeirs` — succession on death of holder

### 4. GL coupling: raw business events; GL system maps

Engine emits raw business events. GL system maintains its own event-to-GL-account mapping. Cleanest architectural separation. Pushes engineering work to the GL system — coordination dependency to be surfaced explicitly in the design notes.

## Decisions deferred to design notes

- **Bitemporal implementation choice.** Three credible: PostgreSQL temporal extensions, XTDB or purpose-built temporal DB, application-level bitemporality. Each has different operational cost. To be resolved with team and operational input.
- **Replay reconciliation specifics.** Daily checksum cadence, full-rebuild frequency, event-count reconciliation per consumer. Required for "event log is source of truth" to be operationally true, not aspirational.
- **Storage and snapshot planning.** Snapshot strategy per N events / per lifecycle / per calendar boundary; replay performance targets; storage growth modelling.
- **Bitemporality regulatory requirement confirmation.** User answered "yes, mandatory" as assumed; needs compliance/audit confirmation before this is locked.

## Risk mitigations for moderate ES experience

The team has moderate event-sourcing experience (concepts understood; production-scale shipping is new). The recommendation lands with explicit risk mitigations the design notes must specify:

- Mandatory event-versioning discipline from day 1; no breaking changes to event schemas without a migration plan.
- Projection-rebuild drills as part of regular ops; not "if needed."
- Side-effect-free event handlers; side effects scheduled as separate events processed by separate handlers (the outbox is part of this discipline).
- Choose a battle-tested event store: Kurrent/EventStoreDB or Postgres-based. Do NOT build one in-house.
- Snapshots are performance optimization, not architecture; replay must work cold.

## Why this is the load-bearing architectural document

The engine's correctness, auditability, and regulatory defensibility all depend on the source-of-truth model being right. Getting this wrong is the highest-cost reversal in the brief — pack pinning depends on it, family-schema versioning depends on it, the bitemporal audit guarantee depends on it. The reframing also closes Open Question 3 and clarifies the integration architecture's relationship to the engine.
design:
Fourth design-notes companion in the `product_concepts/` series, after `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` (shipped) and the three queued (`archie-g1a` config depth, `babelstone-119` coexistence, `archie-67o` build-vs-buy).

The four documents are tightly interlinked:
- `archie-g1a` (config depth) introduces family schemas + variants + the falsifiable agility wedge.
- This issue (event store) introduces strict engine-vs-family separation; family schemas declare event types and handlers; engine is generic.
- `babelstone-119` (coexistence) introduces `LegacyInstanceObserved` as a cross-cutting event consumed from legacy's daily batch.
- `archie-67o` (build-vs-buy) names legacy-integration ownership as the load-bearing thesis; this document strengthens it by clarifying that the engine's value derives from BOTH the generic event-sourced architecture AND the family-schema declarations that compose with it.

Three persistent memories apply:
- `product-concepts-single-operator`: no commercial framing.
- `product-concepts-no-calendar-effort`: refined to allow falsifiable workflow + financial claims; project-effort framings remain forbidden. Replay performance targets are workflow falsifiable claims (in-scope).
- `product-concepts-terminology`: 'the operating bank' / 'the operating organization'.

The reframing has a significant downstream consequence for the wider brief: the architectural commitment to event sourcing means several downstream patterns become non-negotiable (outbox is part of the event store; CQRS read model is one of multiple projections; counterfactual replay is a property, not a deferred capability). The numbered brief gets updated to reflect this.

The user's question on family-specific vs generic events was the most architecturally significant push of the entire brainstorm session. It dissolved a latent tension in the unification claim (`01-product-architecture §1`) and clarified what the engine actually IS. The answer (Approach B: generic engine, family-specific events declared by family schemas) is intellectually clean and operationally correct; getting this right is more important than any individual implementation choice deferred below.

2. Specifies the four time-dimensional capabilities (as-of queries, audit trail, counterfactual replay, forward projection) as architectural requirements, mapped to the event store + projection model.

3. Specifies the event taxonomy split: family-specific events declared by family schemas; cross-cutting generic events declared by the engine. Names the 5 cross-cutting generic events for v1 and the 3 additional family-specific deposit events.

12. Updates `00-product-vision.md §3`, `01-product-architecture.md` (new section), `02-v1-scope §2.3 and §2.4`, and `04-open-questions.md §3` per the reframing.

title: Vision + architecture revision: build-vs-buy thesis with legacy-integration ownership
description:
The current brief is silent on why the bank is building rather than buying a vendor product (Thought Machine, Mambu, Temenos, Tuum, Vault, Finxact). Under single-operator framing, this is the most consequential claim in the entire brief — and right now it's implicit. A steering committee can re-litigate the build at any point in the next 3-5 years; the brief must contain a durable, defensible answer.

## The thesis landed in brainstorm

**Load-bearing claim**: *legacy-estate integration ownership*. The bank's most valuable asset in this estate is the integration shape between core, channels, payments, CRM, GL, IFRS 9, and regulatory reporting — developed over decades and worth substantially more than any vendor engine. Buying a vendor engine forces a rebuild of that integration; building an engine fitted to the existing integration preserves the asset.

This reframes the engine: it is the new product layer that lets us use our existing integration asset with a better product model. The engine is not the headline; integration is.

**Year-5 TCO inflection (aggressive)**. Build TCO is higher than vendor licensing for the first 3-5 years and lower beyond year 5, given a stable engineering team and a stable pack-maintenance function — both of which the bank is explicitly committing to.

**Honest concessions**:
- *No single component of the engine is unique IP.* Cash-flow primitives, configuration models, and pack abstractions all exist in vendor products. The IP is the integrated fit (configuration model matching our workflow, pack maintained by our compliance team, integration fitted to our specific estate), not the components.
- *Build risk includes "we never finish."* Build-it-yourself core banking has a history of failing. Mitigations are explicit: strangler-fig adoption (legacy still runs if v1 fails), scope discipline (out-of-scope list enforced), the falsifiable agility wedge (zero engine code per variant; PM commit to production ≤ 5 working days), and a cash-flow-primitive thesis that has been mathematically validated in `financial_concepts/§9.2` independently of any implementation.

**Deferred**: the build-failure contingency is not part of the thesis. It lives in a separate risk doc not part of the brief.

## Implications across the brief

1. **`00-product-vision.md` adds a "Why build" section.** Either §1.5 between Problem and Wedge, or folded into §1. States all four pieces: claim, year-5 TCO with implied pace concession, no-single-IP concession, never-finish risk with mitigations.

2. **`01-product-architecture.md §5` reframed.** Currently §5 reads "The Integration Seam" with subsections that say "inherited from `integration_concepts/`". Under the new thesis, integration is the bank's most valuable asset and the engine's reason for existing. §5 should not subordinate integration to the engine — it should name integration as the load-bearing asset and the engine as what honours and extends it. Rewrite the framing without redefining the integration patterns themselves (those still live in `integration_concepts/`).

3. **`00-product-vision.md §4 (Out of Scope)` clarification.** Add a sentence: "Out of scope" means "we don't build the system, but we own the integration." Channels, GL, IFRS 9, payments rails, fraud, KYC are out-of-scope *products*; the *integration to them* is in-scope and is the load-bearing asset of the build.

## Hidden commitment surfaced

The year-5 TCO claim implies a delivery pace (v1-v4 collectively ship and stabilise within ~5 years). The brief deliberately stripped project-effort framings, but the financial claim implicitly commits to one. The vision must acknowledge this: "The year-5 inflection claim implies an aggregate delivery pace that the engineering team is committing to deliver against. The roadmap (`03-roadmap.md`) does not state phase windows, but the cumulative phases must complete within the inflection horizon for the financial thesis to hold."

This is the one place where the no-calendar-effort memory bends slightly: the financial claim is a falsifiable internal commitment with calendar consequences, in the same category as the workflow claims (N=5 working days, zero engine code per variant). Memory updated for both — workflow falsifiable claims and financial falsifiable claims are in-scope; project-effort framings (target windows per phase) remain out-of-scope.
design:

The legacy-integration-ownership thesis changes how the engine reads — from "headline engine with integration plumbing" to "preserved integration asset with new product layer on top."

The thesis is internal-only (the bank doesn't have to defend it externally), so it can be more direct about concessions than a vendor brief could. The concessions (no unique IP, never-finish risk) are what make the load-bearing claim credible.

Three persistent memories continue to apply:
- `product-concepts-single-operator`: no commercial framing.
- `product-concepts-no-calendar-effort`: project-effort framings still forbidden; falsifiable internal claims about workflow AND finance both allowed. Memory needs a small refinement to make this explicit.
- `product-concepts-terminology`: 'the operating bank' / 'the operating organization'.

No new design-notes companion document needed for this issue — the edits land directly in the numbered brief. Open follow-ups (deployment cadence as architectural commitment, ES pack timing in roadmap) remain separate small issues to be filed when ready.

title: Strangler-fig coexistence — design-notes companion
description:
The current brief treats coexistence as a thin subsection (`01-product-architecture.md §5`) and an open question (`04-open-questions.md §5`). Under the v1-done definition committed in this brainstorm — "all new term deposits on engine; in-flight mature out on legacy" — that treatment is materially too thin. Coexistence is not a steady state; it is a **multi-year period** during which two peer systems run the same product family concurrently, with seven dimensions of dual operation the brief does not currently cover.

## Scope of the design-notes document

Seven dimensions of dual operation, each needing explicit treatment:

1. **System-of-Record map.** Per product instance, name the SoR (engine vs legacy) and the rule that determines it (date-based for term deposits; product-family-based for others until v4).
2. **Unified read surface.** CQRS read model that spans both systems. Different sources have different staleness profiles.
3. **Settlement plumbing.** Engine debits/credits current accounts on legacy through the ACL (already covered by `integration_concepts/02`, but needs explicit framing for coexistence).
4. **Reconciliation.** End-of-day comparison: engine outbox vs legacy daily batch file. Alerting on mismatches. This is what Open Question 5 was asking about.
5. **Regulatory reporting under coexistence.** BdP retail-deposit statistics, FGD coverage, IRS Modelo 39 — all cross-system aggregations. Currently silent in the brief.
6. **Cutover mechanics.** Pre-cutover shadow run; cutover day; post-cutover monitoring. The first hours and days of coexistence are higher-risk than the steady state.
7. **End state.** When does coexistence end? What does legacy decommissioning look like? When the last in-flight legacy term-deposit matures or the last auto-renewal cycle completes — whichever is later.

## Decisions landed in brainstorm

1. **Legacy emission shape: daily batch file.** Legacy emits a flat file once per day. Up to 24-hour latency. The unified read model is eventually consistent within a day for legacy-sourced data; near-real-time for engine-sourced data. The read model architecture must explicitly handle this staleness asymmetry.

2. **Regulatory reporting: aggregate downstream.** The engine emits its events; legacy emits its batch file; a third system (the reporting application) combines them and produces unified returns. The engine never reads legacy data directly. This commits the brief to naming the reporting application as a real downstream system — currently it's implicit and worth surfacing.

3. **Renewal of legacy in-flight deposit = new instance on engine.** Auto-renewal at maturity creates a fresh deposit on the engine. Legacy emits `DepositMatured` (in its native format); engine emits `DepositConstituted`. The two events are linked via correlation ID and form an SoR transition. Consequence: the bulk of the legacy term-deposit book migrates to the engine within one auto-renewal cycle (3-24 months), not over the full 5-year maturity tail. Only deposits with `auto_renewal_policy = NONE` stay on legacy until full maturity.

## Open sub-questions to surface in the design notes

- **Cutover day operational risk.** On the first auto-renewal cycle after cutover, every legacy deposit that renews lands on the engine. Day-1 load could be substantial if many deposits cluster on a single renewal date. Needs a load-smoothing strategy or explicit cutover scheduling.
- **The reporting application identity.** Who owns it? Is it in-scope for this product or assumed-existing? It's not on the `00-product-vision §4` out-of-scope list, so its status is ambiguous.
- **Read-model latency contract.** Channels reading the unified portfolio see legacy data up to 24 hours stale. Is this acceptable for all channels (mobile app, branch teller, regulatory reports)? Some channels may need explicit "data freshness" indicators.
- **Reconciliation alert thresholds.** How many mismatches per day cross from "operational noise" to "something is fundamentally broken"? Needs a calibration period and SLAs.
- **Legacy batch file format/governance.** The engine consumes legacy's batch file; what's the contract? Schema? Versioning? Failure modes when legacy ships a malformed file?
- **Customer-facing channel routing during coexistence.** A customer wanting to terminate a deposit early — channel needs to know which system holds it. Routing logic must live somewhere (channel? Unified API gateway? Read model?).
- **End-of-coexistence trigger.** What's the operational signal that coexistence is over? Last legacy instance matured? Decision to force-renew remaining? Worth naming.

## Why this is the most consequential design document

The brief's value depends on v1 actually working in production. Configuration-depth is about velocity *after* v1; coexistence is about whether v1 ships at all without a split-brain incident. Every day the coexistence architecture stays underspecified is a day the bank gets closer to discovering missing operational requirements in production, where the cost of discovery is largest.

This is also the document where the integration architecture from `integration_concepts/` is most tested. The CQRS / ACL / outbox patterns are designed for event-driven peers; legacy isn't one. The design notes must spell out how the inherited integration patterns extend to a batch-file peer.
design:
This is the third design-notes companion in the `product_concepts/` series, after:
- `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` (rate sheets + pack vocabulary, already shipped)
- (issue archie-g1a) configuration depth + falsifiable agility wedge

These companions deepen specific load-bearing claims in the numbered brief without bloating the brief itself.

The three persistent memories apply (single-operator framing, no project-effort calendar but yes product-workflow falsifiable claims, terminology). This document is unusually operations-heavy compared to the others; expect more references to specific systems (the reporting application, ACL, CQRS read model) and fewer to abstract architecture.

The integration architecture (`integration_concepts/`) is referenced heavily but should not be redefined. Specifically:
- `02-anti-corruption-layer.md` covers the ACL contract with legacy.
- `03-cqrs-and-read-models.md` covers the read-model pattern, but assumes event-driven peers; this document extends it to batch-file peers.
- `04-plumbing-patterns.md` covers the outbox; outbox is engine-side only, legacy needs no equivalent.
- `08-event-catalog-governance.md` covers event naming/evolution; new events for coexistence (e.g. `LegacyDepositMaturedObserved`) should be named under the same conventions.

The document does not need to resolve every open sub-question; it must surface them with enough context for follow-up sessions or follow-up issues.

1. Frames coexistence as a multi-year *period* with start, middle, and end phases — not a steady state.

title: Configuration surface depth + falsifiable agility wedge — design-notes companion
description:
A PM-mode brainstorm pass over `product_concepts/00-product-vision.md` and `product_concepts/01-product-architecture.md` surfaced three load-bearing decisions that the current brief either dodges or leaves abstract. This issue captures them and commits to a design-notes companion document that resolves them concretely.

## What the brainstorm established

1. **v1 done = "all new term deposits constituted on the new engine".** In-flight deposits mature out on legacy. This implies a 1-5 year coexistence tail and a concrete cutover criterion: legacy DPZ constitution endpoints disabled, new endpoint on engine.

2. **Build-vs-buy rationale = architectural IP + cost/lock-in.** The bank believes its cash-flow-primitive engine is strategically better than Thought Machine / Mambu / Temenos, not just cheaper or more controllable. This is a strong claim that the vision currently hides; it should be stated directly.

3. **Multi-country within 2 years.** Pack abstraction is non-negotiable from day one. The ES pack must be a concrete artefact within 2 years, which means ES pack work overlaps v2-v3 of the roadmap, not after v4 as `03-roadmap.md` currently sequences.

4. **Configuration model = typed schemas + PM-authored YAML instances + layered authoring.**
   - **Primitives** (engine code, months cadence): cash-flow shapes, day-count conventions, withholding mechanics, etc.
   - **Family schemas** (typed schemas, ~quarterly cadence): authored by engineering + product engineering, reviewed by engineering + compliance.
   - **Variants** (YAML instances of a family schema, weekly cadence): authored by PMs/BAs, reviewed by engineer (technical correctness) + automated validator + risk (rate bands / exposure). Compliance review happens upstream at the schema/pack layer, not per-variant.

5. **Family granularity = coarse-start, fine-drift.** Start v1 with one `term-deposit` schema with optional fields covering known variant shapes. As variants accumulate distinct shapes and the schema bloats, split into focused per-shape schemas. Brief should name this evolution path explicitly.

6. **Agility wedge restored as a falsifiable claim, internal-only.** The previous editorial pass removed the '5 working days' claim because it read as a sales promise. With the staffing/workflow now defined, the agility wedge can be restated as a *testable internal commitment* rather than a sales pitch.

## Open sub-questions to resolve in the design notes

- **Exact form of the falsifiable agility claim.** Two candidates worth considering, possibly combined:
  - *Time*: "PM commit → first booked instance in production ≤ N working days end-to-end, including engineer + validator + risk review."
  - *Code*: "Zero lines of engine code per new variant; new families touch only schema + pack-binding code, not engine primitives."
  - The 'zero engine code' version is more falsifiable and more architecturally meaningful; the time version is more user-visible but depends on review cadences outside the engine's control.
- **Validator depth.** Five layers (syntactic / type-check / pack compliance / regulatory coherence / simulation). Which run synchronously at PM commit time (must be fast), and which deferred to CI?
- **Schema evolution under live variants.** Every constituted instance must pin not just to a pack version but also to a family-schema version. Architecture must state this; mechanism is the same as pack pinning in `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` §3.5 but at a different layer.
- **ES pack timing in the roadmap.** Reshape `03-roadmap.md` so v5+ (ES) doesn't start after v4; pack work overlaps v2-v3.

## Why this is a separate document, not edits to the existing brief

The existing brief (00-04) is short by design. The brainstorm output is *load-bearing detail* behind a couple of the brief's load-bearing claims (agility wedge, configurable surface, multi-country pack). Same shape as `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` — that document deepened §01-product-architecture §2 and §4 without bloating them. This new document plays the same role for the configuration-depth layer and the falsifiable agility claim.

After the design-notes document lands, follow-up issues fold its consequences into the numbered brief (vision, architecture, roadmap).
design:
This document follows the same shape and tone as `feature-design-configuration-surface.md`:
- A design-notes companion to the brief, not a numbered member of the series.
- Deepens specific load-bearing claims in the numbered brief without restating them.
- Opens new lettered open questions (Q-R, Q-S, ...) to fold into `04-open-questions.md`.
- States what changes for the brief at the end (§ Consequences for the Brief).

Three persistent memories already established for this series apply directly:
- `product-concepts-single-operator`: no commercial framing.
- `product-concepts-no-calendar-effort`: no target windows; but a *falsifiable* internal claim (time or code count) is now in-scope per user direction.
- `product-concepts-terminology`: 'the operating bank' / 'the operating organization'; not 'customer/buyer/vendor'.

The falsifiable agility claim is the one place the no-calendar-effort memory bends — it now permits a falsifiable target with a number, on the explicit basis that internal challenge is the goal, not external promise. The memory should be updated when the document lands to reflect this nuance.

title: product_concepts/01-product-architecture.md: write the architectural thesis
description:
Write the heart of the brief — the architectural thesis. Five sections, each one a load-bearing piece of the product's identity.

Section 1 — The cash-flow primitive. Cite and quote financial_concepts §9.2 unification equation S(t+Δt) = S(t)·(1 + r·Δt) − payments + drawdowns. Show how every banking product family collapses to this single equation. Frame it as the architectural insight that makes 'one engine across product families' possible.

Section 2 — The configuration surface. The three variable dimensions from §2.2 (cash-flow shape, day-count convention, compounding frequency) plus charges, insurance, regulatory pack. New products = configuration, not new modules. Note that this is where the 'agility' wedge lives concretely.

Section 3 — The two families inside one engine. With-a-plan (forecast cash flows; deposits, credits) vs irregular (observed cash flows; current accounts, cards). Same primitive, two operating modes — reference §8 and §9.

Section 4 — The regulatory pack. PT pack (DL 133/2009, DL 74-A/2017, BdP conventions, IRS 28% withholding, Act/360); ES pack TBD; EU baseline from CCD 2008/48/EC + MCD 2014/17/EU. Packs are swappable from day one — non-negotiable for the geographic roadmap. If regulation is buried in the engine, EU expansion costs a rewrite.

Section 5 — The integration seam. Engine inherits the architecture documented in integration_concepts/, NOT redefines it: events on Redpanda (ADR-001), schema format (ADR-002), saga participation (ADR-003), outbox emission (ADR-004), observability via OpenTelemetry (ADR-007), MCP server exposure path (ADR-010). Plus the deployment-modes story (SaaS multi-tenant + self-hosted, single codebase) and the strangler-fig coexistence patterns (per-product-line onboarding; APIs to coexist with legacy system of record; event contract that lets legacy and new engine react to each other).

title: Conceptual doc: chat agent channel strategy — inbound and outbound
description: The system's UI strategy is shifting away from traditional web/mobile frontends toward chat agents (WhatsApp, Slack, or custom LLM-powered agents). This changes the architecture in two directions: (1) Outbound — saga completion and status updates must be delivered as chat messages (via WhatsApp Business API, Slack webhooks, or similar), not SSE streams. This is the async notification problem (tracked separately), but the chat-platform specifics (message formatting, conversation thread continuity, handling multi-step approvals via chat reply) need their own treatment. (2) Inbound — messages arriving from chat platforms are HTTP POST webhooks sent to the bank's edge by the platform (WhatsApp cloud API, Slack Events API). The gateway must route these inbound webhooks to a chat adapter service that interprets natural-language or structured messages as banking commands (constitute deposit, check balance, confirm approval). The chat adapter is itself a bounded context and likely needs an ACL to translate platform-native message formats into domain commands. Decisions needed: which chat platform(s) to support; whether a single adapter handles all platforms or each platform has its own adapter; how conversational context (multi-turn saga flows) is maintained across platform messages; how human approval steps in the saga surface as interactive chat messages (approval buttons, reply-based confirmation). Deliverable: a new conceptual document in integration_concepts/ covering the chat agent channel pattern, its integration points with the existing saga/event backbone, and the trust model for inbound platform webhooks.

WhatsApp/Slack acknowledged in doc 11 only as user-side surfaces in front of the agent, not as the bank's integration concern. The async-completion subsection describes three patterns (MCP tasks capability per SEP-1686, explicit polling tool, out-of-band callback) and defers callback wire format to babelstone-087. title: ADR-011: Async saga completion notification — out-of-band callback wire format
description: The SSE stream_url pattern in ADR-006 and doc 05 assumes an actively waiting client (browser, mobile app). For sagas with workflow-approval steps that take hours or days, SSE is structurally wrong: the connection dies when the client moves on. Chat agents and async clients need a callback/webhook model instead: the initiating request includes a callback_url, and the orchestrator (or a dedicated notification service) posts the terminal outcome to that URL when the saga completes. Decisions needed: (1) callback URL registration — field on the request body vs. a separate subscription endpoint; (2) delivery guarantees — at-least-once with idempotency key on the callback payload; (3) HMAC signature on outbound webhooks so the receiver can verify authenticity; (4) retry policy for failed deliveries (transient network errors, recipient downtime); (5) which component owns delivery — orchestrator directly, or a dedicated notification service that subscribes to saga terminal events from the backbone; (6) whether the existing SSE path and the webhook path coexist (bifurcated by presence of callback_url in the request) or whether SSE is deprecated in favour of webhooks for all clients. Deliverable: decision captured in either a new ADR or as an amendment to ADR-006 and doc 00/05.
close_reason: ADR-011 written: pre-registered subscription endpoint (SSRF mitigation), at-least-once with HMAC-SHA256 + timestamp, exponential backoff 10 attempts over 12h, dedicated notification service as choreography consumer, SSE and callbacks coexist. Four implementation principles: subscription lifecycle, delivery envelope, notification service as choreography consumer, 202 response amendment.

title: Editorial pass on ADR-005 (CQRS read model storage)

title: PactNet 5.x unpin when pact-foundation/pact-net#530 (message-verification regression) closes
description:
In plain English: the contract-testing library is pinned one major version back because the newest release cannot verify message contracts (a confirmed upstream bug). When the upstream fix ships, unpin and drop the workaround.

PR #446 pinned PactNet 4.5.0 (Directory.Packages.props documents the symptom); revisit when pact-foundation/pact-net#530 closes: bump to 5.x, re-run both pact halves, remove the pin rationale comments (4 sites). Also fold in the broker-sourced verification flow (publish->verify via the compose pact-broker) once a second repo consumes a contract, and mirror the new notification Integration lane in make preflight (two small residuals from the same PR).

title: Route->spec coverage sweep: assert every mapped engine endpoint appears in some catalogued OpenAPI spec
description:
In plain English: the drift suite proves every documented API matches the code, but nothing notices an endpoint that is documented nowhere — two shipped reads went uncatalogued for weeks and no gate could ever see it.

Add the fourth sweep to Babelstone.ContractDrift.Tests: reflect the mapped endpoint table (needs host composition in the hermetic suite — that is the deferral reason from PR #443) and assert every route appears in some catalogued spec (public or internal). Closes the structural blind side the contract-reviewer named on PR #443 (finding 4).

title: Sweep ExecuteScalarAsync callers for the SUM(bigint)->NUMERIC silent-zero pattern
description:
In plain English: a database sum of whole-number cents comes back from PostgreSQL as a decimal, and one store silently treated that as zero for weeks — every balance read 0. The bug pattern (pattern-match on long with a silent fallback) may exist at other aggregate reads.

Sweep all ExecuteScalarAsync call sites over aggregate queries (SUM/COUNT/MAX) for 'is long'-style pattern matches with silent fallbacks; replace with hard casts that throw on shape drift (the PR #444 remedy: (long)result! + ::bigint in SQL). Found by lane 1 (PostgresMovementLedgerStore.GetBalanceCentsAsync latent since PR #379) and hardened per the replay-determinism review.

title: Engine-side runtime enforcement of documented required request fields (constitute trio + internal callers)
description:
In plain English: the public edge enforces required fields at the gateway, but a direct internal caller that omits principal_cents today constitutes a 0-cent deposit with a 201 — the engine itself never checks. The API description now says so honestly (PR #443); this issue makes the engine reject instead.

Add C# required/[JsonRequired] or explicit handler guards (400/422) for ConstituteDepositRequest's required trio (principal_cents, product_id, funding_account) and extend the documented taxonomy; mirror the DeployRateSheetEndpoint.ValidateEnvelope pattern PR #443 added for rate-sheets. Surfaced by the contract-reviewer on PR #443 (STJ binds missing positional record params to CLR defaults; PackMigrationsEndpoints shows the honest pattern).

title: cd.yml deck-sync leg for the loopback-bound Kong Admin: port-forward step + cd-deployer RBAC widening
description:
In plain English: PR #440 binds Kong's admin API to loopback, which is right — but the CI deploy step that syncs Kong's config now needs a tunnel (kubectl port-forward) to reach it, and the CI deploy identity deliberately has no port-forward permission. Deciding to widen that permission is a security call, then the workflow step is easy.

Named as the tracked follow-up in kong-admin-localhost.patch.yaml (PR #440): add a background 'kubectl port-forward deploy/kong 8001:8001 &' + readiness wait before cd.yml step 4e, AND grant pods/portforward to the cd-deployer Role (bootstrap/cd-deploy-rbac.yaml) — the RBAC widening is the decision, flagged by the doc-consistency review.

title: Staging backup bucket: object-lock/retention within the retention window (ADR-PC-005 §P2 immutability)
description:
In plain English: the off-box backups are now fail-closed and alerted (PR #440), but nothing stops an attacker or a bug from deleting/overwriting the objects themselves — an object-lock/retention setting on the Hetzner bucket makes them immutable for their retention window.

Cheap adjacency flagged by central adr-conformance on PR #440 (ADR-PC-005 §P2 'immutable within their retention window'; pre-existing gap, not that PR's drift). Pair with the credential provisioning of babelstone-zla1.12.5.

title: Staging mTLS remainder: internal-CA client-cert trust for engine/orchestrator callers
description:
In plain English: the gated-off internal-mTLS manifests from PR #440 secure the server side, but the calling services can't present client certificates yet — that trust leg (CA in the image or ClientCertificateValidation pinning, plus callers switching to https) must land before the patch can be enabled.

The reported remainder of babelstone-zla1.12.8 sub-gap (c) (PR #440's internal-mtls.patch.yaml header documents the rollout order). Surfaced as a QUESTION by central adr-conformance on PR #440 — ADR-PC-020 §D3 wants the deliberate gap recorded, which this issue is. Refs: ADR-IC-016 plane (i), ADR-IC-006 §P5.

title: Remove the two x-breaking-change-approved waivers on next OpenAPI spec touch
description:
In plain English: two API description files carry a temporary 'this breaking change is approved' flag that was only needed once, to correct seed specs that never matched the real code (PR #433). The flag must come off on the next edit or it quietly waives future breaking-change checks too.

Remove x-breaking-change-approved from orchestrator-edge.openapi.yaml and engine-reads.openapi.yaml (both marked 'remove on next touch' in-file). Guard: the oasdiff gate must then pass clean against the corrected baselines.
close_reason: Merged in PR #443 (feat/openapi-tier2-completion)

title: Webhook contract polish from §P3 review: customer_ref naming + idempotency-key shape note
description:
In plain English: two small honesty fixes the reviewer flagged on the webhook wire format — a field that has a different name on the webhook than on the bus for the same concept, and an idempotency key whose shape deliberately differs from the ADR's original sketch without the ADR saying so.

(a) WebhookDeliveryClient emits customer_ref where the governed Avro carries customer_id, while a doc-comment claims 'the same field set' — rename or fix the claim. (b) idempotency_key is the composite UUID, not ADR-IC-011 §P2's sha256 form; retry-stable semantics hold, but the divergence deserves a dated ADR-IC-011 revision line. From the §P3 contract review of PR #435.
close_reason: Merged: 3o6m/9z9w via PR #447, qpiw.3 via PR #445, 60n8.* and 2t16.14 via PR #446

title: EVENT_DRIVEN due-source: engine NotificationDue emission + bus consumer + /v1/pii/resolve
description:
In plain English: the event-driven webhook leg (PR #435) ships with a placeholder inbox — nothing real feeds it yet, because the engine does not yet emit the 'notification due' signal onto the bus, and the PII-resolve read it renders from does not exist server-side.

Build the engine-side EVENT_DRIVEN NotificationDue emission (over the ADR-IC-004 outbox), the real Redpanda/Avro INotificationDueSource consumer replacing the Null default, and the engine GET /v1/pii/resolve surface (ADR-PC-004 §P3 render-time resolve-by-reference). Named residuals of bd babelstone-60n8.7 (PR #435).

title: Durable webhook delivery stores + NotificationDeliveryExhausted backbone event
description:
In plain English: webhook delivery (PR #435) works, but its memory of what it owes is in-process — a crash can forget an undelivered notification — and when delivery gives up for good, nothing announces that anywhere.

Replace InMemoryDeliveryOutbox/dead-letter with Postgres-backed stores (crash-surviving obligations, ADR-IC-004 outbox discipline) and emit the §D4 NotificationDeliveryExhausted event on 10-attempt dead-letter. Named residuals of bd babelstone-60n8.4/60n8.7 (PR #435). Also covers the §P3 contract-review note that INotificationDueSource's commit-offset-only-after-enqueue rule is only enforceable by convention until the outbox is durable.

title: MSBuild build-time enforcement of the family→core covenant (ADR-PC-040 candidate C)
description:
In plain English: today the default-deny family-agnostic rule is enforced by a CI test that walks project files; a project that breaks the rule still compiles locally and only fails in CI. This builds the deferred stronger layer: the build itself refuses.

Implement ADR-PC-040's reserved candidate C — a shared MSBuild .targets that fails the BUILD when a project with no/Core <BabelstoneRole> references families/**. Layerable onto the existing marker with no re-decision (the ADR says so explicitly). Natural home: the composition/ subtree (beside Babelstone.Composition, the covenant's mechanism + gates), respecting the ADR-PC-019 §P2 extraction-ready-subtree import concern the ADR records. Keep the CI gates (XC-1/XC-2) as the authoritative layer; this adds failure locality.

title: Control-plane & secrets-at-rest hardening (CIS)
description:
Plain English: the cluster keeps no tamper-evident record of who did what through its admin API, and its internal secret database isn't encrypted on disk. Sub-gaps (verified acceptable-for-staging, deferred):

- [medium] Enable apiserver audit logging. Today: k3s ships it off and the config sets no apiserver args, so a compromise via the admin cert would be invisible. Fix: pass --audit-log-path with an --audit-policy-file (Metadata/Request level) shipped off-box to the LGTM/Loki plane. Refs: cluster.yaml (no apiserver args). CIS apiserver section.
- [medium] Enable etcd secrets-at-rest encryption. Today: k3s --secrets-encryption is off by default, so secrets (including the in-cluster Hetzner token, the kubeconfig, the OpenBao token, backup keys) are base64-only in etcd; anyone with disk/snapshot access (Hetzner rescue boot, stolen image, CSI snapshot) reads them in clear. Fix: provision k3s with --secrets-encryption (or a custom EncryptionConfiguration, ideally KMS-backed) and rotate the key periodically; set at next provision. Refs: cluster.yaml:54 (datastore.mode etcd). CIS secrets section.

Severity (theme): medium. CIS Kubernetes Benchmark (apiserver audit + secrets-at-rest).
acceptance_criteria: Production tier: kube-apiserver audit logging enabled with an audit policy shipped off-box to the LGTM plane; etcd secrets-at-rest encryption (k3s --secrets-encryption / EncryptionConfiguration, ideally KMS-backed).
close_reason: Merged to main (PR #440) — closed by post-merge cleanup per the PR's 'bd issues closed on merge' section.

title: Network & transport hardening (ADR-IC-006 / ADR-IC-016)
description:
Plain English: inside the cluster there are no internal walls — every pod can reach the database, the secret store, and (most seriously) the engine's money-moving command port, completely bypassing the front-door login and strong-authentication checks meant to guard it. And the public surface is wider than the "only Kong is public" posture. Sub-gaps (verified acceptable-for-staging on an isolated synthetic box, deferred):

- [high] NetworkPolicies. Today: zero NetworkPolicy anywhere; any pod (e.g. a compromised Backstage/Mission Control) can hit engine:8080 POST /v1/deposits (a deliberately non-public route — direct access bypasses the saga's reserve/debit legs + edge SCA), plus Postgres, OpenBao, Redpanda, and the Kong Admin API on 0.0.0.0:8001. Fix: default-deny ingress + targeted allows (Kong->engine/orchestrator/mcp only; app->Postgres/Redpanda/OpenBao only) and bind Kong Admin to 127.0.0.1. Refs: kong.yaml:55-56, kong.yml:26-29.
- [high] Restrict the public k8s API (6443) off 0.0.0.0/0. Today: open to the world, guarded only by the mTLS client cert (kubeconfig), because the GitHub-hosted cd.yml runner has no stable egress IP. Fix: a self-hosted runner / tunnel (tailscale/wireguard) / bastion, or allow-list GitHub Actions egress ranges + operator IP (cheap partial mitigation available now). Refs: cluster.yaml:37-41. Recorded ADR-PC-020 §D3 drift.
- [medium] Extend internal mTLS (Boundary 2) to the engine + orchestrator hops. Today: only Kong<->mcp is true mutual TLS; engine + orchestrator serve plain HTTP and verify no client cert. Fix: cert-manager server certs from the same internal CA as mcp-mtls.yaml + Kestrel RequireCertificate. Refs: engine.yaml/orchestrator.yaml (plain :8080), bootstrap/mcp-mtls.yaml. ADR-IC-016 plane (i) / ADR-IC-006 §P5.
- [low] Authenticate the public Backstage portal. Today: backstage.babelstone.dev is fronted unauthenticated through Traefik (bypassing Kong); leaks the internal service/schema catalogue. Fix: Logto OIDC in front, or route via Kong, or restrict the host. (Low: catalogue content is already public in this reference repo and the image is still :placeholder.) Refs: ingress.yaml, backstage/app-config.yaml.

Severity (theme): high. ADR-IC-006 §P5, ADR-IC-016 plane (i).
acceptance_criteria: Production tier: default-deny NetworkPolicies with targeted allows + Kong Admin bound to localhost; the k8s API not on 0.0.0.0/0; internal mTLS extended to engine+orchestrator hops; Backstage authenticated or off the public edge.
close_reason: Merged to main (PR #440) — closed by post-merge cleanup per the PR's 'bd issues closed on merge' section.

title: Production HA & DR hardening (ADR-PC-005)
description:
Plain English: the staging box runs one copy of everything on one machine, so a disk loss costs up to a day of data and any upgrade/reboot is a full outage. Fine for a throwaway demo with synthetic data; a production banking tier must run the HA topology (it already exists as overlays/ha). Sub-gaps (all verified acceptable-for-staging, deferred to the prod tier):

- [high] Postgres warm standby + continuous WAL/PITR. Today: single replica, recovery = a daily dump + daily snapshot (~24h RPO) vs ADR-PC-005 §P1's RPO~0 / <=60s. Fix: deploy overlays/ha (postgres-primary-ha + postgres-standby-ha, pgBackRest PITR). Refs: base/postgres.yaml, overlays/staging/kustomization.yaml (count 1).
- [high] Real OpenBao + key-store DR. Today: dev-mode in-memory, fixed 'root' token, NO key-store backup — event ciphertext is backed up but the keys aren't, so a restore yields permanently unreadable data. M.2/babelstone-puu3. Refs: base/openbao.yaml:45-49. ADR-PC-005 §P4, ADR-PC-004.
- [high] Multi-node control-plane/worker separation + HA etcd. Today: schedule_workloads_on_masters + single-member etcd on one node — a container escape from any app pod reaches etcd + the cluster-admin credential. Fix: dedicated tainted control-plane nodes (>=3 etcd members) + a separate worker pool + PodDisruptionBudgets for zero-downtime upgrades. Refs: cluster.yaml:54,59,61-65.
- [medium] Drill the staging restore + automate retention. Today: restore paths documented but never exercised; retention is manual. Fix: periodic restore-into-clean-namespace drill (restore + projection rebuild + sentinel verify) + object-storage lifecycle + snapshot pruning. ADR-PC-005 §P2/§P5.
- [medium] Retain reclaim/deletion policy on volumes + snapshots. Today: Delete on the snapshot class + the hcloud-volumes default, and the snapshotter SA holds the delete verb — a stray kubectl delete cascades to destroy the backing Hetzner volume/snapshot; protect_against_deletion only guards the node, not the data. Refs: bootstrap/volume-snapshot-class.yaml:14, volume-snapshot-cronjob.yaml.

Severity (theme): high. ADR-PC-005 §P1-P5, ADR-PC-004.
acceptance_criteria: Production tier runs the overlays/ha topology: Postgres primary+synchronous standby (RPO~0) + pgBackRest PITR; real OpenBao with key-store DR; multi-node control-plane/worker separation + HA etcd; drilled restore + automated retention; Retain reclaim policy.

title: Move the projection relay/registry/drainer to a shared host seam so personal_loan read models drain without a co-hosted term_deposit
description:
Plain English: personal_loan's read models (and its bitemporal projections) currently only get fed because term_deposit is co-hosted and registers the single projection relay/drainer. If a host ever composes personal_loan WITHOUT term_deposit, those projections silently never drain. The relay/registry/drainer registration should live in a shared host seam owned by neither family.

Found by central adr-conformance on PR #388 (bd 6cpq.12), severity nit / NON-blocking (no action needed for that PR). PersonalLoanHostModule registers neither a ProjectionRegistry nor a relay/drainer; both its bitemporal projections AND the new read_model.installment_calendar runner drain only through the term-deposit-registered relay. When a host composes personal_loan without term_deposit, the relay/registry/drainer registration must move to a shared host seam owned by neither family (cf. ADR-PC-021 host composition root). Tracking note until such a host exists.

title: Extract LifecycleCommandKey into a thin shared assembly so the driver core stops dragging the engine kernel
description:
Plain English: the new lifecycle-driver host's core library references the engine hosting assembly just to reuse one tiny helper, which drags the whole engine kernel + ASP.NET shared framework into a downstream worker — heavier than the clean notification core, and it breaks the 'extraction-ready subtree' claim the project makes. Move that one helper into a thin shared assembly both sides reference.

Found by central adr-conformance on PR #391 (bd 6cpq.7), severity major / NON-blocking. Babelstone.Lifecycle.csproj ProjectReferences engine/src/Babelstone.Engine.Hosting solely to reuse the pure static LifecycleCommandKey.Derive, transitively pulling Babelstone.Engine + Babelstone.Packs + FrameworkReference Microsoft.AspNetCore.App into the driver core. Trips no family-agnostic gate (driver->engine arrow) and honours LCD-1 (one shared server-side derivation), but diverges from the ADR-PC-036 notification-core precedent (notification core references only Babelstone.Cadence) and undercuts the ADR-PC-019 extraction-readiness claim the csproj asserts. Fix: extract LifecycleCommandKey into a thin shared assembly that BOTH Babelstone.Engine.Hosting and the driver core reference (LifecycleDispatchLedger.DispatchId needs the symbol, so host-only relocation is insufficient). Also consider sourcing the ScaServicePrincipal header-name const from the same shared assembly — HttpLifecycleCommandSink hardcodes a duplicate 'X-SCA-Service-Principal'.
notes: 2026-06-29 (central adr-conformance on PR #404): the kernel-independence premise of this issue is UNDERCUT. The lifecycle driver core now ProjectReferences the two family-core projects (for the installment_calendar read + LoanPosition), each of which references Babelstone.Engine (kernel), and InstallmentRule.cs directly uses Babelstone.Engine.JsonStateSerializer<LoanPosition>. So extracting LifecycleCommandKey alone can NOT make the driver core kernel-independent — the kernel arrives via the family cores regardless. RE-SCOPE or close-as-moot: either (a) accept the family-core kernel dependency as intended (ADR-PC-036 §Decision 2/5) and close, or (b) re-aim at a thin family read-model-infrastructure assembly (the host also drags both family .Application assemblies incl. ASP.NET into the Worker — the same heaviness, host-level). Was filed against PR #391 before #404 landed the rules.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Orchestrator note (parallel run 2026-07-03): this issue's own NOTES already say RE-SCOPE or close-as-moot — the kernel-independence premise was undercut by PR #404 (family cores drag the kernel regardless). Maintainer decision needed: (a) accept the family-core kernel dependency as intended per ADR-PC-036 and close as moot, or (b) re-aim at a thin family read-model-infrastructure assembly. Not dispatched this run for that reason.

title: Verify/backfill WithholdingApplied date for pre-field events (per-tax-year slice)
description:

A WithholdingApplied event stored BEFORE this field existed deserialises to default(DateOnly)=0001-01-01 on replay (deterministic, no clock — §P5 holds), but those legacy flows would carry year 0001 and be silently dropped from the per-tax-year statement slice (WithholdingStatementRule filters entry.WithheldOn.Year == taxYear).

Defer the deep replay + tax-year-sum correctness to replay-determinism-auditor + financial-math-reviewer.

title: Cross-SoR renewal orchestration (DEF-1): legacy DDA matures → new engine instance, linked by causation_id
description:
Plain English: while we run the old system and the new engine side-by-side, a term deposit that still lives in the legacy core can reach maturity and auto-renew ONTO the engine — the old instance closes in legacy, a brand-new engine-native deposit is opened, and the two are tied together by an ID carried in the message envelope. Something has to drive that hand-over, and today nothing does: the renewal saga we built only reacts to deposits that matured INSIDE the engine. This issue names that gap as a piece of work under the deferred legacy-coexistence epic, so it isn't lost inside "SoR routing." No v1 action.

Detail: the engine-native RenewalProcess (families/term-deposit/src/Babelstone.Families.TermDeposit.Orchestration/RenewalSagaModule.cs) auto-starts ONLY on the engine's own DepositMatured fact on the term_deposit topic with a non-NONE ce_autorenewalpolicy header, and its two legs (ConstituteRenewal → LinkRenewal) fold a CLOSING STREAM THAT LIVES ON THE ENGINE (POST /v1/deposits/{closing_id}/constitute-renewal, then /renewal-link to fold Matured→Renewed, where {closing_id} = process_id). In the strangler-fig cross-SoR path the matured instance lives in LEGACY: there is no engine closing stream to fold Matured→Renewed, and DepositRenewed is not emitted (it is engine-native only). Per coexistence §9/§9.1 the new engine instance is linked to the legacy maturity by envelope causation_id → the triggering LegacyInstanceObserved fact → legacy_instance_id. RenewalProcess does not subscribe to LegacyInstanceObserved (the daily batch topic), so it cannot drive this path.

Why it is saga-shaped (and not the existing renewal saga, nor a pure fold): it crosses the system-of-record boundary (legacy core → engine) and constitutes a NEW engine-native instance that inherits constitution's character (gated money movement, Core clearance, precondition gathering); a failed engine-side constitution is a re-constitution needing orchestrated handling; and it carries the day-1 cutover renewal-load risk (Q-AD). That is cross-context orchestration with no current owner — distinct from the (built) engine-native RenewalProcess (bd babelstone-mtto) and from the constitution saga.

Scope (when DEF-1 lands): drive renewal off the LegacyInstanceObserved maturity fact, constitute the new engine instance, and establish the cross-SoR link via causation_id (NOT DepositRenewed). Reuse the existing ConstitutionProcess / SettlementProcess machinery for the engine-side constitution + funding; this issue is the orchestration that triggers and links them across the SoR boundary. No new event types — coexistence §9.4: the transition is the relationship between two existing events. No v1 action.

Anchors: feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence.md §9/§9.1; 02-v1-scope-term-deposits.md §2.4.1 (DepositRenewed "not used for the cross-SoR (legacy → engine) renewal path"); 04-open-questions.md Q-AD (cutover-day renewal load spike); LegacyInstanceObserved is deferred to DEF-1 (engine/src/Babelstone.Engine/CrossCuttingEvents.cs). Gated by DEF-1 (babelstone-ub9s) and Epic 0.6 (legacy inventory). Surfaced by the 2026-06-28 term-deposit saga-completeness audit.
acceptance_criteria:
- When built under DEF-1, a legacy term-deposit maturity with a non-NONE renewal policy drives constitution of a NEW engine-native instance and links it to the legacy maturity via envelope causation_id (NOT DepositRenewed).
- Triggered off the LegacyInstanceObserved batch fact, not the engine's own DepositMatured (which the existing engine-native RenewalProcess / bd babelstone-mtto already handles).
- Reuses the existing ConstitutionProcess / SettlementProcess for engine-side constitution + funding; a failed engine-side constitution is handled (re-constitution / park-in-HUMAN_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED), not left dangling.
- Cutover-day renewal load (Q-AD) is considered in the design.
- No v1 behaviour change; no new event types (coexistence §9.4).
