title: EVENT_DRIVEN notification webhook delivery (former a7d4.2 notify half) — shares 60n8.4's transport
description:
Plain English: deliver the customer notifications that are triggered by a domain event (e.g. "your deposit matured") over the SAME signed-webhook transport the SCHEDULED reminders use. This is the notification half of the now-closed babelstone-a7d4.2, moved here because all notification delivery belongs to this DEF-2 epic and the EVENT_DRIVEN and SCHEDULED legs share one delivery transport — they must not be built twice.

Mechanism: consume NotificationDue(trigger_kind=EVENT_DRIVEN) (ADR-PC-025) from the post-commit outbox/bus; render the instance-pinned pack template; resolve PII at render time via the engine-owned authorised PII-resolve surface (never on the bus); deliver via HMAC-SHA256 webhook (ADR-IC-011) with at-least-once + idempotency on notification_id; strictly post-flag — a render/delivery failure never gates or unwinds the producing flow (ADR-PC-025 slot 5).

MUST share, not duplicate, the webhook/outbox machinery built by babelstone-60n8.4 (the SCHEDULED leg): build the transport ONCE and parameterise by trigger_kind. 60n8.4's own description already names this issue's predecessor (a7d4.2) as sharing its machinery.

Provenance: supersedes the notification half of babelstone-a7d4.2 (closed 2026-06-26). The GL half of a7d4.2 was dropped as out-of-repo per ADR-PC-012 (the GL posting adapter is GL-team-owned; the engine's in-repo GL deliverable — the post-commit outbox + event catalogue — is already live via G.6). DEF-2 / post-v1.

Prerequisites / residuals (may need their own issues if not yet covered): EVENT_DRIVEN NotificationDue emission (engine-side, caused by a domain event) — babelstone-60n8.3 covers the SCHEDULED emission only; and the engine PII-resolve surface (GET /v1/pii/resolve) — an unbuilt ADR-PC-025 residual.
acceptance_criteria:
- EVENT_DRIVEN NotificationDue is delivered over the SHARED HMAC-SHA256 webhook transport (babelstone-60n8.4) with at-least-once delivery and notification_id idempotency.
- Strictly post-flag: a render/delivery failure never blocks or unwinds the producing flow (ADR-PC-025 slot 5).
- The template is rendered from the instance-pinned pack; PII is resolved at render time via the engine PII-resolve surface and never rides the bus.
- The webhook/outbox machinery is SHARED with 60n8.4 (one transport, parameterised by trigger_kind), not duplicated.
close_reason: Closed

title: image-build: arm64 image layers are unscanned (syft/grype resolve the index digest to the amd64 child)
description:
Plain English: now that images are multi-arch, the automated vulnerability scan only looks at the Intel/AMD version of each image, not the ARM version that actually runs in staging. The scan is informational (not a merge gate) and the real blocking dependency checks are architecture-independent, so this is a visibility gap, not a hole in the gate. Worth closing so the ARM layers are also scanned.

Discovered during babelstone-zla1.8 (multi-arch images). In .github/workflows/image-build.yml the anchore/sbom-action + anchore/scan-action run over IMAGE@<index-digest>; syft/grype resolve a multi-arch index to the runner-host (amd64) child manifest, so the arm64 child layers are not inventoried/scanned. Options: (a) run the SBOM/scan per-platform (syft <ref> --platform linux/arm64) and upload a second SARIF category; (b) accept amd64-only coverage and document it. Report-only posture per ADR-IC-014 §A2; the blocking SCA layer (§A1) is source/graph-based + arch-independent, so no gate is affected.
close_reason: Closed

title: L3 — retroactive financial recompute on correction (flow-by-flow re-withholding + reversal/settlement legs) — PLACEHOLDER
description:
Plain English: PLACEHOLDER — we may or may not build this. This epic exists so the decision can be made later without losing the thread. When a correction is retroactive (its `effective_from` predates flows that already settled), the already-paid coupons / up-front interest / completed maturity were computed on the wrong value and are NOT fixed by the prospective L2 substitution. Truly correcting them means re-pricing the elapsed period and reversing/adjusting money that already moved.

Why it's hard, and why it's deferred (this is where "money moves", crossing the store-only / no-settlement-leg boundary PR #339 deliberately drew):
- Re-accrue the elapsed period and re-withhold **flow-by-flow** (financial-math §5.4) — NEVER by rescaling the rate. Rate-scaling is a trap for multi-flow PERIODIC deposits: it diverges from the sum-of-per-flow-nets the withholding audit ledger holds, and contradicts the per-coupon `WithholdingApplied`/`InterestPaid` events already on the stream.
- Emit `ScheduleRecomputed`-style new financial facts + reversal/adjustment legs for settled flows (the moratoria "reversal candidates against the corrected vector" pattern), all bitemporally superseding the originals.
- Needs its own contract-shape ADR (six-slot) + a settlement design; likely Avro/AsyncAPI changes.

Scope of relevance: PERIODIC (already-paid coupons) and ADVANCE (up-front interest) deposits, plus any correction reaching a *closed* deposit (which also requires revisiting the F.3 Active-only gate). For AT_MATURITY-corrected-before-maturity there is nothing to recompute — L2 already yields a fully-correct payout.

Decision point: after L2 (the parent value-semantics epic) lands, decide build vs. don't-build. Until then this is a tracked placeholder, NOT committed scope.

## Success Criteria

- A recorded decision (build / don't build) for retroactive financial correction, with the financial + settlement design attached if the decision is to build.
- If deferred indefinitely: a 04-open-questions entry stating the residual limitation (retroactive flows on PERIODIC/ADVANCE corrections are not auto-reversed) so it is a known, documented boundary.

description:

title: v2 — versioned product-config deploy registry (POST /v1/product-configs), replacing the v1 content-hash product_config_version stand-in
description:
In plain English: v1 pins which product-config generation a deposit was opened under by hashing the product-config YAML (a content hash on DepositConstituted, bd babelstone-fk7m.9 / ADR-PC-009 §A2). That works because product-configs are static deploy-time files — but it means there is no audited deploy timeline for product-configs the way rate sheets have (POST /v1/rate-sheets with idempotency, 409, approval). This issue tracks building that real versioned deploy registry for product-configs in v2.

Technical: add a versioned product-config deploy mechanism mirroring the rate-sheet deploy API (ADR-PC-008) — a POST /v1/product-configs endpoint + a product_config_versions Postgres registry (or a content-hash stamped at an audited deploy), with idempotency/409/approval. Then DepositConstituted.product_config_version pins the registry-issued version id instead of the YAML content hash (the v1 stand-in shipped in bd babelstone-fk7m.9). Governing: ADR-PC-009 §A2 (the content-hash pin is explicitly the interim form; the registry is named as later work), ADR-PC-008 §S2 (resolution-in-transaction). REPLAY_PIN_PER_EVENT already covers the pin; this only changes how the version value is minted.

title: Source the maturity reminder's template_ref + opt-out window from the pinned pack (not family-side consts)
description:
Plain English: the term-deposit maturity-reminder rule currently hard-codes the template name (pt.notice.maturity) and a family-side default 14-day opt-out window inside the family contribution. Now that the pt.2026.1 pack DECLARES template_refs (PR #322, merged) and the engine pack parser tolerates that field, the reminder should source BOTH the template_ref and the opt-out window from the INSTANCE-PINNED pack instead — so every deposit discloses under the pack version it was opened with (ADR-PC-007 pinning), and a template the pack does not declare fails loud rather than silently using a const.

Technical: MaturityReminderRule.MaturityTemplateRef ("pt.notice.maturity") and TermDepositNotificationModule.DefaultOptOutWindowDays (14) are family-side constants today. That already satisfies ADR-IC-019 §D1 (they are out of the generic core — relocated by bd babelstone-9u70 / PR #329). This follow-up tightens them to be PACK-sourced:
- NotificationModuleContext surfaces the instance-pinned pack's template_refs + parameters (today it carries only IConfiguration + the engine base URL). The notification CORE may not reference Babelstone.Packs (an ADR-IC-021 §P2 spine project, forbidden by ADR-IC-019 §P2), so either the host resolves the pinned pack and passes the needed values through the context, or the family contribution (which MAY reference the spine) loads it.
- MaturityReminderRule resolves its template_ref from the pinned pack's declared template_refs and validates it (fail-loud if undeclared), and sources the opt-out window from the pinned pack's AutoRenewalOptoutWindowDays.

Prerequisite: the engine PackParser currently only TOLERATES the template_refs manifest field (the ManifestDto property added in PR #322's parser fix, f4a1246) — it does NOT yet surface it on the parsed PackManifest / VerifiedPack. Exposing template_refs on the manifest (mirroring RateSheetRefNames) is a sub-task here.

Relates to ADR-PC-025 (template_pack_version pinned per instance) and bd babelstone-60n8.3 (the NotificationDue emit contract carries template_pack_version). Surfaced by the PR #329 / PR #322 coherence review (2026-06-25).
acceptance_criteria:
- MaturityReminderRule sources its template_ref from the instance-pinned pack's declared template_refs, not a hard-coded const; an undeclared template_ref fails loud.
- The opt-out window is sourced from the pinned pack's AutoRenewalOptoutWindowDays, not a family-side default constant.
- The engine PackParser SURFACES template_refs on the parsed PackManifest (not just tolerates the DTO field, as it does today).
- NotificationModuleContext conveys the pinned-pack template_refs + parameters to the family module WITHOUT the notification core referencing Babelstone.Packs (ADR-IC-019 §P2 preserved; verified by NotificationFamilyAgnosticTests).
close_reason: Closed

title: Harden flaky key-cardinality latency probe (p99-of-15 trips DEGRADING on CI jitter)
description:
Plain English: the key-cardinality latency probe (`KeyCardinalityProbeIntegrationTests.Seeding_per_subject_keys_keeps_op_latency_flat_as_cardinality_grows`) intermittently fails CI with a DEGRADING verdict even when nothing changed in the crypto path — it flaked on PR #316, whose diff (engine cross-cutting events) is completely disjoint from the load harness. The probe is meant to catch a real per-key latency *slope* as key cardinality grows; right now it trips on transient single-request jitter against the dev-mode OpenBao container. Harden it so it keeps the falsifiable scaling signal but stops flaking on CI-runner noise.

Root cause (engine/load/Babelstone.LoadHarness/KeyCardinalityProbe.cs):
- `LatencyIsFlat(toleranceFactor = 4.0)` compares the MAX-cardinality checkpoint's p99 against the FIRST checkpoint's p99 (per op: encrypt/decrypt/destroy), with a 5 ms NoiseFloor. Sound shape.
- BUT the test calls `SeedAndMeasureAsync(totalSubjects: 400, checkpointEvery: 100, seed: 4242, sampleSize: 15)`. With `sampleSize: 15`, the nearest-rank p99 (`Percentile`, no interpolation) is the 15th-of-15 ordered sample — i.e. effectively the SLOWEST single op in the window. So the "p99" at the 400-key checkpoint is one HTTP round-trip's tail latency to a containerised OpenBao; one contended request flips FLAT→DEGRADING.
- Observed flake on PR #316: `at 400 keys: encrypt p99=76.5ms, decrypt p99=33.3ms, destroy p99=75.8ms` → encrypt 400-key slowest-of-15 exceeded 4× the 100-key slowest-of-15.

Candidate fixes (pick in the implementing change; preserve the slope signal):
- Raise `sampleSize` so p99 is a genuine tail percentile over a meaningful window (e.g. 100+), not max-of-15 — the cheapest, most direct fix.
- And/or judge the cardinality slope on a robust central statistic (median / p50, or a trimmed mean) rather than p99 — slope detection doesn't need the tail, and the tail is dominated by container/HTTP jitter on a dev-mode single-node OpenBao. Keep a (looser) tail guard if a tail signal is still wanted.
- And/or add warm-up iterations whose timings are discarded (drop cold-start/JIT/connection-pool spikes), and/or take N measurement rounds and compare medians-of-rounds.

Invariant to keep (do NOT weaken): per-subject named keys scale without per-key op degradation (ADR-PC-004 §P2/§P3) — the production sizing pass dials cardinality to v4 scale on a Raft cluster. The CI probe must still FAIL on a genuine sustained slope, only stop failing on single-sample transient spikes.
acceptance_criteria:
- KeyCardinalityProbeIntegrationTests no longer flips FLAT→DEGRADING on a single transient slow OpenBao round-trip: the cardinality-slope verdict is judged on a robust statistic (larger sampleSize so p99 is a real tail percentile, and/or median/trimmed-mean for the slope, and/or warm-up discards / multi-round medians).
- The probe STILL fails on a genuine sustained per-key latency slope as cardinality grows (the ADR-PC-004 §P2/§P3 falsifiable signal is preserved, not weakened).
- The change is confined to engine/load/Babelstone.LoadHarness (KeyCardinalityProbe.cs) and its test; no production engine/crypto code changes.
- Rationale for the chosen threshold/statistic is documented in the probe so the next reader knows why it is shaped that way.
notes: PR #328 opened (branch fix/key-cardinality-probe-flake): slope verdict now judged on the median (p99 reported as context), warm-up discards added, integration test sampleSize 100. Falsifiable ADR-PC-004 §P2/§P3 / Residual-Risk-6 signal preserved (a genuine sustained slope still fails); flake removed. Awaiting maintainer merge — close on merge per PR hand-off section.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide & build operation-constraining semantics for FundsHeld (legal hold) / AccountFrozen (compliance freeze)
description:
Plain English: PR #316 (bd babelstone-5w90) shipped `FundsHeld` (a legal / court-order / garnishment hold) and `AccountFrozen` (a compliance / AML / sanctions freeze) as STORE-ONLY audit facts — their folds are deliberate no-ops, so recording one today neither earmarks funds nor blocks any operation. For v1 that is correct (ADR-IC-017 §P1). But a production engine eventually has to ACT on them: a legal hold should make the held amount unspendable, and a compliance freeze should block debits/withdrawals on the instance until it lifts. This issue tracks DECIDING and BUILDING those operation-constraining semantics — explicitly a new ADR-PC decision, per 5w90's own scope note, not a completeness fix on the store-only facts.

The open design question (the gap this issue exists to close): ADR-PC-033 (the Account abstraction; the engine half is tracked by babelstone-hkwp.3) models AUTHORIZATION holds — a *different* concern — via a NEW event family `operations.HoldPlaced -> HoldCaptured | HoldExpired` that drives `available balance = accounting balance - Σ active holds`. ADR-PC-033 and hkwp.3 are SILENT on legal holds and compliance freezes (verified: no mention of freeze / court / legal / compliance / AML / sanctions). So decide:

  (a) do FundsHeld / AccountFrozen fold into that same active-hold / available-balance machinery (a legal hold = an active hold that lowers available balance; a freeze = a total block), or
  (b) do they get their own freeze/block guard in the authorization decider (ADR-PC-030 §P3 stages 3-5), distinct from the authorization-hold ledger?

Either way, reconcile with babelstone-hkwp.3 / ADR-PC-033 so the two hold concepts (operational/regulatory holds vs authorization holds) coexist cleanly under the synthetic `operations` aggregate_type and do not collide on the simple-name-keyed codec.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new ADR-PC decision states how FundsHeld (legal hold) and AccountFrozen (compliance freeze) constrain operations, and how they relate to the ADR-PC-033 authorization-hold lifecycle: folded into available balance vs. a separate freeze/block guard.
- The decision is reconciled with babelstone-hkwp.3 / ADR-PC-033 so legal/compliance holds and authorization holds coexist cleanly under the operations aggregate_type (no simple-name codec collision).
- If enforcement is built: a frozen instance refuses debits/withdrawals until the freeze lifts (freeze_expires_at or an explicit unfreeze fact); a legal hold lowers spendable funds by held_amount_cents. Fold-purity / replay-determinism (ADR-PC-010) is preserved.

title: C.7 follow-up — implement SchemaVersionMigrated operator migration write-path (ADR-PC-009 §P3)
description:
Plain English: a live instance is locked to the family-SCHEMA version it was constituted under, and — exactly like a pack migration — the only sanctioned way to move it to a newer schema (when the bank consolidates) is an explicit, audited operator migration. PR #316 (bd babelstone-5w90) built the READ/fold half of `SchemaVersionMigrated`: a store-only no-op fold, because the pin rides the event ENVELOPE, not the projection (ADR-PC-009 §P1/§P3/§B). The WRITE half — the operator command that actually emits `SchemaVersionMigrated` and re-pins the stream from that sequence forward — is unbuilt and was untracked. This issue tracks building it: the schema twin of the now-closed PackVersionMigrated write-path (babelstone-fk7m.10).

Designed shape (ADR-PC-009 §P3):
  SchemaVersionMigrated { instance_id, from_schema_version, to_schema_version, migration_id, operator_actor }
operator-initiated, one event per affected instance, the envelope `schema_version` moving to `to_schema_version` from that sequence forward while prior history stays pinned to `from_schema_version`; `migration_id` is the idempotency / dedupe key.

Follow the fk7m.10 pattern: operator command + idempotent append keyed by migration_id + an instance_filter predicate over the read model (cf. babelstone-7giq, which did the predicate for the pack case). The fold stays a no-op — do NOT add a projection-column pin (ADR-PC-009 §B forbids it). Lower priority than the pack write-path: annual pack rollover is a v1 need, engine-schema evolution is rarer/later (v2+).
acceptance_criteria:
- An operator command emits SchemaVersionMigrated for the targeted instance(s), idempotent on migration_id (re-issuing for an already-migrated instance is a no-op).
- The envelope schema_version moves to to_schema_version from that sequence forward; prior history stays pinned to from_schema_version (ADR-PC-009 §P1/§P3).
- The fold remains a no-op — no projection-column pin (ADR-PC-009 §B).
- Round-trip/replay tests cover the write path; mirrors the PackVersionMigrated write-path (babelstone-fk7m.10).
notes: 2026-06-24: Now realized via the generic bulk-operations runner (babelstone-qpiw.5), not a bespoke schema write-path. Tracked under epic babelstone-qpiw; depends on the runner core babelstone-qpiw.3.
close_reason: Realized via the generic bulk-operations runner (babelstone-qpiw.5 wires the SchemaVersionMigrated adapter), not a bespoke write-path. Superseded by epic babelstone-qpiw.

title: Observed capture/settlement feed contract — schema, dedup, gap-detection ownership
description: Plain English: ADR-PC-032 names an 'Observed' movement origin — an already-cleared movement (e.g. a card capture, a Core-side posting) that arrives via an upstream feed and is recorded only (no cash leg to drive). v1 has NO Observed producer (specified-but-dormant). This task specifies the feed contract: the movement-id dedup key, the schema, and who owns gap-detection. A live producer arrives with shape 3. Governed by ADR-PC-032 (slot 2/3) + ADR-PC-030 §176.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pack-migration preview/emit pagination + cap for large predicate-selected populations (bd babelstone-7giq follow-up)
description: In plain English: the pack-migration predicate instance_filter (bd babelstone-7giq) resolves the whole live population and the preview/migrate loop does one event-store head read per matched instance, with no cap or pagination. That is fine at v1/demo scale, but a large active population means N stream reads per request. Add pagination and/or a cap (and surface the matched count) to the POST /v1/pack-migrations preview and emit paths. Deferred from babelstone-7giq per the maintainer decision to ship uncapped in v1 (PR #295).
notes: 2026-06-24: Superseded by the bulk-operations runner epic babelstone-qpiw. PR #324 will NOT be merged (maintainer decision); the cap becomes the runner batch size, and matched_count + the LIMIT-bounded read are salvaged into babelstone-qpiw.3 / babelstone-qpiw.5. Recommend closing this issue as superseded once the epic lands. See babelstone-qpiw.5.
close_reason: Superseded by epic babelstone-qpiw (Bulk cross-cutting operations runner). PR #324 closed unmerged; the cap becomes the runner batch size; matched_count + LIMIT-bounded read + tests salvaged into babelstone-qpiw.3 / babelstone-qpiw.5.

title: Constitution saga composes the shared settlement leg (rule-of-three cleanup)
description: Plain English: the deposit constitution saga keeps its own rich lifecycle in pass 1 and still hand-invokes reserve/confirm; once the shared settlement leg is proven on the standalone legs, refactor constitution to compose it too, so there is a single leg implementation. Deferred cleanup, not pass 1. Design: feature-design-money-movement-settlement.md §4.2, §10.
acceptance_criteria: - The constitution debit leg is expressed via the shared substrate settlement-leg machinery rather than a hand-coded copy; the constitution saga's approval-fork lifecycle is unchanged; gated-settlement integration tests stay green.
close_reason: Merged in PR #341 (settlement substrate: multi-direction Movement fan-out, settlement-leg step-up-SCA gate, constitution shared-leg cleanup).

title: Delete the eager ISettlementPort / SettlementInstruction / LoggingSettlementPort
description: Plain English: once every cash leg goes through the Movement pattern, delete the old eager settlement port, its DTO, and the stub entirely — Babelstone isn't live, so no compromise is carried forward. Gated by MOVEMENT_APPEND_FIRST (green = no eager callers left). Design: feature-design-money-movement-settlement.md §5, §9 step 6.

- ISettlementPort, SettlementInstruction, and LoggingSettlementPort removed; no references remain in engine/ or families/.
- MOVEMENT_APPEND_FIRST green (zero eager settle call-sites) before deletion; build + all tests green after.
close_reason: Closed

title: Partial-withdrawal credit leg (DEF-1) needs withdrawn-portion accrual/withholding the v1 event does not carry
description:
Plain English: paying a customer for a partial early withdrawal is deliberately out of scope for v1 — today the engine only reduces the principal and moves no money. But when the payout leg IS built later (under the deferred legacy-ACL work), it will need the interest and tax on the withdrawn slice, and the event we record today does not carry those numbers. This is a heads-up so the future credit leg isn't blocked by a missing field.

Detail: WithdrawPartiallyAsync appends DepositPartiallyWithdrawn only and makes NO settlement call — correct per v1 scope (02 section 2.4.1: "reduces the principal"; F.12 shipped decider-only). The DepositPartiallyWithdrawn payload is { deposit_id, withdrawn_amount_cents, remaining_principal_cents, withdrawn_on } — no withholding/interest field. But ADR-PC-016 section 1 and coexistence section 4 specify creditPartialWithdrawal as "withdrawn principal + net accrued interest on the withdrawn portion." So when the DEF-1 credit leg is built, the withdrawn-portion accrued interest + withholding must be computed/carried, which the current store-only event omits.

Scope: when the partial-withdrawal credit leg is built under DEF-1, either compute the withdrawn-portion accrual/withholding at settlement time or extend the event to carry it. Fold into the lifecycle-credit settlement concept. No v1 action.

Anchors: ADR-PC-016 section 1, feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence.md section 4; gated by DEF-1 (babelstone-ub9s). Surfaced by the 2026-06-21 term-deposit feature-completeness audit.
acceptance_criteria:
- The partial-withdrawal credit leg, when built under DEF-1, sources the withdrawn-portion net accrued interest + withholding (computed at settlement or carried on the event).
- Resolved as part of the lifecycle-credit settlement concept, not a separate fork.
- No v1 behavior change (partial withdrawal stays principal-reduction-only until DEF-1).
notes:
GROOMED 2026-06-25 — aligned to ADR-PC-032 (the Movement primitive, Accepted 2026-06-23), mirroring sibling t7o3.13's 2026-06-23 re-scope which this issue predates (created 2026-06-21). Plain English: nothing about v1 changes — partial withdrawal stays principal-reduction-only (store-only DepositPartiallyWithdrawn, no settlement call) — this note just re-points the future credit leg at the architecture that landed after the issue was filed.

The "lifecycle-credit settlement concept" this issue folds into is now the single shared substrate settlement saga (SettlementProcess, bd t7o3.15) decided by ADR-PC-032 — a confirmation-gated Credit leg parameterised by Movement direction, NOT a per-operation fork. So when the DEF-1 credit leg is built, partial withdrawal records an Originated Movement (Credit) carrying withdrawn principal + net accrued interest + withholding on the withdrawn portion (the fields the v1 event omits, per this issue's body); the SettlementProcess auto-starts from the Movement's CloudEvents headers via the engine populate hop (bd t7o3.20). Append-first finality + park-on-failure, no compensation (ADR-IC-003 §P6), exactly as t7o3.13's credit legs.

Re-homed under the DEF-1 epic ub9s (was top-level, related-only). Still gated by DEF-1 (real ACL, babelstone-ub9s); no v1 action.

title: Decide whether a succession heir-credit becomes a 6th confirmation-gated settlement command or stays downstream-observed
description:
Plain English: when a deposit holder dies, the engine RECORDS the transfer to heirs (the event, fold, lifecycle state and projection all exist), but nothing actually moves money to an heir's account, and the design has never decided whether it ever should. The five-command settlement contract (constitution debit + interest/maturity/early-termination/partial-withdrawal credits) deliberately omits a heir credit. This is an undecided contract, not a missing implementation — so the action is to decide, not to build.

Verified state: DepositTransferredToHeirs is store-only and structurally complete as a RECORDING terminator (event Events.cs:259, fold Handlers.cs, projection, lifecycle row TransferToHeirs). There is NO decider/command/service/endpoint/saga that emits or settles it (grep-confirmed; constructed only in a dispatch test). The settlement-command table (feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence.md, ADR-PC-016) lists exactly FIVE commands; transfer-to-heirs is absent. ADR-PC-030 establishes the engine "records" upstream-decided succession; it does not run the workflow.

Decide and record (contract-shape note or a future ADR-PC): does an actual money credit to an heir's current account ever become a SIXTH confirmation-gated settlement leg (same family as the other credits, ADR-PC-016 slot 5), or does the heir money movement stay the upstream succession authority's responsibility with the engine emitting only the observed fact (ADR-PC-030 recorded-not-executed)? Until decided, build nothing — adding a decider/command/saga now would build ahead of an undecided contract.

Anchors: ADR-PC-016, ADR-PC-030, ADR-PC-012 (transfer-to-heirs is in the GL-relevant accounting subset). Surfaced by the 2026-06-21 term-deposit feature-completeness audit as under-specified-by-design.
acceptance_criteria:
- A recorded decision (contract-shape note or ADR-PC) states whether a succession heir-credit is a 6th confirmation-gated settlement command or stays a downstream-observed fact.
- If it becomes a settlement leg, it is folded into the lifecycle-credit settlement concept; if observed-only, the recorded-not-executed stance (ADR-PC-030) is made explicit for succession.
- No implementation is built ahead of the decision.
notes: Decided: observed-only / recorded-not-executed (NOT a 6th settlement command). PR #293 (branch docs/k6r8-heir-credit-recorded-not-executed): ADR-PC-030 names succession recorded-not-executed + v4 re-opening trigger; ADR-PC-012 dated amendment drops transfer-to-heirs from the engine-emitted GL subset (store-only, never on bus). ADR-PC-016 five-command table unchanged. Closes on merge.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add an operator correction command/decider/endpoint that appends DepositCorrected
description:
Plain English: the hard part of corrections — the bitemporal "what we thought vs what we now know" supersession in the read model — is already built and passing an end-to-end acceptance test. What's missing is the simple front door: there is no command or endpoint an operator can call to make a correction; today the DepositCorrected event can only be appended by hand in a test.

Verified state: the bitemporal supersede-then-insert runtime exists (PostgresProjectionStore.SupersedeAndWriteAsync, ADR-PC-002 section P2) and the D.5 ForcedCorrectionRoundTripTests pass on the real term_deposit family (CurrentBelief, AsOf disavowed belief, supersession history, nothing deleted). The DepositCorrected event record, pure fold (tallies CorrectionCount), lifecycle transition (Correct->Active) and family-module registration all exist. What is absent (grep-confirmed): any "correct" command/decider/service-method/endpoint — the D.5 test docstring states "the service has no correction command yet."

Scope: a thin operator-only application surface — a correction command + decider + endpoint that appends DepositCorrected with AppendContext.ValidTime = effective_from (mirroring how the D.5 test constructs the event), guarded to ops actors. No ADR amendment needed; additive to ADR-PC-002 Path A. Not a saga, no money movement (store-only event, opaque value refs, no PII per ADR-PC-004 section P2).

Anchor: ForcedCorrectionRoundTripTests (D.5). Surfaced by the 2026-06-21 term-deposit feature-completeness audit as "partially-implemented" (mechanism done; application surface missing).
acceptance_criteria:
- An operator-guarded correction command + decider exist that append DepositCorrected with valid-time = effective_from.
- An endpoint exposes it (ops-actor-guarded), mirroring the D.5 test's event construction.
- A test covers the command path (not just the hand-appended event).
- No change to the existing bitemporal supersession runtime (already built and tested).
close_reason: Merged in PR #339 (operator correction command/decider/endpoint appending DepositCorrected).

title: Add a per-subject/per-family Avro compat seam + day-one shape-lock snapshots
description: Plain English: schema compatibility is one global BACKWARD default applied to every subject via an env var, and brand-new subjects pass the gate trivially with nothing locking their day-one shape. Add a per-subject or per-family compat seam to avro-compat-check.sh (e.g. a sidecar or x-compat field) and a golden-snapshot that locks each new subject shape so a day-one field-type mistake is caught by a gate, not only review. BACKWARD is correct for these five subjects; this is estate-readiness. Evidence: avro-compat-check.sh COMPAT_LEVEL global default; new loans.* subjects skip the compat leg.
acceptance_criteria:
- avro-compat-check.sh supports a per-subject/per-family compat override.
- Each new subject has a shape-lock snapshot test.
- BACKWARD remains the default; no regression for existing subjects.
close_reason: Merged in PR #340 (per-subject/per-family Avro compat seam + day-one shape-lock snapshots).

title: Keep consumer/reconciliation + Backstage descriptors family-symmetric (acl/notification loan coverage; stale header)
description: Plain English: the loan events list acl and notification as consumers, but the reconciliation contracts cover only term-deposit projections, and the Backstage descriptor still calls itself the term-deposit catalogue. Add personal_loan projection coverage (or an explicit no-projection note) to the acl/notification reconciliation contracts, generalise the catalog-info.yaml header to multi-family, and consider a gate that every authorized consumer has reconciliation coverage for that family. Evidence: LoanDisbursed.asyncapi x-authorized-consumers; acl.reconciliation.yaml term_deposit-only; catalog-info.yaml:1 header.

- catalog-info.yaml self-description is multi-family.

title: Decide the engine-owned-closed-enum-on-the-wire convention (finalidade free-string Avro vs closed CUE)
description: Plain English: the loan purpose is a strictly-closed enum in the config schema but a free string on the event that rides the bus, so the wire contract is weaker than the config contract. Decide and document whether engine-owned closed taxonomies are deliberately free-string on the Avro wire (preserving additive evolution) or should be re-asserted as Avro enums, so the next family does not re-derive the choice. Evidence: LoanDisbursed.avsc finalidade type string; credito-pessoal.cue #Finalidade closed enum.
acceptance_criteria:
- A recorded convention (contracts/avro README or ADR) states whether engine-owned closed enums are free-string on the wire and why.
- finalidade conforms to the chosen convention.
- The convention is reusable by the next family.
close_reason: Resolved by PR #283 commit a2fbd1d: the loan-purpose wire field was renamed finalidade->purpose (Avro + CUE #Purpose + catalogue + code + regenerated docs), and all Portuguese prose in the family code/contracts was translated to English. The decision is recorded by the change itself — the wire field is plain English (purpose, a string), the closed taxonomy (general|education|health|renewables|equipment) stays engine-owned in CUE. No Avro enum re-assertion on the wire (subject is new pre-merge; additive-evolution posture preserved).

title: Promote shared CUE vocabulary (#PrincipalBounds, rate-ref fragments) into common.cue
description: Plain English: two family CUE schemas each define their own identical copy of the principal-bounds shape rather than sharing one, the first instance of per-family vocabulary forking. Promote #PrincipalBounds (and recurring rate-ref fragments) into common.cue, which every family already unifies against, so a bounds-semantics change is one edit not N. If standalone family schemas are deliberate, record it as an ADR-PC-006 amendment. Evidence: term-deposit.cue:185 and personal-loan.cue both define #PrincipalBounds; common.cue holds shared #Cents/#RateRef.
acceptance_criteria:
- Shared CUE shapes duplicated across families are promoted to common.cue, OR the standalone choice is recorded as a governed decision.

title: Wire personal_loan into pack-validate depth-3/4 (registry hardcoded to term_deposit); prefer file-discovery
description: Plain English: the Go pack validator has a hardcoded family list containing only term_deposit, so its deeper pack checks cannot run for loans and a real pack declaring a loan would be rejected as unknown. Wire personal_loan in (registry entry + depth-3/4 rules + a fixture-driven test), or better, replace the hardcoded map with file-discovery from contracts/cue/families/*.cue, mirroring how the Avro and AsyncAPI globs self-discover. The depth-1/2 CUE schema is already gated by contracts/cue/check.sh. Evidence: pack-validate/internal/validate/family.go:18-24,39-45.
acceptance_criteria:
- pack-validate recognises personal_loan (registry entry or file-discovery) and runs the appropriate depth checks.
- A fixture-driven test walks the valid/invalid loan fixtures through the binary.
- A pack declaring personal_loan validates rather than failing unknown-family.

title: Record the missing distressed/arrears lifecycle states as an explicit scope decision
description: Plain English: real loans can be late, partial, or in arrears, but this family models none of that; the only exit from a troubled loan is the terminal write-off. Record an explicit scope decision that the v1 loan lifecycle is the good/closed binary (collections upstream, ADR-PC-030) and that arrears/grace/restructure will be additive new states + transition rows when a richer loan family lands. Evidence: LoanLifecycle enum has no distressed state; LifecycleTransitions all operating transitions only from Active; no missed-installment event.
acceptance_criteria:
- ADR-PC-031 (or ADR-PC-030) records the v1 lifecycle scope cut as a decision, naming arrears/grace/restructure as future additive states.
- The recorded-not-executed option for PARI/PERSI transitions is noted.
- No code change unless a distressed state is brought into scope.
close_reason: Merged via PR #315.

title: Disambiguate the write-off terminal in the read model: add WrittenOffAmount to LoanPosition
description: Plain English: a written-off loan shows the same zero balance as a fully-repaid one, and the lost amount is not on the position, so reconciling principal needs a second event. Add a WrittenOffAmount (or LossRecognised) field to LoanPosition so a written-off loan reconciles principal from the position alone and the OutstandingBalance=0 overload is disambiguated. Evidence: Handlers.cs LoanWrittenOffHandler sets OutstandingBalance Zero; Events.cs LoanWrittenOff carries the loss; LoanPosition has no loss field.
acceptance_criteria:
- LoanPosition carries the written-off loss amount so principal reconciles from the position alone.
- A written-off loan is distinguishable from a settled one without reading the event log.
- Fold/projection tests cover it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make the fin-math doc to kernel-constant correspondence cheaper (reference-not-restate / pack-sourced)
description: Plain English: the financial-math reference doc was hand-corrected to match the code, and nothing automatically checks that the prose still matches the kernel constants. Where a statutory constant lives in both, have the doc cite the kernel symbol or the pack value (reference-not-restate), and consider sourcing regulatory constants from a pack the kernel reads. Evidence: financial_concepts 7.5 source-wins fix; PersonalLoanDecider StatutoryCapBps 50/25; spec-coverage-check gates ADR Test-IDs only, not fin-math prose.

- Numeric statutory constants duplicated between the fin-math doc and the kernel are reduced to a single source (doc cites symbol/pack, or kernel reads pack).
- A decision is recorded on whether any automated doc-to-constant cross-check is warranted.

title: Consolidate the duplicated BasisPointsPerUnit=10000 constant (5 kernel files + a decider local)
description: Plain English: the same constant (10000 basis points = 100 percent) is hand-declared in five kernel files and again as a local in the loan decider, instead of one shared source. Promote BasisPointsPerUnit to a single shared FinancialMath constant and consume it everywhere, including from the decider via a kernel helper rather than a re-declared local. Evidence: Accrual.cs:23, Amortization.cs:64, Rates.cs:23, Withholding.cs:25, RateSchedule.cs inline literals, PersonalLoanDecider.cs:279.

title: Accept-track ADR-PC-031 so CREDITO_PESSOAL_AMORTIZATION_MATH flips Planned to a live CI gate
description: Plain English: the loan core financial-correctness test is not yet a CI gate because the ADR is still a draft. Accept-track ADR-PC-031 so commitment CREDITO_PESSOAL_AMORTIZATION_MATH (catalogue row CP-1) flips from Planned to a live P6-coverage-checked gate, locking amortization conservation and the statutory-cap clamp. Note in the ADR that the for-lift step ordering is reviewer-enforced, not mechanical. Evidence: ADR-PC-031 Status Proposed + Verifiable-commitments; commitment-catalogue CP-1 Planned.

title: Give osv6 an explicit exit condition and bound the triplicated rate-resolution duplication
description: Plain English: the PR correctly defers extracting a shared constitution pipeline, but the repeated rate-resolution block it accepts now lives in three places with no rule for when to stop copying. Give bd osv6 a measurable revisit trigger (e.g. at the Nth call site) and evaluate the NARROW extraction the PR did not separately consider: a DomainRejectedException-free RateSheetResolution.RequireTan helper, or relocating the throw, separate from the full-choreography question. Evidence: rate-resolution two-step in TermDepositConstitutionService 148-158 and 580-588, PersonalLoanConstitutionService DisburseAsync steps 1-2.

- bd osv6 carries a written, countable revisit trigger, not only a qualitative path-shape-matches one.

title: acl OTel instrumentation against the Babelstone.Telemetry ActivitySource + babelstone.* contract when acl source lands
description:
Plain English: every Babelstone service emits OpenTelemetry traces on a shared contract (one estate namespace, the same babelstone.* span attributes) so a request shows up as one connected trace. The acl service does not yet — because acl/ has no source. When acl source lands, instrument it the same way the engine, orchestrator, notification, and mcp-server already are.

Detail: the acl HALF of the now-closed bd babelstone-scd2.1 (K.1b). The notification + mcp-server OTel legs shipped in PR #281; orchestrator OTel landed in PR #73; the engine OTel layer in PR #73 too. acl remains BLOCKED on acl/ source (DEF-1 epic ub9s). When acl is built, instrument it against the SAME Babelstone.Telemetry ActivitySource + babelstone.* attribute contract (ADR-IC-007 §P1/§P2/§P4): service.name=babelstone-acl + service.namespace=babelstone + a fail-fast deployment.environment (OBS-1), spans on the shared source, no PII on any attribute (OBS-3). Origin bd babelstone-scd2.1 (closed); blocker DEF-1 epic babelstone-ub9s.

Acceptance criteria:
- acl is instrumented against the Babelstone.Telemetry ActivitySource + the babelstone.* attribute contract (ADR-IC-007), with the OBS-1 resource (service.name=babelstone-acl / service.namespace=babelstone / deployment.environment).
- Spans appear for acl consistent with the rest of the estate's OTel layer; no PII on any span attribute (OBS-3).
- W3C traceparent propagates across the acl boundary (OBS-4) so an acl-involved flow resolves as one trace.
close_reason: cancelled, not needed for now

title: Hoist step-up-SCA check off the money-mover handlers into an endpoint filter
description:
In plain English: the real step-up-SCA gate added in PR #274 was checked inline at the top of the two money-mover endpoints (mature_deposit, pay_interest), which dragged a cross-cutting security concern — and an HttpContext dependency — into business handlers whose job is just domain orchestration. This moves that check into a small ASP.NET endpoint filter attached to a money-mover route group, so the gate is a declarative route property (gated by construction) and the handlers go back to pure orchestration.

Pure structural refactor: ScaPrecondition.Check (the decision) is unchanged; only the invocation moves from the handler body to ScaPreconditionFilter on the route group in DepositsEndpoints.Map(). Honours ADR-IC-010 §P8 (engine-detected 422 SCA_REQUIRED before any side effect, off gateway-attested X-SCA-Acr/X-SCA-Auth-Time) and ADR-PC-010 §P5 (clock injected, check in the impure shell) unchanged — no amendment needed (confirmed by babelstone-engine:adr-conformance).
acceptance_criteria: Inline ScaPrecondition.Check removed from MatureAsync/PayInterestAsync; both drop the unused HttpContext param; new ScaPreconditionFilter attached via AddEndpointFilter to the money-mover route group; only /maturity and /interest gated (siblings unchanged); engine API integration tests pass unchanged (no-SCA->422, stale->422, fresh->settles); adr-conformance PASS, no ADR amendment.
close_reason: Closed

title: SCHEDULED notification webhook delivery — HMAC + at-least-once
description:
Plain English: once the scheduler has decided a maturity reminder is due and the message shape is defined, this is the part that actually sends it — over an HMAC-signed webhook, retried until it gets through, with the receiver responsible for not acting on the same one twice.

The outbound delivery leg for scheduler-produced NotificationDue(SCHEDULED) signals. Per-service outbox worker (ADR-IC-004) delivering via HMAC-SHA256-signed webhook (ADR-IC-011) with at-least-once semantics. The stable composite notification_id (ADR-PC-025 slot 4) is the dedupe anchor — the communications-system CONSUMER owns the 'already delivered' record, not the engine and not this scheduler (ADR-PC-023 §P3/§P4: the engine tracks no sent/acked/bounced state for clock-driven timing). Distinct from babelstone-a7d4.2, which is the EVENT_DRIVEN GL/notify post-flag delivery ports; this is the SCHEDULED temporal leg. Relates to that issue and shares the webhook/outbox machinery.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduler-produced NotificationDue(SCHEDULED) is delivered via an HMAC-SHA256-signed webhook (ADR-IC-011) through a per-service outbox worker (ADR-IC-004), at-least-once.
- Redelivery carries the same composite notification_id; the consumer dedupes on it (no engine/scheduler-side sent/acked/bounced state — ADR-PC-023 §P3/§P4).
- Delivery failure never gates or unwinds any producing flow (strictly post-flag/downstream).
close_reason: Closed

title: SCHEDULED maturity notification template — pt.notice.maturity
description:
Plain English: the actual template the 14-day maturity reminder fills in and renders. It lives in a regulatory pack, is version-pinned per deposit, and pulls customer PII (name, NIF, address) only at render time — never from the event.

Define the pt.notice.maturity template_ref in a pt.YYYY.N regulatory pack (ADR-PC-007), version-pinned on the instance. The scheduler-emitted NotificationDue carries only references + structural data; the communications system resolves PII at render time via the engine-owned authorised PII-resolve surface (ADR-PC-025 §PII). Likely belongs to the pack/template track rather than DEF-2 proper — filed as a sibling (relates-to the emission contract) so ownership can be settled in planning.
acceptance_criteria:
- pt.notice.maturity template_ref defined in a pt.YYYY.N pack (ADR-PC-007), version-pinned on the instance.

title: NotificationDue(SCHEDULED) emission contract — Avro + EventCatalog + Pact
description:
Plain English: defines the actual on-the-wire message the scheduler sends when a reminder is due, registers it so consumers can rely on it, and pins it with a contract test. The key rule: it carries references and structural data (amounts, dates), never PII.

Author the NotificationDue emit contract for the scheduler-produced signal. trigger_kind=SCHEDULED (ADR-PC-025 deliberately retained SCHEDULED for downstream producers; the engine itself emits only EVENT_DRIVEN + PRE_CONTRACTUAL). Payload per ADR-PC-025: notification_id (idempotency key), instance_id + customer_id as REFERENCES, template_ref + template_pack_version, data = structural-only (amounts/dates/rates/TAE — NO PII, per the no-PII-on-the-durable-bus rule), due_at. Deliverables: governed Avro .avsc, schema-registry registration with BACKWARD compat check, AsyncAPI EventCatalog entry, and a Pact consumer-driven contract (ADR-IC-009). Today contracts/ has only engine domain-event Avro + a light notification.reconciliation.yaml; no NotificationDue schema exists yet.

Relates to babelstone-2t16.14 (Pact CDC for GL/notify emission).
acceptance_criteria:
- Governed NotificationDue Avro .avsc authored; trigger_kind enum includes SCHEDULED; data carries structural values only (no PII).
- Registered in the schema registry and passes the BACKWARD compatibility check; AsyncAPI EventCatalog entry added.
- A Pact consumer-driven contract (ADR-IC-009) exists for the notification consumer.
- No PII (cleartext or ciphertext) appears on the payload — only references resolved at render time.

title: Maturity scheduler timing loop — idempotent projection read
description:
Plain English: this is the heart of auto-maturity. A loop in the notification service periodically reads the maturity calendar, spots deposits entering the 14-day pre-maturity window, and decides a reminder is due — built so that running it twice never double-notifies. The engine stays clockless (ADR-PC-023); this component owns the clock.

Implement the downstream temporal scheduler mandated by ADR-PC-023 + ADR-PC-014 Amendment A1 (now carried by ADR-PC-025). It reads the term_deposit.maturity_calendar projection as-of today, finds deposits whose ScheduledMaturity enters the 14-day opt-out window (02 §2.4.4), and produces a 'notification due' decision. Read cadence/polling, retry, and backoff are owned HERE — ADR-PC-023 §P3 gives the engine no delivery guarantee for clock-driven timing. Idempotency: compute the stable composite notification_id = instance_id + template_ref + schedule-occurrence-id and dedupe on it (ADR-PC-025 slot 4), so re-runs and projection refreshes don't re-notify.

Scoped to MATURITY only. The annual IRS-withholding statement run (accrual-schedule + withholding-ledger) is a separate sibling issue.
acceptance_criteria:
- A loop reads term_deposit.maturity_calendar as-of a date and selects deposits entering the 14-day pre-maturity window (02 §2.4.4).
- Running the loop twice over the same calendar state produces no duplicate notification (dedupe on composite notification_id per ADR-PC-025 slot 4).
- Read cadence/retry/backoff are owned by the scheduler (no reliance on an engine delivery guarantee — ADR-PC-023 §P3).
- No clock read enters any engine projection fold (determinism gate stays green).
close_reason: Closed

title: Real-time authorization technique ADR (sync vs async)
description:
Plain English: decide HOW the engine answers authorization in real time. ADR-PC-030 fixes the COMMITMENT (the engine is the authoritative balance and answers authorization in real time) but explicitly defers the MECHANISM. This issue owns that mechanism decision.

Scope (ADR-PC-030 boxed 'Real-time, technique deferred' note + §Open Action 4): choose between a synchronous call (the ADR-PC-029 idempotent command surface under a heavier load profile) and an asynchronous/reactive design with a fast round-trip — weighing latency/availability (the engine becomes a payment-path dependency), throughput (ADR-PC-001 store, ADR-PC-011 load harness now load-bearing), and the de-settled-command stance (ADR-PC-029). Prerequisite-adjacent to the conta à ordem family build. Follows babelstone-nyan (ADR-PC-030).
close_reason: Merged via PR #319.

title: Scope conta à ordem transactional-account family ADR
description:
Plain English: model the current/demand account — the 4th product shape and the hub the others settle against. This issue is the SCOPING of the conta a ordem family ADR; that ADR is now filed and Accepted as ADR-PC-037 (2026-06-28). Implementation lives in the separate conta a ordem family epic.

Scope (ADR-PC-030 Open Action 4): a family ADR (ADR-PC-021 shape) for conta a ordem — DELIVERED as ADR-PC-037 (Accepted 2026-06-28).

CONFORMANCE UPDATE (the original description predated ADR-PC-032/033/034): the hold model is NOT family-owned Portuguese-named events. ADR-PC-033 (Accepted 2026-06-23) decided holds are the engine cross-cutting, family-agnostic events operations.HoldPlaced / HoldCaptured / HoldExpired, and explicitly rejected holds-as-family-events. So the original MontanteCativado / CativoCapturado / CativoExpirado framing is SUPERSEDED — ADR-PC-037 INSTANTIATES the ADR-PC-033 lifecycle, it does not re-decide it. Likewise the available-balance fold (available = accounting - sum active holds) is ADR-PC-033's, and the real-time authorization technique is DECIDED in ADR-PC-034 (synchronous, on the ADR-PC-029 surface) — no longer a separate open issue. descoberto autorizado as a pack rule and the no-shadow-balance / v4-migration reconciliation are committed in ADR-PC-037.

Implementation is tracked under the conta a ordem family epic (the family build) and babelstone-hkwp (the Account engine foundation). This issue closes when ADR-PC-037 lands (PR filing the ADR).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A family ADR (ADR-PC-021 shape) for conta a ordem is filed (ADR-PC-030 Open Action 4) — DONE: ADR-PC-037.
- The ADR cross-links ADR-PC-016 and the coexistence section 9 migration model, and quotes 02 section 3 commitment 1 so the no-shadow-balance reconciliation stays explicit — DONE in ADR-PC-037 D7.
- The engine-owned authorization stages 3-5 boundary is stated (SCA/fraud/rails external); the real-time technique is decided in ADR-PC-034 — DONE.
acceptance_criteria: A family ADR (ADR-PC-021 shape) for conta a ordem is filed (ADR-PC-030 Open Action 4) - DONE as ADR-PC-037. The ADR cross-links ADR-PC-016 and the coexistence section 9 migration model and quotes 02 section 3 commitment 1 so the no-shadow-balance reconciliation stays explicit - DONE (ADR-PC-037 D7). The hold model INSTANTIATES the ADR-PC-033 cross-cutting operations.HoldPlaced/HoldCaptured/HoldExpired events (the MontanteCativado/CativoCapturado/CativoExpirado family-event framing is superseded by ADR-PC-033, not re-decided); the engine-owned authorization stages 3-5 boundary is stated and the real-time technique is decided in ADR-PC-034 (synchronous) - DONE.
close_reason: ADR-PC-037 filed + Accepted; merged via PR #385. Implementation tracked under epic babelstone-30hf (conta à ordem family) + babelstone-hkwp (Account foundation).

title: Scope credit_card account/revolving-slice family ADR
description:
Plain English: model the credit card the way ADR-PC-030 allows — only the account side (the credit line, revolving interest, the statement cycle, minimum payment). The four-party scheme (authorization, clearing, settlement, chargeback, interchange) stays OUTSIDE the boundary; the engine consumes already-cleared postings.

REORDER (ADR-PC-030 amended 2026-06-28): the credit_card family is now built AFTER the conta a ordem family, not before it. The card account slice is the SECOND instance of the transactional-account abstraction (holds, available balance, real-time authorization) that the conta a ordem family (ADR-PC-037) first proves; it reuses that shape.

SCOPE CHANGE: the settlement/posting-feed contract-shape ADR that this issue originally also scoped has MOVED to the conta a ordem family epic (the conta a ordem is built first and needs the feed first; the card reuses the same contract). This issue now references that contract rather than owning it.

Remaining scope (ADR-PC-030 Open Action 3): the credit_card family ADR (ADR-PC-021 shape) modelling only the account side (credit line, revolving interest, statement cycle, minimum payment), PLUS statement issuance as a SEALED event (legally immutable; corrections are new events next cycle) with grace-period determinism carried in the fold across statement boundaries. Per the conformance advisory, defer the sealed-event concern to the replay-determinism-auditor when authored. Follows ADR-PC-037 (the conta a ordem family) in the build order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A family ADR (ADR-PC-021 shape) for credit_card is filed modelling only the account side; the four-party scheme stays outside the boundary and the engine consumes already-cleared postings via the (conta-a-ordem-owned) settlement/posting-feed contract.
- Statement issuance is specified as a SEALED event (not a replayable projection), with grace-period determinism carried in the fold across statement boundaries.
- The family build is sequenced AFTER the conta a ordem family and reuses its transactional-account shape (holds, available balance, authorize).
acceptance_criteria: A family ADR (ADR-PC-021 shape) for credit_card is filed modelling only the account side (credit line, revolving interest, statement cycle, minimum payment); the four-party scheme stays outside the boundary and the engine consumes already-cleared postings via the conta-a-ordem-owned settlement/posting-feed contract (now babelstone-30hf.5). Statement issuance is specified as a SEALED event (not a replayable projection) with grace-period determinism carried in the fold across statement boundaries. The family build is sequenced AFTER the conta a ordem family (ADR-PC-030 amended 2026-06-28) and reuses its transactional-account shape.

title: 0.3 follow-up — per-primitive pin-or-float pack policy (v2+, ADR-PC-009 §P5)
description:
Today the engine pins everything about a deposit's pack at the moment it is constituted, and the manifest's `pack_effective_from` date does nothing at runtime (informational metadata only — ADR-PC-009 §P5). The agreed FUTURE direction (v2+) is finer-grained: primitives that DEFINE the instrument (cash-flow shape, day-count, the contracted TAN) stay pinned for life, while primitives that merely TRACK regulation (withholding rate, FGD ceiling, disclosure templates) "float" — automatically following the latest pack by accrual date — so a statutory rate change reaches in-flight deposits without a manual per-instance migration. This issue tracks that v2+ deliverable; v1 deliberately ships none of it and pins everything.

The direction is CONFIRMED but DEFERRED: ADR-PC-009 §P5 (additive *Revised 2026-06-10* amendment) and open-questions §8 record it; the design-input question was resolved and closed in 0.3 (babelstone-oa3i). This is the implementation follow-up.

Relationship to PackVersionMigrated (babelstone-fk7m.10): in v1 the only mid-life escape hatch for a statutory rate change is the explicit, audited per-instance `PackVersionMigrated`. The per-primitive float makes that automatic for the regulation-tracking class; explicit migration remains the path for instrument-defining changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pack manifest gains a per-primitive pin-or-float annotation; the reserved `pack_effective_from` placeholder becomes load-bearing (ADR-PC-009 §P5; ADR-PC-007 manifest shape — likely an ADR-PC-007/009 amendment or a new ADR).
- Engine resolution floats regulation-tracking primitives by accrual date while keeping instrument-defining primitives pinned at constitution.
- `pack_effective_from` transitions from informational metadata to a value the engine branches on.
- Flow-by-flow withholding correctness preserved across a float boundary (financial_concepts §5.4) — a mid-life rate change yields the correct per-flow split, not a rescaled aggregate.
- Roadmap addendum (03 §Pack Maintenance) and the docs explanation page ("Why pack_effective_from is metadata-only in v1") updated when this ships.
notes: v2+ / deferred (P3). Filed from investigation of PR #254: the explanation page section "Why pack_effective_from is metadata-only in v1" names this v2+ deliverable, which had no tracking issue (0.3/oa3i was the design-decision task and is closed). This is the implementation tracker.
close_reason: Descoped to v2+ (epic-closure decision 2026-06-26). Canonical v2+ per-primitive pin-or-float tracker (ADR-PC-009 §P5, Revised 2026-06-10): v1 deliberately pins everything and floats nothing. Needs an operating-bank regulatory/tax per-primitive categorisation (open-questions §8) absent from a reference impl, plus date-keyed multi-pack resolution machinery §P5 scoped out of v1. Revisit in v2+.

title: A.14 — Snapshot transaction-time seeding for fully-covered streams
description:
Plain English: a stream whose snapshot covers every event (no tail) would report a null last-transaction-time even though its version is >= 0, because the time was only ever derived from tail events. Fix: the snapshot must carry the transaction_time it was taken at, and rehydrate must seed from it.

Closes the KNOWN GAP comment at engine/src/Babelstone.Engine/AggregateRuntime.cs:104. Add transaction_time to the snapshot record/state seam and seed lastTransactionTime in LoadAsync when there is no tail.
acceptance_criteria: A stream fully covered by a snapshot with zero tail events reports the snapshot's transaction_time as lastTransactionTime; regression test for the no-tail case.

title: Make the partial-withdrawal endpoint idempotent (Idempotency-Key, ADR-PC-029)
description:
Plain English: a partial withdrawal is genuinely repeatable (it leaves the deposit Active), so an at-least-once retry of POST /v1/deposits/{id}/partial-withdrawal would withdraw twice. The endpoint shipped in qze9 mirrors the maturity/interest pattern (no Idempotency-Key), which is safe for those (lifecycle-guarded, one-shot) but not for a repeatable withdrawal.

Scope: add a mandatory Idempotency-Key header → CommandId on the partial-withdrawal endpoint, a command-log pre-check, and thread the CommandId onto WithdrawPartiallyAsync's AppendAsync Context so the in-transaction command_dedup INSERT makes a retry return the original outcome (ADR-PC-029 slot 4), exactly as the constitution / erasure / renewal endpoints do. Add an integration test proving a replayed key appends exactly one DepositPartiallyWithdrawn.

Discovered during the F.12 wiring chain (qze9); deliberately deferred to keep that PR scoped to wiring. ADRs: ADR-PC-029 slot 4.
notes: Work complete; implemented in PR #260 (open, awaiting maintainer merge) — Tier-1 parallel build 2026-06-20.

This adds a canonical corpus instance whose expected event sequence includes DepositPartiallyWithdrawn, and drives it in the depth-5 simulation — exactly the way PR #226 made the banded variant actually replay its early-termination path instead of quietly running to maturity. The withdrawal date and amount are INPUTs (start + N days, fixed cents) so the run stays deterministic and clock-free. Extends F.8 (sealed v1 test corpus, up7t).

- Every page carries a built-vs-pending callout.

title: Engine OCI pack mode: multi-stage image bundling so oras/cosign are present in the chiseled runtime
description:

Scope: add a multi-stage Dockerfile stage that copies oras + cosign binaries into the chiseled runtime image (or an alternative that satisfies pack pull+verify without image bloat), then lift the fail-fast guard for that path. title: Orchestrator-routed constitution tool for the MCP channel (close the get_process_status producer gap)
description:
Plain English: today the MCP agent channel can read a deposit (get_deposit) and, once vjoi lands, poll process status (get_process_status) — but it has NO tool that STARTS a constitution through the saga. The current constitute_deposit MCP tool calls the engine DIRECTLY and returns a deposit_id, not a saga process_id. So an agent can never obtain a process_id to feed get_process_status, which means the MCP async-completion loop (Document 11 Pattern 2) cannot be exercised end-to-end purely over the MCP surface. This issue adds the missing producer.

Surfaced by the vjoi (PR-J1) code-architect blueprint (2026-06-17, see BLUEPRINT-J1-vjoi.md). vjoi ships the READ side (the orchestrator status endpoint + get_process_status tool); this issue ships the WRITE/initiation side so the loop closes.

Scope: a new MCP tool (e.g. constitute_deposit_saga) that POSTs to the orchestrator edge (POST /api/v1/deposits/constitute) rather than the engine, returns the saga process_id, and attaches a follow_up hint pointing the agent at get_process_status(process_id). Reuses the mcp->orchestrator boundary (OrchestratorClient) established by vjoi/PR-J1; deposits:write scope; reads the gateway-attested X-Client-Id (never a tool arg). Decide whether this REPLACES the engine-direct constitute_deposit demo tool or sits ALONGSIDE it (the engine-direct path is the MCP DIRECT walking-skeleton demo). Governed by Document 11 (Pattern 2 producer), ADR-IC-010 (tool shape/scope), ADR-IC-006 (edge ownership). Depends on PR-J1 (vjoi) for the boundary.

Sits ALONGSIDE the engine-direct constitute_deposit (DIRECT walking-skeleton demo), mirroring the engine_client/orchestrator_client dual boundary. deposits:write scope; gateway-attested X-Client-Id (never a tool arg); PII-free body. 124 mcp-server tests pass; docs-verify green (new generated reference/mcp-tools/constitute_deposit_saga.md); adr-conformance PASS (ADR-IC-010 §P4, ADR-IC-006, Document 11 Pattern 2).

title: Agent SSE streaming contract + Mission Control proxy route
description:

- Named SSE frame schema: event: narration {text}; event: tool_call {tool,input}; event: tool_result {tool,output|error}; event: done {summary}. PII-safe — opaque references only, no cleartext PII on the channel (ADR-PC-004 P2; memory pii-on-integration-bus).

title: Real Claude agent loop — backend host driving the MCP tool surface
description:
Plain English: build the server-side brain for the real-AI demo. A small Python process holds the Anthropic API key, connects to the real babelstone MCP server as a client over Streamable HTTP, binds the deposit tools, and runs an agentic loop where Claude reads a natural-language instruction and decides which tools to call. The host plays the gateway role so the MCP server auth actually runs under an AI driver.

- New module/entrypoint under mcp-server/ (babelstone_mcp.agent). Add the anthropic SDK dependency (pinned) to mcp-server/pyproject.toml; anthropic[mcp] for MCP-tool schema derivation via a ClientSession.
- Hand-rolled tool-use loop (NOT the Messages-API mcp_servers connector, which cannot reach a localhost/Kong/mTLS server): loop while stop_reason==tool_use; dispatch each tool_use over an MCP ClientSession to /mcp; append tool_result with the matching tool_use_id; repeat.

Play the Kong stand-in: mint a demo audience-bound bearer (pyjwt, already a dep) with aud == BABELSTONE_MCP_SERVER_URI, and inject gateway-attested X-Client-Id (opaque demo ref) + X-OAuth-Scope (deposits:read deposits:write) so AudienceMiddleware + auth.py scope checks pass (mirrors how serve.py injects X-Client-Id).

- Tests: loop against a stubbed Anthropic client + stubbed MCP server.
ADRs honoured: ADR-IC-010 (transport+auth), ADR-IC-014 (secret handling).

title: Orchestrator: derive the saga topic subscription from the event catalogue
description:
Plain English: stop hand-registering each family's Kafka topic in the orchestrator. Derive the set of family topics the saga listens to from the contracts that already declare them, so adding a family needs zero orchestrator source edits.

Technical:
- Replace the static SagaConsumeTopics constant + ConstitutionProcessTopics list (SagaConsumeTopics.cs:73,80-81; Program.cs:116) with a topic set built at boot from the AsyncAPI catalogue channels (topic == aggregate_type convention, OutboxDrainer.cs:148-150).
- Source the manifest co-located with the orchestrator's OWN deploy inputs — NOT the docs-gen reference tree — to preserve ADR-IC-003 §A8 ('orchestrator depends only on Confluent.Kafka', no coupling to the docs pipeline / engine codec). Prefer an explicit generated list over a Kafka SubscribePattern regex (a too-broad regex can pull deposits.process.events or unrelated topics into the consumer group, breaking one-group-per-consumer, ADR-IC-001).
- Keep the orchestrator-internal process topic (deposits.process.events) on an explicit subscription. The saga transition table stays keyed on (state, event_type) (ConstitutionProcess.cs:185) — NO logic change. SagaCommandRouter is per-saga-command, not per-family — no edit for a family reusing the constitution saga.
- CORRECTNESS: the subscription must be exhaustive AND correct at startup — a missed topic = a saga that silently never advances, no replay-safe mid-flight recovery (earliest-offset auto-attach would replay the backlog). CI-gate the derived list against the catalogue channels (a CI failure, not a runtime stall).
- ADR (same PR): amend ADR-IC-003 — record catalogue-derived subscription + the exhaustive-at-startup constraint (NOTE: no prior amendment made this registry-derived; the 2026-06-15 change only altered WHICH topic is read).
- Independent of the engine-side children; can land in parallel.

Amends ADR-IC-003 §A9–§A12 (additive). gen-saga-topics-check 'up to date' ['term_deposit']; Orchestrator.Tests 158/158. CI fully green.

title: Pack family-manifest + fail-closed version-skew cross-check at host load
description:
Plain English: pin which families a deployment is allowed to run, in the signed regulatory pack, and make the host refuse to start if the code it discovered doesn't match. This closes the risk that a discovered family is a newer version than the instance's pinned pack — which would corrupt the event audit trail.

Technical:
- Add a declarative family-manifest to the pack (ADR-PC-007 layout): {family_name, aggregate_type, schema_version, plugin_assembly} per family — pinning the family set the same way schema_pins pins schema versions.
- The HostModuleLoader cross-checks each scanned module's FamilyName/SchemaVersion against the pinned VerifiedPack's family-manifest and FAILS CLOSED on mismatch or on a pack-declared family with no loadable module (mirrors HostPackLoading fatal-on-load discipline; names the offending assembly at Critical).
- Rationale: every module stamps SchemaVersion onto every EventEnvelope (ADR-PC-009 §P1); replay resolves the pin through the registry (§P2). Skew = audit/replay hazard. The adversarial review judged this cross-check MANDATORY, not optional, for the discovery design to be safe.
- ADR (same PR): amend ADR-PC-007 (pack gains the family-manifest) + ADR-PC-009 (the pinned pack is the authoritative per-deployment family set).
- Depends on the assembly-scan discovery child (the cross-check runs in the loader).

title: Engine API host: assembly-scan discovery — drop familyModules[] list + ProjectReferences
description:
Plain English: stop hand-listing each family in the Engine API host. Instead, the host discovers every family module automatically at startup, so adding a family needs zero host source edits.

Technical:
- Add a HostModuleLoader in Babelstone.Engine.Api mirroring the proven FamilyModuleLoader (FamilyModule.cs:84-129): assembly-scan for public-parameterless-ctor IFamilyHostModule types, fail-loud on duplicate (family, command) collisions exactly as HandlerRegistry throws on duplicate event_type.
- Replace Program.cs:177 'familyModules = [new TermDepositHostModule()]' with loader output; the existing ConfigureServices / MapEndpoints loops (Program.cs:178-181, 244-247) are UNCHANGED.
- Use the §A3-BLESSED in-process scan over compile-referenced assemblies (keeps compile-time type safety, AOT, greppability). Do NOT adopt Assembly.LoadFrom drop-in plugins here (that reverses §A3's out-of-scope scoping; separate future option).
- Reflection stays strictly at the composition root (Babelstone.Engine.Api), never the spine (ADR-PC-010 §P5).
- Preserve engine-before-family read-model migration ordering (ADR-PC-021 §A6) by sorting discovered modules stably.
- ADR (same PR): amend ADR-PC-021 §A3/§P4 — realise the assembly-scan discovery the explicit list deferred.
- Depends on the IFamilyHostModule relocation child.

- Update the ENGINE_FAMILY_AGNOSTIC fitness-function allowlist (parsed off ADR-PC-021 §P2) so the relocated contract assembly isn't mis-flagged; the family→engine arrow stays one-way.

title: Family-count-invariant host & orchestrator — confine a new family to two boxes
description:
Plain English: Today, adding a new product family to the engine forces hand-edits to two services BEYOND the family's own code — the Engine API host (a new host module + its endpoints + a ProjectReference + a one-line entry in the familyModules[] list) and the Orchestrator (registering the family's Kafka topic). This epic makes those two services family-count-invariant, so adding a family touches only its own assembly (slide-11 'Product Families' box) and its contracts (slide-11 'Contracts·Governance' box). The mechanism: turn hand-written wiring into automatic discovery + declarative data.

RECOMMENDED PATH (from the wf_5cce9717 design panel + adversarial ADR-conformance review):
- Host-side IN-PROCESS assembly-scan over compile-referenced family assemblies — the ADR-PC-021 §A3-blessed 'Option B' (keeps compile-time type safety, AOT, and a greppable family list). NOT the Assembly.LoadFrom drop-in plugin model (§A3 placed that out of scope; tracked as a future option, not here).
- Family-owned endpoints RELOCATED into the family assembly — preserves the ENGINE_COMMAND_PACT literal /v1/deposits route + the mandatory Idempotency-Key (no generic /v1/{family}/{cmd} dispatch).
- Orchestrator topic set DERIVED from the AsyncAPI catalogue, co-located with the orchestrator's OWN deploy inputs (NOT the docs-gen reference tree — preserves ADR-IC-003 §A8 'depends only on Confluent.Kafka'). The saga stays event-type-keyed (ConstitutionProcess.cs:185); no saga logic changes.
- A MANDATORY pack family-manifest cross-check (family_name, aggregate_type, schema_version, plugin_assembly) so the host fails closed on version skew.

HONEST FRAMING: this RELOCATES per-family effort into family-owned code + declarative schemas/manifests rather than eliminating it. The catalogue + manifest become load-bearing for at-least-once correctness (a missed topic = a saga that silently never advances, no replay-safe recovery), so each MUST be CI-gated.

OUT OF SCOPE / non-goals:
- Generic schema-driven command dispatch (POST /v1/{family}/commands/{type}) — breaks the Pact, degrades OpenAPI/MCP discoverability. Separate future consideration only.
- The MCP server does NOT collapse — its tools/scopes/elicitation/output-schemas are family-specific authority policy (ADR-IC-010 §P4/P6/P8). 'Two boxes' excludes MCP by design.

DRIFT GATE: each child carries its own ADR amendment in the SAME PR (ADR-PC-020 §D3) — no silent divergence.

TIMING: at the current single-family scale this is the rule-of-three abstraction ADR-PC-021 §A3/§P5 deliberately deferred; the recurring edit removed today is ~3 lines (a ProjectReference pair + one familyModules[] entry + one topic constant). Natural trigger: family #3. This epic tracks it for when that lands. Grounded analysis: workflow run wf_5cce9717-add (5 readers, 3 designs, adversarial conformance).

## Success Criteria

- Adding a new family touches only its own assembly + contracts: the Engine API host discovers families via in-process assembly-scan (ADR-PC-021 §A3 Option B) and the orchestrator derives its topics declaratively.
- A fitness function proves no per-family hand-edit to the host or orchestrator is required.
- All child issues are closed.

title: Pin product_config_version per-event on DepositConstituted once product-configs have a versioned deploy (ADR-PC-009 REPLAY_PIN_PER_EVENT follow-up)
description:
In plain English: PR #200 made the engine resolve a deposit's structural facts from a product-config at constitution time (bd t7o3.11/3k10/c8d8). ADR-PC-009 says each event should pin the versions of the inputs it was produced under — pack_version, schema_version, and rate_sheet_version_id ARE already stamped per-event (via AppendContext). The one input NOT version-pinned is the product-config itself, because product-configs are currently STATIC deploy-time YAMLs with no versioned deploy registry (unlike rate sheets, which have POST /v1/rate-sheets). So there is no product_config_version to pin yet.

Follow-up: once product-configs gain a versioned deploy registry (a POST /v1/product-configs-style mechanism, or a content-hash/version stamped at deploy), stamp product_config_version on DepositConstituted so a replay can prove exactly which product-config generation a deposit was constituted under. Until then pack_version transitively encodes the config generation. Surfaced by the t7o3.11/PR#200 adr-conformance + replay-determinism reviews. Governing: ADR-PC-009 (per-instance pinning / REPLAY_PIN_PER_EVENT), ADR-PC-008 §S2.
acceptance_criteria:
- Product-configs gain a versioned-deploy mechanism (a POST /v1/product-configs-style registry, or a content-hash/version stamped at deploy).
- DepositConstituted stamps product_config_version per-event via AppendContext, alongside the already-pinned pack_version / schema_version / rate_sheet_version_id.
- A replay test asserts the pinned product_config_version (ADR-PC-009 REPLAY_PIN_PER_EVENT, ADR-PC-008 §S2).

title: (Optional, §A2-sensitive) Host-attached collection resource for the MCP channel — the only ADR-conformant resource shape left after §A2
description:
In plain English: bd babelstone-2ep0 (PR #195) shipped the agent PROMPTS, but its 'resources' half is mostly subsumed by ADR-IC-010 §A2 — that Accepted amendment made the single-deposit read a TOOL (get_deposit), not a resource, and the adr-conformance review blocked re-introducing the bank://deposits/{deposit_id} resource template. The ONLY conformant resource shape §A2 preserves is host-attached / subscribable context — e.g. a caller's-deposits COLLECTION (Document 11's bank://clients/{client_id}/deposits example).

This is a MAINTAINER CALL, not a mechanical task: re-introducing ANY deposit resource re-opens the §A2 debate (resources were deliberately removed once). If wanted, the conformant + IDOR-safe design is a collection keyed PURELY on the gateway-attested X-Client-Id (NOT a {client_id} URI param — the hallucinated-parameters rule, Document 11), scope deposits:read, host-attached, no PII in the body. Decide: (a) build the host-attached collection resource, (b) consider 2ep0 satisfied by tools+prompts (the §A2-mandated tool already covers deposit reads) and not build it. Governing: ADR-IC-010 §A1/§A2/§A3/§P4, Document 11.

- A maintainer decision is recorded: either (a) build the host-attached caller's-deposits collection resource, or (b) consider babelstone-2ep0 satisfied by tools+prompts (the §A2-mandated get_deposit tool already covers deposit reads).
