title: Engine: surface the trace id to the caller + AspNetCore instrumentation (parent the deposit.* spans)
description:
**Plain English:** when the engine handles a request, the spans it emits (`deposit.constituted`, `accrual.computed`, `withholding.applied`) are disconnected **root** spans today — each with its own trace id and no link back to the HTTP call that caused them. A caller has no way to learn which trace its request produced, so it can't look that trace up in Tempo afterwards. This makes the engine's request handling traceable end-to-end: instrument the inbound HTTP request as the parent span, and hand the trace id back to the caller.

**Why now:** prerequisite for **bd babelstone-f0ic.9** (Mission Control's Telemetry tab pulling the REAL trace from Grafana Tempo in LIVE·engine mode). Without a stable, caller-known trace id, the browser has nothing to query Tempo by. Split out of f0ic.9 because it is **engine** work (Engine.Api OTel pipeline + a trace-id response mechanism), not demo work (serve.py proxy + UI fetch).

**Current state (verified):** `engine/src/Babelstone.Engine.Api/Program.cs:36` wires `WithTracing(t => t.AddSource("Babelstone.Engine").AddOtlpExporter())` — there is **no** `AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()`, so the inbound request is not a span and the custom `deposit.*` spans are roots. `BabelstoneAttributes` already documents that the saga path joins on the inbound `traceparent` (ADR-IC-007 Layer 1), so this closes the engine side of that join for the synchronous HTTP boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Engine.Api adds .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation() to the WithTracing pipeline (Program.cs:36) so the inbound request is a server span AND an inbound W3C traceparent (when present) becomes the PARENT of the deposit.* custom spans — today they are roots with their own trace ids (ADR-IC-007 Layer 1: traceparent is the join).
- The engine returns the active trace id to the caller on the command + query responses — via the W3C 'traceresponse' header (Trace Context Level 2) OR an explicit response header read from Activity.Current.TraceId; the chosen mechanism is documented in the code + ADR-IC-007.
- No PII on spans or the trace-id header (operational tier only, ADR-IC-007 §P4 / ADR-PC-004 §P2) — the trace id is an opaque hex id, never a subject reference.
- Test (Babelstone.Engine.Api integration): (a) a POST /v1/deposits carrying a traceparent yields deposit.* spans under THAT trace id, not new roots; (b) the response carries the trace-id header equal to Activity.Current.TraceId.
- Verifiable on the dev stack: the returned trace id resolves in Tempo (make up → Grafana localhost:3000) with the deposit.* spans nested under the request span.
- Out of scope (tracked elsewhere): orchestrator OTel wiring (saga.advance spans don't export); W3C traceparent propagation across Redpanda (ADR-IC-007 §P1).
close_reason: Merged in PR #184 (squash 1d9a33a). AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation parents the deposit.* spans under the inbound traceparent; X-Trace-Id response header returns the active trace id on every command+query response. Covered by DepositsApiTracingIntegrationTests + commitment OBS_TRACE_ID_SURFACED_HTTP. Dev-stack Tempo-resolution leg will be exercised end-to-end by the unblocked f0ic.9 demo work.

title: Mission Control: saga-driven LIVE mode (edge -> orchestrator -> engine), not engine-direct
description:
**Plain English:** Today the demo's LIVE mode opens a deposit by calling the engine's command API directly (`POST /v1/deposits`). That's a real, governed boundary (ADR-PC-029 lists the edge, MCP, and saga as co-callers of it), and it's coherent with the demo's MCP-operator framing — but it skips the **constitution saga**. So the deposit gets *recorded* without the money leg: no settlement against the Core account, no approval gate, no compensation. This issue adds an end-to-end path that opens a deposit *through* the orchestrator's edge front door so the demo can show the bank actually opening a deposit, not just appending the fact of one.

## Why
ADR-PC-029 §Residual (resolved 2026-06-14, bd `babelstone-t7o3.4`): `ConstituteAsync` now DECIDES + APPENDS only — the principal debit is the saga's gated `ReserveAccountBalance → ConfirmDebit` step delivered by the dispatcher to the Core ACL. A direct `POST /v1/deposits` therefore produces a `DepositConstituted` with **no settlement**. The intended operator flow is edge → saga orchestrates → engine records → terminal `DepositConstituted` (ADR-IC-003 / Document 05). The current README calls LIVE mode "the bank working" / "genuinely real," which slightly oversells the engine-direct constitution path.

## Good news — the parts already exist (this is wiring, not new architecture)
- **Edge front door** (`orchestrator/src/Babelstone.Orchestrator/Edge/ProcessApiEndpoints.cs`): `POST /api/v1/deposits/constitute` → `202` + `process_id` + `stream_url`; SSE `GET /api/v1/processes/{processId}/stream` streams structural saga state (never PII), with per-process authz (caller `client_id` must match the owning client — `process_id` is not a capability token).
- **Dispatcher** (`Dispatch/SagaCommandDispatcherService.cs`, `SagaCommandDispatchDrainer.cs`): drains `saga_outbox` and HTTP-POSTs the engine `/v1` command surface (ADR-PC-029).
- **Core-ACL settlement stub** (`infra/compose.yaml` → `core-acl-stub`, wiremock 3.9.1): success path + an `InsufficientBalance` refusal path — a real, refusable settlement target (the real ACL is DEF-1, bd `babelstone-ub9s`).
- **Gated-settlement integration test** already exists: `orchestrator/tests/.../GatedSettlementWireMockIntegrationTests.cs`.

## The work
1. **Bring-up.** The demo is deliberately the Postgres-only walking skeleton (`scripts/demo-mcp.sh`). A saga path needs **Redpanda + the orchestrator host (Kestrel edge + consume loop + dispatcher) + the `core-acl-stub`** in addition to Postgres + engine. Extend `demo-mcp.sh` (or add a `scripts/demo-saga.sh`) to stand these up. This is the heavy part.
2. **Proxy.** `serve.py` currently relays `/v1/*` → engine. Add a relay for `/api/v1/*` → orchestrator (different port), or point the saga mode at the orchestrator origin.
3. **UI (`index.html`).** Constitute becomes **async**: POST `/api/v1/deposits/constitute` → `202`, then subscribe to the SSE `stream` and render saga transitions (STARTED → settlement reserved/confirmed → `DepositConstituted`) as process/ledger cards. Demo the **refusal branch** too (ACL `InsufficientBalance` → compensation) — that's the saga's whole point.
4. **Mode framing.** Either a third toggle state (DEMO / LIVE·engine / LIVE·saga) or replace LIVE; keep honest captions distinguishing "engine records the deposit" from "saga opens the deposit."

## Dependencies / risks
- Saga completeness is still in flight: approval fork wiring (bd `babelstone-t7o3.1`), and the command-outcome → result-event bridge so compensation fires (bd `babelstone-t7o3.8`, dep). The refusal-branch beat depends on t7o3.8 landing.
- **Authz:** the SSE stream enforces `client_id` ownership; the demo needs a gateway-attested `client_id` (or a documented dev bypass) to read its own stream.
- **No PII on the stream** (ADR-PC-004 §P2) — the demo must render only the structural state names, same rule as the bus.

## Acceptance
- Opening a deposit via `POST /api/v1/deposits/constitute` returns `202` + `process_id`; the UI follows the SSE stream to a terminal `DepositConstituted`, with the **settlement leg visibly exercised** against `core-acl-stub`.
- The `InsufficientBalance` refusal path is demoable: settlement refuses → saga compensates → UI shows the failure branch.
- README/UI wording updated so LIVE·saga vs LIVE·engine is explicit and honest (this supersedes the lighter doc-only clarification — option 1 in the review thread).

title: Dispatcher per-aggregate FIFO guard for future sagas that enqueue ordered commands
description:
In plain English: the saga command dispatcher (PR #170, bd babelstone-t7o3.3) is safe to run active-active across pods because it claims saga_outbox rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and the engine dedupes redelivery on the Idempotency-Key. Ordering across instances is NOT preserved, but that is fine TODAY because the constitution saga is single-writer per process_id and advances on the resulting event — so there is at most one in-flight (PENDING) command per saga instance at a time, with nothing to reorder (the only concurrent pair, ReserveAccountBalance and ValidateProductLimits, is order-independent).

The latent risk: the moment a future saga emits two ORDER-DEPENDENT commands for the same aggregate into saga_outbox at once (without waiting for the first's event), multiple dispatcher instances — or even a single instance's skip-on-5xx path — could deliver them out of order. Before such a saga lands (e.g. a future renewal/termination flow), add a per-aggregate FIFO guard to SagaCommandDispatchDrainer: partition the drain by process_id, or take a per-process advisory lock, so ordered commands for one aggregate are delivered in seq order. Governing: ADR-PC-029 slot 3 (per-aggregate ordering is the caller's responsibility). Surfaced reviewing PR #170.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #241 (feat/dispatch-per-aggregate-fifo). Per-aggregate FIFO guard: in-process FIFO head (DISTINCT ON process_id) + a per-process_id pg_try_advisory_xact_lock for cross-instance serialisation; migration 0007 (additive partial index). 3 new integration tests; adr-conformance PASS (conformant hardening of ADR-PC-029 slot 3).

comments.author: jhosm
comments.text: Per-aggregate FIFO guard implemented in the saga command dispatcher. Two layers: (1) ReadPendingSeqAsync now drains at most one PENDING head per process_id (DISTINCT ON), served by new partial index saga_outbox_pending_fifo_idx (migration 0007); (2) ClaimAsync takes a per-process_id transaction advisory lock (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock), serialising two pods on one aggregate while different aggregates run in parallel. New SagaCommandDispatcherFifoIntegrationTests proves ordered-per-aggregate, parallel-across-aggregates, and active-active in-order delivery. adr-conformance verdict PASS (conformant hardening of ADR-PC-029 slot 3, no amendment owed). Dispatcher tests 7/7 green; full orchestrator suite 192/195 (3 failures are Redpanda Testcontainer startup flakes unrelated to this change, pass in isolation). PR #241 opened, closes on merge.

title: ADR-IC-017 §P4: ratify InterestAccrued/WithholdingApplied vs coarse InterestPaid promotion
description:
In plain English: the catalog-gated relay (PR #168, bd babelstone-a7d4.3) made the bus publish only catalogued integration events, but it deliberately did NOT touch WHICH events are catalogued — that judgement was deferred. ADR-IC-017 §P4 says a family's current schema set is not presumed correct: it floats InterestAccrued and WithholdingApplied as candidate-INTERNAL accrual mechanics (fine-grained calc steps) and the coarse InterestPaid as the candidate INTEGRATION event that downstream contexts actually react to.

This issue performs that per-event classification pass against the three-part criterion (coarse business fact / named external consumer / stable contract) and records the resulting v1 consumer map. If the verdict de-promotes InterestAccrued/WithholdingApplied, that is a contract change (remove the .avsc + AsyncAPI entry, consider ADR-IC §09 forward-only evolution + any live consumer) and must land in its own reviewed PR with the contract-reviewer + a schema-registry/Backstage orphan sweep — NOT a silent edit. If InterestPaid is promoted, author its .avsc + AsyncAPI entry. Either way the catalogue (the .avsc set) stays the single promotion record (ADR-IC-017 §P2). title: Retention sweeper for the dedup ledgers (command_dedup 0015 + inbox 0012) — bound unbounded growth
description:
In plain English: the engine's two dedup ledgers — the new command_dedup (migration 0015, command-ingress idempotency) and the existing inbox (migration 0012, event-consume dedup) — both grow one row per command/message forever. Each migration ships the SEAM for cleanup (a created_at/processed_at timestamp, a btree index to make a range-delete cheap, and a GRANT ... DELETE to the runtime role) but NOT the actual sweeper job. Surfaced 2026-06-13 reviewing PR #164 (t7o3.6).

Build the operational retention sweeper (a cron/hosted job) that deletes rows older than the retention window. Consistent with ADR-PC-029 slot 4 ('a bounded retention window is an implementation detail') and the 0012/0015 'sweep is operational, out of schema scope — the index is the seam' notes.

CORRECTNESS CONSTRAINT (not just disk): the command_dedup window is load-bearing. ADR-PC-029 slot 4 requires the uniqueness window be 'at least the stream's active lifetime'. Pruning a receipt too early lets a late retry of the same command_id either (a) re-execute and hit events_stream_seq_uq -> 409 for a deterministic deposit_id, or (b) WORSE, open a SECOND deposit for a server-generated deposit_id. So the window MUST exceed the dispatcher's max retry horizon (and per the ADR, the stream's active lifetime). The inbox window is the simpler Kafka-retention x N (7-30 days, Document 04). Pick per-table windows; do not assume one size fits both.

Also a GDPR data-minimization angle (the ledgers carry only structural ids/sequences, no PII, but retention discipline still applies). v1 is fine at low volume + no-op settlement; this is a pre-production gate.

title: spec-coverage-check.sh: code-anchor scan false-fails on macOS/BSD grep for the JSON fuzz test
description:
In plain English: the local spec-coverage hook (and a direct run of .github/scripts/spec-coverage-check.sh) reports a false failure on macOS for EVERY commitment-catalogue edit, because its 'code anchors point to a live ADR' scan greps engine/tests/Babelstone.Engine.Api.Tests/EngineApiJsonEnvelopeFuzzTests.cs, which BSD grep under a C/POSIX locale treats as binary (the fuzz corpus has non-UTF8/embedded bytes). grep then emits 'Binary file <path> matches', which the checker parses as a bogus code anchor -> '::error:: Code anchor ... resolves to no ADR file'. CI (Linux/GNU grep, UTF-8 locale) does NOT trip on this, so main is green and PRs pass; it is a local-only false positive. Pre-existing (reproduces on pristine main), surfaced 2026-06-13 while flipping ENGINE_COMMAND_IDEMPOTENT to Live in PR #164.

Fix options: (a) make the checker locale-robust / binary-skipping — set LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 for the greps, or add grep -I (skip binary) / -a, on the code-anchor scan at spec-coverage-check.sh ~line 156; (b) stop the fuzz test embedding raw non-UTF8 bytes (encode the corpus). (a) is the smaller, safer fix and keeps macOS dev hooks honest.
close_reason: Merged via PR #171 (fix/spec-coverage-binary-grep). Added -a (--binary-files=text) to the line-156 code-anchor grep so a fuzz-corpus test's non-text bytes no longer false-fail the gate; real anchors still extracted. Removes the local --no-verify workaround.

The v1 engine command ingress is synchronous REST (Option 2), chosen for operational simplicity and Primitive-1 alignment. Revisit after v1 once the load harness (Epic L) has throughput data: if the engine command leg is a measured bottleneck under the v4 burst targets, or a no-synchronous-in-estate-calls rule is adopted, migrate to an engine Kafka command-inbox (swap the dispatcher HTTP sink for a command topic + the engine InboxConsumer, which already exists). Low-regret either way: the saga and saga_outbox are unchanged.

title: Pact CDC consumer-driven contracts for GL/notify emission (ADR-IC-009)
description:
Stand up the ADR-IC-009 Pact consumer-driven contract (CDC) layer for the GL-posting and customer-notification emit contracts — the AUTHORITATIVE behavioural gate the G.6 emit-contract fitness tests (babelstone-2eo0, PR #122) defer to in their doc-comments.

WHY: the G.6 tests are cheap STRUCTURAL tripwires — a positive injected-dependency allowlist on the decide/append path, a 'static decider holds no port' assertion, and an outbox-shape assertion on AggregateRuntime. They prove no synchronous GL/notify port is wired and emission rides the post-commit outbox. They do NOT prove the emitted-event SHAPE meets each downstream consumer's expectations (field presence, never-null identity trio, money-as-cents, etc.). That closed-world behavioural guarantee is Pact producer verification in the engine's CI, per ADR-IC-009 (Pact + self-hosted Pact Broker).

GAP: Q.2 (babelstone-2f6q, Contracts CI) explicitly scopes itself to Avro/SR compat + EventCatalog 'npx validate' and EXCLUDES CDC (see its comment). So CDC has no filed home until this issue — the 'authoritative gate' the G.6 comments name was untracked.

SCOPE: GL-posting + notification consumer Pact message contracts; producer verification wired into the engine CI job; Pact Broker in the dev stack (ADR-IC-009 §S1).

GOVERNS: ADR-IC-009. VERIFIES the ADR-PC-012 / ADR-PC-025 slot-5 emit contracts. Depends on the GL/notify delivery ports/consumers (babelstone-a7d4.2) existing first.

title: Drop the dead act_act_isda entry from pt.2026.1 (declared formula_ref the engine does not implement)
description:
`packs/pt.2026.1/primitives/day-count.yaml` declares:

    act_act_isda:
      formula_ref: engine.day_count.actual_actual_isda
      permitted_for: []

But the engine does NOT implement that formula: `VerifiedPack.PackDayCount.ToConvention()`
has no `engine.day_count.actual_actual_isda` case, and `DayCountConvention`
(`DayCount.cs`) has no Act/Act ISDA member. The entry is DEAD — it would throw
`PackLoadException` at engine resolution. It is harmless TODAY only because
`permitted_for: []` blocks every variant from naming it (depth-4), so the
resolver is never reached.

Decision (per maintainer): DROP the dead entry rather than implement Act/Act
ISDA. Remove the `act_act_isda` block from
`packs/pt.2026.1/primitives/day-count.yaml`.

Timing / immutability: pt.2026.1 is NOT yet published or signed (cosign signing
unwired, depth-5 corpus pending), so this is a pre-publication correction edited
in place — NOT a violation of the pack-immutability rule. If pt.2026.1 were
already published, the fix would have to ship as a new pack version instead. Do
this BEFORE pt.2026.1 is ever signed/published, so a dead `formula_ref` never
ships.

Done = `act_act_isda` removed from `pt.2026.1/primitives/day-count.yaml`;
`make pack-validate PACK=pt.2026.1` still green; every `formula_ref` remaining in
the pack resolves in `VerifiedPack.ToConvention()`.

Discovered while building the `docs/product-docs/` Diátaxis POC
(`how-to/add-a-day-count-primitive.md`); see sfnt.15 (engine-primitives
reference), which would make such dead entries visible.
close_reason: Merged in 34c0fb2 / gh-120 (dropped dead act_act_isda from pt.2026.1).

title: Engine emits a machine-readable primitive manifest for docs-gen (replace regex-over-C#)
description:
Upgrade path for the engine-primitives reference renderer (sfnt.15). sfnt.15's
MVP parses the engine's implemented `formula_ref` set out of C# source by REGEX
(`VerifiedPack.ToConvention()` switch + the `DayCountConvention` enum). That is
brittle to reformatting: a valid re-style of the switch can make the renderer
miss cases. sfnt.15 mitigates by failing loud on a parse miss — but that is a
hard CI break, not a fix.

Trigger (deferred — pick up on need): when the regex approach starts breaking (a
`ToConvention()` reformat breaks docs-gen), or proactively if adding a second
primitive family (withholding, …) makes C#-parsing too fragile to maintain.

The fix is to stop parsing C# and instead have the ENGINE emit a
machine-readable manifest of its implemented primitives that docs-gen consumes —
single source of truth, so the resolver and the published catalogue cannot
diverge. See design.

Done = docs-gen sources `reference/engine-primitives/` from the engine-emitted
manifest (not regex); `make docs-verify` stays byte-identical and green; the
sfnt.15 regex parser is removed.

Anchors: ADR-PC-022 §P1/§P2 (generated reference, NO_DRIFT/BANNERED), ADR-PC-006,
ADR-PC-007. Run via `mise exec --`.
design:
Two options to emit the manifest:

(a) A tiny `dotnet run` tool (e.g. `tools/PrimitiveCatalog`) that prints the
    implemented {formula_ref -> convention -> description} set as JSON; docs-gen
    reads the JSON and renders the table.
(b) A `[FormulaRef("engine.day_count.actual_360")]` attribute on the resolver
    cases / convention enum members, scanned via reflection by that tool.
    Strongest form: the resolver and the published catalogue derive from the
    same attributes, so they cannot drift.

Cost: this adds a `dotnet` dependency to the docs-gen path. Today docs-gen needs
only python + mise + cue; `make docs-verify` in CI would then also need the .NET
toolchain (and a build). That cost is exactly why it is the upgrade-when-needed,
NOT the MVP — sfnt.15's regex renderer ships first; this replaces it if/when it
earns its keep.

Source: the robustness note recorded in sfnt.15's design, promoted to its own
deferred issue at maintainer request.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs-gen sources reference/engine-primitives/ from an engine-emitted machine-readable manifest, not a regex over C# source.
- make docs-verify stays byte-identical and green.
- The sfnt.15 regex parser is removed (ADR-PC-022 §P1/§P2 NO_DRIFT/BANNERED honoured).
close_reason: Closing as deferred/won't-do-now so Epic R (sfnt) can close. P3 upgrade-when-needed for the engine-primitives renderer; verified (per the 2026-06-17 trigger check) neither trigger is hit — the day-count regex renderer still works, make docs-verify is green, no ToConvention() reformat has broken docs-gen. Reopen when the regex breaks or a second primitive family makes C#-parsing too fragile.

title: Generate an engine-primitives reference set (formula_ref catalogue) in docs-gen
description:
**Gap.** `formula_ref` (in a pack's `primitives/day-count.yaml`, and the other
`primitives/*.yaml`) is the one pack field whose validity the pack toolchain
**cannot check**. `make pack-validate` confirms the string is well-formed and
(for a variant) that the *pack* carries the day-count; it does NOT confirm the
engine implements the formula. That binding is resolved only at engine load — an
unimplemented `formula_ref` throws there (`VerifiedPack.PackDayCount.ToConvention()`),
never at validate time.

The authoritative list of implemented primitives therefore lives ONLY in engine
C# source. Unlike events (Avro), family schemas (CUE), and pack-format (pack.cue),
it is NOT rendered into the generated reference (`docs/product-management/reference/`).
So a config author has no drift-proof place to look up which `formula_ref` values
are valid — they must read the resolver switch.

**What to build.** A 7th renderer in `scripts/docs-gen/generate.py` emitting
`docs/product-management/reference/engine-primitives/`, listing the day-count
`formula_ref` values the engine actually implements, under the existing
`make docs-verify` gate (ADR-PC-022 §P2 NO_DRIFT/BANNERED). Today the resolver
implements exactly three: `engine.day_count.{actual_360, actual_365,
thirty_360_european}`. Extend to withholding `formula_ref`s (same pattern) as a
follow-on.

**Latent defect this surfaces (decide whether to file separately).**
`packs/pt.2026.1/primitives/day-count.yaml` declares
`act_act_isda -> engine.day_count.actual_actual_isda`, but `ToConvention()` has no
such case and `DayCountConvention` has no such member — the engine does NOT
implement it. It passes `make pack-validate` and would throw at engine load;
harmless TODAY only because its `permitted_for: []` blocks every variant from
reaching the resolver. The renderer would make this visible (a declared key with
no implemented row). Consider a separate Epic C / pack-correctness bug to either
implement Act/Act ISDA or drop the dead entry.

**Done =** `mise exec -- make docs-verify` passes byte-identical against a fresh
`make docs-gen`; `reference/engine-primitives/README.md` lists exactly the
`formula_ref` cases in `VerifiedPack.ToConvention()`; the page carries the
DO-NOT-EDIT banner; the root reference index (`render_root_index`) gains its row.

Source files: `engine/src/Babelstone.Packs/VerifiedPack.cs`
(`PackDayCount.ToConvention()` switch), `engine/src/Babelstone.FinancialMath/DayCount.cs`
(`DayCountConvention` enum + `<summary>` docs). Anchors: ADR-PC-022 §P1/§P2,
ADR-PC-007 (formula_ref rejected at load), ADR-PC-006.

Discovered while building the `docs/product-docs/` Diátaxis POC
(`how-to/add-a-day-count-primitive.md`): a reader asked "how do I know which
engine primitives exist?" and the honest answer was "read the C# switch."
design:
Sketch — fits generate.py's "one renderer per source kind" pattern; pure
file-read + regex, NO new toolchain dep (does not need cue/dotnet, so it runs
even when the CUE-pinned renderers can't).

Add `render_engine_primitives(slugs)` returning
`{"engine-primitives/README.md": ...}`; register in `build()`; add a row to
`render_root_index()`; update the module docstring's renderer list (currently
"Five renderers").

Parse BOTH source files and JOIN, so the page cannot silently drift:
- From VerifiedPack.cs: regex the ToConvention() switch arms
    "(engine\.[a-z0-9_.]+)"\s*=>\s*DayCountConvention\.([A-Za-z0-9]+)
  -> list of (formula_ref, enum_member), sorted by formula_ref.
- From DayCount.cs: isolate `enum DayCountConvention { ... }`, pair each member
  with the first sentence of its /// <summary> XML doc (strip tags, collapse
  whitespace) -> {member: description}.
- Emit: | `formula_ref` | Convention (member) | Description |.

Fail loud (raise RuntimeError) if: no switch arms matched (ToConvention()
reformatted -> renderer must be updated), or a switch arm maps to an enum member
that doesn't exist (engine inconsistency). This keeps the regex approach honest:
a parse miss fails the build instead of silently emitting an empty/wrong page.

Banner cites both sources: banner(f"{rel(VERIFIEDPACK_CS)} + {rel(DAYCOUNT_CS)}").
Determinism: two fixed files, rows sorted by formula_ref, no timestamps/abs
paths -> docs-verify diffs cleanly.

Brittleness note + more robust alternative: regex-over-C# is brittle to
formatting. If it proves fragile, the durable form is to have the engine emit a
machine-readable manifest of implemented primitives (e.g. a small
`dotnet run` tool that prints JSON, or a [FormulaRef("engine.day_count.actual_360")]
attribute scanned via reflection) that docs-gen consumes — single source of
truth, no parsing. That adds a dotnet dependency to the docs-gen path, so only
do it if the regex MVP starts breaking.

Mirrors sibling bd babelstone-sfnt.14 (another deferred generate.py renderer).
Run/verify via `mise exec --` per CLAUDE.md.

title: DEFERRED: generated collapsed-current-truth-view renderer for amended ADRs
description:
@
DEFERRED follow-up (P3) — not part of the "start just with PC-014" active set. Superseding PC-014 (R.15) already
removes the one demonstrated replay-the-log wart, so this is the PROPHYLACTIC for the remaining/future amended
ADRs that keep their amendments in place (e.g. ADR-PC-010s .NET 9->10 + Money->FinancialTypes namespace rename
replay-in-miniature; ADR-PC-004s A1 KV-secrets mini-spec). Pick this up only if those reads start to hurt or a
new contract-shape ADR accretes an amendment that is NOT resolved by supersede-clean.

When taken up: extend scripts/docs-gen/generate.py with a renderer that emits, under docs/product-management/
reference/, a current-truth view of each amended ADR with its Decision + Amendment blocks + inline *Revised* lines
FLATTENED into one present-tense reading (ADR source stays immutable; reader gets a clean view; cannot drift —
generated + CI-diffed by the existing docs-verify lane). Honours ADR-PC-022 §P2 NO_DRIFT/BANNERED.
@
design:

Keep `deposit_position` as the family-layer table name (it does not collide with the engine's `projections`).

title: Extract generic ConstitutionPipeline from family deciders (DRY, on the 2nd decider)

Rule-of-three: extract on the second instance, NOT the first, so AT_MATURITY-specific assumptions don't get frozen (PERIODIC/ADVANCE lifecycles differ). E.3's decider is deliberately structured for-lift so this is a refactor, not a rewrite. Relates to Epic F (babelstone-k6r8).

- On the second decider, the common constitution choreography is extracted into a generic engine-level ConstitutionPipeline plus a pure IDecider<TState> abstraction (family supplies only Decide(inputs,state)->events and SettlementsFor(events)).

title: RateBand correct-by-construction via JsonConverter

title: B.8b — DL 133/2009 / Banco de Portugal regulator-published TAEG anchor
description: Deferred from B.8 (archie-mi05.2): the independent external-anchor tier shipped with closed-form/spreadsheet anchors, but the regulator-published cross-check was deferred because citing a published TAEG requires the authentic figures (fabricating one defeats the tier's auditable-provenance purpose). Source the DL 133/2009 Anexo / Banco de Portugal worked example's exact CF vector + published TAEG, add it as a CorpusTier.IndependentAnchor case in FinancialMathGoldenCorpus, and assert the §6 solver reproduces the published figure. Anchors: financial_concepts §6.2.
notes:
INVESTIGATION 2026-05-27 (could not complete faithfully — keep blocked):

1. PREMISE CORRECTION: The DL 133/2009 Anexo has NO numeric worked examples. Confirmed by reading the authoritative original Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I (OJ L 133, 22.5.2008, which Portugal transposes verbatim): it contains only the present-value equation, Remarks (a)-(e), and Part II assumptions (a)-(j). The 2002-proposal example set was NOT retained in the binding text. So 'DL 133/2009 Anexo worked examples' do not exist as numbers in the law.

2. The genuine published examples live in EC guidance (2012 Guidelines SWD(2012)128; 2009 APRC study) and Banco de Portugal consumer materials — not the law. The EC PDFs returned 404/403; bportugal.pt returned 403 to WebFetch.

3. One accessible BdP example (page 'O que e a TAEG'): loan EUR 12,000 / 60 months / TAN 8% / EUR 200 initial commission -> published TAEG 10.3%. BUT a faithful reconstruction (net disbursement 11,800; 60 installments of 243.32 computed at 0.08/12; annualize monthly IRR by 12) yields TAEG = 9.1%, not 10.3%. The €200 alone moves TAE 8.3% -> 9.1%; the published 10.3% must include charges the consumer-page summary does not itemize (most likely a per-installment processing fee, which enters the TAEG). This is the 'external numbers disagree for non-bug reasons' risk noted in the issue.

NEXT STEP to unblock: obtain a FULLY ITEMIZED regulator/EC worked example — the complete CF vector with every charge (upfront + per-installment) and the published TAEG — then encode it as a CorpusTier.IndependentAnchor and assert the §6 solver reproduces it to 1-decimal precision. The kernel CAN model it (equally-spaced monthly => integer-period IRR + annualize by 12 = the directive's annual TAEG). No code was added (no faithful anchor available); B.8's closed-form independent tier already shipped and stands.
DEFERRED 2026-05-27 (owner decision): the B.8 independent tier (closed-form quadratic-IRR-vs-Newton + spreadsheet anchors on fresh inputs) gives sufficient method-independence; the regulator-published cross-check is nice-to-have hardening, not load-bearing. Reopen if/when a fully-itemized regulator worked example (complete CF vector + every charge + published TAEG) is available.
close_reason: Descoped to v2 (epic-closure decision 2026-06-26). Blocked on external data: a fully-itemized regulator/EC TAEG worked example (full CF vector + every charge + published TAEG) could not be sourced (DL 133/2009 Anexo has no worked numbers; EC '44 examples' not machine-fetchable; the BdP example omits charge itemization → reconstructs to 9.1% vs published 10.3%). P3 hardening, not load-bearing — the closed-form IndependentAnchor tier already gives method-independence. Roadmap places TAEG-with-charges in v2 (personal credit). Re-open in v2 when an itemized example is in hand.

title: ADR-PC-015: IFRS 9 signal contract
description:
IFRS 9 implementation is out of scope; the signal contract between the engine and the external IFRS 9 system is in scope. Contract-shape ADR. v2-relevant (lands with personal credit) but flag now so 04-open-questions.md §2 has a tracked decision.

Three signal families:
- Staging triggers (Stage 1 → Stage 2 on significant increase in credit risk; Stage 2 → Stage 3 on default).
- Days-past-due tracking (continuous signal per exposure).
- Restructuring events (LoanRestructured with contextual data; IFRS 9 system interprets regulatory meaning).

Two shapes for the contract:
(a) One big event per staging change (Stage1To2, Stage2To3).
(b) Two signals — continuous days-past-due tracker plus discrete restructuring/forbearance events — from which the IFRS 9 system derives staging.

(b) is more compositional and reusable across IFRS 9 vendors. (a) is simpler if the bank uses a single known IFRS 9 vendor.

Unblocked by: IFRS 9 SME conversation (risk-quant or model-validation lead at the operating bank, or consultant who has integrated several IFRS 9 vendors).

Source: §2 in 04-open-questions.md.
close_reason: Filed ADR-PC-015 (IFRS 9 signal contract), contract-shape ADR adopting shape (b): engine emits raw operational facts (continuous days-past-due tracker + discrete restructuring/write-off events); IFRS 9 system derives staging/ECL. No stage event emitted. Indexed in adrs/README.md; partial-commitment note added to 04-open-questions §2; live cross-link added in ADR-PC-014. SME conversation + v2 credit scope remain the production gate.

title: Revisit ADR-011 D6: evaluate fully deprecating the saga status SSE stream for all clients
description:
ADR-011 D6 decided that SSE (the stream_url in the 202 response, doc 05 / ADR-006) coexists with webhook callbacks rather than being deprecated. The rationale was that SSE remains correct for browser/mobile clients that can hold a connection.

The question to re-examine: should the saga status SSE be deprecated for ALL clients — including browser/mobile — in favour of polling (get_process_status, Pattern 2) + callbacks (Pattern 3, ADR-011)?

Background:
- The MCP transport SSE (HTTP+SSE from spec 2024-11-05) is already deprecated and replaced by Streamable HTTP per ADR-010. That is a separate and settled matter.
- The saga status SSE is NOT Streamable HTTP's replacement target. Streamable HTTP is MCP-specific; browsers don't use MCP. If the saga status SSE were deprecated, the replacement for browser clients would be polling + callbacks, not Streamable HTTP.
- Keeping SSE means Kong must maintain the extended read_timeout and X-Accel-Buffering:no configuration (ADR-006 P4) indefinitely. It also means the 202 response carries stream_url for all clients even if most will ignore it once the webhook path matures.

Arguments for deprecating:
- One completion model (polling + callbacks) for all clients simplifies the surface considerably: one path to maintain, test, and document
- Browser/mobile clients can use polling (get_process_status) for saga tracking; the UX is slightly less real-time but adequate for sagas that take hundreds of milliseconds to complete
- The SSE path is the operationally complex one (long-lived connections, Kong read_timeout tuning, load balancer idle timeout configuration)

Arguments against deprecating:
- Browser UX for fast sagas (~700ms) regresses: instead of watching the saga complete in near-real-time, the client must poll
- Owned clients (bank's own mobile app, web frontend) should not be forced to adopt an async model that was designed for disconnected agents
- ADR-011 D6 was a deliberate decision with a sound rationale; revisiting it should require a concrete trigger

Deliverable: either affirm ADR-011 D6 (coexistence is correct) with a note on when to revisit, or produce an amendment to ADR-006, ADR-011, and docs 00/05 that removes stream_url and the SSE path.
close_reason:
Evaluated — affirm ADR-011 D6: coexistence is correct.

Rationale:
1. The 202 arrives in ~150ms; the saga finishes in ~850ms. For a browser client watching 'Processing...', SSE delivers real-time completion with zero polling latency. Replacing SSE with polling adds 0-500ms perceived latency and extra round-trips — a real regression for owned browser/mobile clients.

2. The operational concern (long-lived connections, Kong config) is already closed: ADR-006 P4 documents exactly the required Kong configuration (extended read_timeout, X-Accel-Buffering:no). Operational surface is a few lines of kong.yaml, not ongoing burden.

3. No concrete trigger exists. The issue's own text says 'revisiting should require a concrete trigger.'

Trigger conditions for future revisitation:
- If the bank's owned browser/mobile clients are redesigned to go through MCP (at which point MCP tasks + get_process_status already exist and SSE becomes genuinely redundant)
- If Kong SSE proxying produces measurable operational incidents in a production environment
- If the polling + callback path proves sufficient in a production deployment and the SSE path adds no meaningful UX benefit over polling with aggressive intervals (<200ms)

title: ADR-010 candidate: MCP server runtime and SDK selection
description: Doc 11 (chat agent channel strategy, babelstone-407) commits to exposing a bank-owned MCP server as the integration surface for LLM agents but does not pick the runtime, SDK, or transport implementation. Candidates include the official Python SDK (modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk), TypeScript SDK (modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk), or a Go/Rust implementation; transport choice between Streamable HTTP (current default for remote servers in MCP spec 2025-11-25) and SSE; hosting model (alongside the existing edge gateway behind Kong from ADR-006, or as a separate service with its own ingress); and the OAuth 2.1 authorisation server integration (existing IAM that already issues JWTs for the REST edge, vs. a dedicated MCP-specific authorisation server with dynamic client registration enabled). This ADR should follow the ADR-000 evaluation framework and reference doc 11 as the conceptual grounding for what the MCP server must support (tools, resources, prompts, elicitation form+url modes, tasks capability per SEP-1686, server-initiated notifications).

title: Cross-cutting editorial sweep across ADR series
description: Apply consistent edits across all ADRs as a single pass: (1) Audit and strike 'trivially/trivial' usages — if it is trivial, the word is unnecessary; if it is not, the word is wrong. (2) Replace softener phrases ('effectively zero', 'effectively open') with the actual constraint. (3) Audit 'may/should' inside Implementation Principles sections (ADR-003 through ADR-008); principles are normative, so prefer 'must' or declarative present tense. (4) Reduce em-dash density in opening paragraphs and dense analytical passages — three em-dashes per paragraph reads as nested asides. (5) Anchor all relative date phrases ('since 2020', 'as of 2026') to the ADR header date or a specific calendar date.
close_reason: Four targeted edits across the series: (1) ADR-004 line 134 'trivially implemented' -> 'a handful of lines' (the one remaining claim-of-trivial in the series — others matching the grep are legitimate uses of 'non-trivial' meaning 'difficult'); (2) ADR-001 line 75 'effectively zero' -> 'negligible' (the assertive form); (3) ADR-002 line 89 'effectively seamless' -> 'seamless'; (4) ADR-007 P4 'should use pseudonymous identifiers wherever possible' rewritten to 'must default to pseudonymous identifiers; raw identifiers require an explicit justification at the call site that survives code review' — strengthens the normative verb while preserving the legitimate exception path. Deliberately did NOT do: em-dash reduction (28-44 per file is mostly structural use, not nested asides — flattening it would damage the author's voice for negligible clarity gain) and broad date-anchor sweep (almost all 'as of YEAR' / 'in YEAR' references already carry a year, which is itself an anchor; the residual unanchored 'since 2020' was already fixed in P2). Most 'may/should' inside Implementation Principles are normatively-correct prohibitions ('No saga may hold...') or permissions ('Services may add...').
